docs.title: Frappe Framework
docs.text:
Frappe Framework is a full-stack web framework in Python and JavaScript. It is metadata driven. You describe data as DocTypes, and Frappe makes the database tables, the REST API, the desk forms, lists and reports, and the permission checks. You put your code in apps. A bench runs many sites, and each site installs a set of apps.

Version: develop (unreleased)

These pages describe the develop branch (17.0.0-dev). Every page was verified against the code of this branch. For a release, read the v16 docs or the v15 docs.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: If you want to Read Install Frappe and make a site Installation Understand how the parts fit Architecture Build a first app Quickstart Look up a term Glossary See what changed since version 16 What's New

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
• User Guide: use the desk, set up users and permissions, automate work, print, report and publish web pages.
  • Developer Guide: build apps: DocTypes, controllers, hooks, the database API, REST, background jobs, desk scripts, website pages and tests.
  • Reference: complete lists of hooks, CLI commands, REST endpoints, site config keys, Python and JavaScript APIs, field types and DocTypes.
  • For AI Agents: rules and facts for agents that write or change Frappe apps.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Examples use the app sample_app, the DocTypes Sample Item and Sample Order, the role Sample Role and the user user1@example.com.
  • File paths in frappe/... are relative to the frappe app repository. Paths in sample_app/... are files in your app.
  • Commands run from the bench folder. Replace <site> with your site name.

docs.title: For AI Agents
docs.text: Read this page before you write or change code for a Frappe app on develop (17.0.0-dev). Every fact here was checked in this branch. For an index of all pages with one-line summaries, read llms.txt.

docs.title: Know the version first
docs.text:
1. Run bench version or read frappe/__init__.py __version__. These docs are for 17.0.0-dev.
  2. Do not use an API from another version without checking it. For example, frappe.read_doc, frappe.enqueue_task, bench enable-app exist only in develop. extend_doctype_class exists in version 16 and later.

docs.title: Where to look
docs.text: Question Page Which hooks exist and what shape they take Hooks reference Run order of controller methods and doc_events Controllers Signatures of frappe.*, frappe.db.*, frappe.utils.* Python API, Database API, Utils Client-side frappe.* and frm API JavaScript API, Form Scripts REST routes REST Endpoints CLI commands and flags CLI Config keys Site Config Field types and DB columns Field Types

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use frappe.session.user for the current user. frappe.user is None on develop.
  • Check permissions in every whitelisted method. Use frappe.read_doc or doc.check_permission(). frappe.get_doc does not check read permission.
  • frappe.get_all ignores permissions. frappe.get_list applies them. Neither has a default row limit on develop. Pass limit (or page_length).
  • frappe.db.set_value, frappe.db.sql and frappe.qb skip validations, controller methods and permissions. frappe.db.set_value clears the document cache. Raw SQL and frappe.qb updates do not.
  • frappe.qb.get_query ignores permissions by default and adds no ORDER BY.
  • Write SQL functions in fields in the dict form. A string such as "count(name) as c" raises ValidationError.
  • Do not call frappe.db.commit() in a request handler or a controller method. The request commits when it succeeds. Inside doc_events handlers a commit is ignored with a warning. Writes in a GET request are rolled back.
  • Use enqueue_after_commit=True when a job reads data that the current request writes.
  • Add type annotations to every whitelisted method. Request arguments are validated against them. Apps made by bench new-app set require_type_annotated_api_methods = True, so a method without annotations fails.
  • A whitelisted method without methods=[...] accepts GET. Restrict methods that write: @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"]).
  • The server does not evaluate depends_on, mandatory_depends_on or read_only_depends_on. Only the desk does.
  • Dotted paths in hooks.py fail only when the hook runs. Check that each path imports.
  • override_doctype_class, extend_doctype_class, doctype_js and doctype_list_js do not apply to custom DocTypes (custom = 1).
  • Deleting a DocType or a Custom Field leaves its database table or column in place.

docs.title: Lifecycle order (insert)
docs.text: before_insert → before_naming → autoname → before_validate → validate → before_save → DB insert → after_insert → on_update → on_change. For each step, Frappe runs the controller method, then the doc_events handlers for the DocType, then the "*" handlers. See Controllers for save, submit, cancel, delete and the exact rules.

docs.title: Pitfalls seen in this code base
docs.text:
• naming_series: reads only the naming_series field.
  • All format: names with {#####} and no fixed prefix share one counter in tabSeries.
  • A Server Script with event "Before Save" runs on validate, not on before_save.
  • server_script_enabled works only in common_site_config.json.
  • Fixture import deletes and inserts again any record that already exists. Changes made on the site to a fixture record are lost at each bench migrate.
  • frappe.sendmail(now=True) sends after the transaction commits.
  • A query report runs in a read-only transaction. Uncommitted writes in the same transaction raise ImplicitCommitError.
  • Error, access and activity logs are in sites/<site>/private/files/sqlite.db, not in the main database.

docs.title: What's New in develop
docs.text:
This page lists the changes in develop (17.0.0-dev) since version 16. Each item was checked in both code bases. For steps to move an app, see Upgrading.

Unreleased

develop is not a release. APIs on this page can change before version 17.

docs.title: New features
docs.text: Area Change Docs Apps An app can be disabled on a site and stay installed. New commands bench enable-app and bench disable-app. New hooks before_enable, after_enable, before_disable, after_disable. New functions frappe.get_active_apps() and frappe.get_disabled_apps(). App State Files Storage v2 (alpha): pluggable drivers (storage_drivers hook), the File Blob DocType, signed URLs. It is off unless the storage_v2 site config flag is set. New hooks after_file_upload and ignore_file_permissions. Files Jobs frappe.enqueue_task() and the Background Task DocType. MapReduce Job and MapReduce Task DocTypes. Background Jobs Permissions frappe.read_doc() gets a document and checks read permission. Permissions REST API v2 bulk endpoints: /api/v2/document/<doctype>/bulk_delete, /api/v2/document/<doctype>/bulk_update, /api/v2/method/bulk_delete, /api/v2/method/bulk_update. The HTTP QUERY method is accepted for list calls. REST API Whitelisted methods Hook require_type_annotated_api_methods: when true, a whitelisted method without type annotations fails when called. New apps set it to true. Hook use_json_request_body. Whitelisted Methods Requests Hook streaming_request_paths. Hooks reference Printing The default PDF generator is PlutoPrint. wkhtmltopdf is removed. A patch moves sites that used it to Chrome. Print Formats Logs Error Log, Access Log, Activity Log, Route History and Web Page View rows are stored in sites/<site>/private/files/sqlite.db. A database backup does not include them. Back up files too. Backups Desk The list sidebar group-by is replaced by "Customize Quick Filters". Saved list layouts are List Filter documents. New Kanban boards use Kanban v2. List View

docs.title: New DocTypes
docs.text: Background Task, Custom Icon, Document Template, DocType Layout Child Table, File Blob, MapReduce Job, MapReduce Task, Notification Webhook URL, Server Script Variable, Workflow Condition.

docs.title: Moved, renamed or removed
docs.text: Item Change DocType Layout, DocType Layout Field Moved from the Custom module to the Core module. Slack Webhook URL Renamed to Notification Webhook URL. The patches rename_slack_webhook_url and migrate_slack_notifications move existing data. A Notification with channel Slack in an app fixture or a JSON export is converted when it loads. Sidebar Item Group, Sidebar Item Group Link Removed. frappe/__init__.py Public names load lazily from other modules. frappe.<name> still works. Path and app helpers (get_app_path, get_site_path, get_module_path, get_installed_apps, get_attr, scrub and others) are defined in other modules now. Import them from frappe, not from their new module. Build esbuild is updated to version 0.28. @frappe/esbuild-plugin-postcss2 is removed. Tests The cypress/ folder is removed.

docs.title: Unchanged requirements
docs.text: Python >=3.14,<3.15 and Node >=24, the same as version 16. See Installation.

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text:
Build and extend Frappe apps: app structure, data model, fields and controls, database, security, APIs, background work, desk UI, website, output, low-code tools, testing and operations.

Topic What it covers Building Apps Create an app, use hooks, extend other apps, ship fixtures and patches, translate, and enable or disable apps. Data Model Define DocTypes, naming rules, controllers and the document lifecycle, and handle files. Fields and Controls How each field type works in the desk, its properties, its stored value, and the JavaScript control API. Database Read and write data with frappe.db and frappe.qb, and control transactions. Permissions and Security Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code. Requests and APIs Follow a request through the framework, expose whitelisted methods, use and customize the REST API, and connect AI clients over MCP. Jobs, Realtime and Caching Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data. Desk UI Script forms and lists, call the server from JavaScript, and build desk pages and navigation. Website and Portal Build website pages, portal pages, routes and web forms. Reports, Printing and Email Write script and query reports, print formats and PDFs, and send email and notifications. Low-Code and AI Use server and client scripts, the automation engine, Flow agents and Studio apps. Testing and Performance Test apps and make them fast. Configuration and Operations Configure sites, deploy to production and upgrade between versions.

docs.title: Requests and APIs
docs.text:
Follow a request through the framework, expose whitelisted methods, use and customize the REST API, and connect AI clients over MCP.

Page What it covers Request Lifecycle Follow one HTTP request through frappe.app.application, from site resolution, session and auth to dispatch, commit, response, cleanup and errors. Whitelisted Methods Expose Python functions over HTTP with @frappe.whitelist, validate arguments with type annotations, restrict access by role, rate limit, and override methods of other apps. REST API Read and change documents and call whitelisted methods over HTTP with /api/v1 (resource, method) and /api/v2 (document, doctype, method), including list parameters, bulk operations, responses and errors. API Internals How Frappe routes an /api request to a function, checks whitelist, guest and HTTP method rules, binds arguments, and turns frappe.response into JSON, files, redirects and errors. Customizing APIs Every way an app can add or change API behavior in Frappe, from whitelisted methods and overrides to doc_events, permission hooks, request hooks, auth hooks, CORS, response formats, versioning and tests. MCP and API Discovery Connect AI agents to a site through the built-in MCP endpoint at /api/v2/mcp, and describe whitelisted methods with the /api/v2/discovery endpoints.

docs.title: API Internals
docs.text:
This page shows what Frappe does with a request after the path starts with /api/. Read it to debug an API call, to understand an error response, or to return something other than JSON. For how to call the API, see REST API. For the steps before /api dispatch (site, session, before_request), see Architecture.

All examples were run on http://frappe.localhost:8000 with bench start. Responses are shortened. Long tracebacks are shown as "<traceback>".

docs.title: Where /api starts
docs.text:
application() in frappe/app.py sends every path that starts with /api/ to frappe.api.handle(request). Before that, init_request() has built frappe.form_dict and loaded the session, and validate_auth() has set the user from the Authorization header or auth_hooks.

Note

A request with a cmd form value goes to frappe.handler.handle() before the /api/ check. This form is deprecated. Use /api/method/<dotted.path>.

frappe.api.handle() (frappe/api/__init__.py) does this:

  1. If System Settings log_api_requests is on, it queues an API Request Log with the path, user and HTTP method.
  2. It matches the path against API_URL_MAP. No match raises frappe.DoesNotExistError (HTTP 404).
  3. It calls the endpoint with the URL arguments (for example doctype, name, method).
  4. If the endpoint returns a werkzeug Response, Frappe sends it as is.
  5. Otherwise, a return value that is not None goes into frappe.response["data"].
  6. build_response("json") makes the response from frappe.response.

docs.title: URL map
docs.text:
API_URL_MAP is a Werkzeug Map with three mounts. strict_slashes=False, so a trailing slash is optional.

Mount Rules Endpoints in /api v1 frappe/api/v1.py /api/v1 v1 (same rules) frappe/api/v1.py /api/v2 v2 frappe/api/v2.py

v1 rules:

Rule HTTP methods Endpoint /method/<path:method> all handle_rpc_call /resource/<doctype> GET, QUERY document_list /resource/<doctype> POST create_doc /resource/<doctype>/<path:name> GET read_doc (or execute_doc_method with run_method) /resource/<doctype>/<path:name> PUT update_doc /resource/<doctype>/<path:name> DELETE delete_doc /resource/<doctype>/<path:name> POST, QUERY execute_doc_method

v2 rules (discovery and MCP rules are left out, see MCP and API Discovery):

Rule HTTP methods Endpoint /method/login all login (does nothing) /method/logout POST logout /method/ping all frappe.ping /method/upload_file POST frappe.handler.upload_file /method/bulk_delete, /method/bulk_update POST bulk_delete, bulk_update /method/run_doc_method GET, POST, QUERY run_doc_method /method/<method> all handle_rpc_call /method/<doctype>/<method> all handle_rpc_call with doctype /document/<doctype> GET, QUERY document_list /document/<doctype> POST create_doc /document/<doctype>/bulk_delete, /document/<doctype>/bulk_update POST bulk_delete_docs, bulk_update_docs /document/<doctype>/<path:name> GET read_doc /document/<doctype>/<path:name>/copy GET copy_doc /document/<doctype>/<path:name> PATCH, PUT update_doc /document/<doctype>/<path:name> DELETE delete_doc /document/<doctype>/<path:name>/method/<method> GET, POST, QUERY execute_doc_method /doctype/<doctype>/meta GET get_meta /doctype/<doctype>/count GET, QUERY count

Rules with a fixed path win over rules with variables. So /api/v2/method/run_doc_method goes to run_doc_method, not to handle_rpc_call. The v2 <method> part cannot contain /. The v1 <path:method> part can, and v1 drops everything after the first /.

The endpoints in frappe/api/v2.py are not whitelisted functions. The route itself is the permission to call them. They check document permissions in their own code.

docs.title: Route errors
How a method call is resolved
docs.text:
/api/method/<path> and /api/v2/method/<path> both end in the same checks. v1 goes through frappe.handler.handle() and execute_cmd(). v2 calls handle_rpc_call() in frappe/api/v2.py.

  1. v1 only: Frappe sets frappe.form_dict.cmd to the dotted path. If the path is login, nothing is called. The login already ran in LoginManager (see Login).
  2. v2 with /method/<doctype>/<method>: Frappe loads the controller module of the DocType and makes the path <module>.<method>.
  3. frappe.override_whitelisted_method(path) replaces the path with the last value of override_whitelisted_methods for that key.
  4. If an enabled Server Script of type API has this path as its method name, the script runs. The steps below are skipped.
  5. resolve_method() imports the function with frappe.get_attr. A path without a dot is looked up in frappe/handler.py (v1 only, deprecated).
  6. frappe.is_whitelisted(fn) checks the whitelist (see Whitelist checks).
  7. is_valid_http_method(fn) checks the HTTP method against the methods of @frappe.whitelist.
  8. frappe.call(fn, **frappe.form_dict) calls the function (see Argument binding).
  9. v1 puts the return value in frappe.response["message"]. v2 puts it in frappe.response["data"]. A None return value adds no key.

frappe.handler.run_doc_method is the one exception in v1: execute_cmd() does not run steps 6 and 7 on it. It checks the whitelist and HTTP method on the controller method instead.

If the import fails in step 5, a user who may see tracebacks gets the reason. Other users get "Method not found". Both are frappe.ValidationError (HTTP 417).

curl -s -b cookies.txt "$S/api/v2/method/frappe.nonexistent.fn"

{"errors": [{"type": "ValidationError", "exception": "<traceback>",
  "message": "Failed to get method for command frappe.nonexistent.fn with No module named 'frappe.nonexistent'",
  "as_table": false, "title": "Message", "indicator": "red"}]}

docs.title: Whitelist checks
docs.text:
frappe.is_whitelisted(fn) in frappe/__init__.py raises an error in these cases:

Case Exception HTTP The app of the function (first part of fn.__module__) is disabled on the site frappe.AppDisabledError 417 fn has no @frappe.whitelist() frappe.PermissionError "Function ... is not whitelisted." 403 The user is Guest and fn has no allow_guest=True frappe.PermissionError 403 As above, and the session cookie has expired (frappe.response.session_expired) frappe.SessionExpired 401

For a guest call to a method without xss_safe=True, Frappe then sanitizes every string in frappe.form_dict with frappe.utils.sanitize_html_payload. <script>x</script><b>hi</b> becomes <b>hi</b>.

is_valid_http_method(fn) raises frappe.PermissionError "Not permitted" (HTTP 403) when the request method is not allowed. It does not check in a background job or in a Server Script (frappe.flags.in_safe_exec). @frappe.whitelist() without methods allows GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and QUERY. PATCH is not in this list.

curl -s -b cookies.txt -X PATCH "$S/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" -w ' %{http_code}\n'

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.PermissionError: Not permitted", "exc_type": "PermissionError", "exc": "<traceback>",
 "_server_messages": "[\"{\\\"message\\\":\\\"Not permitted\\\", ...}\"]"} 403

docs.title: Controller methods
docs.text:
A whitelisted method on a DocType controller runs through one of these routes:

Route Loads the document with Permission checked v1 POST /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with run_method frappe.get_doc(doctype, name) write v1 GET or QUERY /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with run_method same read v2 /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> same read for GET, QUERY. write for POST v1 /api/method/run_doc_method (frappe.handler.run_doc_method), args method, dt, dn or docs, args saved document with check_permission=True (read), or the docs dict read v2 /api/v2/method/run_doc_method, args method, document, kwargs the document dict, checked with check_if_latest() read for GET. write (create if not saved) for POST

In each case Frappe checks doc.is_whitelisted(method) (or frappe.is_whitelisted) and the HTTP method, then calls doc.run_method(method, ...). The document after the call is added to frappe.response.docs, with fields the user cannot read removed. v1 run_doc_method with as_csv=1 returns the result as a CSV file.

docs.title: Argument binding
docs.text:
init_request() builds frappe.form_dict once per request (make_form_dict() in frappe/app.py):

Request body frappe.form_dict Content-Type: application/json, a JSON object The object only. The query string is ignored. Content-Type: application/json, a JSON list {"data": [...]} Invalid JSON frappe.DataError "Invalid request body" (HTTP 417) Form or multipart body, or no body Query string values, then form values (form wins)

The key _ is removed. Files of a multipart body are in frappe.request.files, not in frappe.form_dict.

frappe.call(fn, **frappe.form_dict) then uses frappe.get_newargs():

  • Keys that are not parameters of fn are dropped, unless fn has **kwargs.
  • ignore_permissions and flags are always dropped.
  • In v1, cmd is in frappe.form_dict, so a function with **kwargs gets cmd too.
  • A missing required argument raises Python TypeError (HTTP 500).

The function that @frappe.whitelist() registers is a wrapper from validate_argument_types(). During a request, it converts and checks each annotated argument. A bad value raises frappe.FrappeTypeError (HTTP 417). See Whitelisted Methods.

Results of a test function def r2_args(a: int, b: str = "x"):

Request message GET ...?a=1&b=2&c=3 {"a": 1, "b": "2"} POST ...?b=fromquery with JSON {"a": 5} {"a": 5, "b": "x"} POST ...?b=fromquery with form a=5 {"a": 5, "b": "fromquery"} POST with JSON [1, 2] TypeError: r2_args() missing 1 required positional argument: 'a' (HTTP 500)

docs.title: frappe.response
docs.text:
frappe.response (frappe.local.response) is a dict that frappe.init() creates for each request as {"docs": []}. Code adds keys to it. as_json() serializes all keys of the dict, so a custom key appears in the JSON. Keys that control the response:

Key Set by Becomes message v1 method return value message in JSON data v1 resource and all v2 return values data in JSON docs document methods, v2 bulk update docs in JSON. Removed when empty. has_next_page v2 list has_next_page in JSON http_status_code your code, delete_doc (202), bulk routes (202) HTTP status. Removed from the JSON. type your code The response builder, see Response types filename, filecontent, content_type, display_content_as your code File for download, pdf, binary result, doctype build_csv_response() Body and file name for csv and txt location your code Target of redirect route, context frappe.respond_as_web_page() Page for page 
# test function in the console, then GET /api/method/<path>
@frappe.whitelist()
def r2_none():
    frappe.response["custom"] = 5

{"custom": 5}

docs.title: Messages and logs
docs.text:
make_logs() in frappe/utils/response.py adds messages to JSON responses. The shape depends on the API version (frappe.api.get_api_version(): v2 when the path starts with /api/v2, else v1).

Source v1 key v2 key frappe.msgprint(), frappe.throw() (frappe.local.message_log) _server_messages: a JSON string of a list of JSON strings messages: a list of objects. A throw message moves into its error in errors. frappe.log() (frappe.local.debug_log) _debug_messages: a JSON string. Only if tracebacks are allowed. debug: list of {"message": ...}. Only if tracebacks are allowed. frappe.errprint() and error tracebacks (frappe.local.error_log) exc: a JSON string of a list of tracebacks. _exc_source: the app that raised. Only if tracebacks are allowed. not sent. The traceback is in errors[].exception. frappe.flags.error_message (set by frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True)) _error_message not sent 
@frappe.whitelist()
def r2_msg():
    frappe.msgprint("Saved two rows")
    frappe.log("debug line")
    return {"ok": 1}

v1 (/api/method/...):

{"message": {"ok": 1},
 "_server_messages": "[\"{\\\"message\\\":\\\"Saved two rows\\\",\\\"as_table\\\":false,\\\"title\\\":\\\"Message\\\"}\"]",
 "_debug_messages": "[\"debug line\"]"}

v2 (/api/v2/method/...):

{"data": {"ok": 1},
 "messages": [{"message": "Saved two rows", "as_table": false, "title": "Message"}],
 "debug": [{"message": "debug line"}]}

frappe.msgprint(..., realtime=True) sends the message over the realtime connection instead of the response.

docs.title: Serialization
docs.text: as_json() uses orjson with json_handler(). Dates and times become strings, timedelta becomes H:MM:SS, Decimal becomes a float, a Document becomes its dict (__json__), and other iterables become lists. Another object raises TypeError (HTTP 500).

docs.title: Response types
docs.text:
Set frappe.response.type to use another builder (build_response() in frappe/utils/response.py). The return value of the function is ignored by these builders, so return None.

type Uses HTTP response json (default) all keys application/json download filename, filecontent, optional content_type, display_content_as (default attachment) MIME type from content_type or the file name pdf filename, filecontent application/pdf, inline binary filename, filecontent application/octet-stream, attachment csv result, doctype (file name without .csv) text/csv, attachment; filename=<doctype>.csv txt result, doctype text, attachment; filename=<doctype>.txt redirect location HTTP 302 to location page route, context, http_status_code HTML page. frappe.respond_as_web_page(title, html) sets it.

download, pdf, binary, csv and txt do not add messages, and they do not read http_status_code.

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from frappe.utils.csvutils import build_csv_response


@frappe.whitelist()
def export_notes():
    frappe.response.type = "download"
    frappe.response.filename = "sample.txt"
    frappe.response.filecontent = "hello"


@frappe.whitelist()
def export_items():
    build_csv_response([["name", "rate"], ["Laptop", 900]], "SampleItems")

GET /api/method/sample_app.api.export_notes -> 200
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=sample.txt

GET /api/method/sample_app.api.export_items -> 200
Content-Type: text/csv; charset=utf-8
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=SampleItems.csv

docs.title: Return a Response object
docs.text:
A function can return a werkzeug.wrappers.Response. Both v1 and v2 send it without changes. No messages are added. Frappe still adds Cache-Control, CORS and cookie headers in process_response().

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from werkzeug.wrappers import Response


@frappe.whitelist()
def plain():
    return Response("plain text", mimetype="text/plain", status=201)

GET /api/v2/method/sample_app.api.plain -> 201 text/plain; charset=utf-8
plain text

To change only the status of a JSON response, set frappe.response.http_status_code:

@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def create_sample():
    frappe.response.http_status_code = 201
    return "created"

{"message": "created"}

docs.title: v1 and v2 envelopes
Errors and HTTP status
docs.text:
An exception in the endpoint goes to handle_exception() in frappe/app.py:

  1. The status is http_status_code of the exception class, or 500.
  2. If the exception is frappe.DoesNotExistError and the user has no permission on its DocType, Frappe raises frappe.PermissionError instead. A user without access does not learn if a document exists.
  3. For /api/ paths (unless Accept starts with text), and for requests with Accept: application/json or X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest, the response is JSON from report_error(). Other requests get an HTML error page.
  4. frappe.AuthenticationError clears the login cookies.
  5. For status 500 and higher, or in developer mode, Frappe saves an Error Log (log_error_snapshot()).
  6. application() rolls back the transaction.

A werkzeug.exceptions.HTTPException (for example NotFound, Forbidden, MethodNotAllowed) skips handle_exception(). Werkzeug makes its own HTML response.

HTTP Exception classes (frappe/exceptions.py) 200 frappe.RequestToken 400 frappe.CSRFTokenError and its subclasses InvalidAuthorizationHeader, InvalidAuthorizationPrefix, InvalidAuthorizationToken 401 frappe.AuthenticationError, frappe.SessionExpired 403 frappe.PermissionError 404 frappe.DoesNotExistError, frappe.PageDoesNotExistError 409 frappe.NameError, frappe.DuplicateEntryError 410 frappe.LinkExpired 415 frappe.UnsupportedMediaType 417 frappe.ValidationError and subclasses without their own code (for example MandatoryError, LinkValidationError, DataError, AppNotInstalledError), frappe.FrappeTypeError 429 frappe.RateLimitExceededError, frappe.TooManyRequestsError 500 Other exceptions, frappe.SessionBootFailed 501 frappe.OutgoingEmailError 503 frappe.SessionStopped, frappe.ServiceUnavailableError, frappe.InReadOnlyMode, frappe.QueueOverloaded 508 frappe.QueryTimeoutError, frappe.QueryDeadlockError

frappe.Redirect(http_status_code=301) takes the status as an argument. For your own exception, subclass one of these classes or set http_status_code on the class.

# sample_app/exceptions.py
import frappe


class SampleQuotaExceeded(frappe.ValidationError):
    http_status_code = 402

docs.title: msgprint and throw in an API call
docs.text:
• frappe.msgprint(msg) adds a message and the call continues. The message is in _server_messages (v1) or messages (v2) of a successful response.
  • frappe.throw(msg, exc=frappe.ValidationError) adds a message with raise_exception and raises exc. The status comes from exc. In v2, the message moves from messages into the error object.
  • frappe.throw_permission_error() raises frappe.PermissionError with "Not permitted".
  • When frappe.flags.mute_messages is set, no message is added, but the exception is still raised.

docs.title: Login
docs.text:
LoginManager.__init__() in frappe/auth.py logs in only when frappe.request.path == "/api/method/login". It reads usr and pwd from frappe.form_dict. frappe.handler.handle() then skips the login command.

Warning

/api/v1/method/login and /api/v2/method/login do not log in. They return HTTP 200 with {}, also for a wrong password, and start a Guest session. Use POST /api/method/login.

docs.title: File uploads
docs.text:
upload_file (frappe.handler.upload_file, also POST /api/v2/method/upload_file) reads a multipart body:

Form field Default Description file none The file content. Without it, file_url or library_file_name gives the file. is_private 1 0 saves under /files/, 1 under /private/files/. doctype, docname, fieldname none Attach to this document. The user needs write on it. folder Home File folder. file_url none Make a File record for an existing URL. optimize, max_width, max_height none Shrink images and PDFs. chunk_index, total_chunk_count, chunk_byte_offset, total_file_size none Upload in parts. Only the last part creates the File. method none Dotted path of a whitelisted function to call instead of creating a File. It reads frappe.local.uploaded_file and frappe.local.uploaded_filename.

Rules:

  • A Guest can upload only when System Settings allow_guests_to_upload_files is on. Otherwise HTTP 403.
  • Guests and users without desk access can upload only the MIME types in ALLOWED_MIMETYPES (frappe/handler.py).
  • The after_file_upload hooks run with doc= before the File is saved.
  • The method is rate limited to 300 calls per 60 seconds per user.
curl -s -b cookies.txt -X POST "$S/api/v2/method/upload_file" -F "file=@sample-notes.txt" -F "is_private=0"

{"data": {"name": "5da45e78f1", "file_name": "sample-notes.txt", "is_private": 0, "file_size": 13,
  "file_url": "/files/sample-notes.txt", "folder": "Home", "doctype": "File"}}

frappe.handler.download_file?file_url=<url> returns a file with type = "download". It raises frappe.PermissionError when the user cannot read the File. See Files.

docs.title: Commit and after the response
docs.text:
frappe.api.handle() does not commit. application() does it after the endpoint returns (sync_database()):

  • POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH commit. GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and QUERY roll back, unless frappe.local.flags.commit is set.
  • Any exception rolls back.
  • after_request hooks run after the commit or rollback, also for errors.

See Database.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A JSON body hides the query string. Send all arguments in the body, or use a form body.
  • A wrong HTTP method on a route returns a Werkzeug HTML page with HTTP 405, not JSON. Check the status before you parse the body.
  • GET /api/v2/method/logout returns HTTP 417, because only POST matches the logout rule.
  • Do not return a value and also set frappe.response.type = "download". The return value is not sent.
  • Messages from frappe.msgprint are not in responses that you build as a Response object or a file.
  • A Server Script of type API with the same method name replaces your function on both v1 and v2.

docs.title: Customizing APIs
docs.text:
An app can add API endpoints and change how existing ones behave, without changes to Frappe or to other apps. This page lists each way, what it changes, and when it runs. For how a request is routed and answered, see API Internals. For the hook list, see Hooks reference.

The hook examples on this page were checked on the develop site with the hooks added at runtime and a Werkzeug test client. The function names are examples.

docs.title: Choose a mechanism
docs.text:
You want to Use Add an endpoint @frappe.whitelist() function Replace an endpoint of another app override_whitelisted_methods Change what REST create, read, update and delete do Controller methods, doc_events, extend_doctype_class, override_doctype_class Hide documents or deny access has_permission, permission_query_conditions Change the v2 list query of your DocType Static get_list(query) on the controller Run code on every request before_request, after_request Authenticate with your own header or token auth_hooks Limit calls @rate_limit, site config rate_limit Serve a route outside /api website_route_rules, page_renderer, www/ pages Return a file, CSV or redirect frappe.response.type, or return a Response Allow browser calls from another origin Site config allow_cors

An app cannot add rules to the /api URL map (API_URL_MAP in frappe/api/__init__.py). New endpoints under /api are whitelisted methods.

docs.title: Add a whitelisted method
docs.text:
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order(name: str) -> str:
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.check_permission("write")
    doc.status = "Completed"
    doc.save()
    return doc.status

The method is at /api/method/sample_app.api.close_order and /api/v2/method/sample_app.api.close_order. See Whitelisted Methods for decorator options, type validation and permission checks.

docs.title: Override a method of another app
docs.text:
override_whitelisted_methods maps the dotted path that clients call to your function. Frappe applies it in frappe.override_whitelisted_method() before it imports the function, for v1 and v2.

# sample_app/hooks.py
override_whitelisted_methods = {
    "frappe.auth.get_logged_user": "sample_app.api.get_logged_user",
}

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_logged_user() -> str:
    return "override:" + frappe.session.user

{"message": "override:user1@example.com"}
  • Your function must also be whitelisted. The whitelist and HTTP method checks run on your function, not on the original.
  • If several apps override the same path, the last value in the hook list wins.
  • Frappe looks for a Server Script of type API after it applies the override. A script with the original path does not run when the path is overridden. A script with the new path does.
  • Python code that imports the original function still calls the original.
  • Document routes (/api/resource/..., /api/v2/document/...) and fixed v2 routes such as /api/v2/method/upload_file do not use this hook.

docs.title: Change document behavior
docs.text:
REST create, update and delete call doc.insert(), doc.save() and frappe.delete_doc(). So every controller method and doc_events handler runs, the same as in the desk. Use these hooks to change what the REST routes do for a DocType of another app:

Hook Effect See doc_events Run functions on document events (validate, on_update, on_trash, ...). An exception stops the request. Extending Other Apps extend_doctype_class Add a mixin class to the controller. Several apps can extend one DocType. Extending Other Apps override_doctype_class Replace the controller class. Last app wins. Extending Other Apps 
# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "ToDo": {"validate": "sample_app.events.todo_validate"},
}

# sample_app/events.py
import frappe


def todo_validate(doc, method):
    if doc.description == "forbidden":
        frappe.throw("Sample rule: forbidden description")

curl -s -X POST "$S/api/v2/document/ToDo" -H "$AUTH" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"description": "forbidden"}' -w ' %{http_code}\n'

{"errors": [{"type": "ValidationError", "message": "Sample rule: forbidden description", "title": "Message", "indicator": "red"}]} 417

A whitelisted method on the controller (or on an extend_doctype_class mixin) is callable with the document method routes. See API Internals.

Do not call frappe.db.commit() in these handlers. The request commits when it succeeds.

docs.title: Change who can see and change documents
Run code on every request
docs.text:
Hook When Called with before_request In init_request(), after frappe.form_dict and the cookie session are loaded, before validate_auth() no arguments after_request In application(), after the commit or rollback, also for errors response=, request= 
# sample_app/hooks.py
before_request = ["sample_app.request.before_request"]
after_request = ["sample_app.request.after_request"]

# sample_app/request.py
import frappe


def before_request():
    frappe.local.sample_started = frappe.utils.now()


def after_request(response, request):
    response.headers["X-Sample-App"] = "1"

The X-Sample-App header was on every response, also on HTTP 403, 404 and 417 errors.

  • In before_request, frappe.session.user is the cookie user, or Guest. A user from an Authorization header or auth_hooks is not set yet.
  • An exception in before_request stops the request and returns an error response.
  • An exception in after_request is logged and ignored. Writes in after_request are not committed by the request.
  • These hooks run on every request that reaches application(), also for desk and website pages. Keep them fast.

docs.title: Authenticate with auth_hooks
docs.text:
validate_auth() in frappe/auth.py reads the Authorization header (token, Basic, Bearer), then calls each auth_hooks function with no arguments. A hook sets the user with frappe.set_user().

# sample_app/hooks.py
auth_hooks = ["sample_app.auth.validate_sample_key"]

# sample_app/auth.py
import frappe


def validate_sample_key():
    if frappe.get_request_header("X-Sample-Key") != "let-me-in":
        return
    form_dict = frappe.local.form_dict
    frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
    frappe.local.form_dict = form_dict

Warning

frappe.set_user() resets frappe.local.form_dict to an empty dict. Save it before the call and put it back after, as the built-in token check does. Without this, the request loses all its arguments. In the test, POST /api/v2/document/ToDo then failed with MandatoryError.

  • If the Authorization header has two parts and no check sets a user, Frappe raises frappe.AuthenticationError (HTTP 401) after the hooks.
  • A header with one part (for example Authorization: foo) is ignored. The request runs as Guest.
  • When a hook changes the user, Frappe checks the restrict_ip of that user.
  • A real hook must compare a secret, for example a hash stored in a DocType. The fixed value above is only for the example.

See Authentication.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
• @rate_limit(...) from frappe.rate_limiter limits calls of one method per IP or per user. Put it below @frappe.whitelist(). Over the limit: frappe.RateLimitExceededError (HTTP 429).
  • Site config rate_limit ({"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}) limits total request time for the site. Responses get X-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Limit and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers.

See Whitelisted Methods.

docs.title: Custom routes outside /api
docs.text:
application() sends every path that starts with /api/ to the API URL map. Other GET, HEAD and POST paths, except /backups, /files, /private/files and /.well-known, go to the website router (frappe.website.serve.get_response()). So a custom route must be outside /api.

Hook or folder Use website_route_rules Map a URL pattern to a page. Path parts go into frappe.form_dict. page_renderer A class with can_render() and render(). It runs before the built-in renderers and can return JSON or any Response. www/ pages HTML pages with get_context.

These routes use the same session, commit rules and before_request/after_request hooks as /api. They do not use @frappe.whitelist. Check permissions in your code. Errors give an HTML page, unless the request has Accept: application/json or X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. See Website.

docs.title: Custom response formats
docs.text:
A whitelisted method can return a file, a CSV, a redirect or a web page. Set frappe.response.type, or return a werkzeug Response:

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from werkzeug.wrappers import Response


@frappe.whitelist()
def order_label(name: str):
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.check_permission("read")
    frappe.response.type = "download"
    frappe.response.filename = f"{doc.name}.txt"
    frappe.response.filecontent = f"Order {doc.name} for {doc.customer_name}"


@frappe.whitelist()
def ping_text():
    return Response("pong", mimetype="text/plain")

See API Internals for all types and the keys they read.

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
Site config allow_cors sets the origins that may call the site from a browser. The value is "*", one origin, or a list. process_response() adds the headers only when the request has an Origin header that matches.

bench --site frappe.localhost set-config allow_cors '["https://app.example.com"]' --parse

A preflight OPTIONS request gets HTTP 200 and no body. Frappe does not run the endpoint. Response headers for a matching origin:

Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Vary: Origin
Access-Control-Allow-Methods: POST
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type
Access-Control-Max-Age: 86400

Access-Control-Allow-Methods and Access-Control-Allow-Headers repeat the values that the browser asked for. Access-Control-Max-Age is not sent in developer mode. An origin that does not match gets no CORS headers.

An app can set frappe.local.allow_cors in a before_request hook. It replaces the site config value for that request.

# sample_app/request.py
import frappe


def before_request():
    frappe.local.allow_cors = ["https://app.example.com"]

docs.title: Version your API
docs.text:
Frappe has no version setting for app methods. The dotted path is the contract.

  • Do not rename or move a whitelisted function. Clients call it by module path.
  • Add new parameters with a default. Do not change the type or meaning of an existing parameter.
  • For a breaking change, add a new function, for example sample_app.api.v2.close_order, and keep the old one.
  • Use /api/v2/method/... in new clients. The v1 and v2 envelopes differ (message against data).

docs.title: Deprecate a method
docs.text:
1. Add the new function.
  2. Keep the old function as a whitelisted wrapper that calls the new one.
  3. Log each call, so that you know who still uses it.
  4. Remove the old function in a later major version of your app.
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order_v2(name: str, reason: str | None = None) -> str:
    ...


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order(name: str) -> str:
    frappe.logger("sample_app").warning(f"deprecated sample_app.api.close_order called by {frappe.session.user}")
    return close_order_v2(name)

You can also point the old path at the new function with override_whitelisted_methods in your own hooks.py. frappe/utils/deprecations.py is internal to Frappe. Do not import it in your app.

docs.title: Test an API
docs.text:
Call the function directly in an IntegrationTestCase to test its logic. Test the HTTP layer with a request, so that whitelist, HTTP method, type and permission checks run.

frappe.tests.test_api.FrappeAPITestCase is the base class that Frappe uses for its own API tests. It is in a test module, not a public API, so it can change. It sends requests to the site with the Werkzeug test client (frappe.utils.get_test_client()):

Member Does version "" (v1, default) or "v2" method(path), resource(doctype, name), doctype_path(...) Build the URL sid Session id of Administrator get, post, put, patch, delete, query Send a request. The data is sent as JSON. 
# sample_app/tests/test_api.py
from frappe.tests.test_api import FrappeAPITestCase


class TestSampleAPI(FrappeAPITestCase):
    version = "v2"

    def test_logged_user(self):
        response = self.get(self.method("frappe.auth.get_logged_user"), {"sid": self.sid})
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
        self.assertEqual(response.json["data"], "Administrator")

TEST_CLIENT is a class attribute, so all subclasses share one client and its cookies. After a request with sid, later requests without sid also run as Administrator. Also test as a normal user (for example with API keys of user1@example.com), not only as Administrator. See Testing.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An auth_hooks function that calls frappe.set_user() without saving frappe.local.form_dict drops all request arguments.
  • before_request runs before token authentication. Do not check the user there for token requests.
  • override_whitelisted_methods does not change document routes. Use doc_events or a controller hook.
  • has_permission does not filter lists. Pair it with permission_query_conditions.
  • doc_events and controller methods run for desk, REST and Python calls alike. Check frappe.request only if you must know the source.
  • A route outside /api is not protected by @frappe.whitelist. Check permissions in the renderer or page.

docs.title: MCP and API Discovery
docs.text: Each site has a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at /api/v2/mcp. An AI agent (an MCP client) connects as a desk user and gets tools to search DocTypes, read and write documents, and call whitelisted methods. Every tool goes through the same permission checks as the REST API. The API discovery endpoints at /api/v2/discovery describe the whitelisted methods of the site, with their arguments and docstrings. MCP uses them, and you can call them from any API client.

docs.title: Enable MCP
docs.text:
MCP is on by default. The settings are in System Settings > AI Agents > MCP Settings:

Field Default Description enable_mcp 1 Off: /api/v2/mcp returns HTTP 404. server_name host name Name sent to clients in serverInfo. The default is the host name with other characters changed to _, such as frappe_localhost_8000. agent_instructions empty Text added to the server instructions that agents get when they connect. Tell agents what the site is for.

docs.title: Connect a client
docs.text:
The endpoint uses the Streamable HTTP transport with plain JSON responses. It keeps no protocol session.

  • URL: https://<site>/api/v2/mcp
  • Method: POST only. Other methods get HTTP 405.
  • Headers: Content-Type: application/json, and an Accept that allows application/json.
  • Authentication: any method the REST API accepts: OAuth 2 bearer token, API key and secret (Authorization: token <key>:<secret>), or a session cookie. See Authentication.
  • The user must have the Desk User role. Guests get HTTP 401. Users without the role get HTTP 403.
  • A request with an Origin header from another host must match allow_cors in site config.

Without credentials, the response is HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<site>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". MCP clients use it to start an OAuth flow. The metadata endpoint is served when OAuth Settings > Show Protected Resource Metadata is on. See Integrations.

Protocol versions: 2025-11-25 (with initialize) and 2026-07-28 (with server/discover and the MCP-Protocol-Version, Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers). A request without MCP-Protocol-Version uses 2025-11-25.

docs.title: Example with curl
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "initialize",
       "params": {"protocolVersion": "2025-11-25", "capabilities": {},
                  "clientInfo": {"name": "sample-client", "version": "1.0"}}}'

{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": {
  "protocolVersion": "2025-11-25",
  "capabilities": {"tools": {"listChanged": false}},
  "serverInfo": {"name": "frappe_localhost_8000", "version": "17.0.0-dev"},
  "instructions": "This is a Frappe Framework site at frappe.localhost:8000.\nYou are connected as Administrator (Administrator).\n..."}}

Call a tool:

curl -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/mcp" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/call",
       "params": {"name": "list_documents",
                  "arguments": {"doctype": "Sample Item", "fields": ["name", "rate"],
                                "filters": {"category": "Hardware"}, "limit": 2}}}'

The result has content (JSON as text), structuredContent and isError. A tool that fails returns isError: true with the error text, for example "Sample Item nope not found". Protocol errors (bad JSON, unknown method) return a JSON-RPC error.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool Arguments Annotation Description search_doctypes query, limit read-only Find DocType names that contain the query. get_doctype_schema doctype read-only Fields and permissions of a DocType. search_methods query read-only Search whitelisted methods and document methods. get_method_schema method, doctype read-only Arguments and docstring of a method. list_document_methods doctype read-only Whitelisted document methods of a DocType. list_documents doctype, filters, fields, order_by, start, limit read-only Like frappe.get_list. get_document doctype, name, fields read-only One document with child tables. count_documents doctype, filters read-only Count matching documents. create_document doctype, data, fields not destructive Insert a document. update_document doctype, name, data, fields destructive Change fields of a document. delete_document doctype, name destructive Delete a document. call_method method, args destructive Call a whitelisted method or an API Server Script. call_document_method doctype, name, method, args destructive Call a whitelisted controller method, such as submit.

Tool arguments take the same values as the matching REST API v2 endpoints. Arguments are validated strictly: unknown arguments and wrong types fail. If a method returns a file, the tool describes it. Images up to 5 MB are sent to the model as image content.

Changes made through MCP with a token or OAuth are recorded in Version with the agent name. The agent name is the OAuth client name, else the clientInfo.name that the client sent, else MCP.

docs.title: API discovery endpoints
docs.text:
All endpoints use GET and need the Desk User role.

Route Returns /api/v2/discovery Counts of methods and document methods, and the links below. /api/v2/discovery/search?q=<words> Up to 50 methods whose path or docstring has all the words. /api/v2/discovery/method Index of all whitelisted methods. /api/v2/discovery/method/<dotted.path> One method: HTTP methods, allow_guest, parameters with types and defaults, endpoint, docstring and source. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype> Whitelisted controller methods of a DocType. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype>/method/<method> One controller method: endpoint, HTTP methods, required permission per HTTP method, parameters, docstring. 
curl "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/discovery/method/frappe.client.get_value" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>"

{"data": {"type": "method", "kind": "rpc", "path": "frappe.client.get_value", "name": "get_value",
  "http_methods": ["GET", "POST", "PUT", "DELETE", "QUERY"], "allow_guest": false,
  "params": [{"name": "doctype", "required": true, "type": "str"},
             {"name": "fieldname", "required": true, "type": "str | list[str] | dict[str, Any]"}, "..."],
  "endpoint": "/api/v2/method/frappe.client.get_value",
  "docstring": "Return a value from a document. ...",
  "source": "@frappe.whitelist()\ndef get_value(..."}}

docs.title: The discovery cache
docs.text:
Frappe builds the method index in the background and keeps it in Redis for 24 hours (1 hour in developer mode). The job runs after each bench migrate (after_migrate hook) with the job ID api-v2-discovery-build. If the cache is empty, the endpoints start the job and return HTTP 503 with "API discovery cache is being generated. Please try again in 10 seconds."

The index is built by reading the Python files of each app for functions with @frappe.whitelist. API Server Scripts are listed for users who can read them.

docs.title: Make your methods discoverable
docs.text:
• Add type hints to every argument. Discovery shows them as type.
  • Write a docstring. The first line is the description in search results. The search also reads the docstring.
  • Source code is returned only when the app sets expose_discovery_source = True in hooks.py. Frappe sets it. Leave it out of a closed-source app.
# sample_app/hooks.py
expose_discovery_source = True

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_open_orders(customer: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[dict]:
    """Return open Sample Orders of a customer, newest first."""
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters={"customer_name": customer, "status": "Open"},
        fields=["name", "order_date", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
        limit=limit,
    )

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An agent can do everything its user can do. Give agents their own user with only the roles they need.
  • call_method reaches every whitelisted method the user may call. Check permissions in your methods. See Whitelisted Methods.
  • A new method does not show in discovery until the cache is rebuilt. Run bench migrate, or wait for the cache to expire.

  • REST endpoints reference

docs.title: Request Lifecycle
docs.text: This page follows one HTTP request through the code of frappe/app.py, step by step. Use it to debug a request, or to find the right place to change how your app handles requests. For how to call the API, see REST API and Whitelisted methods. For the short overview, see Architecture.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• WSGI entry point: frappe.app.application. Gunicorn calls it in production. bench serve calls it through the Werkzeug development server.
  • frappe.local: state for one request, local to the thread. frappe.init() resets it at the start of each request. frappe.destroy() releases it at the end.
  • Transaction: one database transaction for each request. sync_database() commits it or rolls it back after the handler returns.
  • Hooks: before_request, auth_hooks and after_request let an app run code at fixed points. See Hooks.

docs.title: 1. WSGI wrappers
docs.text:
application is wrapped twice in frappe/app.py:

  1. @Request.application turns the WSGI call into a werkzeug.Request object.
  2. @after_response_wrapper returns a ClosingIterator. It runs run_after_response_callbacks() and then frappe.destroy() after the server has sent the response body.

bench serve adds more middleware in frappe.app.serve():

Middleware Condition What it does SharedDataMiddleware Unless NO_STATICS is set Serves /assets/* from sites/assets. StaticDataMiddleware (frappe/middlewares.py) Unless NO_STATICS is set Serves /files/* from sites/<site>/public/files. Files that are not on disk go on to Frappe. ProxyFix --proxy or USE_PROXY Reads X-Forwarded-* headers. ProfilerMiddleware --profile or USE_PROFILER Prints a profile for each request.

In production, nginx serves /assets and the files that exist in /files. When FRAPPE_SENTRY_DSN and SENTRY_TRACING_SAMPLE_RATE are set, SentryWsgiMiddleware also wraps the application.

docs.title: 2. Site resolution
docs.text:
init_request() picks the site name in this order:

  1. The site given to bench serve. bench serve uses --site, then FRAPPE_SITE, then default_site from common_site_config.json (get_sites() in frappe/utils/bench_helper.py).
  2. The X-Frappe-Site-Name request header.
  3. The Host header without the port (get_site_name(get_request_host(request))).

currentsite.txt is not used. The CLI only prints a warning about it.

curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/method/ping -H 'X-Frappe-Site-Name: frappe.localhost'
# {"message":"pong"}

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/method/ping
# 404   (body: "127.0.0.1 does not exist.")

If the site folder has no site_config.json, get_site_config() in frappe/config.py raises IncorrectSitePath and the response is HTTP 404. When developer_mode is set in common_site_config.json, that 404 page also lists all sites on the bench.

docs.title: 3. frappe.init and frappe.connect
docs.text:
1. frappe.init(site, force=True, is_request=True) releases the old frappe.local and fills it again. It loads the merged site config (cached for requests) into frappe.local.conf.
  2. init_request() sets frappe.local.request and adds request.after_response, a CallbackManager.
  3. frappe.local.is_ajax is True when X-Requested-With is XMLHttpRequest.
  4. frappe.connect(set_admin_as_user=False) opens frappe.local.db. The user is not set yet.
  5. If maintenance_mode is set in the site config, and allow_reads_during_maintenance is not false, setup_read_only_mode() sets frappe.flags.read_only. It connects to the read replica (read_from_replica) or starts a read-only transaction. If allow_reads_during_maintenance is false, the request fails with frappe.SessionStopped (HTTP 503).

These keys of frappe.local are set for each request:

Key Set by Value site, site_path, conf frappe.init Site name, site folder and merged config flags frappe.init _dict with defaults such as read_only, mute_messages, in_import, ignore_links response frappe.init _dict({"docs": []}). Becomes the JSON body for API calls. response_headers frappe.init Headers(). Added to the response in process_response(). message_log, error_log, debug_log frappe.init Messages from frappe.msgprint, frappe.errprint and debug output lang frappe.init, then HTTPRequest.set_lang conf.lang or en, then the request language session frappe.init, then Session _dict(user="Guest", data=_dict()), then the loaded session db frappe.connect Database connection request init_request The werkzeug.Request (also frappe.request) is_ajax init_request True for X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest form_dict make_form_dict Request parameters (frappe.form_dict) http_request init_request frappe.auth.HTTPRequest instance (not for OPTIONS) request_ip HTTPRequest.set_request_ip Client IP address cookie_manager HTTPRequest.set_cookies CookieManager for cookies to set or delete login_manager HTTPRequest.set_session LoginManager session_obj LoginManager.make_session frappe.sessions.Session rate_limiter, monitor, _recorder before_request hooks Only when the feature is on

docs.title: 4. Body size and frappe.form_dict
docs.text:
init_request() sets request.max_content_length first:

  • Upload paths (/api/method/upload_file, /api/v1/method/upload_file, /api/v2/method/upload_file): get_max_file_size().
  • A PUT to a path in the streaming_request_paths hook: no limit. The body is not read. form_dict gets only the query string.
  • All other requests: max_file_size from the site config, or 25 MB.

Then make_form_dict() builds frappe.form_dict:

Body frappe.form_dict JSON object (Content-Type: application/json) The object. The query string is ignored. JSON array {"data": [...]} Invalid JSON frappe.DataError "Invalid request body" (HTTP 417) Form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded) or multipart Query string values, then form values on top. Files stay in frappe.request.files. No body The query string

The key _ (a jQuery cache buster) is always removed.

# The JSON body replaces the query string, so doctype is lost
curl -s -b cookies.txt -X GET "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.client.get_count?doctype=ToDo" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"filters":{}}'
# HTTP 500: {"exception": "TypeError: get_count() missing 1 required positional argument: 'doctype'", ...}

# A form body is merged with the query string
curl -s -b cookies.txt -X GET "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.client.get_count?doctype=ToDo" \
  -d 'filters={}'
# {"message":5}

docs.title: 5. Session and user: frappe.auth.HTTPRequest
docs.text:
For every method except OPTIONS, init_request() creates HTTPRequest(). It runs these steps in order:

  1. set_request_ip(): the remote address under bench serve. Otherwise the first X-Forwarded-For value, then REMOTE_ADDR, then 127.0.0.1.
  2. set_cookies(): creates frappe.local.cookie_manager.
  3. set_session(): creates LoginManager().
    • For /api/method/login, it runs the login. See Authentication.
    • For other paths, Session(resume=True) reads the sid from form_dict or the sid cookie. It loads the session from the Redis cache, then from the Sessions table.
    • If the session is missing or expired, the user is Guest. The response gets session_expired: 1 and the login cookies are deleted.
  4. set_lang(): get_language() in frappe/translate.py. The order is _lang in the form, the user language (logged-in users), the preferred_language cookie, Accept-Language, then System Settings.
  5. validate_csrf_token(). See CSRF.
  6. cookie_manager.init_cookies(): queues the sid cookie.

A Guest request still gets sid=Guest and the cookies system_user, full_name, user_id and user_lang.

docs.title: 6. CSRF check
docs.text:
HTTPRequest.validate_csrf_token() raises frappe.CSRFTokenError (HTTP 400) only when all of these are true:

  • The method is POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH.
  • ignore_csrf is not set in the site config.
  • The session has a saved csrf_token. A session gets one when the desk or a website page calls frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token().
  • The X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header (or the csrf_token form value) does not match.
  • Referer or Origin is not in allowed_referrers of the site config.

The check runs before validate_auth(), so it uses the cookie session. A token request has a Guest session with no saved token, so it is not checked.

# Cookie session after /desk was loaded once
curl -s -b cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user
# HTTP 400: {"exception": "frappe.exceptions.CSRFTokenError: Invalid Request", "exc_type": "CSRFTokenError", ...}

curl -s -b cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user \
  -H "X-Frappe-CSRF-Token: <csrf_token>"
# {"message":"Administrator"}

docs.title: 7. before_request hooks
docs.text:
init_request() then calls each function in the before_request hook with frappe.call(). Frappe registers these in frappe/hooks.py:

Function What it does frappe.recorder.record Starts the Recorder if it is on (Recorder in the desk, frappe.recorder.start). frappe.monitor.start Creates frappe.local.monitor if monitor is set in the site config. frappe.rate_limiter.apply Applies the site rate limit (rate_limit in the site config). frappe.integrations.oauth2.set_cors_for_privileged_requests Sets CORS for some OAuth and /.well-known/ requests.

App hooks run after these, in the order of installed apps. The user is the cookie session user here. Token and bearer authentication has not run yet. An exception in a before_request hook stops the request and goes to error handling.

docs.title: 8. Rate limiting
docs.text:
frappe.rate_limiter.apply() reads rate_limit = {"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>} from the site config. It counts the total request time of the site in microseconds, in a Redis key for each window. The counter is for the whole site, not for each user or IP. If the counter is above the limit, the request fails with frappe.TooManyRequestsError (HTTP 429).

  • process_response() adds X-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and Retry-After for rejected requests.
  • frappe.rate_limiter.update runs after the response and adds the time of this request to the counter.

The @rate_limit decorator and the rate_limit option of @frappe.whitelist are separate. They limit one method. See Whitelisted methods.

docs.title: 9. Token, bearer and auth hooks: validate_auth()
docs.text:
application() calls validate_auth() in frappe/auth.py after init_request():

  1. It splits the Authorization header on spaces.
  2. With exactly two parts, validate_oauth() handles Bearer <token>.
  3. With exactly two parts, validate_auth_via_api_keys() handles token <key>:<secret> and Basic <base64>. OAuth client credentials on the token, revoke and introspect endpoints are skipped here.
  4. validate_auth_via_hooks() calls each function in auth_hooks.
  5. With a two-part header, if the user is still Guest, Frappe raises frappe.AuthenticationError (HTTP 401).
  6. If the user changed, Frappe checks the restrict_ip of the user and reads X-Frappe-Agent.

A token or bearer user is set with frappe.set_user(). No session row is made and no sid cookie is set for that user.

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user \
  -H 'Authorization: token 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2'
# 401   (unknown key)

curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user \
  -H 'Authorization: token a b'
# 403   (three parts: the header is ignored and the request runs as Guest)

docs.title: 10. Dispatch by path
docs.text:
application() picks the handler in this order:

Condition Handler OPTIONS Empty Response() (CORS preflight). No session and no cookies. frappe.form_dict.cmd is set frappe.handler.handle(), then build_response("json"). Deprecated. Path starts with /api/ frappe.api.handle(request). See API internals. Path starts with /backups frappe.utils.response.download_backup(). Needs System Manager. Path starts with /private/files/ frappe.storage.serve.serve_private_file(). Checks file permission. Path starts with /files/ frappe.storage.serve.serve_public_file(). Only for files that nginx or StaticDataMiddleware did not find on disk. GET /.well-known/security.txt Text from Security Settings. HTTP 404 if the scheme is not https. GET /.well-known/* handle_wellknown() (OAuth metadata) Other GET, HEAD or POST frappe.website.serve.get_response(). Desk (/desk), /app redirects, www/ pages, web forms and other website routes. Anything else NotFound (HTTP 404)

/assets/* never reaches application(). nginx or SharedDataMiddleware serves it. For the website route order, see Website.

If the System Settings field log_api_requests is set, frappe.api.handle() also queues an API Request Log with deferred_insert().

docs.title: 11. Commit or rollback
docs.text:
If the handler returns without an exception, sync_database() runs:

  • For POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH (UNSAFE_HTTP_METHODS), it commits.
  • For other methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, QUERY), it rolls back. If code set frappe.local.flags.commit = True, it commits. For example, frappe/boot.py sets it when the desk creates missing Notification Settings.
  • It queues session.update() on frappe.request.after_response.

If the handler raises, application() calls frappe.db.rollback(chain=True) after it builds the error response.

Other rules:

  • frappe.db.commit() in your code commits at once, for any HTTP method.
  • frappe.db.after_commit.add(fn) runs fn after the next commit. A rollback drops it. frappe.db.after_rollback.add(fn) works the other way. A failing callback is written to the Error Log and does not change the response.
  • frappe.publish_realtime(..., after_commit=True) queues the event on after_commit. A rollback drops the event.
  • frappe.enqueue(..., enqueue_after_commit=True) enqueues the job only after the commit.
  • In read-only mode (maintenance, or frappe.db.read_only()), a commit is a rollback.

See Database API for transaction details.

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_item(name: str):
    frappe.db.set_value("Sample Item", name, "disabled", 1)
    # runs only if the request commits
    frappe.db.after_commit.add(lambda: frappe.publish_realtime("sample_item_closed", {"name": name}))

docs.title: 12. after_request hooks and the response
docs.text:
1. run_after_request_hooks() runs in a finally block, for success and error. It calls each after_request function with frappe.call(fn, response=response, request=request). A function gets only the arguments it declares. An exception is logged and ignored. Frappe registers frappe.monitor.stop and frappe.flow.launcher.add_to_page.
  2. log_request() writes one line to the frappe.web logger if enable_frappe_logger is set in the site config.
  3. process_response() changes the response:
    • Sets Cache-Control: no-store,no-cache,must-revalidate,max-age=0, unless the handler set Cache-Control.
    • Adds the rate limit headers.
    • Adds X-Frappe-Request-Id when the monitor is on.
    • Adds CORS headers from allow_cors in the site config, or from frappe.local.allow_cors, if the Origin matches.
    • Adds WWW-Authenticate to 401 and 403 responses when OAuth resource metadata is on.
    • Adds the headers in frappe.local.response_headers.
    • Sets the queued cookies, unless Cache-Control contains public.

The after_request hook gets the final werkzeug Response. It can change headers or the body.

docs.title: 13. Errors
docs.text:
When an exception escapes the handler, application() makes the response:

  • A werkzeug.exceptions.HTTPException (for example NotFound, Forbidden) uses its own response.
  • Other exceptions go to handle_exception() in frappe/app.py.

handle_exception() works like this:

  1. The status is http_status_code of the exception class, or 500. See frappe/exceptions.py and REST API errors.
  2. A frappe.DoesNotExistError for a DocType that the user cannot access becomes a frappe.PermissionError (HTTP 403). This hides which documents exist (handle_does_not_exist_error in frappe/permissions.py).
  3. The response is JSON when the request has an Accept header and is AJAX or accepts application/json. It is also JSON for /api/ paths, unless Accept starts with text. Then report_error() builds the body. See API internals.
  4. Other requests get an HTML error page (ErrorPage) for 401, 403, 404 and 500. frappe.SessionStopped gets the maintenance page. 429 gets "Too Many Requests".
  5. frappe.AuthenticationError also deletes the login cookies.
  6. If the status is 500 or more, or developer_mode is on, log_error_snapshot() writes an Error Log (with defer_insert). Exceptions with skip_error_log = True (AuthenticationError, CSRFTokenError) are not logged.
  7. In developer_mode, a non-JSON error prints the traceback to the console.
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{content_type}\n" -H 'Accept: text/html' \
  http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user
# 403 text/html; charset=utf-8

curl -s http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/nothing
# HTTP 404: {"errors":[{"type":"DoesNotExistError"}]}

The traceback goes into the JSON body (exc in v1, exception in v2) only if is_traceback_allowed() in frappe/utils/response.py is true:

  • The site runs under bench serve (frappe._dev_server), for any user, Guest too.
  • Or System Settings allow_error_traceback is on, the user is a System User, and frappe.flags.disable_traceback is not set.

developer_mode alone does not show tracebacks to clients. For 404 errors, the traceback is sent only when logging is set in the site config.

docs.title: 14. After the response and cleanup
docs.text:
After the server sends the body, ClosingIterator runs these in order:

  1. frappe.rate_limiter.update: adds the request time to the rate limit counter.
  2. frappe.recorder.dump: saves the recorded request if the Recorder is on.
  3. Each function in frappe.request.after_response, in the order it was added. This includes session.update() from sync_database() and the queue of frappe.db.commit_after_response.
  4. frappe.destroy(): closes frappe.local.db and releases frappe.local.

A failing callback is logged to the after_response logger. It cannot change the response, which is already sent.

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_report():
    # do slow work after the client has the response
    frappe.request.after_response.add(lambda: frappe.logger("sample_app").info("report sent"))
    return {"ok": True}

commit_after_response(fn) in frappe/database/utils.py runs fn after the response in a savepoint and then commits. Outside a request, or in tests, it runs fn at once.

docs.title: Request logging, Recorder and Monitor
docs.text:
Tool Turn on Output Request log enable_frappe_logger: 1 in the site config One line for each request in the frappe.web logger: site, IP, user, path, method, status API Request Log System Settings log_api_requests One API Request Log document for each /api/ request Recorder Recorder in the desk (frappe.recorder.start). It turns off after 10 minutes. SQL queries and timing of each request, in the desk Monitor monitor: 1 in the site config JSON for each request in Redis, written to logs/monitor.json.log by the scheduled job frappe.monitor.flush

Send X-Frappe-Request-Id with a request to use your own trace ID in the monitor. It must match TRACE_ID_PATTERN in frappe/monitor.py.

docs.title: Other execution contexts
docs.text:
Code also runs outside frappe.app.application. These contexts have no frappe.request:

Context Start User Commit Hooks Background job frappe.utils.background_jobs.execute_job The user who called frappe.enqueue Commits on success. On error, rolls back, writes the Error Log and commits it. Retries deadlocks and timeouts up to 5 times. before_job, after_job Scheduled job The scheduler enqueues Scheduled Job Type jobs. Workers run them as background jobs. Administrator As background job before_job, after_job bench execute frappe/commands/execute.py Administrator Commits after the call None bench console frappe/commands/utils.py Administrator No auto commit. Rolls back on exit. Call frappe.db.commit(). None Socket.IO server bench socketio The user of the sid cookie or Authorization header None None

Other differences:

  • is_valid_http_method() in frappe/handler.py skips the HTTP method check in a background job.
  • frappe.form_dict is empty unless the code fills it.
  • The Socket.IO server does not run Frappe code for the socket. It calls frappe.realtime.get_user_info and frappe.realtime.has_permission over HTTP on the web server, with X-Frappe-Site-Name. These are normal requests.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A JSON body replaces the query string. Send all parameters in the body, or none.
  • A missing required argument raises TypeError, which is HTTP 500, not 417.
  • A GET handler that writes data loses the writes, unless it calls frappe.db.commit() or sets frappe.local.flags.commit.
  • An Authorization header that does not split into exactly two parts is ignored. The request runs as Guest.
  • before_request hooks run before token authentication. Do not read frappe.session.user there for token requests.
  • Under bench serve, Guests also get tracebacks. Do not judge production error output from a development server.
  • The site rate limit is shared by all clients of the site.
