docs.title: Data Model
docs.text:
Define DocTypes, naming rules, controllers and the document lifecycle, and handle files.

Page What it covers DocTypes The DocType JSON, standard and custom DocTypes, the main DocType properties, child tables, singles, trees and virtual DocTypes. Naming How Frappe sets the name of a document, with autoname options, naming series, the autoname controller method and rename. Controllers The Document class, controller lifecycle methods and their exact run order, doc_events, flags, db_set, change detection and whitelisted controller methods. Files Store and attach files with the File DocType, upload them over HTTP, choose public or private storage, and know the alpha File Storage v2 flag.

docs.title: Controllers
docs.text: A controller is the Python class of a DocType. It inherits from frappe.model.document.Document and adds business logic with lifecycle methods such as validate and on_submit. Put validation and side effects for your own DocTypes in the controller. Use doc_events to add logic to DocTypes of other apps.

docs.title: The controller file
docs.text:
Frappe makes the file when you save a standard DocType in developer mode. The class name is the DocType name without spaces and hyphens.

# sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe
from frappe import _
from frappe.model.document import Document


class SampleOrder(Document):
    _DOCTYPE_NAME = "Sample Order"

    # begin: auto-generated types
    # This code is auto-generated. Do not modify anything in this block.

    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from frappe.types import DF
        from sample_app.selling.doctype.sample_order_item.sample_order_item import SampleOrderItem

        amended_from: DF.Link | None
        customer_name: DF.Data
        items: DF.Table[SampleOrderItem]
        order_date: DF.Date
        status: DF.Literal["Draft", "Confirmed", "Delivered"]
        total: DF.Currency
    # end: auto-generated types

    def validate(self):
        self.total = sum(row.qty * row.rate for row in self.items)
        if not self.items:
            frappe.throw(_("Add at least one item"), title=_("Missing Items"))

    def on_submit(self):
        self.db_set("status", "Confirmed")

Custom DocTypes have no controller file. They use Document, or NestedSet for trees.

docs.title: Type hints
docs.text:
The block between # begin: auto-generated types and # end: auto-generated types lists the fields with types from frappe.types.DF. Frappe rewrites it when you save the DocType in developer mode, if the app sets export_python_type_annotations = True in hooks.py. Do not edit the block.

DF type Python type DF.Data, DF.Link, DF.Text, DF.SmallText ... str DF.Int int DF.Float, DF.Currency, DF.Percent float DF.Check bool \| int DF.Date, DF.Datetime, DF.Time str \| date, str \| datetime, str \| time DF.Literal[...] A Select field with its options DF.Table[RowClass] list of child documents

A field that is not mandatory gets | None.

docs.title: Lifecycle methods
docs.text:
Define any of these methods on the controller. Frappe calls each one through run_method, so doc_events, Notifications, Webhooks and Server Scripts for the same event also run.

Method When before_insert Before naming, on insert only. before_naming Before the name is set. autoname Sets self.name. See Naming. before_validate Before validate, on save and submit. Runs even with flags.ignore_validate. validate On save and submit. Throw here to stop the save. before_save After validate, on save of a draft. before_submit After validate, on submit. before_cancel On cancel. before_update_after_submit On save of a submitted document. after_insert After the row is inserted. Before on_update. on_update After the row is written, on insert, save and submit. on_submit After on_update, on submit. on_cancel After the row is updated, on cancel. on_update_after_submit After the row is written, on save of a submitted document. on_change At the end of every insert, save, submit, cancel, db_set and delete. before_change In db_set, before the database write. on_trash On delete, before the row is deleted. after_delete On delete, after the row is deleted. before_discard, on_discard Before and after a draft is discarded. before_rename(old, new, merge), after_rename(old, new, merge) Around a rename. before_rename can return a new name. onload When the desk loads the document in a form. Use self.set_onload(key, value) to send extra data. before_print(settings) Before a print view renders.

docs.title: Run order
docs.text: These tables come from frappe/model/document.py and frappe/model/delete_doc.py. They were confirmed by tracing run_method while inserting, submitting, cancelling and deleting a Sample Order on a develop site. Rows in bold are controller methods.

docs.title: Insert (doc.insert())
docs.text:
1. Set defaults, owner, creation and modified.
  2. Check create permission.
  3. check_if_latest: load the stored copy and check the docstatus transition.
  4. Validate Link fields.
  5. before_insert
  6. Set the name: before_naming, Document Naming Rule, autoname, autoname property. Child rows are named too.
  7. Reset fields that the user cannot write at a higher permission level.
  8. before_validate
  9. validate
  10. before_save, or before_submit if docstatus is 1.
  11. Standard checks: mandatory, data formats, select options, length, sanitizing HTML, password fields, workflow.
  12. Insert the parent row and all child rows.
  13. after_insert
  14. on_update
  15. on_submit, if docstatus is 1.
  16. Clear the document cache, publish doc_update and list_update, update global search, save a Version.
  17. on_change

docs.title: Save a draft (doc.save())
docs.text:
1. Check the document lock, set defaults.
  2. Check write permission. Set modified and modified_by.
  3. check_if_latest: throw TimestampMismatchError if the stored modified is newer than the copy you loaded.
  4. Reset fields at higher permission levels. Validate Link fields.
  5. before_validate
  6. validate
  7. before_save
  8. Standard checks.
  9. Update the parent row. Insert, update and delete child rows.
  10. on_update
  11. Cache, realtime, global search, Version.
  12. on_change

save() on a new document calls insert().

docs.title: Submit (doc.submit())
docs.text:
Same as save, with docstatus set to 1 and submit permission checked:

before_validate > validate > before_submit > standard checks > update rows > on_update > on_submit > cache, realtime, Version > on_change

docs.title: Update after submit (doc.save() on a submitted document)
docs.text:
before_update_after_submit > standard checks > check that only fields with allow_on_submit changed > update rows > on_update_after_submit > cache, realtime, Version > on_change

before_validate and validate do not run. A change to another field throws UpdateAfterSubmitError.

docs.title: Cancel (doc.cancel())
docs.text:
before_cancel > update rows with docstatus 2 > on_cancel > check that no submitted document links to it > cache, realtime, Version > on_change

Cancel checks cancel permission. It skips Link validation and the standard field checks.

docs.title: Delete (doc.delete() or frappe.delete_doc)
docs.text:
1. Check delete permission. Throw if the document is submitted.
  2. on_trash
  3. on_change, with flags.in_delete set.
  4. Check that no other document links to it. Skipped with force=True.
  5. Delete the row and child rows.
  6. after_delete
  7. Delete attachments. Enqueue the cleanup of dynamic links.
  8. Clear cache, remove global search and tags, add a Deleted Document unless delete_permanently=True.

ignore_on_trash=True skips steps 2 and 3.

docs.title: Discard a draft (doc.discard())
docs.text:
before_discard > db_set("docstatus", 2), which runs before_change and on_change > on_discard

Only drafts can be discarded. It needs write permission. No validation runs.

docs.title: db_set
docs.text: before_change > database update > on_change

docs.title: doc_events and controller order
docs.text:
For each event, run_method runs in this order:

  1. The controller method.
  2. doc_events handlers for the DocType, from all apps in app order.
  3. doc_events handlers for "*", from all apps in app order.
  4. Notifications for the event.
  5. Webhooks.
  6. Server Scripts of type DocType Event.
  7. Automations.

Server Script event names map to controller methods in frappe/core/doctype/server_script/server_script_utils.py. "Before Save" maps to validate, and "After Save" maps to on_update.

Handlers get (doc, method) or, with one parameter, (doc). Events with arguments, such as before_rename, pass them after method. A handler runs even when the controller does not define the method.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doc_events = {
    "Sample Order": {"validate": "sample_app.events.check_order"},
    "*": {"on_update": "sample_app.events.log_change"},
}

Frappe disables frappe.db.commit() and frappe.db.rollback() inside doc_events handlers. The call shows a warning and does nothing.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Set flags on doc.flags before insert, save or delete.

Flag Effect ignore_permissions Skip permission checks. Also an argument of insert and save. ignore_links Skip Link validation. Also an argument of insert. ignore_mandatory Skip the mandatory field check. Also an argument of insert. ignore_validate Skip validate, before_save, before_submit, before_cancel and before_update_after_submit. before_validate and the standard checks still run. ignore_validate_update_after_submit Allow changes to fields without allow_on_submit. ignore_version Do not save a Version. Also an argument of save. Default is True in tests. notify_update Set to False to skip the doc_update and list_update realtime events. ignore_save_passwords True, or a list of fieldnames, to skip saving Password fields. in_insert Read only. True during insert. in_delete Read only. True in on_change during delete.

insert also takes ignore_if_duplicate=True to return without error on a duplicate name, set_name to force a name, and set_child_names=False.

doc = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Order", "customer_name": "Customer A"})
doc.flags.ignore_mandatory = True
doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True)

Warning

ignore_permissions lets the current user write data they cannot normally write. Use it only for system actions, never to fix a permission problem. See Security.

docs.title: db_set
docs.text:
db_set writes one or more fields to the database without the save cycle.

doc.db_set("status", "Delivered")
doc.db_set({"status": "Delivered", "delivered_on": frappe.utils.today()})
doc.db_set("status", "Delivered", update_modified=False, notify=True)
Parameter Default Description fieldname Fieldname, or a dict of fieldnames and values. value None New value. update_modified True Update modified and modified_by. Inside on_update and other post-save methods, modified does not change. notify False Publish doc_update for open forms. commit False Commit the transaction.

db_set skips validation, permission checks, mandatory checks and Version. It runs before_change and on_change. Use it in on_submit or on_update to set status fields without a second save.

docs.title: Detect changes
Whitelisted controller methods
docs.text:
Add @frappe.whitelist() to a method to call it from the client or the REST API.

class SampleOrder(Document):
    @frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
    def apply_discount(self, percent: float):
        self.check_permission("write")
        for row in self.items:
            row.rate = row.rate * (1 - percent / 100)
        self.save()
        return self.total

Call it from a form script:

frm.call("apply_discount", { percent: 10 }).then((r) => {
    frappe.show_alert(__("New total: {0}", [r.message]));
});

Or with REST:

POST /api/v2/document/Sample Order/SO-00001/method/apply_discount
Content-Type: application/json

{"percent": 10}
Route Permission checked frm.call (run_doc_method) read on the document. The client sends the current form values, which can be unsaved. GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> read POST /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> write POST /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> with run_method write

The call goes through run_method, so doc_events for the method name also run. The response includes the document. The form syncs it after frm.call. See Whitelisted Methods for methods, allow_guest and type checks.

docs.title: Other Document methods
docs.text: Method Description frappe.get_doc(doctype, name) Load a document. Use for_update=True to lock the row. frappe.read_doc(doctype, name) Load a document after a read permission check, with fields the user cannot read removed. The result cannot be saved. frappe.new_doc(doctype) A new document with defaults. doc.reload() Load the document again from the database. doc.append(fieldname, row) Add a child row. Returns the row. doc.check_permission(ptype) Throw frappe.PermissionError if the user lacks ptype. doc.has_permission(ptype) True or False. Returns True if flags.ignore_permissions is set. doc.is_new() True before insert. doc.add_comment(comment_type, text) Add a comment to the timeline. doc.queue_action(action, **kwargs) Run submit, cancel or another method in a background job. Locks the document. doc.get_title() Value of the title field, or the name.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not call self.save() inside validate, on_update or other lifecycle methods. Use db_set in post-save methods.
  • Do not commit inside lifecycle methods or doc_events.
  • after_insert runs before on_update. Code in on_update runs on both insert and save.
  • validate does not run on cancel or on update after submit. Put checks for those in before_cancel and before_update_after_submit.
  • A whitelisted method called with frm.call needs only read permission. Check write in the method if it changes data.
  • A whitelisted method without methods accepts GET. Use methods=["POST"] for methods that change data.
  • A fieldname cannot match a controller method name.

docs.title: DocTypes
docs.text: A DocType defines a type of record: its fields, permissions, naming and behavior. Frappe makes a database table tab<DocType name> for each DocType and builds the form, list view and REST API from it. A record of a DocType is a document. Make a DocType for each kind of business record your app stores. Use Customize Form to change a DocType of another app.

docs.title: Standard and custom DocTypes
docs.text:
Standard (custom = 0) Custom (custom = 1) Where it lives JSON file in an app, also in the database Database only Who can make it Administrator in developer mode Users with DocType permission, any mode Python controller <doctype>.py class in the app None. Uses Document (or NestedSet for trees). Ships with the app Yes. bench migrate syncs it. No. Export it with fixtures if needed. Can be virtual Yes No

Saving a standard DocType outside developer mode raises CannotCreateStandardDoctypeError. Turn on developer_mode in site_config.json on your development site.

When you save a standard DocType in developer mode, Frappe writes these files into <app>/<module>/doctype/<doctype>/:

  • <doctype>.json, the definition.
  • <doctype>.py, the controller, if it does not exist.
  • <doctype>.js and test_<doctype>.py, for DocTypes that are not child tables.
  • <doctype>_tree.js for trees, <doctype>_calendar.js when is_calendar_and_gantt is on.
  • templates/ with three HTML files when has_web_view is on.

Existing files are not overwritten. Edit DocTypes in the desk form, not by hand in the JSON.

docs.title: The DocType JSON
docs.text:
{
 "doctype": "DocType",
 "name": "Sample Item",
 "module": "Selling",
 "autoname": "field:item_name",
 "naming_rule": "By fieldname",
 "title_field": "item_name",
 "sort_field": "creation",
 "sort_order": "DESC",
 "track_changes": 1,
 "field_order": ["item_name", "category", "rate"],
 "fields": [
  {"fieldname": "item_name", "fieldtype": "Data", "label": "Item Name", "reqd": 1, "unique": 1},
  {"fieldname": "category", "fieldtype": "Select", "label": "Category", "options": "Hardware\nSoftware\nService"},
  {"fieldname": "rate", "fieldtype": "Currency", "label": "Rate"}
 ],
 "permissions": [
  {"role": "System Manager", "read": 1, "write": 1, "create": 1, "delete": 1}
 ],
 "actions": [],
 "links": [],
 "states": []
}
Key Description fields Rows of DocField. Each has fieldname, fieldtype, label, options and flags such as reqd, unique, in_list_view, read_only, hidden, permlevel. See Field Types. field_order Order of fields in the form. permissions Rows of DocPerm: role, permission level and rights. See Permissions. actions, links, states Form buttons, connections and status colors. See below. modified Timestamp. bench migrate uses it with migration_hash to decide whether to import the file.

docs.title: Standard columns
docs.text:
Every table has these columns in addition to your fields:

Column Description name Primary key. See Naming. owner User who made the document. creation, modified Timestamps. modified_by User who saved last. docstatus 0 draft, 1 submitted, 2 cancelled. idx Row order, used by child tables. parent, parentfield, parenttype Child tables only. Link the row to its parent document. _user_tags, _comments, _assign, _liked_by Desk data. Not added to child tables. _seen is added when track_seen is on.

docs.title: Main properties
docs.text:
Property Type Default Description module Link Module Def Module that owns the DocType. Sets the folder of the files. is_submittable Check 0 Documents can be submitted and cancelled. Adds amended_from. istable Check 0 Child table. Used only inside a Table field of another DocType. issingle Check 0 One record only. Values are stored in tabSingles. is_tree Check 0 Tree with nested set fields. See below. is_virtual Check 0 No database table. The controller loads and saves data. editable_grid Check 1 Child table rows can be edited in the grid. quick_entry Check 0 New records open in a dialog with the mandatory fields. track_changes Check 0 Save a Version with the changes on each save. track_seen Check 0 Mark the document as seen when a user opens it. track_views Check 0 Log each view in View Log. autoname, naming_rule Data, Select How the name is set. See Naming. allow_rename Check 1 Users can rename documents. allow_import Check 0 Allow Data Import. title_field Data Field to show as the title. search_fields Data Comma-separated fields shown in link search results. sort_field, sort_order Data, Select creation, DESC Default sort of the list view. image_field Data An Attach Image field to use as the image. has_web_view Check 0 Each document gets a web page at route. read_only Check 0 "User Cannot Search". in_create Check 0 "User Cannot Create" from the desk. max_attachments Int Max number of attachments. make_attachments_public Check 0 New attachments are public by default. force_private_attachments Check 0 All attachments must be private. queue_in_background Check 0 Submit and cancel in a background job (beta). is_calendar_and_gantt Check 0 Turn on calendar and Gantt views. email_append_to Check 0 Make documents from incoming email. Needs subject_field and sender_field.

For a Single, Frappe sets allow_import, allow_rename, is_submittable and istable to 0. For a child table, Frappe clears permissions and sets allow_import to 0.

To read properties in code, use frappe.get_meta:

meta = frappe.get_meta("Sample Order")
meta.is_submittable           # 1
meta.has_field("customer_name")
meta.get_field("items").options   # "Sample Order Item"
meta.get_table_fields()
meta.get_link_fields()

docs.title: Child tables
docs.text:
A child table is a DocType with istable = 1. Add it to a parent through a Table or Table MultiSelect field whose options is the child DocType name. Rows are saved and loaded with the parent.

order = frappe.new_doc("Sample Order")
order.customer_name = "Customer A"
order.append("items", {"item": "Laptop", "qty": 2})
order.insert()

for row in order.items:
    print(row.idx, row.item, row.qty, row.parent)
  • Child tables have no permissions of their own. Access follows the parent.
  • Controller events run on the parent. Child rows get only before_naming and autoname. Field checks such as mandatory and select values also run on rows.
  • doc.remove(row) removes a row. Saving the parent deletes it from the database.

docs.title: Single DocTypes
docs.text:
A Single has one record. Its name is the DocType name. Values are stored as rows in tabSingles with doctype, field and value.

settings = frappe.get_single("System Settings")
settings.time_zone

frappe.db.get_single_value("System Settings", "time_zone")
frappe.db.set_single_value("Sample Settings", "enabled", 1)

frappe.db.set_single_value writes to the database without running the controller. Use get_single and save when the controller must validate.

docs.title: Trees
docs.text:
Set is_tree = 1 to store a hierarchy with the nested set model. When you save, Frappe adds these fields if lft is missing:

Field Type Description lft, rgt Int, hidden Nested set bounds. is_group Check Only group nodes can have children. old_parent Link, hidden Previous parent, used when a node moves. parent_<doctype> Link The parent node. Set as nsm_parent_field.

The controller of a standard tree DocType inherits from NestedSet:

# sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_category/sample_category.py
from frappe.utils.nestedset import NestedSet


class SampleCategory(NestedSet):
    pass

NestedSet updates lft and rgt in on_update and on_trash. If you override these methods, call super(). It also blocks loops, a non-group parent, and deleting a node that has children.

Function or method Returns doc.get_parent() The parent document. doc.get_children() A generator of child documents. doc.get_ancestors() Names of all ancestors. frappe.utils.nestedset.get_descendants_of(doctype, name) Names of all descendants. Uses get_list, so permissions apply. frappe.utils.nestedset.get_ancestors_of(doctype, name) Names of all ancestors. frappe.utils.nestedset.get_root_of(doctype) Name of the root node. frappe.utils.nestedset.rebuild_tree(doctype) Recalculates lft and rgt for all nodes.

docs.title: Virtual DocTypes
docs.text:
A virtual DocType has no table. Its controller reads and writes the data, for example from an external API or a file. Only standard DocTypes can be virtual.

When you save a virtual DocType, Frappe makes a controller with stubs. Implement all of them:

# sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_remote_order/sample_remote_order.py
import frappe
from frappe.model.document import Document


class SampleRemoteOrder(Document):
    def db_insert(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Save a new record in the backend."""

    def load_from_db(self):
        """Load the record for self.name, then call self.init_from_dict(data)."""

    def db_update(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Update the record in the backend."""

    def delete(self, *args, **kwargs):
        """Delete the record from the backend."""

    @staticmethod
    def get_list(filters=None, page_length=20, **kwargs):
        """Return a list of dicts for the list view and frappe.get_list."""

    @staticmethod
    def get_count(filters=None, **kwargs):
        """Return the number of records."""

    @staticmethod
    def get_stats(**kwargs):
        """Return sidebar stats."""

On save, Frappe checks the controller. It shows a message if a static method is missing or an instance method still uses the Document version. The required interface is in frappe/model/virtual_doctype.py.

docs.title: Document actions, links and states
docs.text:
These child tables of DocType change the form.

Table Fields Effect actions (DocType Action) label, group, action_type (Server Action or Route), action, hidden Adds a button. Server Action calls the whitelisted dotted path in action with doc. Route opens the route in action. links (DocType Link) link_doctype, link_fieldname, group, parent_doctype, table_fieldname, is_child_table, hidden Adds a group in the connections dashboard of the form. states (DocType State) title, color Sets the indicator color for a value of the status field.

A Server Action returns the document to update the form:

# sample_app/selling/actions.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def recalculate(doc):
    doc = frappe.get_doc(frappe.parse_json(doc))
    doc.check_permission("write")
    doc.save()
    return doc

docs.title: Module functions
docs.text:
A controller module can define two module-level functions that run when the DocType is saved:

Function When it runs on_doctype_update() After each save of a standard DocType, also when bench migrate imports a changed JSON. Use it to add database indexes. after_doctype_insert() After the DocType is made for the first time. 
# sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe


def on_doctype_update():
    frappe.db.add_index("Sample Order", ["customer_name", "order_date"])

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A fieldname cannot match a method or property of the controller. Frappe throws "Fieldname ... conflicting with a controller method".
  • A DocType name must be unique across all apps on the site.
  • Changing the module of a DocType does not move its files. Move or delete the old folder yourself.
  • Deleting a DocType does not drop its database table.
  • override_doctype_class and extend_doctype_class do not apply to custom DocTypes.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Every uploaded or generated file in Frappe has a File document. The document stores the name, URL, size, folder, privacy and the document it is attached to. The bytes are on disk in the site folder (storage v1, the default). Use the File DocType from code when you make, attach or read files. Use the upload_file endpoint from a client.

docs.title: Public and private files
docs.text:
Public Private is_private 0 1 Disk path sites/<site>/public/files/<file_name> sites/<site>/private/files/<file_name> file_url /files/<file_name> /private/files/<file_name> Who can read Anyone with the URL. nginx serves it with no permission check. Users who pass the File permission check. Guests get HTTP 403.

Read permission on a private file is given when one of these is true:

  • The user is Administrator, or the owner of the file.
  • The file is shared with the user.
  • The file is attached to a document and the user can read that document. Write, create and delete on the file need write permission on the document.

The ignore_file_permissions hook turns off these checks for all files.

Make files private unless they must be public, such as website images. DocType settings change the defaults:

  • Force Private Attachments (force_private_attachments): files attached to this DocType cannot be public.
  • Make Attachments Public by Default (make_attachments_public): the desk uploader selects "public" by default.
  • System Settings Only Allow System Managers to Upload Public Files (only_allow_system_managers_to_upload_public_files).

docs.title: File fields
docs.text: Field Description file_name File name. file_url URL of the file. For a remote file, the full http(s) URL. is_private Private file. file_size Size in bytes. file_type Extension in capitals, such as PDF. content_hash MD5 hash of the content. folder Parent folder, such as Home or Home/Attachments. is_folder The record is a folder. attached_to_doctype, attached_to_name Document the file is attached to. attached_to_field Attach field of that document that holds the file URL. thumbnail_url Thumbnail of an image. blob Link to File Blob. Only set with storage v2.

docs.title: Make a file from code
docs.text:
file = frappe.get_doc(
    {
        "doctype": "File",
        "file_name": "order-summary.txt",
        "attached_to_doctype": "Sample Order",
        "attached_to_name": "SO-00001",
        "content": b"Total: 100",
        "is_private": 1,
    }
).insert()

file.file_url        # /private/files/order-summary.txt
file.get_content()   # b"Total: 100"
file.get_full_path() # ./<site>/private/files/order-summary.txt
  • content can be bytes or str. Set "decode": True if the content is base64.
  • The insert checks write permission on the attached document, unless you set ignore_permissions=True.
  • If a different file with the same name exists on disk, Frappe adds a suffix to the new file name. The suffix is the last 6 characters of the content hash, or a random one if that name is taken too.
  • If a file with the same content hash and privacy exists, the new File row uses the same file on disk.
  • Without folder, an attached file goes to Home/Attachments and a file that is not attached goes to Home.
  • get_content() returns str for text files and bytes for binary files.
  • Deleting a File row deletes the file on disk after commit, when no other File row has the same file_url.
  • You cannot delete a File while its URL is still set in an Attach field of the attached document. Clear the field first, or set file.flags.force_delete = True.

For a remote file, set file_url to the full URL and no content.

docs.title: Attach fields
docs.text:
An Attach or Attach Image field stores the file_url. To fill one from code, make the File with attached_to_field set, then set the field:

order = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
file = frappe.get_doc(
    {
        "doctype": "File",
        "file_name": "signed.pdf",
        "attached_to_doctype": "Sample Order",
        "attached_to_name": order.name,
        "attached_to_field": "signed_copy",  # an Attach field on Sample Order
        "content": pdf_bytes,
        "is_private": 1,
    }
).insert()
order.db_set("signed_copy", file.file_url)

An Attach Image field accepts only image files.

docs.title: Legacy helper
docs.text: frappe.utils.file_manager.save_file(fname, content, dt, dn, folder=None, decode=False, is_private=0, df=None) makes a File and returns it. New code can make the File document directly.

docs.title: Upload over HTTP
docs.text:
POST /api/method/upload_file takes multipart/form-data. It is rate-limited to 300 calls per minute per user.

curl -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/upload_file" \
  -H "Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>" \
  -F "file=@summary.pdf" \
  --form-string "doctype=Sample Order" \
  --form-string "docname=SO-00001" \
  --form-string "is_private=1"

The response message is the new File document.

Form field Default Description file The file. is_private 1 0 for a public file. doctype, docname none Attach to this document. Needs write permission on it. fieldname none Attach field to fill. folder Home Target folder. file_url none Make a File for an existing URL instead of uploading bytes. file_name file name Name for a file_url upload. library_file_name none Name of an existing File to attach again. optimize off Compress an image or a PDF. Use max_width and max_height for images. method none Whitelisted method to call instead of making a File. It reads frappe.local.uploaded_file and frappe.local.uploaded_filename. chunk_index, total_chunk_count, chunk_byte_offset, total_file_size none Chunked upload. The desk sends chunks of file_chunk_size bytes.

Rules:

  • Guests can upload only when System Settings Allow Guests to Upload Files is on. Allowed DocTypes for Guest Uploads limits the target DocTypes.
  • Guests and website users can upload only JPG, PNG, GIF, PDF, TXT, CSV and Microsoft Office files.
  • The size limit is System Settings Max File Size in MB, else max_file_size in site config in bytes, else 25 MB.
  • Each function in the after_file_upload hook gets doc=<File> before save and must return the document.

To download a file with a token, call GET /api/method/download_file?file_url=/private/files/<name>. It applies the same permission checks.

docs.title: Storage hooks
docs.text: Hook Description before_write_file Called with file_size before content is written. write_file Replaces how file content is written. Used by storage v1 and save_file. delete_file_data_content Replaces how file content is deleted. after_file_upload Changes the File document in upload_file before save. ignore_file_permissions Any true value turns off the File permission checks. storage_drivers Registers File Storage v2 drivers.

docs.title: File Storage v2 (alpha)
docs.text:
Alpha

File Storage v2 is experimental. Its design, APIs, URLs and tables can change or be removed. Do not build on it outside Frappe's own apps.

Storage v2 is off by default. Turn it on per site with the storage_v2 site config key:

bench --site frappe.localhost set-config storage_v2 1

With the flag on:

  • New uploads make a File Blob row (checksum, size, sniffed MIME type, driver, key) and the File.blob link.
  • Bytes go through a storage driver. Core has local (default), s3 and memory (tests). Select one with storage_driver, and configure it with storage_driver_config.
  • New file URLs have two parts: /files/<blob>/<file_name> and /private/files/<blob>/<file_name>. The random blob name makes public URLs hard to guess.
  • Private files are served after a permission check. Drivers such as s3 can serve them through signed, expiring URLs.
  • Old v1 files keep their URLs and stay readable, so you can turn on the flag on an existing site.
  • frappe.storage.gc.collect_garbage runs daily and deletes blobs that no File row uses.

Check the flag in code with frappe.storage.enabled(). The full design is in frappe/storage/SPEC.md.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Public files have no permission check. Anyone with the URL can download them.
  • A file name is not unique. Find a File by file_url and the attached document, not by name alone.
  • Changing is_private moves the file and changes its URL. Frappe updates the attached_to_field of the attached document. Other places that store the old URL keep it.
  • Files that you write to disk without a File row are not listed in the desk and are never cleaned up.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: Every document has a name. It is the primary key of the table and the value that Link fields store. Frappe sets the name once, on insert, from the naming rule of the DocType. Choose the rule when you design the DocType, because changing it later does not rename old documents. Use Rename to change the name of one document.

docs.title: Naming rules
docs.text:
In the DocType form, the Naming Rule (naming_rule) field sets the Auto Name (autoname) property. Frappe uses autoname at runtime.

Naming Rule autoname value Example name Set by user prompt my-name Autoincrement autoincrement 5 (an integer) By fieldname field:item_name Sample Widget By "Naming Series" field naming_series: SO-2026-00001 Expression SO-.YYYY.-.##### or {customer_name}-.### SO-2026-00001, Customer A-001 Expression (old style) format:SO-{MM}-{customer_name}-{#####} SO-11-Customer A-00001 Random hash n7jg1d7hvg UUID UUID 019a... (UUID v7) By script empty Set in the autoname controller method.

If autoname is empty and no method sets a name, Frappe uses hash.

docs.title: Set by user (prompt)
docs.text:
The user types the name in the new form. In code, set __newname, or pass set_name to insert:

doc = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Code", "title": "A"})
doc.set("__newname", "CODE-A")
doc.insert()

frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Code", "title": "B"}).insert(set_name="CODE-B")

Without a name, insert fails with "Please set the document name".

docs.title: By fieldname (field:<fieldname>)
docs.text: The name is the value of the field, with spaces trimmed at the ends. When you save the DocType, Frappe sets unique on that field. If the field is empty on insert, Frappe throws " is required".

docs.title: Naming series (naming_series:)
docs.text:
The DocType needs a Select field with the fieldname naming_series. Each option is a series prefix. The user picks one, and Frappe adds .##### to it.

SO-.YYYY.-
SR-.YYYY.-

If the document has no naming_series value, Frappe uses the first non-empty option. Frappe keeps the counters in the Series table (tabSeries), one row per prefix.

Note

The field must be named naming_series. The desk describes the format as naming_series:[fieldname], but the code reads only doc.naming_series.

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
An expression has parts separated by dots. Frappe joins the parts:

Part Value #, ##, ##### ... Next number of the counter for the prefix built so far. The count of # sets the digits. YY, YYYY Year, 2 or 4 digits. MM, DD Month, day. JJJ Day of the year. WW Calendar week. timestamp Current date and time. {fieldname} or fieldname Value of that field of the document. Any other text Used as it is.

SO-.YYYY.-.##### makes SO-2026-00001, then SO-2026-00002. The counter key is SO-2026-, so the count starts again each year.

SO-.customer_name.-.#### uses a separate counter for each customer: SO-Customer A-0001, SO-Customer B-0001.

docs.title: Expression (old style, format:)
docs.text:
format: replaces every braced part and keeps other text. Frappe shows a warning when you save a DocType with format:.

Warning

A braced number part such as {#####} evaluates with an empty prefix. All format: patterns that use {#...} share one counter, the row with an empty name in tabSeries. Use the dot syntax (SO-.#####) when you need a counter per prefix.

docs.title: Autoincrement
docs.text: The name is an integer from a database sequence. The name column is an integer column. You can change to or from autoincrement only while the DocType has no records. Customize Form cannot change it.

docs.title: UUID
docs.text: The name is a UUID v7 string. On MariaDB the name column uses the uuid data type, so the database must support it. If you set a name before insert, Frappe checks that it is a valid UUID.

docs.title: Naming order
docs.text:
Document.insert calls set_new_name after before_insert. frappe.model.naming.set_new_name runs these steps:

  1. Run before_naming on the document.
  2. If autoname is autoincrement, take the next sequence value and stop.
  3. If autoname is UUID, keep a valid name or make a new one, and stop.
  4. If the document has amended_from, make the amended name. See below.
  5. If the DocType is a Single, use the DocType name.
  6. Apply the enabled Document Naming Rule records for the DocType, by priority.
  7. Run the autoname controller method.
  8. Apply the autoname property of the DocType.
  9. If there is still no name, use hash.
  10. Validate the name. It cannot contain < or >, and it cannot equal the DocType name.

insert(set_name="...") and a prompt name with __newname skip these steps. Child rows are named with the same steps. Steps 2 and 3 return early, so the autoname method does not run for autoincrement and UUID.

See Automation for Document Naming Rule and Document Naming Settings.

docs.title: The autoname method
docs.text:
Set the name in code with an autoname method on the controller. Leave the naming rule empty or set it to "By script".

# sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
import frappe
from frappe.model.document import Document
from frappe.model.naming import make_autoname


class SampleOrder(Document):
    def autoname(self):
        prefix = "SO-" + frappe.scrub(self.customer_name)[:3].upper() + "-.####"
        self.name = make_autoname(prefix, doc=self)

Use before_naming to set fields that the naming rule reads, such as naming_series.

docs.title: Helpers
docs.text:
Function Description make_autoname(key, doctype="", doc="") Returns a name from an expression. "hash" returns a random 10-character name. NamingSeries(series).get_preview(doc=None) Returns three sample names without using the counter. NamingSeries(series).get_current_value(doc=None) Returns the current counter value. NamingSeries(series).update_counter(new_count, doc=None) Sets the counter. A wrong value can make duplicate names. append_number_if_name_exists(doctype, value) Returns value, or value-1, value-2 ... if it exists. 
from frappe.model.naming import NamingSeries, make_autoname

make_autoname("SAMPLE-.YY.-.#####")          # 'SAMPLE-26-00001'
NamingSeries("SAMPLE-.YYYY.-.###").get_preview()
# ['SAMPLE-2026-001', 'SAMPLE-2026-002', 'SAMPLE-2026-003']

docs.title: Custom series parts
docs.text:
Add your own expression part with the naming_series_variables hook. The function gets the document and the part and returns a string.

# sample_app/hooks.py
naming_series_variables = {
    "REGION": "sample_app.naming.get_region",
}

# sample_app/naming.py
def get_region(doc, part):
    return doc.get("region_code") or "XX"

Now SO-.REGION.-.#### makes SO-EU-0001.

docs.title: Amended documents
docs.text: When you amend a cancelled document, the new document has amended_from. With the default setting (Amend Counter in Document Naming Settings), the name is the original name with a counter: SO-00016 becomes SO-00016-1, then SO-00016-2. Set Default Naming to use the normal naming rule instead. The Amended Document Naming Settings table sets this per DocType.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
Rename changes the name and updates every Link and Dynamic Link field that points to it.

doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", "Sample Widget")
doc.rename("Sample Gadget")              # needs write permission

frappe.rename_doc("Sample Item", "Sample Gadget", "Sample Widget")
frappe.rename_doc("Sample Item", "Sample Old", "Sample Widget", merge=True)
Parameter of frappe.rename_doc Default Description doctype, old, new DocType, current name, new name. force False Rename even if allow_rename is off. merge False Merge into an existing document new, then delete old. ignore_if_exists False Do not throw if new exists. show_alert True Show a message after rename. rebuild_search True Enqueue a rebuild of the global search for the DocType.

The rename runs before_rename(old, new, merge) and after_rename(old, new, merge) on the document. before_rename can return a new name. Rename checks write permission and the allow_rename property. Single DocTypes cannot be renamed. After the rename, Frappe adds a comment and publishes a doc_rename realtime event.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Changing the naming rule does not rename existing documents.
  • A field: name changes only by rename. Editing the field later does not change the name.
  • Names from hash are random. Do not use them in URLs that users must type.
  • Deleting the last document of a series can lower the counter by one (revert_series_if_last). Do not rely on gaps.
  • A name that is a number is stored as a string, except with autoincrement.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• DocTypes
  • Controllers
  • Automation

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
Read and write data with frappe.db and frappe.qb, and control transactions.

Page What it covers Database API Read and write data with frappe.db and frappe.get_list / get_all, the filter syntax, and when Frappe commits or rolls back a transaction. Query Builder Build SQL queries in Python with frappe.qb (PyPika): DocType tables, conditions, functions, joins, subqueries and frappe.qb.get_query.

docs.title: Database API
docs.text:
frappe.db is the connection to the site database for the current request or job. frappe.get_list and frappe.get_all query many rows of a DocType with filters. Use the document API (frappe.get_doc, doc.save()) when you need validation, hooks and permission checks. Use the functions on this page when you only need values, or when you need a fast write without controller logic.

All examples on this page were run in bench --site frappe.localhost console. The full list of methods is in the Database API reference.

docs.title: get_value
docs.text:
frappe.db.get_value(doctype, filters=None, fieldname="name", ignore=False, as_dict=False,
    debug=False, order_by=DefaultOrderBy, cache=False, for_update=False,
    *, run=True, pluck=False, distinct=False, skip_locked=False, wait=True)

filters is a document name, a filter dict or list, or a query builder criterion. The method returns the first match, or None.

frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Laptop", "rate")
# 900.0
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Laptop", ["item_name", "rate"])
# ('Laptop', 900.0)
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Laptop", ["item_name", "rate"], as_dict=True)
# {'item_name': 'Laptop', 'rate': 900.0}
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", {"category": "Software", "rate": (">", 100)}, "name")
# 'Office Suite'
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Nope", "rate")
# None
Option Description cache=True Keep the result in frappe.db.value_cache until the transaction ends. for_update=True Lock the row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) until commit or rollback. skip_locked, wait With for_update: skip locked rows, or fail at once instead of waiting. ignore=True Return None instead of an error when the table or column is missing.

docs.title: Other read methods
docs.text:
Method Returns frappe.db.get_values(doctype, filters, fieldname, ...) All matching rows as tuples, or dicts with as_dict=True. frappe.db.get(doctype, filters) The first matching row with all columns, as a dict. frappe.db.get_single_value(doctype, fieldname, cache=True) One field of a Single DocType, cast to the field type. frappe.db.exists(doctype, name_or_filters) The name of the first match, or None. frappe.db.count(doctype, filters=None) The number of matching rows. frappe.db.sql(query, values) Raw SQL result. 
frappe.db.get_values("Sample Item", {"category": "Hardware"}, ["name", "rate"], order_by="rate desc")
# (('Laptop', 900.0), ('Monitor', 250.0), ('Keyboard', 45.0))
frappe.db.get_single_value("System Settings", "time_zone")
# 'Asia/Kolkata'
frappe.db.exists("Sample Item", "Laptop")               # 'Laptop'
frappe.db.exists("Sample Item", {"category": "Hardware"})  # 'Keyboard'
frappe.db.count("Sample Item", {"category": "Hardware"})   # 3

docs.title: Query lists: get_list and get_all
docs.text:
frappe.get_list(doctype, **kwargs) applies the permissions of the current user. frappe.get_all(doctype, **kwargs) takes the same arguments and sets ignore_permissions=True. frappe.db.get_list and frappe.db.get_all are aliases.

In develop both run on the query builder engine (frappe.model.qb_query.DatabaseQuery and frappe.database.query.Engine). The older frappe.model.db_query.DatabaseQuery is still in the code but frappe.get_list does not use it.

frappe.get_all("Sample Item",
    filters={"category": "Hardware"},
    fields=["name", "rate"],
    order_by="rate desc")
# [{'name': 'Laptop', 'rate': 900.0}, {'name': 'Monitor', 'rate': 250.0}, {'name': 'Keyboard', 'rate': 45.0}]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description fields list, str ["name"] Fields to select. See Fields. filters dict, list, str None Conditions joined with AND. See Filters. or_filters dict, list None Conditions joined with OR, then joined to filters with AND. order_by str DocType sort settings For example "rate desc" or "category asc, rate desc". group_by str None For example "category". limit int no limit Maximum number of rows. offset int 0 Rows to skip. pluck str None Return a flat list of the values of one field. as_list bool False Return tuples instead of dicts. distinct bool False SELECT DISTINCT. ignore_permissions bool False (True for get_all) Skip permission conditions. ignore_user_permissions bool False Skip User Permission conditions only. user str current user Apply the permissions of another user. parent_doctype str None Required to query a child DocType with permissions. with_comment_count bool False Add _comment_count to each row. run bool True Set to False to get the query object instead of rows. debug bool False Print the query.

limit_start, limit_page_length, start and page_length still work but show a deprecation warning. Use offset and limit.

Warning

In develop, frappe.get_list has no default limit. It returns all permitted rows. Pass limit when the table can be large. The REST endpoints and frappe.client.get_list keep a default of 20.

frappe.get_all("Sample Item", fields=["name", "rate"], order_by="rate desc", limit=2, as_list=True)
# (('Laptop', 900.0), ('Support Plan', 300.0))
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", order_by="rate desc", limit=2, offset=2, pluck="name")
# ['Monitor', 'Office Suite']

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The same filter syntax works in frappe.get_list, frappe.get_all, frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_values, frappe.db.exists, frappe.db.count, frappe.db.set_value, frappe.db.delete, frappe.qb.get_query and the REST API.

Form Example Meaning Dict, equality {"category": "Hardware"} category = 'Hardware' Dict, operator {"rate": [">", 100]} or {"rate": (">", 100)} rate > 100 List of conditions [["rate", ">=", 100], ["category", "in", ["Hardware", "Service"]]] Both, with AND Condition with DocType [["Sample Order Item", "item", "=", "Laptop"]] Filter on a child table field Nested and / or [[["category", "=", "Service"], "or", ["rate", ">", 800]]] Grouped logic List of names ["Laptop", "Monitor"] name in (...) One name "Laptop" name = 'Laptop' Criterion frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Item").rate > 800 Query builder term 
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters=[["rate", ">=", 100], ["category", "in", ["Hardware", "Service"]]], pluck="name")
# ['Support Plan', 'Monitor', 'Laptop']
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", or_filters={"category": "Service", "rate": [">", 800]}, pluck="name")
# ['Support Plan', 'Installation', 'Laptop']
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters=[[["category", "=", "Service"], "or", ["rate", ">", 800]]], pluck="name")
# ['Support Plan', 'Installation', 'Laptop']
frappe.get_all("Sample Order", filters=[["Sample Order Item", "item", "=", "Laptop"]], pluck="name")
# ['SO-00006', 'SO-00001']

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
The operators are in OPERATOR_MAP in frappe/database/operator_map.py, plus the date and tree operators handled in frappe/database/query.py.

Operator Value Notes =, !=, <, >, <=, >= scalar =< and => are also accepted. in, not in list or comma-separated string An empty list with in matches nothing. With not in it matches everything. like, not like pattern with % Case-insensitive on MariaDB (default collation) and on Postgres (uses ILIKE). ilike pattern Postgres only. On MariaDB the query fails with a SQL syntax error. Use like there. regex pattern REGEXP on MariaDB, ~* on Postgres. There is no not regex. between [from, to] Dates in a Datetime field cover the full day. is "set" or "not set" not set also matches the empty value of the field type. timespan for example "this year", "last week" Converted to between. previous, next for example "1 week" Converted to between. ancestors of, descendants of, not ancestors of, not descendants of, descendants of (inclusive) document name For tree DocTypes. 
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters={"rate": ["between", [50, 150]]}, pluck="name")
# ['Installation', 'Antivirus', 'Office Suite']
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters={"item_name": ["like", "%top%"]}, pluck="name")
# ['Laptop']
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters={"category": ["not in", ["Hardware"]]}, pluck="name")
# ['Support Plan', 'Installation', 'Antivirus', 'Office Suite']

Apps can add operators with the filters_config hook.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Form Example Result Field name "rate" Column of the DocType Alias "rate as price" Column with another key All fields "*" All permitted columns Child table field "items.item" One row per child row Child table as list {"items": ["item", "qty"]} A list of child rows in each parent row Link field value "item.category" Field of the linked document (join) Function {"COUNT": "*", "as": "count"} Aggregate or SQL function Arithmetic {"MUL": ["qty", "rate"], "as": "value"} ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV 
frappe.get_all("Sample Order", fields=["name", {"items": ["item", "qty"]}], filters={"name": "SO-00001"})
# [{'name': 'SO-00001', 'items': [{'item': 'Laptop', 'qty': 2.0}, {'item': 'Monitor', 'qty': 2.0}]}]
frappe.get_all("Sample Order Item", fields=["item", "item.category"], limit=2)
# [{'item': 'Laptop', 'category': 'Hardware'}, {'item': 'Antivirus', 'category': 'Software'}]
frappe.get_all("Sample Item",
    fields=["category", {"COUNT": "*", "as": "count"}, {"SUM": "rate", "as": "total_rate"}],
    group_by="category", order_by="category asc")
# [{'category': 'Hardware', 'count': 3, 'total_rate': 1195.0},
#  {'category': 'Service', 'count': 2, 'total_rate': 380.0},
#  {'category': 'Software', 'count': 2, 'total_rate': 180.0}]

The supported functions are in FUNCTION_MAPPING in frappe/database/query.py: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN, ABS, EXTRACT, LOCATE, TIMESTAMP, IFNULL, CONCAT, NOW, NULLIF, MONTHNAME, QUARTER, MONTH, YEAR.

Warning

SQL functions written as strings are rejected:

frappe.get_all("Sample Item", fields=["count(name) as c"])
# frappe.ValidationError: SQL functions are not allowed as strings in SELECT: count(name) as c.
# Use dict syntax like {'COUNT': '*'} instead.

docs.title: Raw SQL
docs.text:
frappe.db.sql(query, values=(), *, as_dict=0, as_list=0, debug=0, pluck=False, as_iterator=False, ...)

Always pass values as parameters. Never format them into the query string.

frappe.db.sql("select name, rate from `tabSample Item` where category=%s order by rate",
    ("Software",), as_dict=True)
# [{'name': 'Antivirus', 'rate': 60.0}, {'name': 'Office Suite', 'rate': 120.0}]
frappe.db.sql("select name from `tabSample Item` where rate > %(min)s order by rate",
    {"min": 200}, pluck=True)
# ['Monitor', 'Support Plan', 'Laptop']

Table names are tab plus the DocType name. frappe.db.sql also accepts a query builder object. Prefer the query builder, which works on MariaDB, Postgres and SQLite.

docs.title: Write values
docs.text:
Method Description frappe.db.set_value(doctype, name_or_filters, field, val=None, modified=None, modified_by=None, update_modified=True) Updates columns with SQL. field can be a dict of field values. frappe.db.set_single_value(doctype, fieldname, value=None, *, update_modified=True) Updates a Single DocType. frappe.db.delete(doctype, filters=None) Deletes matching rows. frappe.db.bulk_insert(...) Inserts many rows, one statement per chunk of 1,000 rows (chunk_size). Postgres uses COPY. 
frappe.db.set_value("Sample Item", "Keyboard", "rate", 50)
frappe.db.set_value("Sample Item", "Keyboard", {"rate": 50, "disabled": 0}, update_modified=False)

frappe.db.set_value does not run validations, controller methods or doc_events. It does not check permissions and does not add a Version entry. It sets modified and modified_by unless update_modified=False. It clears the document cache. Use doc.db_set or doc.save() when hooks must run. See Controllers.

Calling frappe.db.set_value on a Single DocType is deprecated. Use frappe.db.set_single_value.

docs.title: Transactions
docs.text: Frappe opens a transaction for each request and each background job. The code that runs in it shares one connection, frappe.db.

docs.title: When Frappe commits
docs.text:
Context On success On error HTTP request with POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH Commit Rollback HTTP request with GET or other safe methods Rollback, unless frappe.local.flags.commit is set Rollback Background job (frappe.enqueue) Commit Rollback bench execute, bench console, patches You call frappe.db.commit()

The request logic is sync_database in frappe/app.py. UNSAFE_HTTP_METHODS is defined in frappe/auth.py.

Warning

Writes in a GET request are rolled back. Declare methods=["POST"] on a whitelisted method that writes. See Whitelisted methods.

docs.title: doc_events and controller hooks
docs.text:
Controller methods and doc_events handlers run inside the same transaction as the request. An exception in any of them rolls back the whole request, including writes made before the exception.

Inside doc_events handlers, frappe.db.commit() and frappe.db.rollback() do nothing. Document.run_method increments frappe.db._disable_transaction_control while hooks run, and the database shows a warning instead. Do not commit in document events.

docs.title: Run code after commit
docs.text:
API Description frappe.db.after_commit.add(fn) Run fn after the next commit. Dropped on rollback. frappe.db.before_commit.add(fn) Run fn before the next commit. frappe.db.after_rollback.add(fn), frappe.db.before_rollback.add(fn) Run fn around a rollback. frappe.enqueue(..., enqueue_after_commit=True) Put the job in the queue only after the commit. A worker then sees the committed data. 
frappe.db.after_commit.add(lambda: print("after commit ran"))
frappe.db.commit()
# after commit ran

An exception in an after-commit callback is logged in Error Log. It does not fail the request. See Background jobs.

docs.title: Manual control
docs.text:
Method Description frappe.db.commit() Commit and start a new transaction. frappe.db.rollback() Roll back and start a new transaction. frappe.db.savepoint(name) Create a savepoint. frappe.db.rollback(save_point=name) Undo changes after the savepoint only. frappe.db.release_savepoint(name) Remove a savepoint. with frappe.db.read_only(): Run a block in a read-only transaction. The open transaction must have no writes. 
frappe.db.savepoint("sample_sp")
frappe.db.set_value("Sample Item", "Keyboard", "rate", 1)
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Keyboard", "rate")   # 1.0
frappe.db.rollback(save_point="sample_sp")
frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", "Keyboard", "rate")   # 45.0

A rollback to a savepoint undoes database changes only. Callbacks and files are not undone.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.get_all and frappe.db.* do not check permissions.
  • frappe.get_list returns all rows when you do not pass limit.
  • frappe.db.get_value returns None when nothing matches. A tuple unpack of the result then fails.
  • frappe.db.exists with filters returns the name of a matching row, not a boolean. It adds no ORDER BY, so do not depend on which row it returns.
  • On MariaDB, a DDL statement (CREATE, ALTER) after writes in the same transaction raises frappe.exceptions.ImplicitCommitError, because it would commit them. Commit first, or run DDL before writes.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Query builder
  • Permissions
  • Controllers
  • Background jobs
  • Performance
  • Database API reference

docs.title: Query Builder
docs.text:
frappe.qb builds SQL queries from Python objects. It is a dialect of PyPika for MariaDB, Postgres and SQLite. Use it when frappe.get_all cannot express the query, for example for joins, subqueries, CASE or complex aggregates. Values are always sent as query parameters, so the query builder protects you from SQL injection.

All examples on this page were run in bench --site frappe.localhost console.

docs.title: Tables and fields
docs.text:
frappe.qb.DocType(name) returns the table of a DocType (tab<name>). Get a field as an attribute or with brackets.

from frappe.query_builder import Order

Item = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Item")

query = (
    frappe.qb.from_(Item)
    .select(Item.name, Item.rate)
    .where((Item.category == "Hardware") & (Item.rate > 100))
    .orderby(Item.rate, order=Order.desc)
)
query.get_sql()
# SELECT `name`,`rate` FROM `tabSample Item` WHERE `category`='Hardware' AND `rate`>100 ORDER BY `rate` DESC
query.run(as_dict=True)
# [{'name': 'Laptop', 'rate': 900.0}, {'name': 'Monitor', 'rate': 250.0}]

frappe.qb.Table("Singles") returns a table that is not a DocType. Item["field name"] works for field names that are not valid Python names.

docs.title: Run a query
docs.text:
query.run() runs the query on frappe.db. It takes the options of frappe.db.sql:

Option Result none Tuple of tuples as_dict=True List of dicts pluck=True Flat list of the first column debug=True Prints the query 
frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name).where(Item.category.isin(["Software", "Service"])).run(pluck=True)
# ['Antivirus', 'Installation', 'Office Suite', 'Support Plan']

query.walk() returns the SQL with placeholders and the parameter dict:

frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name).where(Item.name == "Laptop").walk()
# ('SELECT `name` FROM `tabSample Item` WHERE `name`=%(param1)s', {'param1': 'Laptop'})

Warning

query.get_sql() and str(query) put the values into the SQL text. Use them to read the query, not to run it with frappe.db.sql.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Python SQL Item.rate == 10, !=, <, >, <=, >= comparison (a) & (b), (a) \| (b), ~(a) AND, OR, NOT Item.category.isin([...]), .notin([...]) IN, NOT IN Item.item_name.like("Lap%"), .not_like(...) LIKE (ILIKE on Postgres) Item.description.isnull(), .isnotnull() IS NULL, IS NOT NULL Item.rate[50:150] BETWEEN 50 AND 150 Item.item_name.regex("^L") REGEXP on MariaDB, ~* on Postgres

Put parentheses around each side of & and |. Python operator precedence binds & before ==.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Import functions from frappe.query_builder.functions. It exports all PyPika functions (Count, Sum, Avg, Max, Min, Coalesce, IfNull, ...) and adds database-aware ones such as GroupConcat, Locate, DateFormat, Timestamp, UnixTimestamp, DateDiff, CombineDatetime, JSONExtract, Match, Round, Abs.

from frappe.query_builder.functions import Count, Sum

query = (
    frappe.qb.from_(Item)
    .select(Item.category, Count(Item.name).as_("count"), Sum(Item.rate).as_("total"))
    .groupby(Item.category)
    .orderby(Item.category)
)
query.run(as_dict=True)
# [{'category': 'Hardware', 'count': 3, 'total': 1195.0},
#  {'category': 'Service', 'count': 2, 'total': 380.0},
#  {'category': 'Software', 'count': 2, 'total': 180.0}]

CASE expressions:

from frappe.query_builder import Case

band = Case().when(Item.rate >= 200, "High").else_("Low")
frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name, band.as_("band")).where(Item.category == "Hardware").orderby(Item.name).run()
# (('Keyboard', 'Low'), ('Laptop', 'High'), ('Monitor', 'High'))

Shortcut aggregates on frappe.qb take a DocType, a field and optional filters:

frappe.qb.max("Sample Item", "rate")                                 # 900.0
frappe.qb.sum("Sample Item", "rate", filters={"category": "Hardware"})  # 1195.0

frappe.qb.min and frappe.qb.avg also exist.

docs.title: Joins
docs.text:
SalesOrder = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Order")
Row = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Order Item")

query = (
    frappe.qb.from_(SalesOrder)
    .join(Row).on(Row.parent == SalesOrder.name)
    .select(SalesOrder.name, SalesOrder.customer_name, Row.item, Row.qty)
    .where(Row.item == "Laptop")
    .orderby(SalesOrder.name)
)
query.run(as_dict=True)
# [{'name': 'SO-00001', 'customer_name': 'Customer A', 'item': 'Laptop', 'qty': 2.0},
#  {'name': 'SO-00006', 'customer_name': 'Customer F', 'item': 'Laptop', 'qty': 1.0}]

.join() is an inner join. Use .left_join() for a left join. Child rows link to their parent with parent, parenttype and parentfield.

docs.title: Subqueries
docs.text:
A query object can be the value of isin:

laptop_orders = frappe.qb.from_(Row).select(Row.parent).where(Row.item == "Laptop")

frappe.qb.from_(SalesOrder).select(SalesOrder.name).where(SalesOrder.name.isin(laptop_orders)).run(pluck=True)
# ['SO-00001', 'SO-00006']

docs.title: Updates, inserts and deletes
docs.text:
frappe.qb.update(Item).set(Item.disabled, 1).where(Item.name == "Keyboard").run()
frappe.qb.into(Item).columns("name", "item_name").insert("Sample X", "Sample X").run()
frappe.qb.from_(Item).delete().where(Item.name == "Sample X").run()

These statements skip controllers, validations, doc_events and permission checks, like frappe.db.set_value. They also do not set modified or clear the document cache. Use them for bulk work in patches and jobs.

docs.title: frappe.qb.get_query
docs.text:
frappe.qb.get_query builds a query from the same fields, filters and order_by syntax as frappe.get_all. It returns a query object that you can extend with query builder methods.

frappe.qb.get_query(
    table, fields=None, filters=None, order_by=None, group_by=None, limit=None, offset=None,
    distinct=False, for_update=False, update=False, into=False, delete=False,
    *, skip_locked=False, wait=True, ignore_permissions=True, ignore_user_permissions=False,
    user=None, parent_doctype=None, reference_doctype=None, or_filters=None, db_query_compat=False,
)

query = frappe.qb.get_query(
    "Sample Item",
    fields=["name", "rate"],
    filters={"category": "Hardware"},
    order_by="rate desc",
    limit=2,
)
query.run(as_dict=True)
# [{'name': 'Laptop', 'rate': 900.0}, {'name': 'Monitor', 'rate': 250.0}]

frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Item", fields=["name"], filters={"category": "Hardware"}).where(Item.rate < 500).run(pluck=True)
# ['Keyboard', 'Monitor']

Differences from frappe.get_list:

  • ignore_permissions defaults to True. Pass ignore_permissions=False to apply the permission rules of the current user (or of user). See Permissions.
  • Without order_by, the query has no ORDER BY. frappe.get_list uses the sort settings of the DocType.
  • The query is immutable after get_query returns. Each method such as .where() returns a new query.
frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Order", fields=["name"], ignore_permissions=False).run()
# raises frappe.PermissionError

The REST endpoint GET /api/v2/document/<doctype> builds its query with frappe.qb.get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False). A DocType controller can change that query with a static get_list(query) method. See REST API.

docs.title: Use criteria in the database API
docs.text:
frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_values, frappe.db.count, frappe.get_all and others accept a query builder criterion as filters:

frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", Item.rate > 800, "name")
# 'Laptop'

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Field names are not checked against the DocType. A wrong name fails only when the query runs.
  • frappe.qb does not apply permissions. Check them before you return results to a user.
  • In Server Scripts, only SELECT queries are allowed.

docs.title: Desk UI
docs.text:
Script forms and lists, call the server from JavaScript, and build desk pages and navigation.

Page What it covers Form Scripts Add client-side behavior to a desk form with frappe.ui.form.on events, the frm object API and the doctype_js hook. List View Settings Customize the desk list, tree, calendar, gantt and kanban views of a DocType with _list.js and the related view settings files and hooks. Client API Call the server, read data, show messages and dialogs, route, and format values from desk JavaScript with frappe.call, frappe.db, frappe.model, frappe.ui.Dialog and related helpers. Desk Pages Build a custom desk screen with the Page DocType, its JSON, JS, CSS and HTML files, frappe.pages events and frappe.ui.make_app_page. Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock Ship desk navigation from an app with Workspace, Sidebar and Dock JSON records and the add_to_apps_screen hook. Islands Draw desk pages and widgets with Vue islands, self-contained bundles that the desk mounts in a shadow root by name.

docs.title: Client API
docs.text: The desk loads a global frappe object in the browser. Form scripts, list settings, desk pages and Client Scripts use it to call the server, read documents, show messages and move between pages. All examples on this page were run in the desk browser console as Administrator. For a full list of functions, see the JavaScript API reference.

docs.title: frappe.call
docs.text:
frappe.call(opts) sends a request to /api/method/<method>. The method must be whitelisted. See Whitelisted Methods.

const r = await frappe.call({
    method: "frappe.client.get_value",
    args: { doctype: "Sample Item", filters: {}, fieldname: "item_name" },
});
console.log(r.message); // { item_name: "Antivirus" }

The short form is frappe.call(method, args, callback). The return value is a jQuery promise that resolves with the full response object. The return value of the Python method is in r.message.

Option Type Default Description method string Dotted path of the whitelisted method. args object {} Arguments for the method. type string "POST" HTTP method. callback(r) function Runs on success. error(r) function Runs on failure. always(r) function Runs after success or failure. freeze bool false Block the page until the response comes back. freeze_message string Text shown while frozen. btn element Disable this button while the request runs. doc object Run a whitelisted controller method on this document (run_doc_method). async bool true Set false for a blocking request. Avoid it. headers object {} Extra HTTP headers. quiet bool false No effect. It sets no_spinner, which frappe.call does not read. silent bool false Do not show the server messages (_server_messages). Some status-code handlers still show a dialog, for example the HTTP 403 "Not permitted" message. api_version string Call /api/<version>/method/<method>, for example "v2". url string Call this URL instead of /api/method/<method>. cache bool Let the browser cache a GET response.

Note

In develop, apps listed in frappe.boot.json_request_apps get a JSON request body. Other apps get form-encoded arguments. Set json: true or json: false to force one.

docs.title: frappe.xcall
docs.text:
frappe.xcall(method, args, type) is a shorter promise form. It resolves with r.message and rejects on error. The default type is POST.

const count = await frappe.xcall("frappe.client.get_count", { doctype: "Sample Order" });

Use frm.call() in form scripts to call a controller method of the open document. See Form Scripts.

docs.title: Read and write data: frappe.db
docs.text:
frappe.db wraps the frappe.client and frappe.desk.reportview methods. All functions return promises. The server checks permissions for each call.

Function Resolves with get_list(doctype, {fields, filters, order_by, limit, ...}) List of rows. Default fields: ["name"], limit: 20. get_value(doctype, name_or_filters, fieldname_or_list) The full response. The values are in r.message. get_single_value(doctype, field) The value of a field of a Single DocType. get_doc(doctype, name) The document. Also adds it to locals. exists(doctype, name_or_filters) true or false. count(doctype, {filters}) A number. set_value(doctype, name, fieldname_or_object, value) The full response with the updated document in r.message. insert(doc) The inserted document. doc must have a doctype key. delete_doc(doctype, name) The server response. get_link_options(doctype, txt, filters) Link search results. 
const orders = await frappe.db.get_list("Sample Order", {
    fields: ["name", "status"],
    filters: { status: "Open" },
    limit: 2,
});
// [{ name: "SO-00007", status: "Open" }, { name: "SO-00005", status: "Open" }]

const { message } = await frappe.db.get_value("Sample Order", "SO-00001", ["customer_name", "status"]);
// message = { customer_name: "Customer A", status: "Open" }

await frappe.db.count("Sample Order", { filters: { status: "Draft" } }); // 2
await frappe.db.exists("Sample Order", { customer_name: "Customer A" }); // true

Warning

frappe.db.get_value and frappe.db.set_value resolve with the response object, not with the value. Read r.message.

docs.title: Documents in the browser: frappe.model
docs.text:
Loaded documents live in the global locals[doctype][name]. frappe.model works on these local copies.

Function Description frappe.get_doc(doctype, name) Get a loaded document from locals. frappe.model.with_doc(doctype, name) Load a document from the server if needed. Returns a promise. frappe.model.with_doctype(doctype) Load the meta of a DocType. Returns a promise. frappe.get_meta(doctype) Get a loaded meta. frappe.model.set_value(doctype, name, fieldname, value) Set a value on a local document and run form events. Use it for child rows. frappe.model.add_child(parent_doc, child_doctype, parentfield) Add a row to a local document. frappe.model.get_new_doc(doctype) Make a new local document with default values. frappe.new_doc(doctype, values) Open a new form (or quick entry dialog) with these values. frappe.model.sync(docs) Put documents from a server response into locals.

docs.title: Messages
Dialogs: frappe.ui.Dialog
docs.text:
frappe.ui.Dialog shows a modal with form fields. Fields use the same definitions as DocType fields: fieldname, fieldtype, label, options, reqd, default, depends_on, read_only, description.

const d = new frappe.ui.Dialog({
    title: __("Enter details"),
    fields: [
        { label: __("Customer"), fieldname: "customer_name", fieldtype: "Data", reqd: 1 },
        { label: __("Date"), fieldname: "order_date", fieldtype: "Date", default: "Today" },
    ],
    primary_action_label: __("Create"),
    primary_action(values) {
        // values = { customer_name: "Customer A", order_date: "2026-11-22" }
        frappe.new_doc("Sample Order", values);
        d.hide();
    },
});
d.show();

primary_action gets the values only if all mandatory fields have values. If it returns a promise, the button shows a busy state until the promise settles.

Option Description title Dialog title. fields List of field definitions. size "small", "large" or "extra-large". primary_action_label, primary_action(values) The main button. secondary_action_label, secondary_action() The second button. static Do not close on outside click or Esc. minimizable Let the user minimize the dialog. indicator Color of the title indicator.

Methods: show(), hide(), get_values(), get_value(fieldname), set_value(fieldname, value), set_values(object), get_field(fieldname), set_df_property(fieldname, property, value), set_query(fieldname, fn), set_primary_action(label, fn), disable_primary_action(), enable_primary_action(), set_title(text), set_message(text), clear(). Set d.onhide = () => {} to run code when the dialog closes.

docs.title: Routing
Formatting and utilities
docs.text:
frappe.format(1234.5, { fieldtype: "Currency" });   // HTML with the formatted amount
frappe.format("2026-01-15", { fieldtype: "Date" });  // "15-01-2026" (user date format)
flt("12.3456", 2);                                   // 12.35
cint("7x");                                          // 7
frappe.datetime.get_today();                         // "2026-11-22"
frappe.datetime.add_days("2026-01-30", 3);           // "2026-02-02"
Function Description frappe.format(value, df, options, doc) Format a value as the desk shows a field of type df.fieldtype. Returns HTML. __(text, args) Translate a string. See Translations. flt(value, precision), cint(value), cstr(value) Convert to float, integer or string. frappe.datetime.get_today(), nowdate(), now_datetime() Today and now in system format. frappe.datetime.add_days(date, n), add_months(date, n), get_diff(d1, d2) Date math. frappe.datetime.str_to_user(value), user_to_str(value) Convert between system and user date formats. frappe.utils.escape_html(text) Escape HTML. Use it for user data that you put into HTML. frappe.utils.debounce(fn, wait), throttle(fn, wait) Limit how often a function runs. frappe.utils.copy_to_clipboard(text) Copy text and show an alert. frappe.utils.get_form_link(doctype, name) URL of a form. frappe.require(assets) Load JS or CSS bundles on demand. Returns a promise. frappe.run_serially(functions) Run functions one after the other. Waits for returned promises.

docs.title: Session and boot
docs.text:
Object Description frappe.session.user The logged-in user, for example "Administrator". frappe.session.user_email, frappe.session.user_fullname Email and full name. frappe.user.has_role(role) Check if the user has a role. frappe.boot Data loaded once at desk start: sysdefaults, user, lang, time_zone, module_app, workspaces, dock, ui_islands and more. frappe.sys_defaults System defaults such as date and number formats.

To add your own keys to frappe.boot, use the boot_session hook. See Extending Apps. Boot data is loaded once, so it is stale until the user reloads the page.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not put permission checks only in the browser. The server must check them.
  • frappe.call with async: false blocks the page. Use promises.
  • frappe.throw stops your code with an exception. Catch it if the code must continue.
  • locals holds only documents that the browser loaded. Use frappe.model.with_doc or frappe.db.get_doc before frappe.get_doc.
  • Escape user data with frappe.utils.escape_html before you put it into HTML.
