docs.title: Desk Pages
docs.text: A desk page is a custom screen in the desk that is not a form, list or report. Examples in Frappe are backups (Download Backups) and profile. Use a page for a dashboard, a tool or a board that needs its own layout. A page is a record of the Page DocType plus files in your app. For a page drawn by a Vue component, see Islands.

docs.title: Page files
docs.text:
A standard page lives in the page folder of a module:

sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/
├── __init__.py
├── order_board.json     # the Page record
├── order_board.js       # page script
├── order_board.css      # optional styles
├── order_board.html     # optional templates
└── order_board.py       # optional whitelisted methods

The folder and file names are the scrubbed page name (order-board becomes order_board). bench migrate imports the JSON into the Page table.

docs.title: Create a page
docs.text:
1. Turn on developer mode for the site. A new Page needs it.
  2. Log in as Administrator. Only Administrator can create or edit a Page.
  3. Go to /desk/page/new.
  4. Set Page Name, Title and Module. Keep Standard = Yes.
  5. Add the roles that can open the page in Roles. With no roles, all desk users can open it.
  6. Save.

On save, Frappe writes <page_name>.json and a starter <page_name>.js into the module folder. The record name comes from Page Name: lowercase, spaces become hyphens, and it is cut to 20 characters. The page opens at /desk/<name>.

docs.title: The page script
docs.text:
The starter script runs when the page loads for the first time:

// sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.js
frappe.pages["order-board"].on_page_load = function (wrapper) {
    const page = frappe.ui.make_app_page({
        parent: wrapper,
        title: __("Order Board"),
        single_column: true,
    });

    page.set_primary_action(__("New Order"), () => frappe.new_doc("Sample Order"), "add");
    page.add_inner_button(__("Refresh"), () => load_orders(page));

    page.status_field = page.add_field({
        label: __("Status"),
        fieldname: "status",
        fieldtype: "Select",
        options: ["", "Draft", "Open", "Completed"],
        change: () => load_orders(page),
    });

    $(page.body).html(`<div class="order-board"></div>`);
    load_orders(page);
};

frappe.pages["order-board"].on_page_show = function (wrapper) {
    load_orders(wrapper.page);
};

function load_orders(page) {
    frappe
        .xcall("sample_app.sample_module.page.order_board.order_board.get_orders", {
            status: page.status_field.get_value(),
        })
        .then((orders) => {
            $(page.body).find(".order-board").html(
                frappe.render_template("order_board", { orders })
            );
        });
}

frappe.pages[name] is the page wrapper element. The desk calls these functions on it:

Function When it runs on_page_load(wrapper) Once, after the page script is loaded. on_page_show(wrapper) Each time the page is shown, also the first time. refresh(wrapper) Each time the page is shown, after on_page_show.

frappe.ui.make_app_page(opts) makes a frappe.ui.Page and stores it as wrapper.page. Options: parent (required), title, single_column. A frappe.ui.Page has these parts and methods:

Member Description page.body, page.main The main content area (a jQuery object). page.sidebar The side section, used when single_column is not set. set_title(title), set_indicator(label, color), clear_indicator() Title and status indicator. set_primary_action(label, fn, icon), set_secondary_action(label, fn, icon) The main buttons. add_inner_button(label, fn, group) A toolbar button, or a dropdown item if group is set. add_menu_item(label, fn) An item in the "..." menu. add_action_item(label, fn) An item in the Actions menu. add_field(df) A filter control in the page form bar. Returns the control. page.fields_dict holds them. clear_primary_action(), clear_inner_toolbar(), clear_menu() Remove buttons.

docs.title: Server methods
docs.text:
Put whitelisted functions in <page_name>.py and call them by dotted path:

# sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_orders(status: str | None = None):
    filters = {"status": status} if status else {}
    return frappe.get_list("Sample Order", filters=filters, fields=["name", "customer_name", "status"])

The Page Roles control only who can open the page. They do not protect these methods. Use frappe.get_list or an explicit permission check in each method. See Whitelisted Methods.

docs.title: CSS and HTML templates
docs.text:
• <page_name>.css is loaded with the page.
  • Each .html file in the folder becomes frappe.templates["<file name>"]. Render it with frappe.render_template("<file name>", data). The syntax is the desk micro-template: {{ value }}, {% if %}, {% for item in list %} and {% endfor %}, or plain JavaScript inside {% %}.
  • If an .html file contains <!-- jinja -->, the server renders it with Jinja first. The context comes from get_context(context) in <page_name>.py. Such a page is not cached in the browser.
<!-- sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.html -->
{% for order in orders %}
    <div class="order-row">{{ order.customer_name }}: {{ order.status }}</div>
{% endfor %}

docs.title: Add code to another app's page
docs.text:
The page_js hook adds a script to a page that another app owns. The script runs after the page script.

# sample_app/hooks.py
page_js = {"backups": "public/js/backups_extra.js"}

docs.title: Page fields
docs.text: Field Type Description page_name Data Name used for the record name and route. title Data Title in the breadcrumb and browser tab. module Link Module that holds the page folder. standard Select Yes for a page shipped in an app. roles Table (Has Role) Roles that can open the page. Empty means all desk users. type Select Empty for a script page, Frappe UI for an island page. island Data For Frappe UI pages: the name of an island the app builds. Empty means the island is built from the page folder. system_page Check The page opens with no sidebar. shared_page Check The page opens in the sidebar that is on screen, instead of the sidebar of its module. Cannot be set with system_page.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Outside developer mode, the browser caches the page script in localStorage. Reload after a change. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache if it does not update.
  • A Page can be deleted only in developer mode. In developer mode, deleting it also deletes its folder.
  • The frappe.pages[...] key is the record name with hyphens, not the scrubbed folder name.
  • A Frappe UI page does not run <page_name>.js. See Islands.

docs.title: Form Scripts
docs.text: A form script is JavaScript that runs in the desk form of a DocType. Use it to react to form events, change field properties, add buttons, filter Link fields and call the server. Keep business rules and validation on the server, in the controller. A form script only improves the user interface. A user can skip it with a direct API call.

docs.title: Where form scripts come from
docs.text:
When the desk loads a DocType, frappe/desk/form/meta.py collects all form code into the __js and __custom_js keys of the DocType meta. The browser runs them in this order:

  1. <doctype>.js in the DocType folder of the app that owns the DocType, for example sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js.
  2. regional/<country>.js in the same folder, if System Settings has a country and the file exists.
  3. The files that other apps add with the doctype_js hook, in app order.
  4. The client script of the active DocType Layout, if the form opens with one.
  5. All enabled Client Script records with view = Form for the DocType, oldest first. These do not run when a DocType Layout is active.

Steps 1 to 3 apply only to standard DocTypes. A DocType with custom = 1 gets no file-based code, so use a Client Script record for it. Client Script records are described in Server and Client Scripts.

To add code to a DocType that another app owns, use the doctype_js hook. The path is relative to the app package.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_js = {
    "ToDo": "public/js/todo.js",
    "User": ["public/js/user.js", "public/js/user_extra.js"],
}

The value can be a string or a list of strings. See Extending Apps for the other extension hooks.

docs.title: Register event handlers
docs.text:
Use frappe.ui.form.on(doctype, handlers). Each key is a form event or a fieldname. Each handler gets frm, and for child rows also cdt (child DocType) and cdn (child row name).

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    setup(frm) {
        frm.set_query("item", "items", () => ({ filters: { disabled: 0 } }));
    },
    refresh(frm) {
        if (!frm.is_new()) {
            frm.add_custom_button(__("Mark as Completed"), () => {
                frm.set_value("status", "Completed").then(() => frm.save());
            }, __("Actions"));
        }
    },
    customer_name(frm) {
        frm.set_intro(__("Customer changed. Check the items."), "orange");
    },
});

You can call frappe.ui.form.on many times for the same DocType. All handlers for an event run, one after the other, in the order they were registered. If a handler returns a promise, the next handler waits for it. frappe.ui.form.off(doctype, event) removes all handlers for that event.

To run another handler from your code, use frm.trigger("event_name"). It returns a promise.

docs.title: Form events
docs.text:
The event order below was checked in the browser on a Sample Order form.

Action Events, in order Open a form for the first time (new or existing document) setup, before_load, onload, refresh, onload_post_render Open a document that is already loaded in this session refresh Change a field value <fieldname> Save validate, before_save, (server save), after_save, refresh Submit before_submit, validate, before_save, (server submit), after_save, on_submit, refresh Cancel before_cancel, (server cancel), after_cancel, refresh Delete after_delete

setup runs once for each form instance, that is once for each DocType in a browser session. Put set_query and other one-time setup there. Put buttons and anything that depends on the document in refresh.

All form events:

Event When it runs setup Once, when the form object for the DocType is made. before_load Before onload, the first time a document opens. onload The first time a document opens in this session. refresh Every time the form renders: after load, after save, submit or cancel, and when you go back to the form. onload_post_render After the first refresh of a document. <fieldname> After the value of that field changes. validate Before save. Stop the save with frappe.throw() or frappe.validated = false. before_save After validate, before the request to the server. after_save After the server saved the document. before_submit Before submit. Stop it with frappe.validated = false. on_submit After the server submitted the document. before_cancel Before cancel. Stop it with frappe.validated = false. after_cancel After the server cancelled the document. before_discard, after_discard Before and after the user discards a draft. after_delete After the document was deleted, before the browser goes back. before_workflow_action, after_workflow_action Before and after a workflow action. frm.selected_workflow_action holds the action name. timeline_refresh After the timeline renders. dashboard_update After the connections dashboard loads its counts. on_tab_change After the user changes the form tab. on_hide When the user leaves the form page. <button fieldname> When the user clicks a Button field.

docs.title: Child table events
docs.text:
Register child table events on the child DocType, not on the parent. The handler gets (frm, cdt, cdn). Use locals[cdt][cdn] or frappe.get_doc(cdt, cdn) to read the row.

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order Item", {
    qty(frm, cdt, cdn) {
        const row = locals[cdt][cdn];
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "amount", flt(row.qty) * flt(row.rate));
    },
    items_add(frm, cdt, cdn) {
        frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, "qty", 1);
    },
    items_remove(frm) {
        frm.set_value("total", frm.get_sum("items", "amount"));
    },
});
Event When it runs <child fieldname> After a field in a row changes. <table fieldname>_add After the user adds a row in the grid. frm.add_child() does not trigger it. before_<table fieldname>_remove Before a row is removed. <table fieldname>_remove After a row is removed. <table fieldname>_move After the user drags a row to a new position. <table fieldname>_delete After the user deletes selected rows or all rows. form_render When the row editor of a row opens.

docs.title: The frm object
docs.text:
frm is the frappe.ui.form.Form instance (frappe/public/js/frappe/form/form.js). The global cur_frm points to the form on screen, but use the frm argument in handlers.

Common properties:

Property Description frm.doc The document as a plain object. Child tables are arrays of row objects. frm.doctype, frm.docname The DocType and the document name. frm.meta The DocType meta. frm.fields_dict Field controls by fieldname. frm.fields_dict.items.grid is the grid of a table field. frm.page The frappe.ui.Page of the form. frm.custom_buttons Buttons added with add_custom_button, by label.

Methods:

Method Description set_value(fieldname, value) or set_value({field: value, ...}) Set values and run the change events. Returns a promise. Pass an array to replace a child table. refresh_field(fieldname) Render one field again after you change frm.doc directly. refresh_fields() / refresh() Render all fields again / render the whole form again. set_df_property(fieldname, property, value) Change a field property, for example read_only, hidden, reqd, options, label, description. set_df_property(table, property, value, docname, child_field, row_name) Change a property of a child field for one row. toggle_display(fieldnames, show) Show or hide one field or a list of fields. toggle_reqd(fieldnames, mandatory) Make fields mandatory or not. toggle_enable(fieldnames, enable) Make fields editable or read-only. set_query(fieldname, fn) / set_query(child_field, table, fn) Set the filters of a Link field. fn returns { filters } or { query, filters }. add_custom_button(label, fn, group) Add a toolbar button. A group puts it in a dropdown. Returns the button. remove_custom_button(label, group), clear_custom_buttons() Remove one button or all custom buttons. change_custom_button_type(label, group, type) Change the button style, for example "primary". add_child(table_fieldname, values) Add a row to a child table. Call refresh_field(table) after it. Returns the row. clear_table(table_fieldname) Remove all rows of a child table. get_sum(table_fieldname, fieldname) Sum a column of a child table. update_in_all_rows(table_fieldname, fieldname, value) Set a value in all rows. get_selected() Selected rows of each grid, as {table_fieldname: [row names]}. call(method, args) Call a whitelisted method of the document controller. See below. save(action), savesubmit(), savecancel(), savetrash() Save, submit, cancel or delete with the standard confirm dialogs. save() returns a promise. reload_doc() Load the document again from the server. is_new(), is_dirty(), dirty() Check if the document is unsaved or changed, or mark it as changed. has_perm(ptype) Check a permission on the document, for example "write". set_intro(text, color) Show a message at the top of the form. Call with no text to clear it. set_indicator_formatter(fieldname, get_color, get_text) Show a colored indicator in a Link column of a grid. disable_save(), enable_save(), disable_form() Hide the save button, show it again, or make the whole form read-only. scroll_to_field(fieldname) Scroll to a field and focus it. set_active_tab(tab_fieldname) Open a form tab. add_fetch(link_field, source_field, target_field) Copy a field of the linked document into the form when the link changes. Prefer fetch_from in the DocType. trigger(event) Run the handlers of an event. copy_doc(), amend_doc(), print_doc(), email_doc(), rename_doc() Open the standard actions.

The helpers in frappe/public/js/frappe/form/script_helpers.js (refresh_field, hide_field, unhide_field, set_field_options) are older globals that act on cur_frm. Use the frm methods in new code.

docs.title: Call the server
docs.text:
frm.call(method, args) runs a whitelisted method of the controller class of the document. The current document is sent with the request. If the method changes the document, the form updates its fields.

# sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    @frappe.whitelist()
    def get_open_count(self):
        return frappe.db.count("Sample Order", {"customer_name": self.customer_name, "docstatus": 0})

// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frm.call("get_open_count").then((r) => {
            frm.set_intro(__("{0} draft orders for this customer", [r.message]));
        });
    },
});

If you pass an object with method and no doc, and the method has no dot, frm.call prefixes it with the Python module of the DocType. For other server calls, use frappe.call or frappe.xcall. See Client API.

docs.title: Class-based controllers
docs.text: Older code uses a controller class. frappe.ui.form.set_controller(doctype, Class) binds a class whose methods have event names. These methods get (doc, cdt, cdn), not frm. They run after the frappe.ui.form.on handlers for the same event. Use frappe.ui.form.on in new code.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not trust form scripts for validation. Repeat each rule in the controller validate.
  • Add buttons in refresh, not in onload. The toolbar is rebuilt on every refresh.
  • frm.add_child() and direct changes to frm.doc do not render. Call frm.refresh_field() after them.
  • frm.set_value() is asynchronous. Use await or .then() before you read dependent values or save.
  • A handler that returns a promise delays the next handler and the save. A promise that never settles blocks the form.
  • frappe.model.set_value(cdt, cdn, ...) sets a child row value. frm.set_value sets parent fields only.
  • If a form uses a DocType Layout, Client Script records with view = Form do not run. Put the code in the client script of the layout.

docs.title: Islands
docs.text:
An island is a Vue UI unit that an app builds and the desk mounts in a shadow root. The island bundle carries its own Vue, frappe-ui and everything it imports, so the desk page needs nothing loaded first. Use an island when you want to write a desk page or widget in Vue with frappe-ui instead of jQuery. The desk pages profile, search and notifications, the Flow chat and desk charts are islands.

There are two ways to use islands:

Way You write Who builds it Island name Page island A Page with type = Frappe UI, plus a .vue file in the page folder Frappe, in bench build <app>.page.<page name> App island An entry file and a build script in your app frontend Your app, from the build script of its package.json Any name. Prefix it with the app name.

docs.title: The island registry
docs.text:
An island is registered by its build. The build writes <name>.island.js (and <name>.island.css) into sites/assets/assets.json. frappe/utils/island.py reads that file and keeps only the islands of apps installed on the site. The list is in frappe.boot.ui_islands:

frappe.boot.ui_islands;
// ["frappe.chart", "frappe.flow.chat", "frappe.page.notifications", "frappe.page.profile", "frappe.page.search"]

A host without desk boot can resolve a name with the whitelisted method frappe.utils.island.get_island_assets(name). It returns {js, css}, or throws if the island is not on the site.

docs.title: Page islands
docs.text:
A page island draws the body of a desk page. The desk keeps its own page header and sets the title and menu from what the island reports.

  1. Turn on developer mode for the site.
  2. Create a Page as described in Desk Pages. Set Type to Frappe UI and keep Standard = Yes.
  3. Save. Frappe writes the starter files next to the page JSON.
  4. Run bench build, or keep bench watch running.
  5. Open /desk/<page name>.
sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/
├── order_board.json        # "type": "Frappe UI"
├── order_board.island.js   # the entry, written once
└── order_board.vue         # the component, yours to edit

The entry file exports mount:

// sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.island.js
import { mountVueIsland } from "@framework/ui/island";

import Page from "./order_board.vue";

export const mount = (el, context) => mountVueIsland(el, { ...context, component: Page });

The component gets the route below the page as props and reports its title and actions:

<!-- sample_app/sample_module/page/order_board/order_board.vue -->
<script setup>
import { onMounted } from "vue";
import { createResource, frappeRequest } from "frappe-ui";
import { useHost } from "@framework/ui/island";

defineProps({
    route: { type: Array, default: () => [] },
    query: { type: Object, default: () => ({}) },
});
const emit = defineEmits(["title", "actions"]);
const host = useHost();

const orders = createResource({
    url: "frappe.client.get_list",
    params: { doctype: "Sample Order", fields: ["name", "customer_name", "status"] },
    resourceFetcher: frappeRequest,
    auto: true,
});

onMounted(() => {
    emit("title", "Order Board");
    emit("actions", [
        { label: "New Order", onClick: () => host.navigate("/desk/sample-order/new") },
    ]);
});
</script>

<template>
    <div class="h-full overflow-y-auto p-5">
        <div v-for="order in orders.data" :key="order.name" class="text-sm text-ink-gray-8">
            {{ order.customer_name }}: {{ order.status }}
        </div>
    </div>
</template>
Prop or event Description route (prop) URL segments after the page name. query (prop) URL query parameters. title (event) A string or null. The desk shows it in the breadcrumb and browser tab. actions (event) A list of {label, icon?, onClick} or {label, icon?, href}. The desk shows each as a page menu row. An href opens in a new tab.

A route change updates route and query in place. The island is not mounted again. The island stays mounted while the page is hidden.

Note

Frappe builds all page islands of the bench in one build, rooted at apps/frappe/island-toolchain/. A page island can import only vue, frappe-ui, @framework/ui and what they bring. It cannot import code from your app frontend. If it must, build an app island instead.

A Frappe UI page does not run <page_name>.js. The first bench build runs yarn install in apps/frappe/island-toolchain/. If a page island build fails, bench build reports it and continues.

docs.title: App islands
docs.text:
An app island is built by your app. Use it to reuse your own components, or to mount an island in a place that is not a full page.

  1. Add @framework/ui to your frontend as a linked package and add its Vite plugin. The steps are in apps/frappe/ui/README.md.
  2. Write an entry that exports mount:
// sample_app/frontend/src/islands/order_board.js
import { mountVueIsland } from "@framework/ui/island";
import OrderBoard from "./OrderBoard.vue";

export const mount = (el, context) => mountVueIsland(el, { ...context, component: OrderBoard });
  1. Build all entries of the app in one script:
// sample_app/frontend/build-islands.mjs
import { buildIslands } from "@framework/ui/vite/island";

await buildIslands({
    app: "sample_app",
    root: import.meta.dirname,
    entries: { "sample_app.order_board": "src/islands/order_board.js" },
    production: process.argv.includes("--production"),
    watch: process.argv.includes("--watch"),
});
  1. Call the script from the build script in the package.json at the root of your app. bench build runs that script for each app. Output goes to sites/assets/<app>/dist/island/.

mountVueIsland also accepts configure(app) to register plugins, and routes and history for a vue-router inside the island.

docs.title: Mount an app island in the desk
docs.text:
Use frappe.ui.mount_island(name, el, props) in any desk code:

const island = frappe.ui.mount_island("sample_app.order_board", page.body[0], {
    status: "Open",
    onTitle: (title) => page.set_title(title),
});
island.update({ status: "Completed" });
await island.ready;
island.unmount();

The third argument is the Vue props object. Event listeners are on* keys, for example onTitle. The handle returns at once. ready resolves when the island is on the page and rejects if the load fails. frappe.ui.unmount_island(el) removes the island from an element.

To use an app island as a whole desk page, create a Page with type = Frappe UI and set Island to the island name. Frappe then builds and scaffolds nothing for the page. The page does not need to be Standard. On save, Frappe checks that the island is in the registry.

docs.title: The host context
docs.text:
Inside an island component, useHost() from @framework/ui/island returns what the desk passes in. Every key is optional.

Key Description locale User language, from frappe.boot.lang. timezone User or system time zone. user The session user. base_url Site URL. navigate(route) Go to a desk route with frappe.set_route. Use it instead of plain links. format(value, df, doc) Format a value as the desk does, as text. developer_mode true on a developer-mode site. first_day_of_the_week From system defaults. theme The desk theme. Added by the mount contract.

docs.title: Charts
docs.text: Desk charts use the framework island frappe.chart. Draw a chart with frappe.ui.chart(el, config). It returns {update(config), destroy(), ready}. frappe.Chart, frappe.utils.make_chart and frappe.ui.RealtimeChart are deprecated.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Island names share one namespace on the bench. Prefix every name with your app name. Two builds that write the same key fail.
  • A plain <a href> inside an island reloads the page, because the shadow root hides the click from the desk router. Use host.navigate().
  • bench watch runs the framework and page island builds in watch mode. An app island needs its own watch script, for example node build-islands.mjs --watch.
  • A page island build that fails does not fail bench build. The page then shows its unbuilt state. Check the build output.
  • An island named in a Page island field must be built and its app installed, or the Page does not save.

docs.title: List View Settings
docs.text: Each desk view of a DocType reads a settings object from a global registry. An app fills the registry in a JavaScript file next to the DocType, for example sample_order_list.js for the list view. Use these files to add indicators, row buttons, column formatters, default filters and view-specific options. To change columns or the page size without code, users have List Settings in the desk. See List View.

docs.title: Files and registries
docs.text:
frappe/desk/form/meta.py reads these files from the DocType folder and from hooks. The browser runs them when it loads the DocType meta, in this order: list, calendar, tree, kanban, then Client Script records with view = List. A Client Script can therefore override the file-based settings.

File in the DocType folder Hook for other apps Registry it fills <doctype>_list.js doctype_list_js frappe.listview_settings["<DocType>"] (list, report, kanban and image views) <doctype>_calendar.js doctype_calendar_js frappe.views.calendar["<DocType>"] (calendar and gantt views) <doctype>_tree.js doctype_tree_js frappe.treeview_settings["<DocType>"] (tree view) <doctype>_kanban.js doctype_kanban_js frappe.kanban_v2.settings["<DocType>"] (Kanban boards that use Kanban v2)

The <doctype> part is the scrubbed DocType name, for example sample_order. A file regional/<country>_list.js is also added to the list code when System Settings has that country. A custom DocType (custom = 1) loads no files. Use a Client Script with view = List for it.

# sample_app/hooks.py
doctype_list_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_list.js"}
doctype_calendar_js = {"ToDo": "public/js/todo_calendar.js"}

A hook file runs after the file of the owning app. Assigning a new object replaces the settings of the owning app. Change single keys instead:

// sample_app/public/js/todo_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"] = frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"] || {};
frappe.listview_settings["ToDo"].add_fields = ["priority"];

docs.title: List view settings
docs.text:
// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_order/sample_order_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["Sample Order"] = {
    add_fields: ["status", "total"],
    has_indicator_for_draft: 1,
    get_indicator(doc) {
        const colors = { Draft: "gray", Open: "orange", Completed: "green", Cancelled: "red" };
        return [__(doc.status), colors[doc.status] || "gray", "status,=," + doc.status];
    },
    button: {
        show: (doc) => doc.status === "Open",
        get_label: () => __("Complete"),
        get_description: (doc) => __("Mark {0} as Completed", [doc.name]),
        action: (doc) =>
            frappe.db.set_value("Sample Order", doc.name, "status", "Completed")
                .then(() => cur_list.refresh()),
    },
    formatters: {
        order_date: (value) => `<span class="text-muted">${frappe.datetime.prettyDate(value)}</span>`,
    },
    onload(listview) {
        listview.page.add_inner_button(__("Open Orders"), () =>
            listview.filter_area.add([["Sample Order", "status", "=", "Open"]])
        );
    },
};

The list in the image has no Workflow. If the DocType has an active Workflow, a row with a workflow state shows that state instead of the result of get_indicator. This does not happen when every active Workflow of the DocType has Don't Override Status (override_status) set.

Key Type Description add_fields list Extra fields to fetch for each row. Add every field that get_indicator, button or formatters reads. filters list Default filters, as [fieldname, operator, value]. Used only when the user has no saved filters. hide_name_column bool Hide the name (ID) column. hide_name_filter bool Hide the ID filter in the standard filter bar. get_indicator(doc) function Return [label, color, filter] for the status indicator. filter is "field,operator,value" and is applied when the user clicks the indicator. has_indicator_for_draft bool For a submittable DocType, use get_indicator for drafts instead of the "Draft" indicator. has_indicator_for_cancelled bool The same for cancelled documents. formatters object {fieldname: (value, df, doc) => html}. Formats a column. button object One button per row: show(doc), get_label(doc), get_description(doc), action(doc). dropdown_button object A dropdown per row: get_label (a string) and buttons, a list of {get_label, show(doc), get_description(doc), action(doc)}. onload(listview) function Runs once after the view is set up. Add page buttons and menu items here. before_render() function Runs before each render of the rows. refresh(listview) function Runs after each data refresh. primary_action() function Replaces the action of the "Add" button. get_form_link(doc) function Return the URL a row opens.

listview is the frappe.views.ListView instance. Useful members: listview.page (a frappe.ui.Page), listview.filter_area, listview.data, listview.get_checked_items(), listview.refresh(). To add an item to the Actions menu of selected rows, call listview.page.add_actions_menu_item(label, fn).

The indicator rules in frappe/public/js/frappe/model/indicator.js run in this order: unsaved, workflow state, draft and cancelled (for submittable DocTypes), DocType states that match doc.status, get_indicator, submitted, status, enabled, disabled.

docs.title: Calendar and gantt settings
docs.text:
// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_event/sample_event_calendar.js
frappe.views.calendar["Sample Event"] = {
    field_map: {
        start: "starts_on",
        end: "ends_on",
        id: "name",
        title: "subject",
        allDay: "all_day",
    },
    gantt: true,
    get_events_method: "frappe.desk.calendar.get_events",
};
Key Description field_map Maps start, end, id, title, allDay and convertToUserTz to fieldnames. The gantt view also reads progress, color, is_milestone and depends_on. get_events_method Dotted path of a whitelisted method. Default frappe.desk.calendar.get_events, which takes doctype, start, end, field_map, filters, fields, order_by. update_event_method Dotted path of a whitelisted method that saves an event after the user drags or resizes it. Default frappe.desk.calendar.update_event, which takes args and field_map. get_css_class(event) Return danger, success, warning or default to color an event. fields Fields to fetch for each event. A set list replaces the default list (field_map start, end and title, and name), so include those fields too. options Extra FullCalendar options. gantt true, or an object of keys that override this object in the gantt view. order_by Sort order of the gantt view. apply_to_custom_calendar_views Also apply fields and get_css_class to Calendar View records.

docs.title: Tree view settings
docs.text:
A tree view needs a DocType with is_tree = 1. See DocTypes. Common keys of frappe.treeview_settings["<DocType>"]:

Key Description get_tree_nodes Method that returns child nodes. Default frappe.desk.treeview.get_children. add_tree_node Method that adds a node. Default frappe.desk.treeview.add_node. root_label Label of the root node. get_tree_root Set false to skip the root node lookup. title Page title. filters Filter fields shown above the tree. fields, ignore_fields Fields of the "Add Child" dialog. onload(treeview), post_render(treeview) Run after load and after render. onrender(node), on_node_render(node, deep), click(node) Node hooks. get_label(node) Return the label of a node. toolbar, extend_toolbar Node buttons. With extend_toolbar: true your buttons are added to the standard ones. menu_items Extra page menu items. disable_add_node Hide "Add Child".

docs.title: Kanban settings
docs.text: <doctype>_kanban.js fills frappe.kanban_v2.settings["<DocType>"]. It applies to Kanban boards that have use_kanban_v2 set. Keys include card_context_menu(card, page), bulk_actions(ids, page), callbacks (canMoveCard, onBeforeCardMove, onCardMove, onAfterCardMove, onCardClick), select_styles, options and boards (overrides for one board by name). An app that extends another app calls frappe.kanban_v2.extend_settings(doctype, patch) so the base settings stay.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A field that get_indicator or button.show reads is undefined unless it is a list column or in add_fields.
  • For submittable DocTypes, get_indicator is ignored for drafts and cancelled documents unless you set has_indicator_for_draft or has_indicator_for_cancelled.
  • A formatter on the first (subject) column is shown as plain text. HTML tags appear as text. Use formatters on other columns for HTML.
  • The filters key of frappe.views.calendar is not read by the calendar view in this version.
  • The settings code comes with the DocType meta, which the browser caches. After you change a settings file, reload the page. Outside developer mode, also run bench --site <site> clear-cache.

docs.title: Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock
docs.text:
The desk has three levels of navigation. The dock is the icon rail at the left edge. Each dock entry opens a sidebar, the list of links next to it. A sidebar link can open a workspace, a page with shortcuts, cards, charts and number cards. An app ships all three as JSON records in its folders. bench migrate imports them. The apps screen lists installed apps, and an app joins it with the add_to_apps_screen hook. For the user view, see Desk.

Record File in the app Exported when Workspace <app>/<module>/workspace/<name>/<name>.json Saved with standard = 1 and a module, in developer mode. Sidebar <app>/<module>/sidebar/<name>/<name>.json, or <app>/sidebar/<name>/<name>.json for a sidebar with no module Saved with standard = 1, in developer mode. Dock <app>/dock/<app>/<app>.json Saved with standard = 1, in developer mode.

<name> is the scrubbed record name. During migrate, Frappe also deletes a standard Workspace, Sidebar or Dock record whose file is gone from the app.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
A workspace is a Workspace record. Its content field holds the page layout as a JSON list of blocks. The child tables hold the widgets that the blocks point to.

Field Description label, title Name of the workspace. The route is /desk/<slug of the title>, for example /desk/automation. module The module the workspace belongs to. Decides where it is exported and which sidebar lists it. icon, indicator_color Icon and color. public Visible to all users with access. A private workspace belongs to for_user. standard Shipped by an app. content JSON list of blocks: headers, paragraphs and widgets (shortcut, card, chart, number_card, quick_list, custom_block). shortcuts, links, charts, number_cards, quick_lists, custom_blocks Widget definitions. A block finds its row by label. roles Roles that can see the workspace. Empty means all. parent_page, sequence_id, is_hidden Nesting, order and visibility. type, link_type, link_to, external_link Workspace (default), or Link / URL for an entry that opens a DocType, Page, Report or URL.

To make or change a standard workspace:

  1. Turn on developer mode for the site.
  2. Open the workspace in the desk and edit it.
  3. Make sure standard is set and module points to a module of your app.
  4. Save. Frappe writes the JSON file into the module folder.
  5. Commit the file in your app.

Outside developer mode, a user cannot change the content of a standard workspace directly. The desk saves the change as a Custom Workspace record. That record holds the difference, so it survives app updates.

docs.title: Sidebars
docs.text:
A sidebar belongs to a module. There are two sources:

  1. A Sidebar record that an app ships as JSON.
  2. A computed sidebar, made from what the module holds: its workspaces, DocTypes, reports, dashboards and pages. Frappe uses it when the app ships no Sidebar for the module.

The desk then hides items the user cannot open, and applies Custom Sidebar records. These hold site and user changes on top of the base sidebar.

Sidebar fields:

Field Description title Name and record name (autoname: field:title). module Module that owns the sidebar. app App the sidebar is placed in. Derived from the module when set. header_icon Icon in the sidebar header. standard Shipped by an app. Needs developer mode to set. items Table of Sidebar Item rows.

Sidebar Item fields:

Field Description type Link, Section Break or Spacer. label, icon Text and icon. link_type DocType, Page, Report, Workspace, Dashboard or URL. link_to The record the link opens. url Target of a URL link. route Path inside the page, for example payroll opens /desk/<page>/payroll. filters, route_options JSON filters or route options for the opened view. child, indent, collapsible, keep_closed Nesting under a Section Break. hidden Hide the item. open_in_new_tab Default 1.

A shipped sidebar file looks like this (shortened):

{
 "doctype": "Sidebar",
 "name": "Sample Module",
 "title": "Sample Module",
 "module": "Sample Module",
 "app": "sample_app",
 "header_icon": "package",
 "standard": 1,
 "items": [
  {"type": "Link", "label": "Sample Order", "link_type": "DocType", "link_to": "Sample Order", "icon": "list"},
  {"type": "Link", "label": "Sample Item", "link_type": "DocType", "link_to": "Sample Item", "icon": "box"}
 ]
}

To ship a sidebar:

  1. Turn on developer mode for the site.
  2. Open the module and select Edit Sidebar in the sidebar header.
  3. Arrange the items.
  4. Save to the layer named after your app (not "Just for me" or "For everyone"). Frappe saves the Sidebar record as standard and writes its JSON file.
  5. Commit the file in your app.

docs.title: Old sidebar fixtures
docs.text:
In develop, the flat <app>/workspace_sidebar/*.json files are no longer imported. Convert them to per-module Sidebar files:

bench --site frappe.localhost convert-sidebar-fixtures --app sample_app --dry-run
bench --site frappe.localhost convert-sidebar-fixtures --app sample_app

The command does not overwrite existing files. Delete the old folder after you check the result. Until you convert, the modules of the app use computed sidebars. The Workspace Sidebar DocType stays only as an archive that this conversion reads.

docs.title: Dock
docs.text:
The dock is a Dock record. An app ships one at <app>/dock/<app>/<app>.json. Its rows are the entries of the app on the rail. A module that the record does not name is not on the rail.

{
 "doctype": "Dock",
 "name": "sample_app",
 "app": "sample_app",
 "standard": 1,
 "items": [
  {"link_type": "Sidebar", "link_to": "Sample Module", "icon": "package", "title": "Sample Module", "added": 0, "hidden": 0},
  {"link_type": "Workspace", "link_to": "Sample Reports", "icon": "chart", "title": "Reports", "added": 0, "hidden": 0},
  {"link_type": "URL", "url": "https://example.com/help", "icon": "help", "title": "Help", "added": 0, "hidden": 1}
 ]
}

Dock fields:

Field Description app The app whose dock this is. Required. standard The app's own dock, exported to the app. The record name is then the app name. user Empty for the app or site layer. A user name for that user's own arrangement. mount_on For a companion app: the host app whose rail gets this app's entries. Only on the standard record. items Table of Dock Item rows. Row order is the rail order.

Dock Item fields:

Field Description link_type Sidebar (select that sidebar and open its landing route), Workspace (open that workspace and derive the sidebar from its module) or URL (leave the desk). link_to The sidebar or workspace name. url Target of a URL row. icon, title How the rail shows the entry. hidden Off by default. A site or a user can show it again in Manage Dock. added Set when the row adds a new entry, not a change to an entry from a lower layer.

The site arrangement and each user's arrangement are stored as more Dock records on top of the app's dock. They can reorder, hide, relabel and add entries. They cannot change what an app row points to.

To author the dock:

  1. Turn on developer mode for the site.
  2. Open the user menu and select Manage Dock.
  3. Arrange the entries.
  4. Select Export to app. Frappe writes <app>/dock/<app>/<app>.json. Each later save updates the file.
  5. Commit the file in your app.

If you delete the file and run bench migrate, the app has no dock. Its sidebar then shows an app switcher in the header.

docs.title: Apps screen: add_to_apps_screen
docs.text:
The add_to_apps_screen hook puts an app on the apps screen. It is a list with one dict per app.

# sample_app/hooks.py
add_to_apps_screen = [
    {
        "name": "sample_app",
        "logo": "/assets/sample_app/images/logo.svg",
        "title": "Sample App",
        "route": "/desk/sample-module",
        "has_permission": "sample_app.api.has_app_permission",
    }
]
Key Description name App name. title Label on the apps screen. logo Logo URL. Falls back to the app_logo_url hook. route Where the icon goes. Falls back to the app_home hook. has_permission Dotted path of a function that returns True if the user may see the app. sequence_id Sort order. Lower shows first. Frappe uses 1000 to stay last. desk_route For an app whose UI is not the desk: a desk route shown as a second link, "Open in Desk". module_icons List of {title, logo, route} shown behind the app icon.

An app with mount_on in its dock does not get its own slot on the apps screen.

docs.title: Desktop icons
docs.text: The Desktop Icon grid is being retired. Its rows are created, and <app>/desktop_icon/*.json fixtures are imported, only when Desktop Settings > desktop_page is Desktop Icons. The default is Apps. Use add_to_apps_screen and a Dock record in new apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A standard record with no file in the app is deleted on the next bench migrate. Commit the exported files.
  • Export works only in developer mode. On other sites, desk changes go to Custom Workspace, Custom Sidebar or site Dock records, not to files.
  • A Dock row with link_type = Sidebar needs a matching Sidebar record or Module Def.
  • The get_desktop_icons hook listed in old documentation is not read in develop.

docs.title: Fields and Controls
docs.text:
How each field type works in the desk, its properties, its stored value, and the JavaScript control API.

Page What it covers Field Properties How DocField properties behave on the desk and on the server - names, defaults, depends_on rules, fetch_from, constraints, permissions, list and print settings. Text Fields How Data, Small Text, Text, Long Text, Text Editor, Markdown Editor, HTML Editor, Code, JSON, Password and Read Only fields store values, behave in the desk and validate on save. Number Fields How Int, Float, Currency, Percent, Check, Rating and Duration fields store values, format numbers and currencies, and validate on save. Date and Time Fields How Date, Datetime and Time fields store values, use the System Settings formats, convert between user and system time zones, and work with frappe.datetime and frappe.utils. Link and Select Fields How Link, Dynamic Link, Select and Autocomplete fields store values, search and filter in the desk, and validate on save. Table Fields How Table and Table MultiSelect fields store child rows, how the desk grid works, and the Python, JavaScript and REST APIs for rows. Media and Special Fields How Attach, Attach Image, Image, Signature, Barcode, Geolocation, Color, Icon and Phone fields store values, behave in the desk and validate on save. Layout and Display Fields How the desk builds a form from Section Break, Column Break, Tab Break and Fold fields, and how Heading, HTML, Button, Attachment Gallery and Vue Component fields work. Controls Use the desk control JavaScript API - control classes, make_control, control methods, FieldGroup and Dialog fields, dialog-only controls, and custom controls from an app.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: A control is the JavaScript object that renders one field in the desk. Forms, grids, dialogs, field groups, filters and web forms all build their fields as controls. Use this page when you build a dialog or a desk page, read or change a field from a form script, or add a control from an app. For the frm object and form events, refer to Form Scripts. For frappe.ui.Dialog options, refer to Client API.

docs.title: Class hierarchy
docs.text:
Each fieldtype has a class frappe.ui.form.Control<Fieldtype>, with the spaces removed. The classes are in frappe/public/js/frappe/form/controls/. control.js imports all of them.

Class Extends Adds Control - Wrapper, display status (get_status), set_value, get_value, change event. Used directly by layout-only controls. ControlInput Control Label, description, input area, read-only display area, mandatory and invalid styles. ControlData ControlInput The <input>, change binding, maxlength, Email/Phone/Name/URL/IBAN/Barcode options. ControlInt > ControlFloat > ControlCurrency, ControlPercent, ControlRating ControlData Number parsing and formatting. ControlDate > ControlDatetime, ControlTime ControlData Date picker. ControlLink > ControlDynamicLink, ControlTableMultiSelect ControlData Search dropdown, link validation, fetch_from. ControlText > ControlCode > ControlTextEditor, ControlMarkdownEditor ControlData Text areas and editors. ControlAutocomplete > ControlMultiSelect, ControlMultiSelectPills ControlData Dropdown from a list of options. ControlCheck > ControlSwitch ControlData Checkbox, value 0 or 1. ControlTable, ControlHTML, ControlImage, ControlMultiCheck, ControlVueComponent Control No standard input.

Aliases: ControlReadOnly is ControlData, ControlLongText is ControlText, ControlLongInt is ControlInt.

docs.title: Combobox variants
docs.text: System Settings has the check box Enable Combobox Fields (Beta) (enable_combobox_link_field, default off). When it is on, make_control adds the suffix Combobox for these fieldtypes: Link, Dynamic Link, Autocomplete, Table MultiSelect, MultiSelectPills and MultiSelect. For example, a Link field then uses ControlLinkCombobox. Check the setting with frappe.ui.form.is_combobox_link_enabled(). The combobox controls accept the same get_query and set_query hooks. They also accept map_options(rows, { query, start }) on the control or on the df to change, remove or group the rows before they show.

docs.title: Make a control
docs.text:
frappe.ui.form.make_control(opts) finds the class from opts.df.fieldtype and returns a new instance. It returns undefined and logs Invalid Control Name if no class exists.

const control = frappe.ui.form.make_control({
    df: {
        fieldtype: "Link",
        fieldname: "item",
        label: __("Item"),
        options: "Sample Item",
        change() {
            console.log(control.get_value());
        },
    },
    parent: page.main.find(".sample-filters"),
    render_input: true,
});
control.set_value("Keyboard");
Option Description df The field definition. Same keys as a DocField, plus the keys in Keys only for dialogs and field groups. parent Element or jQuery object. The control appends its wrapper to it. render_input If true, the constructor calls refresh() and builds the input. If false, the input is built on the first refresh(). only_input Render only the input, without label and description. frm, doctype, docname, doc Bind the control to a document. A form sets them. Without them the control is standalone.

A standalone control (no doctype and no docname) has the status Write unless df.hidden or df.read_only is set. set_value then updates the input and doc[fieldname] if a doc is given. In a form, set_value calls frappe.model.set_value and runs the form events.

docs.title: Control methods and properties
docs.text:
Name Description get_value() The parsed value of the input when the status is Write. Otherwise the last set value. For example ControlInt returns a number. set_value(value, force) Validate, store and show the value, then run df.change or df.onchange. Returns a promise. Skips the change if the value is the same, unless force is true. set_input(value) Show a value in the input and the display area only. It does not change the document and does not run change events. get_input_value() The raw value of the input, before parse. parse(value), validate(value), format_for_input(value) Hooks that subclasses override. validate can return a promise, for example the link validation. refresh() Compute the status again and render the label, description, value and read-only state. refresh_input() Render the input part only. refresh() calls it. get_status(explain) "Write", "Read" or "None". Pass true to log the reason to the console. toggle(show) Set df.hidden and refresh. set_label(label) Change the label. set_description(text) Change the description under the field. set_new_description(html), set_empty_description() Show other text in the help box, or clear it, without changing df.description. toggle_label(show), toggle_description(show) Show or hide the label or the description. set_focus() Focus the input. df The field definition that the control uses. $wrapper / wrapper The outer .frappe-control element. It has data-fieldname and data-fieldtype. $input, input The input element, after the input is built. label_area, input_area, disp_area The label, the input container and the read-only display area. value, last_value The current and the previous value. frm, doc, layout The form, the document and the layout that own the control. grid, grid_row Set when the control is in a child table.

get_status returns "None" for hidden fields. It returns "Read" for read-only fields, for virtual fields, for Read Only fields, and for fields in a read-only grid. In a document, it also checks the permission level. In a form, a read-only field with no value gets "None" if System Settings has Hide Empty Read-Only Fields on (default on). This does not apply to HTML, Image, Button, Attachment Gallery, Geolocation and Vue Component.

docs.title: Controls in a form
docs.text:
frm.fields_dict[fieldname] and frm.get_field(fieldname) return the same control. The df of a form control is the copy of the DocField for this document, from frappe.meta.get_docfield(doctype, fieldname, docname). So frm.set_df_property, frm.toggle_display, frm.toggle_reqd and frm.toggle_enable change one document only. The DocType meta does not change. They set hidden, reqd and read_only on that copy and refresh the field. The full method list is in Form Scripts.

frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        const field = frm.get_field("customer_name");
        field.set_description(__("Name as printed on the invoice"));
        frm.toggle_enable("order_date", frm.is_new());
    },
});

Tip

To change a value in a form, use frm.set_value. control.set_input changes only what the user sees, and the value is not saved.

docs.title: frappe.ui.FieldGroup
docs.text:
frappe.ui.FieldGroup renders a list of field definitions as a layout without a modal. frappe.ui.Dialog extends it. Use it to put fields in a desk page or in an HTML field.

const group = new frappe.ui.FieldGroup({
    fields: [
        { fieldtype: "Data", fieldname: "customer_name", label: __("Customer"), reqd: 1 },
        { fieldtype: "Date", fieldname: "order_date", label: __("Date"), default: "Today" },
        { fieldtype: "Check", fieldname: "urgent", label: __("Urgent") },
        { fieldtype: "Small Text", fieldname: "note", label: __("Note"), depends_on: (doc) => doc.urgent },
    ],
    body: page.main.find(".sample-form"),
});
group.make();
group.get_values(true); // {order_date: "2026-11-22", urgent: 0}
group.get_values(); // null, and a "Missing Values Required" message for Customer
Option Description fields List of field definitions. A field with a label and no fieldname gets the label in lower case with _ for spaces. body or parent Where to render. doc A document to bind to. If it is saved, defaults are not applied. no_submit_on_enter Do not run the primary action when the user presses Enter. no_focus Do not focus the first input.

Methods: make(), get_values(ignore_errors, check_invalid), get_value(fieldname), set_value(fieldname, value), set_values(object), get_field(fieldname), has_field(fieldname), get_input(fieldname), set_df_property(fieldname, prop, value), set_query(fieldname, fn), set_query(child_field, table_field, fn), add_fetch(link_field, source_field, target_field), clear(), refresh_dependency(). Property: fields_dict.

How get_values works:

  • It leaves out fields with an empty value.
  • If a mandatory field is empty, it shows Missing Values Required and returns null. With ignore_errors set, it returns the other values.
  • With check_invalid set, a field with df.invalid (for example a wrong email) shows Invalid Values and returns null.
  • If df.include_default is set and the value is empty, it uses df.default.

Defaults: Today (Date) and now (Datetime, Time) give the current date or time. __user or user gives the session user, and user_fullname gives the full name.

In a FieldGroup or Dialog, depends_on, mandatory_depends_on and read_only_depends_on are evaluated against the current values. depends_on also accepts a function (values) => boolean or a boolean, as well as the eval: string. Refer to Field Properties for the expression syntax.

docs.title: Keys only for dialogs and field groups
docs.text:
A DocField does not store these keys. Set them in JavaScript on the df you pass to a Dialog, a FieldGroup or make_control. Some of them also work on a form df from a form script.

Key Fieldtypes Description change, onchange All with an input Function called after the value is set. this is the control. on_make All with an input on_make(control), called once after the input is built. get_status All get_status(control) returns "Write", "Read" or "None" and replaces the standard check. initial_value All with an input Value set when the control is built. include_default All get_values returns default if the value is empty. click Button Function called on click. primary, btn_size, icon, title Button Primary style, size suffix (btn-<size>, default xs), icon name, and tooltip. get_query Link, Autocomplete Function that returns the query or filters for the dropdown. Same as set_query. Refer to Link and Select Fields. filters Link Object of filters added to every search. only_select Link Hide Create a new ... and Advanced Search in the dropdown. filter_description Link Text shown at the end of the dropdown in place of the generated filter description. get_route_options_for_new_doc Link fn(control) returns the values for a new document made from the dropdown. ignore_link_validation Link, Table MultiSelect Do not check that the value exists. get_options Dynamic Link fn(control) returns the DocType to search. In a dialog, the default reads the field named in options. get_data MultiCheck, MultiSelect, MultiSelectPills, MultiSelectList, Table Function that returns the options (or the rows of a Table). It can return a promise. MultiSelectPills and MultiSelectList pass the typed text. max_items Autocomplete Number of items in the dropdown. Default 99. ignore_validation Autocomplete, MultiSelect Accept a value that is not in the options. min_date, max_date, disabled_dates Date, DateRange Limits of the date picker. disabled_dates is a list of YYYY-MM-DD strings (Date only). hide_timezone Datetime Do not add the time zone to the description. min_lines, max_lines, wrap Code Editor height and line wrap. enable_mentions, get_toolbar_options, theme Text Editor @ mentions, a custom Quill toolbar, the Quill theme (default snow). fields, data, in_place_edit, cannot_add_rows, cannot_delete_rows, on_setup, on_add_row Table Child fields, rows, edit in the grid without a row form, block add or delete, and grid hooks. with_copy_button Data Show a button that copies the value. input_css, input_class Data and subclasses CSS and classes for the input. is_filter Data Skip the Email, Phone, Name and URL checks. Filters use it. columns, select_all, on_change MultiCheck Grid layout (3, "15rem" or "15rem 5"), Select All buttons, change callback.

Warning

MultiCheck does not call change or onchange. It calls df.on_change() when a box changes.

docs.title: Dialog-only controls
docs.text:
These controls have no DocField fieldtype. Use them in a Dialog, a FieldGroup or with make_control.

Fieldtype Value from get_value Options MultiCheck Array of checked values, for example ["a"]. options is a list of {label, value, checked}, or a JSON string. Options are sorted by label unless sort_options is false. MultiSelect Comma-separated string, for example "p, q". options list, or get_data(). MultiSelectPills Array of values. get_data(txt) returns [{value, label}]. MultiSelectList Array of selected values. options or get_data(txt) returns strings or {value, label, description}. DateRange ["YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DD"]. min_date, max_date. Switch 1 or 0. A Check shown as a toggle switch. Comment HTML. A Text Editor with the comment box frame. The form timeline uses it. 
const d = new frappe.ui.Dialog({
    title: __("Export Orders"),
    fields: [
        {
            fieldtype: "MultiCheck",
            fieldname: "statuses",
            label: __("Status"),
            columns: 2,
            options: [
                { label: __("Draft"), value: "Draft", checked: 1 },
                { label: __("Submitted"), value: "Submitted" },
            ],
        },
        { fieldtype: "DateRange", fieldname: "period", label: __("Period") },
        { fieldtype: "Switch", fieldname: "include_items", label: __("Include Items"), default: 1 },
    ],
    primary_action(values) {
        // {statuses: ["Draft"], period: ["2026-01-01", "2026-01-31"], include_items: 1}
        d.hide();
    },
});
d.show();

A Table field in a dialog takes its columns from fields and its rows from data. get_values() returns the rows as a list of objects with idx and name. For grid details, refer to Table Fields.

docs.title: Add a custom control from an app
docs.text:
make_control looks up the class at call time. So an app can add a new class to frappe.ui.form from a desk bundle.

  1. Make the bundle sample_app/public/js/sample_app.bundle.js.
  2. Add it to app_include_js in hooks.py.
  3. Define the class in the bundle.
# sample_app/hooks.py
app_include_js = "sample_app.bundle.js"

// sample_app/public/js/sample_app.bundle.js
frappe.ui.form.ControlSampleSlider = class ControlSampleSlider extends frappe.ui.form.ControlData {
    static input_type = "range";
    parse(value) {
        return cint(value);
    }
};

new frappe.ui.Dialog({
    title: __("Priority"),
    fields: [{ fieldtype: "Sample Slider", fieldname: "level", label: __("Level"), default: 30 }],
}).show();

The fieldtype Sample Slider maps to ControlSampleSlider. ControlData reads the static properties html_element (default input), input_type (default text) and input_mode. Set static trigger_change_on_input_event = false to run the change event only on change, not while the user types.

Note

A DocField fieldtype must be one of the standard fieldtypes, so a new control works only in dialogs, field groups and pages. To change a standard fieldtype in forms, assign a subclass to its name, for example frappe.ui.form.ControlRating = class extends frappe.ui.form.ControlRating {}. Classes that already extend it keep the old parent.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• get_value() returns undefined when the field is hidden or read-only and has no value. Read frm.doc[fieldname] in a form.
  • set_value does nothing if the new value equals the current value. Pass force = true to run the change event again.
  • A Data input runs its change event 500 ms after the user stops typing, not on each key.
  • In a dialog, the mandatory style shows only after the user clicks the primary action.
  • frappe.ui.form.make_control returns undefined for an unknown fieldtype. Check the result.

docs.title: Date and Time Fields
docs.text: Use Date for a calendar day, Datetime for a point in time, and Time for a time of day. The database always holds the system format (yyyy-mm-dd, HH:mm:ss) in the system time zone. The desk shows and reads values in the formats from System Settings. Only Datetime converts between the user and system time zones. For column types, see Field Types.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Fieldtype Python value after load REST JSON Desk control Date datetime.date "2026-11-22" Date picker with a "Today" button Datetime datetime.datetime "2026-11-22 10:30:00" Date picker with time sliders and a "Now" button Time datetime.timedelta on MariaDB "10:30:00" Time sliders with a "Now" button

After insert() or save(), the object in memory keeps the value you set, for example a string. frappe.get_doc() and frappe.db.get_value() return the types above. On Postgres, Time is a datetime.time. Use frappe.utils.get_time() to get a datetime.time on any database.

docs.title: Formats and time zones
docs.text:
Setting Where Effect date_format System Settings yyyy-mm-dd, dd-mm-yyyy, dd/mm/yyyy, dd.mm.yyyy, mm/dd/yyyy or mm-dd-yyyy. Used to show and to read dates. time_format System Settings HH:mm:ss (default) or HH:mm. With HH:mm, the picker has no seconds slider. first_day_of_the_week System Settings First column of the date picker. Default Sunday. time_zone System Settings The system time zone. All stored datetimes are in this zone. time_zone User The user time zone. If empty, the system time zone applies.

The desk gets both zones in frappe.boot.time_zone (system and user).

docs.title: What converts
docs.text:
Fieldtype Shown in Stored in Date User format yyyy-mm-dd. No time zone conversion. Datetime User format, user time zone yyyy-mm-dd HH:mm:ss, system time zone Time User time format HH:mm:ss. No time zone conversion.

The Datetime control converts to the system time zone in parse() and back in format_for_input(). For example, with system zone Asia/Kolkata and user zone America/New_York, the stored value 2026-11-22 10:30:00 shows as 22-11-2026 00:00:00.

The server never converts time zones. Python code, REST calls and Data Import must send Datetime values in the system time zone.

docs.title: Desk behavior
docs.text:
• Picker: the controls use AirDatepicker. Arrow keys do not move in the calendar. The input shows the user format.
  • Shortcut: press t in the input to set today (Date) or now (Datetime, Time).
  • Relative input: type a value in the user format, then offsets. Date accepts d, M and y. Time accepts h, m and s. Datetime accepts all six. Use M for months and m for minutes.
Input (format dd-mm-yyyy) Fieldtype Value 22-11-2026 +5d Date 2026-11-27 22-11-2026 +1M -1d Date 2026-12-21 22-11-26 Date 2026-11-22 22-11-2026 10:30:00 +90m Datetime 2026-11-22 12:00:00 10:30:00 -15m Time 10:15:00
  • Validation: if the value is not a valid date, the desk shows "Date {0} must be in format: {1}" and clears the field. Time shows "Time {0} must be in format: {1}".
  • Description: Datetime adds the user time zone name below the field. Set hide_timezone: 1 on the df to hide it. Time adds the system time zone name only when the user zone differs.
  • List view and grid: frappe.format() shows the user format. Datetime is converted to the user time zone.

docs.title: Datepicker options
docs.text:
For Date and Datetime, set options to a JSON object. The control merges it into the AirDatepicker options. Invalid JSON logs a console warning and is ignored.

{"fieldname": "delivery_date", "fieldtype": "Date", "label": "Delivery Date", "options": "{\"minDate\": \"2026-11-10\", \"weekends\": [5, 6]}"}

In a dialog or field group, you can also set these df keys:

Key Type Effect min_date Date First date the user can pick max_date Date Last date the user can pick disabled_dates list of "yyyy-mm-dd" strings Dates the user cannot pick hide_timezone 0 or 1 Hide the time zone in the Datetime description 
const d = new frappe.ui.Dialog({
    title: __("Pick a date"),
    fields: [
        {
            fieldname: "visit_date",
            fieldtype: "Date",
            label: __("Visit Date"),
            min_date: new Date(),
            disabled_dates: ["2026-12-25"],
        },
    ],
    primary_action(values) {
        d.hide();
    },
});
d.show();

docs.title: Defaults
docs.text:
default Fieldtype New document value Today Date Current date. Python uses the system time zone. The desk uses the user time zone. now (any case) Datetime Current datetime in the system time zone now (any case) Time Current time. Python uses the system time zone. The desk uses the user time zone.

Python sets them in frappe/model/create_new.py (frappe.new_doc(), and insert() for fields that are empty). The desk sets them in frappe.model.get_default_value(). See Field Properties for other defaults.

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
• get_valid_dict() stores an empty string "" as NULL for all three fieldtypes.
  • Frappe does not parse or check the value on save. The database does. On MariaDB, 22-11-2026 in a Date fails with "Incorrect date value". 2026-11-22T10:30:00 in a Datetime is accepted.
  • A Date value with a time part, such as 2026-11-22 10:00:00, is stored as 2026-11-22.
  • Datetime and Time columns keep microseconds.

docs.title: Python helpers
docs.text:
All functions are in frappe.utils. Current values use the system time zone.

Function Example Result getdate(value=None, parse_day_first=False) getdate("22-11-2026", parse_day_first=True) datetime.date(2026, 11, 22). No argument gives today. get_datetime(value=None) get_datetime("2026-11-22") datetime.datetime(2026, 11, 22, 0, 0). No argument gives now. get_time(value) get_time("10:30") datetime.time(10, 30) get_timedelta(value=None) get_timedelta("10:30:00") datetime.timedelta(seconds=37800) nowdate(), today() "2026-11-22" nowtime() "16:30:23.053810", with microseconds now() "2026-11-22 16:30:23.053818" now_datetime() datetime.datetime without tzinfo add_to_date(date, days=10) add_to_date("2026-11-22", days=10) "2026-12-02". A string in gives a string out. date_diff(end, start) date_diff("2026-12-01", "2026-11-22") 9 format_date(value, format_string=None) format_date("2026-11-22") "22-11-2026" with format dd-mm-yyyy format_datetime(value) format_datetime("2026-11-22 10:30:00") "22-11-2026 10:30:00". No time zone conversion. format_time(value) format_time("10:30:00") "10:30:00" get_system_timezone() "Asia/Kolkata" convert_utc_to_system_timezone(dt) Aware datetime in the system time zone

frappe.format_value(value, {"fieldtype": "Date"}) calls format_date(). Without a df, it guesses the fieldtype from the Python type. For the full list, see Utilities.

import frappe
from frappe import _
from frappe.utils import add_to_date, getdate

order = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00006")
if getdate(order.order_date) < getdate():
    frappe.throw(_("Order date is in the past"))

next_week = add_to_date(order.order_date, days=7)  # datetime.date in, datetime.date out

docs.title: JS helpers
docs.text:
All functions are in frappe.datetime. Strings use the system formats (YYYY-MM-DD, HH:mm:ss) unless the name has user.

Function Result now_date(), get_today(), nowdate() Today in the user time zone, "2026-11-22" now_time() Current time in the user time zone now_datetime() Current datetime in the user time zone system_datetime() Current datetime in the system time zone str_to_user(value, only_time, only_date) System string to user format. A full datetime is converted to the user time zone. user_to_str(value, only_time) User format to system string. No time zone conversion. str_to_obj(value), obj_to_str(date) String to Date object and back convert_to_user_tz(value, format) System time zone to user time zone. Pass false as format to get a moment object. convert_to_system_tz(value, format) User time zone to system time zone is_system_time_zone() true if both zones have the same UTC offset now add_days(date, n), add_months(date, n) "YYYY-MM-DD". add_months("2026-01-31", 1) is "2026-02-28". get_diff(a, b) Days from b to a month_start(), month_end(), week_start(), year_start() and others Dates of the current period validate(value) true if the value is a valid system date, datetime or time string global_date_format(value) "22nd November 2026" 
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    order_date(frm) {
        if (frm.doc.order_date < frappe.datetime.get_today()) {
            frappe.msgprint(__("Order date is in the past"));
        }
    },
});

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not compare a Datetime value with frappe.datetime.now_datetime(). That is user time. Use system_datetime().
  • Send dates as yyyy-mm-dd to the API. The server does not read the user format.
  • Date default Today can differ between the desk and Python near midnight, when the user and system zones differ.
  • A Time value is a timedelta on MariaDB. Use get_time() or format_time() before you show it.
  • In relative input, m is minutes and M is months.
