docs.title: Text Fields
docs.text: Use these fieldtypes for strings: short values, multi-line text, rich text, source code, JSON and secrets. Each one has a column in the parent table. In Python and in REST JSON, the value is a str or None. For column types and options, see Field Types. For properties that apply to all fields, see Field Properties.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Fieldtype Desk control Server on save Data One-line input Length check. Validates Email, Name, Phone, URL and IBAN options. Small Text Text area, 150px high HTML sanitized Text Text area, 300px high HTML sanitized Long Text Same control as Text HTML sanitized Text Editor Quill rich text editor HTML sanitized and linkified. Inline images saved as File. Markdown Editor Ace editor in Markdown mode, with preview HTML sanitized HTML Editor Ace editor in HTML mode, with preview HTML sanitized Code Ace editor Not sanitized. Python and PythonExpression are parsed. JSON Ace editor in JSON mode Not sanitized. A dict or list is stored as JSON text. Password Password input Value encrypted in __Auth. Column keeps * characters. Read Only Display only Length check. Non-string values become str.

docs.title: Sanitization on save
docs.text:
_sanitize_content() in frappe/model/document.py runs on every insert and save. It changes each string value that contains < or > with sanitize_html(). Script tags and event attributes such as onerror are removed. Safe tags such as <b> stay.

The server skips a field when one of these is true:

  • The field has ignore_xss_filter = 1.
  • The fieldtype is Code, JSON, Attach, Attach Image or Barcode.
  • The fieldtype is Data, Small Text or Text with options Email.
  • The document is cancelled, or submitted and the field has no allow_on_submit.
doc = frappe.get_doc({"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "A", "description": "Hi <script>x</script><b>B</b>"})
doc.insert()
doc.description  # 'Hi <b>B</b>'

docs.title: Data
docs.text:
• Stores: a string up to length characters, 140 by default.
  • Desk: a text input with maxlength set to length. A paste longer than the limit shows a "Data Clipped" message. The change event runs 500 ms after typing stops, except in a grid. If the DocType uses autoname: field:<fieldname>, a new document shows "already exists" under the field when the name is taken.
  • Properties: length, options, unique, translatable, in_global_search, alignment, placeholder, mask.
  • Server: _validate_length() throws frappe.CharacterLengthExceededError when the value is longer than length. A list value throws "cannot be a list". Single DocTypes skip the length check.
  • JS: frappe.ui.form.ControlData. The with_copy_button df key adds a copy button. Set it in a dialog or field group.

docs.title: Data options
docs.text:
Set options to one of these values. Any other value shows an "Invalid Data Field" message when you save the DocType, but the save continues.

Options Desk Server check on save Email Red border if an address is not valid. Accepts a list separated by commas. validate_email_address() on each address. Throws frappe.InvalidEmailAddressError. Name Red border if not a valid person name validate_name(): letters, digits, ' and -, words split by one space Phone Red border if not valid validate_phone_number(): 1 to 20 of digits, spaces and + _ - , . * # ( ) URL An "Open Link" button shows for a valid URL validate_url(). Needs a scheme, or a path that starts with /. Rejects unsafe schemes such as javascript:. Barcode A "Scan" button opens the camera scanner None IBAN Shows the value in groups of 4. Removes spaces before it sets the value. validate_iban() checks the checksum

The desk only marks the field red. The server rejects the value when you save. The Email check is skipped when the owner and the value are both standard users, such as Administrator.

{"fieldname": "contact_email", "fieldtype": "Data", "label": "Contact Email", "options": "Email"}

docs.title: Small Text, Text and Long Text
docs.text:
• Stores: a string. Long Text has a larger column on MariaDB.
  • Desk: a <textarea>. Small Text is 150px high. Text and Long Text are 300px high. The read-only view keeps line breaks and indentation. In list view and grid, new lines show as <br> if the value has no <p>, <div>, <br> or <table> tag.
  • Properties: max_height (for example 200px) limits the height. The DocType save throws if the unit is not px or em. translatable and in_global_search apply. search_index is not allowed.
  • JS: ControlSmallText and ControlText. ControlLongText is the same class as ControlText.

docs.title: Text Editor
docs.text:
• Stores: HTML. The control wraps the content in <div class="ql-editor read-mode">...</div>.
  • Desk: a Quill editor with a toolbar: headings, font size, bold, italic, underline, strike, colors, quote, code block, text direction, link, image, lists, alignment, indent and tables. In a grid row, the toolbar is hidden. Pasted or dropped images become inline data: URLs. The editor removes <script> and <style> before it sets the value.
  • Properties: max_height, placeholder (default "Type something..."), translatable, in_global_search, ignore_xss_filter.
  • Server: _extract_images_from_text_editor() saves each data: image as a private File attached to the document. It then puts the file URL in the src. Files are public if the DocType has make_attachments_public and not force_private_attachments. sanitize_html() also makes URLs in the text into links.
  • JS: frappe.ui.form.ControlTextEditor. Set enable_mentions: 1 on the df to show @ user mentions. Set get_toolbar_options on the df to a function that returns a Quill toolbar array.
  • Format: Python frappe.format_value() returns <div class='ql-snow'>...</div>.

docs.title: Markdown Editor and HTML Editor
docs.text:
• Stores: Markdown or HTML text.
  • Desk: an Ace editor with line wrap and a "Preview" button. The button changes to "Edit" while the preview shows. The HTML preview removes <script> and <style>. Drop an image on the editor to upload it to Home/Attachments. The control inserts ![](/files/sample.png) at the cursor. Other file types are rejected.
  • Server: sanitized like other text, unless the value contains <!-- markdown --> and no HTML tags.
  • Format: Python frappe.format_value() converts Markdown Editor to HTML with frappe.utils.markdown(). The desk list view shows the raw text.
  • JS: ControlMarkdownEditor and ControlHTMLEditor. Both extend ControlCode. ControlHTMLEditor always sets options to HTML.

Note

The HTML Editor control also inserts the Markdown syntax ![](/files/sample.png) for a dropped image, not an <img> tag.

docs.title: Code
docs.text:
• Stores: the source text, not sanitized.
  • Desk: an Ace editor, 300px high, with an "Expand" button that changes the height to 600px. In read mode, a copy button shows. The keyboard mode comes from the code_editor_type field of the user: vscode (default), vim or emacs. In list view and grid, the value shows escaped inside <pre>.
  • Properties: options sets the language. See Field Types for the list. An unknown value logs a console warning and uses plain text. max_height applies. search_index is not allowed.
  • Server: _validate_code_fields() parses Python as a script and PythonExpression as one expression. A syntax error throws "Invalid python code on line N".
  • JS: frappe.ui.form.ControlCode. The df keys max_lines, min_lines and wrap set Ace options. With max_lines, min_lines or max_height, the "Expand" button does not show. To add autocompletion, set autocompletions to a list of strings or {value, caption, meta, score} objects, or to a function that returns one:
// sample_app/sample_module/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.js
// "script" is a Code field. Server Script uses the same call for its own script field.
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Item", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frm.set_df_property("script", "autocompletions", ["frappe.db.get_value", "frappe.get_doc"]);
    },
});

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
• Stores: JSON text. You can set a dict or list in Python. get_valid_dict() stores it as compact JSON ({"a":1}).
  • Python: after a reload, frappe.get_doc and frappe.db.get_value return a str, not a dict. Use frappe.parse_json(doc.data). REST JSON also returns the string.
  • Desk: an Ace editor in JSON mode. The control does not check that the JSON is valid.
  • Server: not sanitized. Frappe does not parse the value. On MariaDB, the json column rejects text that is not valid JSON with a database error.
doc.settings = {"a": 1}
doc.save()
doc.reload()
doc.settings  # '{"a":1}'
frappe.parse_json(doc.settings).a  # 1

docs.title: Password
docs.text:
• Stores: the column holds one * for each character. The real value is encrypted with the site encryption key in the __Auth table.
  • Desk: an <input type="password"> with an eye button to show the text. While you type, a strength bar shows. It calls frappe.core.doctype.user.user.test_password_strength. Call disable_password_checks() on the control to turn the bar off.
  • Server: _save_passwords() runs on save. A new value is encrypted, then the field is set to * characters. A value of only * characters keeps the stored password. An empty value removes the stored password. Set doc.flags.ignore_save_passwords to True, or to a list of fieldnames, to skip this.
  • Read the value: in Python, call doc.get_password("fieldname"). Over HTTP, call frappe.client.get_password with doctype, name and fieldname. Only a System Manager can call it. frappe.get_doc, frappe.db.get_value and REST return the * characters.
# "api_secret" is a Password field of the DocType
doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", "ITEM-0001")
api_secret = doc.get_password("api_secret", raise_exception=False)

docs.title: Read Only
docs.text:
• Stores: a string up to length characters, 140 by default. Fill it with fetch_from or from code.
  • Desk: always shows as text, never as an input, also for a new document.
  • Server: get_valid_dict() converts a value that is not a str to str before it writes. After insert(), the object in memory keeps the value you set. A reload returns the string. _validate_length() applies. unique is allowed.
  • JS: frappe.ui.form.ControlReadOnly is the same class as ControlData.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The desk marks a bad Email or URL red but still sets the value. Only the server blocks it.
  • Text fields keep safe HTML. Do not render them with |safe in Jinja or innerHTML unless the field must hold HTML.
  • ignore_xss_filter turns off sanitization for every writer of the field, also REST clients.
  • A JSON value comes back as a string. Parse it before you use it.
  • Never log or return a Password value from get_password() in an API response.

docs.title: Low-Code and AI
docs.text:
Use server and client scripts, the automation engine, Flow agents and Studio apps.

Page What it covers Server Scripts and Client Scripts Write Python Server Scripts and JavaScript Client Scripts in the desk, enable server scripts, and know the restricted API that safe_exec allows. Automation Engine Extend Automation Flows from an app with the automation_events, automation_actions and automation_relationships hooks, emit() and skip_automations. Flow Development Ship Flow AI agents, tools and triggers from an app with frappe.flow.Agent, @tool, Trigger and the flow_agents, flow_tools and flow_triggers hooks. Studio Development Store Studio apps in an app repo, sync and export them, build them with bench, and pass boot data with the studio_app_boot hook.

docs.title: Automation Engine
docs.text: The automation engine runs Automation Flow documents. A flow has a trigger and a list of steps. Users build flows in the desk. An app extends the engine with its own events, actions and relationships, so users can build flows about the app's domain. Use this page when your app must add a trigger such as "Order was paid", or a step such as "Add Order Comment". For the flow builder, see Automation Flow.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Name What it is Automation Flow The flow. Fields include document_type, trigger_type, custom_event, filters, condition, relationships, actions, run_as, enabled. Automation Action One step (child table actions). Fields: step_key, step_type (Action, Wait, WaitForEvent, If), action_type, target, output_alias, params, step_condition. Trigger type Doc Created, Doc Updated, Field Value Changed, Doc Deleted, Doc Submitted, Doc Cancelled, Date Based, Scheduled, Custom Event, Manual. Event A named domain event that an app emits. It starts Custom Event flows and resumes WaitForEvent steps. Action A Python class that does one step. Relationship A named path from a document to related records. Steps can target the records.

The public API is in frappe.automation_engine:

from frappe.automation_engine import emit, is_enabled, skip_automations

docs.title: How a flow runs
docs.text:
1. Document.run_method calls frappe.automation_engine.dispatch.run_automations after document hooks, notifications, webhooks and server scripts.
  2. Dispatch matches enabled flows of the DocType. It writes a queue row for each match.
  3. After the commit, dispatch enqueues one deduplicated drain job on the default queue.
  4. The drainer runs each queued flow. Each step runs in a savepoint. A failed step rolls back its own changes.

Dispatch does not run during install, patch or migrate. It also stops at a depth of max_depth (default 3) when flows trigger other flows.

Scheduler entries in frappe/hooks.py:

Schedule Method Description every 5 minutes frappe.automation_engine.scheduler.process_cron Queues Scheduled flows that are due. every 5 minutes frappe.automation_engine.drainer.drain_due Runs queue rows that are due, such as resumed waits. hourly frappe.automation_engine.scheduler.process_date_based Queues Date Based flows. daily maintenance frappe.automation_engine.drainer.purge_queue Deletes old queue rows.

docs.title: Add events
docs.text:
Declare event names in the automation_events hook. An entry is a name, or a dict of names to a schema.

# sample_app/hooks.py
automation_events = [
    {
        "sample_app.order_paid": {
            "label": "Order was paid",
            "description": "A payment closed the order.",
            "subject": {"doctype": "Sample Order", "name_key": "order"},
            "correlation_options": [{"label": "This order", "value": "{{ doc.name }}"}],
        },
    }
]
Schema key Description label The label in the builder. Default: made from the name. description Help text in the builder. subject The record the event is about. Use doctype and name_key, or doctype_key, name_key and an optional doctypes list. The keys name keys of the payload. correlation_options Choices for the correlation key of a WaitForEvent step. Each item has label and value (a Jinja template).

With a subject, the engine runs the flow on the subject record, not on the document that the code passed. The builder offers the event as a trigger on the subject DocTypes.

docs.title: Emit an event
docs.text:
# sample_app/payments.py
from frappe.automation_engine import emit, is_enabled


def on_payment_submit(doc, method=None):
    if not is_enabled():
        return
    emit(
        "sample_app.order_paid",
        payload={"order": doc.order, "amount": doc.amount},
        correlation_key=doc.order,
    )

emit(event, doc=None, payload=None, correlation_key=None) -> dict

Argument Description event A registered event name. An unknown name raises ValidationError, unless allow_unregistered_events is set in Automation Settings. doc The document to match flows against, when the event has no subject. payload A dict. The engine adds event_name. Flows read it as {{ payload.<key> }}. Its JSON size must be under event_payload_limit (default 65536 bytes). correlation_key Resumes WaitForEvent steps that wait on this event with this rendered key.

emit returns {"queued": <flows queued>, "resumed": <waits resumed>}. It only writes queue rows. The flows run in the drain job after the commit. Keep payloads to identifiers, because the engine stores them in run logs and subscriptions.

docs.title: Add actions
docs.text:
Subclass AutomationAction and list the class in the automation_actions hook.

# sample_app/automation/actions.py
from typing import ClassVar

from frappe import _
from frappe.automation_engine.actions.base import AutomationAction, AutomationParamError, render_value


class AddOrderComment(AutomationAction):
    action_type = "SampleAddOrderComment"
    label = "Add Order Comment"
    description = "Add a comment to a Sample Order."
    applicable_doctypes: ClassVar[list] = ["Sample Order"]
    output_schema: ClassVar[dict] = {"comment": {"fieldtype": "Data"}}
    params_schema: ClassVar[list] = [
        {"fieldname": "text", "label": "Text", "fieldtype": "Small Text", "reqd": 1, "templatable": 1},
    ]

    def validate(self, params, doctype):
        if not params.get("text"):
            raise AutomationParamError(_("Text is required"), fieldname="text")

    def execute(self, doc, params, context):
        comment = doc.add_comment("Comment", render_value(params["text"], doc, context))
        return {"detail": _("Added comment {0}").format(comment.name), "comment": comment.name}

# sample_app/hooks.py
automation_actions = ["sample_app.automation.actions.AddOrderComment"]

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text: Name Type Default Description action_type str "" The unique key stored in the step. Two classes with one key raise an error. label str "" The label in the builder. description str "" Help text in the builder. applicable_doctypes list or None None The DocTypes the action works on. None means all. requires_document bool True Set False when the action can run without a target document. transactional bool True Set False when the action reaches outside the database, such as an HTTP call. The run is then never replayed from the start. supported_trigger_types list or None None The trigger types that can use the action. None means all. params_schema list [] The parameters, as DocField-like dicts: fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, reqd. Editor hints: options_source, control, link_filters, exclusive_with, templatable. output_schema dict or None None The output keys that later steps can read.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
Method Description validate(params, doctype) Check the params when the flow is saved and before each step runs. Raise AutomationParamError(message, fieldname=...). execute(doc, params, context) Do the step on the target doc. Return a short string, or a dict with detail and output keys. output_doctype(params) The DocType of the record the action makes, when known. Later steps can then target output_alias.
  • Use render_value(value, doc, context) for a param that can hold Jinja. The template gets doc, target, trigger, payload and context.
  • Before execute, the engine checks write permission on the target for the run user.
  • Return {"destination_reference": {"doctype": ..., "name": ...}} to make the record available under the step's output_alias.
  • Raise StopAutomation(message, resume_after=60) to pause the run. It resumes at the next step after resume_after seconds.
  • A step output larger than step_output_limit (default 65536 bytes) is replaced with {"truncated": true}.

The built-in actions are SetFieldValue, IncrementFieldValue, CreateDocument, SendNotification, AssignToUser, CallWebhook and RunScript, in frappe/automation_engine/actions/core.py.

docs.title: Add relationships
docs.text:
The engine derives relationships from the schema: Link, child-table Link and Dynamic Link fields, in both directions. Add a provider only for paths that the schema does not know.

# sample_app/automation/relationships.py
import frappe
from frappe.automation_engine.relationships import AutomationRelationshipProvider


class SampleRelationshipProvider(AutomationRelationshipProvider):
    def get_definitions(self, source_doctype):
        if source_doctype != "Sample Order":
            return []
        return [
            {
                "name": "owner_todos",
                "label": "Open ToDos of the Order Owner",
                "cardinality": "many",
                "target_doctype": "ToDo",
            }
        ]

    def resolve(self, source_doc, relationship, params):
        names = frappe.get_all(
            "ToDo",
            filters={"allocated_to": source_doc.owner_user, "status": "Open"},
            pluck="name",
        )
        return [{"doctype": "ToDo", "name": name} for name in names]

# sample_app/hooks.py
automation_relationships = ["sample_app.automation.relationships.SampleRelationshipProvider"]
automation_relationship_ignore = ["Sample Log"]
Method Description get_definitions(source_doctype) Return a list of definitions for the DocType. Each needs name and cardinality (one or many). Add label and target_doctype or target_doctypes. resolve(source_doc, relationship, params) Return a list of {"doctype", "name"} references. query(source_doc, relationship, filters, limit) Optional. The default resolves all references, then filters them with frappe.get_list. Override it for large many relationships.
  • A hook entry can name a class or an instance.
  • App providers come before the schema provider. An app definition with the name of a derived one replaces it.
  • Set derived_from to the name of a derived relationship to rename or relabel it.
  • Every returned reference must exist, match the allowed target DocTypes, and be readable by the run user. Otherwise the step fails.
  • automation_relationship_ignore is a list of DocTypes that the schema provider leaves out.

docs.title: Stop automations
docs.text:
is_enabled() returns False when:

  • the code runs inside skip_automations(),
  • automation_disabled is set in site config, or
  • disable_automations is set in Automation Settings.

Use skip_automations() for bulk writes that must not start flows, such as data fixes and imports:

from frappe.automation_engine import skip_automations

with skip_automations():
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="name"):
        frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name).save()

The context manager sets frappe.flags.skip_automations and restores the old value after the block.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Automation Settings fields and defaults:

Field Default Description disable_automations 0 Stop all dispatch. max_depth 3 The depth limit of flows that trigger flows. failure_threshold 10 Consecutive failed runs before the engine disables the flow. stale_running_minutes 30 When a running queue row counts as stale. max_attempts 3 The retries of a queue row. drain_seconds 0 The time budget of one drain job. 0 means a part of the queue timeout. commit_every 50 Rows per commit in the drainer. queue_retention_days 7 Days to keep finished queue rows. step_output_limit 65536 The size limit of a step output in bytes. event_payload_limit 65536 The size limit of an event payload in bytes. allow_unregistered_events 0 Accept emit of names that no hook declares.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• emit and dispatch queue work only. The drain job runs after the commit. A rolled-back transaction runs nothing.
  • Name events with your app prefix, such as sample_app.order_paid. All apps share one event namespace.
  • action_type must be unique across all installed apps.
  • A non-transactional action cannot be undone by a rollback. Set transactional = False for it, so a retry does not repeat it.

docs.title: Flow Development
docs.text: Flow is the AI agent system of Frappe. An app can ship its own agents, tools and triggers in Python code. Flow writes them to the site as locked Flow Agent, Flow Tool and Flow Trigger documents after bench migrate and after app installs. Use this page when your app must give users an agent that knows your DocTypes, or must run an agent when a document changes. For the desk side of Flow (chat, models, approvals), see Flow.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Name What it is Flow Model A chat model and its credentials. An agent uses one Flow Model, by its title. Flow Agent Instructions, a model, tools, skills, knowledge bases and sub-agents. Flow Tool A function the model can call. Types: Script, Imported, Server. App tools are Imported. Flow Trigger Runs an agent on a document event or on a cron schedule, with a prompt template. Flow Session One conversation with an agent. Flow Run One turn of a session. Fields include status, input, output, error, usage. Flow server A bench-wide daemon that runs the model loop. It calls tools back on the site.

The public API is in frappe.flow:

from frappe.flow import Agent, Tool, ToolContext, Trigger, build_schema, is_enabled, tool
from frappe.flow.knowledge import Knowledge

Naming rules:

  • An app agent is named <app>/<name>, for example sample_app/Order Assistant.
  • An app tool is the Flow Tool <app>/<function name>. The model calls it <app>__<function name>, for example sample_app__open_orders.
  • An app trigger is named <app>/<title>.
  • Flow takes <app> from the module that constructs the Agent or Trigger. It uses the first part of the module's __name__.

docs.title: Write a tool
docs.text:
Decorate a module-level function with @tool. The function must take a keyword-only ctx: ToolContext argument. Without it, @tool raises TypeError at import.

# sample_app/ai/tools.py
from typing import Annotated, Literal

import frappe
from frappe.flow import ToolContext, tool


@tool
def open_orders(
    customer_name: Annotated[str, "Customer name, as on the order"],
    limit: int = 20,
    *,
    ctx: ToolContext,
) -> list[dict]:
    """List the open Sample Orders of one customer."""
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters={"customer_name": customer_name, "status": "Open"},
        fields=["name", "order_date", "total"],
        limit=limit,
    )


@tool(
    requires_confirmation=True,
    confirm_prompt=lambda args: f"Mark {args['name']} as {args['status']}",
)
def set_order_status(
    name: str,
    status: Literal["Open", "Completed", "Cancelled"],
    *,
    ctx: ToolContext,
) -> str:
    """Change the status of one Sample Order."""
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.status = status
    doc.save()
    return f"{name} is now {status}"

@tool makes the JSON schema of the arguments from the type hints (build_schema):

  • str, int, float, bool, list[...], dict, Literal[...], Enum and Pydantic models map to JSON schema types.
  • Annotated[str, "text"] adds a description to the argument.
  • An argument with a default, or typed X | None, is not required.
  • ctx, self and cls are left out of the schema.
  • The docstring is the tool description, unless you pass description.

The schema of set_order_status is:

{"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}, "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["Open", "Completed", "Cancelled"]}}, "additionalProperties": false, "required": ["name", "status"]}

When a tool is called, Pydantic validates the arguments against the type hints. A wrong value raises a validation error. The return value goes to the model as text. A str goes as is. Other values go as JSON.

docs.title: @tool options
docs.text: Name Type Default Description name str function name The tool name. Use it when two tools in one app have the same function name. description str docstring What the model reads about the tool. requires_confirmation bool or callable(args) -> bool False Pause for approval before the call. A callable decides per call. confirm_prompt callable(args) -> str None The text of the approval card. Without it, the card shows the arguments as JSON. background bool or callable(args) -> bool False Run the call as a job on the long queue. The timeout is flow_background_tool_timeout in site config, else 1500 seconds. needs_user bool False The approval card takes input from the user, so no reviewer can answer it for them. display_template str None A template of the call for the transcript. It can name only argument names. Other names raise ValueError.

docs.title: ToolContext
docs.text:
Flow passes ctx to every call. The model never sees it.

Field Type Description session_id str The Flow Session name. agent str The Flow Agent name that called the tool. user str The session owner. The call runs as this user. result_token str or None The token of a call whose result comes later. read_only bool True when the call runs unapproved in a read-only transaction. failure Exception or None A failed write that was undone, or a stopped call, in this call.

docs.title: Write an agent
docs.text:
Return a list of Agent objects from a function. Constructing an Agent does not touch the database.

# sample_app/ai/agents.py
from frappe.flow import Agent

from sample_app.ai.tools import open_orders, set_order_status


def get_agents() -> list[Agent]:
    return [
        Agent(
            name="Order Assistant",
            model="Default Model",
            description="Answers questions about Sample Orders.",
            instructions="You help the sales team with Sample Orders. Use the tools.",
            tools=[open_orders, set_order_status],
            max_iterations=20,
        )
    ]

docs.title: Agent arguments
docs.text:
All arguments are keyword-only.

Name Type Default Description name str required The agent name. The document is <app>/<name>. model str required The title of a Flow Model. Flow sets it only when it creates the document, or when the current model is gone. instructions str required The system instructions. description str "" A short description. tools list[Tool] None @tool functions. Flow writes each as an Imported Flow Tool. knowledge Knowledge or list[Knowledge] None Flow Knowledge Bases the agent can search. skills list[str] None Flow Skill names. A name without an app prefix is this app's skill if it ships one, else the site's skill of that name. sub_agents list[Agent] None Agents this agent can hand a task to. Flow syncs them first. max_iterations int 100 The iteration limit of one run. auto_approve bool False Sessions started with Agent.new_session() or Agent.run() skip approvals. public bool False Open the agent to guests through the guest API. Their chats run tools without approval.

Warning

Knowledge("<title>") gets or inserts a Flow Knowledge Base when you construct it. Construct it inside the hook function, not at module import.

docs.title: Skills an app ships
docs.text: Flow reads <app repo>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md of every installed app. It writes each file as a locked Flow Skill named <app>/<name>. For example, the frappe repo ships skills/studio-app-building/SKILL.md as frappe/studio-app-building. The built-in frappe/Flow assistant gets every app skill.

docs.title: Write a trigger
docs.text:
A trigger runs an agent on a document event or on a schedule. Pass doctype and doc_event, or pass cron. Do not pass both.

# sample_app/ai/agents.py
from frappe.flow import Trigger


def get_triggers() -> list[Trigger]:
    return [
        Trigger(
            title="Review New Order",
            agent="Order Assistant",
            doctype="Sample Order",
            doc_event="after_insert",
            condition="doc.total > 1000",
            prompt="Check Sample Order {{ doc.name }} for {{ doc.customer_name }} and add a comment.",
            run_as="user1@example.com",
        ),
        Trigger(
            title="Daily Open Orders",
            agent="Order Assistant",
            cron="0 9 * * *",
            prompt="Summarize the open Sample Orders as of {{ now }}.",
        ),
    ]

docs.title: Trigger arguments
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description title str required The trigger name. The document is <app>/<title>. agent str required An agent of this app by name, or another app's agent as <app>/<name>. prompt str required A Jinja template. It gets doc (the document, or None) and now. It renders in a sandbox without database access. doctype str None The DocType to watch. doc_event str None One of after_insert, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel, on_trash. cron str None A cron expression. The scheduler checks it every 5 minutes. condition str None One Python expression. It gets doc, utils and len. The trigger runs only when it is true. run_as str "Administrator" The email or ID of the user that runs the agent.

How a trigger runs:

  • A document event enqueues frappe.flow.triggers.fire after the commit. It skips events during install and migrate.
  • The trigger skips a document that run_as cannot read. Field-level read permissions apply to doc in the prompt.
  • Trigger sessions use the Auto-approve approval mode. Tools run without approval.
  • A synced trigger starts enabled. The desk can only switch it on or off.

Warning

A trigger runs as Administrator when you leave out run_as. Make a user with only the roles that the trigger needs, and set run_as to that user.

docs.title: Register them in hooks
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
flow_agents = ["sample_app.ai.agents.get_agents"]
flow_triggers = ["sample_app.ai.agents.get_triggers"]
flow_tools = ["sample_app.ai.tools.open_orders"]
Hook Shape Read by Description flow_agents list of dotted paths frappe.flow.lib.agent.sync_agents Each path names a function that returns a list of Agent. flow_tools list of dotted paths frappe.flow.lib.agent.sync_tools Each path names a @tool object. Flow writes it as a locked Flow Tool that any agent can use. flow_triggers list of dotted paths frappe.flow.lib.trigger.sync_triggers Each path names a function that returns a list of Trigger.

You do not need to list an agent's tools in flow_tools. Agent.sync() writes them. Use flow_tools for tools that site admins can add to their own agents.

Sync behavior:

  • Frappe runs the three sync functions in after_migrate and after_app_install. It also syncs triggers in after_app_uninstall.
  • Synced documents have is_system_generated set. The desk can enable or disable an agent and change its model. It cannot change anything else.
  • An entry that fails is skipped and logged in Error Log. The other entries still sync.
  • A trigger whose agent does not exist yet is not written. A later sync writes it.
  • Flow deletes system-generated triggers that no hook declares anymore. Their Flow Runs stay.
  • If a site already has a Flow Agent with the same name that code does not own, the sync of that agent fails with "Agent Conflict".

docs.title: Run an agent from code
docs.text:
Get the synced Flow Agent document and call run(). It starts a new session on the flow server and returns the Flow Run with status Running. It does not wait for the result.

# sample_app/ai/jobs.py
import frappe


def review_order(order: str):
    agent = frappe.get_doc("Flow Agent", "sample_app/Order Assistant")
    agent.run(
        f"Review Sample Order {order}.",
        reference_doctype="Sample Order",
        reference_name=order,
        on_complete="sample_app.ai.jobs.on_review_done",
    )


def on_review_done(run):
    if run.status == "Completed":
        frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", run.reference_name).add_comment("Comment", run.output)
  • on_complete is a dotted path. Flow calls it with the Flow Run once the run ends with Completed, Denied or Failed.
  • Flow calls on_complete in a request of the session owner, inside a savepoint. An exception rolls it back and goes to Error Log.
  • new_session() commits the database transaction, so the flow server can find the session. Do not call run() in the middle of a write that must stay atomic. Call it from a background job.
  • The Agent object also has new_session(title=None) and run(input, on_complete=None). They need the synced document.

frappe.flow.is_enabled() returns True when the site has an enabled chat model with a key or an address, or with an enabled provider. Use it to hide AI features when Flow cannot chat. It does not check the access of the user.

docs.title: How tool calls run
docs.text:
1. The flow server sends the call to frappe.flow.daemon.callback.callback on the site.
  2. The callback checks the X-Harness-Token header against flow_server_secret in site config.
  3. It sets the user to the session owner. The tool runs with the permissions of that user.
  4. If the tool raises an exception, the whole transaction rolls back. The model gets the error text, cut to 500 characters.

The model sees only the enabled tools of the agent. When server scripts are disabled, Flow leaves out Script tools and the built-in frappe/execute tool. A session keeps the tools that it started with. Changes to an agent apply to new sessions only.

docs.title: The flow server
docs.text:
The flow server is the flow program in the bench environment. One server serves all sites of the bench.

Command Description bench flow-server setup Give every site a flow_server_secret, start the server, and sync server tools. bench flow-server start Start the server if it does not answer. bench flow-server stop Stop the server. bench flow-server restart Restart the server. Use it to load new extensions. bench flow-server status Show if the server answers and which sites it serves. bench flow-server serve Run the server in the foreground, for supervisor.

Install and migrate also give the site its secret and start the server. A server that cannot start does not fail the install or the migrate.

Config key File Description flow_server_secret site_config.json The shared secret of the callbacks. Flow writes it. flow_server_manager common_site_config.json local (default) or supervisor. With supervisor, stop and restart refuse to run. Use supervisorctl. flow_server_url common_site_config.json The base URL for callbacks. Default: http://127.0.0.1:<webserver_port>. flow_redis_url common_site_config.json The Redis for session events. Default: redis_queue. flow_background_tool_timeout site_config.json The timeout of background tools in seconds. Default: 1500.

Paths on the bench: the socket is flow-server/flow.sock, the log is logs/flow-server.log, and sessions of a site are in <site>/private/flow/.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Construct Agent and Trigger objects in a module of your app. Flow takes the app name from the calling module. In a bench console, the name is wrong.
  • Export each tool as a module-level attribute of an installed app. The callback imports it by its dotted path. Otherwise the sync fails with "Invalid Tool".
  • Two tools of one app with the same function name fail with "Tool Conflict". Give one a name=.
  • model must be the title of an existing Flow Model. Otherwise the agent fails to sync and is logged.
  • The desk can change the model of a synced agent. Flow keeps that choice on later syncs.

docs.title: Server Scripts and Client Scripts
docs.text:
Server Script and Client Script are DocTypes that store code in the database. You write them in the desk, without an app. Use them for small, site-specific changes. Use app code (controllers, hooks, form scripts) for logic that must be versioned, reviewed, tested, or shipped to more than one site.

Server Script Client Script Language Restricted Python (RestrictedPython) JavaScript Runs On the server In the browser of the user Role to create Script Manager System Manager Must be enabled Yes, server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json No, but each script has enabled (default off)

docs.title: Enable server scripts
docs.text:
Server scripts are off by default. Frappe reads the key only from sites/common_site_config.json, not from site_config.json (is_safe_exec_enabled in frappe/utils/safe_exec.py). The setting applies to all sites of the bench.

bench set-config -g server_script_enabled 1

When the key is off, every Server Script raises ServerScriptNotEnabled with the message "Server Scripts are disabled". This also applies to other features that use safe_exec, such as Script Reports written in the desk.

docs.title: Server Script types
docs.text:
Set Script Type (script_type):

Type Extra fields Runs when Variables in scope DocType Event reference_doctype, doctype_event The document event fires doc API api_method, allow_guest, rate limit fields A request to /api/method/<api_method> frappe.form_dict Scheduler Event event_frequency, cron_format, queue The scheduler runs the job none Permission Query reference_doctype frappe.get_list builds the query user, active_child_tables, set conditions Workflow Task none A Workflow Action Master runs the task doc

docs.title: DocType Event
docs.text:
doctype_event maps to controller events:

doctype_event Controller event Before Insert before_insert Before Validate before_validate Before Save validate After Insert after_insert After Save on_update Before Rename / After Rename before_rename / after_rename Before Submit / After Submit before_submit / on_submit Before Cancel / After Cancel before_cancel / on_cancel Before Discard / After Discard before_discard / on_discard Before Delete / After Delete on_trash / after_delete Before Save (Submitted Document) / After Save (Submitted Document) before_update_after_submit / on_update_after_submit Before Print before_print

The payment events (On Payment Paid and others) are also available. Scripts run after the controller and doc_events handlers for the same event. They do not run during bench install-app or bench migrate.

# Server Script: DocType Event, Sample Order, Before Save
total = 0
for row in doc.items:
    row.amount = frappe.utils.flt(row.qty) * frappe.utils.flt(row.rate)
    total += row.amount
doc.total = total

if doc.total <= 0:
    frappe.throw(_("Total must be more than zero"))

frappe.db.commit, frappe.db.rollback and frappe.db.add_index are removed in DocType Event scripts.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
The script runs at /api/method/<api_method> and /api/v2/method/<api_method>. Set the response in frappe.response["message"]. If you set values on frappe.flags, Frappe returns the flags as the message instead.

# Server Script: API, api_method = sample_item_count
category = frappe.form_dict.get("category")
frappe.response["message"] = frappe.db.count("Sample Item", {"category": category})

curl -b jar "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/sample_item_count?category=Hardware"
  • With allow_guest off, a Guest gets PermissionError.
  • With allow_guest on, you must set enable_rate_limit. Frappe does not save the script otherwise.
  • rate_limit_count defaults to 5 and rate_limit_seconds to 86400 when they are empty.
  • The script name has priority: an API script with the same path as a Python method replaces it.

docs.title: Scheduler Event
docs.text: Saving the script creates or updates a Scheduled Job Type that points to it. event_frequency takes All, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly, the Long variants, or Cron with cron_format. Disabling the script stops the job.

docs.title: Permission Query
docs.text:
Set conditions to a SQL condition string. Frappe adds it to the WHERE clause of frappe.get_list for reference_doctype.

# Server Script: Permission Query, Sample Order
conditions = f"`tabSample Order`.owner_user = {frappe.db.escape(user)}"

docs.title: Variables (frappe.env)
docs.text: The Variables table (variables) stores keys and secret values for a script. Read them with frappe.env.<key>. Values are decrypted on access. Outside a Server Script, frappe.env raises an error. Keys must start with a letter and contain only letters, digits and underscores.

docs.title: The restricted environment
docs.text:
safe_exec compiles the script with RestrictedPython and runs it with the globals from get_safe_globals().

  • import is not allowed. Use the names below.
  • Attributes and keys that start with _ are not allowed.
  • print() writes to frappe.log, not to the console.
  • frappe.db.sql allows only SELECT and EXPLAIN without ANALYZE. It rejects INTO OUTFILE, DUMPFILE and queries on __Auth.
  • HTTP helpers block requests to private and local addresses.

docs.title: Allowed API
docs.text:
Top-level names:

frappe, json (loads, dumps), orjson, as_json, _, _dict, dict, log, args (the form dict), scrub, guess_mimetype, html2text, get_toc, get_next_link, get_visible_columns, run_script, FrappeClient, style, dev_server, and the builtins abs, all, any, bool, dict, enumerate, isinstance, issubclass, list, max, min, range, set, sorted, sum, tuple.

frappe.*:

Group Names Documents get_doc, new_doc, copy_doc, get_cached_doc, get_last_doc, get_mapped_doc, rename_doc, delete_doc, get_meta Lists get_list, get_all, qb Database (frappe.db.*) get_list, get_all, get_value, get_single_value, set_value, exists, count, escape, get_default, sql (read-only), commit, rollback, add_index, after_commit, before_commit, after_rollback, before_rollback Messages and errors msgprint, throw, log_error, errprint, log, and all exception classes of frappe.exceptions (for example frappe.ValidationError) Calls and jobs call (calls a whitelisted method or API script), enqueue (enqueues a whitelisted method or API script), is_job_queued HTTP make_get_request, make_post_request, make_put_request, make_patch_request, make_delete_request Email and print sendmail, get_print, attach_print, render_template Formatting format, format_value, format_date, bold, date_format, time_format, number_format, sanitize_html Session and request session (user, csrf_token), user, full_name, form_dict, request (path), response, flags, lang Users get_fullname, get_gravatar, get_identicon Other get_hooks, get_system_settings, get_url, website (abs_url, extract_title, get_boot_data, get_home_page, get_html_content_based_on_type), socketio_port, json_handler, env

frappe.utils contains a fixed list of helpers from frappe/utils/data.py (VALID_UTILS in frappe/utils/safe_exec.py). Examples: flt, cint, cstr, getdate, get_datetime, nowdate, now, today, add_days, add_months, date_diff, fmt_money, money_in_words, strip_html, escape_html, get_url_to_form, parse_json, generate_hash. Other functions of frappe.utils are not available.

In Server Scripts, frappe.get_doc, frappe.get_list, frappe.get_all and the other document functions are the normal functions. They behave as in app code: get_list checks permissions of the session user, get_all does not, and doc.save() checks write permission.

docs.title: Client Script
docs.text:
A Client Script adds JavaScript to the form or list of a DocType. Set:

Field Description dt The DocType. view Form (default) or List. enabled Default off. Turn it on, or the script does not load. module Optional. Scripts of disabled modules do not load. script The code. 
// Client Script: Sample Order, Form
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        if (frm.doc.docstatus === 0) {
            frm.add_custom_button(__("Recalculate"), () => frm.trigger("recalculate"));
        }
    },
});

Frappe appends all enabled scripts of the DocType, ordered by creation, to the form script or the list script (add_custom_script in frappe/desk/form/meta.py). For a List script, set frappe.listview_settings["<DocType>"]. See Form Scripts and List View Settings for the API.

A Client Script runs only in the desk. Validation in a Client Script does not protect the data. The REST API, Data Import and server code skip it. Put rules that must hold on the server.

docs.title: Ship scripts with an app
docs.text:
Server Scripts and Client Scripts can be fixtures:

# sample_app/hooks.py
fixtures = [
    {"dt": "Server Script", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
    {"dt": "Client Script", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]},
]

For code that you own, prefer controllers, doc_events and doctype_js in the app. They do not need server_script_enabled, and they run under your tests.

docs.title: Test with server scripts
docs.text:
Use the enable_safe_exec context manager from frappe.tests in tests. It sets server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json and restores the old value after the block.

from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase


class TestSampleScript(IntegrationTestCase):
    def test_api_script(self):
        with self.enable_safe_exec():
            ...

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• server_script_enabled in site_config.json has no effect. Use bench set-config -g.
  • Only one Permission Query script per DocType is used.
  • A Server Script with an error in a Before Save event blocks all saves of the DocType. Test on a copy of the site first.
  • Server Scripts are cached in server_script_map. Saving or deleting a script clears the cache.
  • Do not build SQL from user input. Use frappe.db.escape or frappe.qb.

docs.title: Studio Development
docs.text: Studio is the visual app builder of Frappe. A Studio app is a Studio App document with Studio Page documents and source files. An app developer can store a Studio app in an app repo, so it installs and builds with the app. This page shows the file layout, how sync and export work, how to build, and the hooks. For the editor itself, see Studio.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Name What it is Studio App The app. Fields: app_name, app_title, route, app_home, favicon, is_standard, frappe_app. Studio Page One page. Fields: page_title, route, tab_title, published, allow_guest, blocks, draft_blocks, resources, variables, script. Its name is page-<hash>. Studio Component A reusable block tree with a script. With studio_app set, its name is <studio_app>/<component_id>. Without it, the component is global. Studio App File A source file of a custom app, stored in the database.

There are two kinds of Studio app:

Detail Custom app (is_standard 0) Standard app (is_standard 1) Source Studio App File records and the script field of each page Files in <app repo>/studio/<studio_app>/ Languages .js, .json, .css .js, .json, .css, .ts, .vue Edit In Studio, on any site The files, or Studio in developer mode Build output sites/<site>/public/files/app_builds/<studio_app>/ <app>/public/app_builds/<studio_app>/ Served from /files/app_builds/<studio_app>/ /assets/<app>/app_builds/<studio_app>/

An app ships standard apps. The rest of this page is about standard apps.

docs.title: File layout in an app repo
docs.text:
The studio folder is at the root of the app repo, next to the Python package. The folder name of each Studio app is frappe.scrub(<studio app name>), so my-app is stored in my_app.

apps/sample_app/
  sample_app/                          # the Python package
  studio/
    sample_portal/
      sample_portal.json               # the Studio App document
      tsconfig.json                    # written by Studio, maps @app/* to this folder
      router.ts                        # optional app router config
      tailwind.config.js               # optional extra Tailwind content paths
      components/OrderBadge.vue        # optional Vue components
      studio_page/
        orders/
          orders.json                  # the Studio Page document
          orders.ts                    # optional page script
      studio_components/
        order_card.json                # a Studio Component
        order_card.js                  # its script

Studio treats a subfolder of studio/ as an app only if it holds <folder>/<folder>.json. Other folders are ignored.

The app JSON is a normal document export:

{
 "app_home": "page-8599f810",
 "app_name": "sample_portal",
 "app_title": "Sample Portal",
 "doctype": "Studio App",
 "frappe_app": "sample_app",
 "is_standard": 1,
 "name": "sample_portal",
 "route": "portal"
}

Rules for the files:

  • name in a page JSON is the scrubbed page title. page_name is the document ID. Do not change page_name.
  • When you change a page title on disk, rename its folder, JSON file and script file to frappe.scrub(page_title).
  • A page script lives only in its .ts or .js file. The script field of an exported page stays empty.
  • Keep one script file per module. Studio rejects a write that makes both orders.ts and orders.js.
  • app_home holds a page document ID.

docs.title: Create a standard app
docs.text:
1. Turn on developer_mode in the site config.
  2. Create the app in Studio, or insert a Studio App with is_standard set to 1 and frappe_app set to an installed app.
  3. Save. Studio writes the export folder.

To convert a custom app, call enable_app_export(target_app) on the Studio App document. It sets is_standard and frappe_app, writes the JSON files, and moves the source files to disk. disable_app_export(confirm_discarded=False) makes the app custom again. It stops when files that a custom app cannot keep (such as .ts and .vue) exist, unless you confirm their deletion.

Warning

Do not copy an export folder by hand to change the app type. A copy does not update is_standard or frappe_app.

docs.title: Export and sync
docs.text:
Export writes documents to disk. It runs in on_update of Studio App, Studio Page and Studio Component, only when can_export in frappe/studio/export.py is true:

  • The document is standard.
  • developer_mode is on.
  • The site is not installing, uninstalling or importing.

Outside developer mode, a save of a standard app, page or component fails with "Standard apps can only be edited in developer mode." Install, migrate, import and patches can still write them.

Sync reads files into the database:

When Function What it does bench migrate frappe.studio.sync.after_migrate Imports the app, page and component JSON of every installed app. Deletes standard apps and pages whose files are gone. Rebuilds published custom apps. App install frappe.studio.sync.after_app_install Imports the Studio apps of the installed app. App uninstall frappe.studio.sync.before_app_uninstall Deletes the Studio apps whose frappe_app is the app. bench --site <site> watch-studio frappe.studio.watch.watch Imports changed JSON and component scripts while it runs.

watch-studio needs the watchdog package, a dev dependency. It finds studio/ folders when it starts, so restart it after you add a folder. It does not sync deletions. Run it next to bench start, which runs the Vite dev server of Studio. The dev server serves page scripts and .vue files to the editor and preview.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Command Description bench build --app sample_app Builds the app assets. Then frappe.studio.build.after_app_build builds every standard Studio app of the built apps. A failed Studio build fails the command. bench --site <site> build-studio-app <studio_app> Builds one Studio app. It exits with code 1 on failure and logs the error in Error Log.

You do not need a build to edit. The preview at /dev/<app_route><page_route> uses the editor renderer and shows drafts and unpublished pages. The user needs read access on Studio Page.

The published route /<app_route> uses the build. It serves an app only when the app has a published page. A guest can open it only when a published page has allow_guest. A guest who cannot open it is redirected to /login. Without a build, the published route falls back to the editor renderer.

The build output is generated. You can keep it out of git, for example with sample_app/public/app_builds in .gitignore.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Frappe registers these hooks for Studio in frappe/hooks.py:

Hook Value Description page_renderer frappe.studio.doctype.studio_app.studio_app.StudioAppRenderer Serves /<app_route> and /dev/<app_route>. website_route_rules /studio/<path:app_path> to studio Opens the Studio editor. after_app_build frappe.studio.build.after_app_build Builds the standard Studio apps of the built apps.

An app can add one hook:

Hook Shape Read by Description studio_app_boot dict of Studio app name to dotted path StudioApp.get_boot The function returns a dict. The page gets it as the global boot before the first navigation. 
# sample_app/hooks.py
studio_app_boot = {"sample_portal": "sample_app.studio_boot.get_boot"}

# sample_app/studio_boot.py
import frappe


def get_boot() -> dict:
    return {
        "user_full_name": frappe.utils.get_fullname(frappe.session.user),
        "is_guest": frappe.session.user == "Guest",
    }

If several apps set a function for one Studio app, the last one wins. An exception is logged in Error Log and boot is empty. The whitelisted method frappe.studio.api.get_app_boot(app_name) returns the same dict.

Page scripts, bindings and the router config read boot.<key>. Keys can be missing, so use ?. for nested keys.

docs.title: App router config
docs.text:
Put app-wide aliases, redirects and guards in router.ts or router.js at the root of the export folder. Use export default. Studio reads three optional keys: routerOptions (options for createRouter, except routes and history), extendRoute(route) and setup(router).

// studio/sample_portal/router.js
export default {
    routerOptions: { scrollBehavior: () => ({ top: 0 }) },
    setup(router) {
        router.beforeEach((to) => {
            if (boot.is_guest && to.name !== "Login") {
                return { name: "Login" }
            }
        })
    },
}

Each page is one route. The route name is the page title.

docs.title: File API
docs.text:
Use the whitelisted methods in frappe/studio/api.py to read and write source files. They work for both app types and take frappe_app and studio_app.

Method Description list_studio_files List the source files. read_studio_file Read one file. Returns path, content and hash. write_studio_file Write a file. Pass known_hash to reject the write when the file changed. create_studio_file Create an empty file. Fails if it exists. create_studio_folder Create a folder. rename_studio_file Rename a file or change its extension. delete_studio_file Delete a file.

The write methods need write permission on Studio Page. They reject writes to the app, page and component JSON that Studio generates. Change those through the document fields.

docs.title: AI in Studio
docs.text: The Studio editor has its own AI agent, separate from Flow. Its endpoints are in frappe/studio/ai/api.py. It reads an OpenRouter key from the ai_api_key field of Studio Settings. Without the key, the run endpoint fails. The frappe repo ships the Flow Skill frappe/studio-app-building, which tells Flow agents how to build Studio pages. See Flow Development.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Saving a standard document in Studio writes the file on disk. Wait for the watcher to sync disk changes before you edit the same document in Studio.
  • bench migrate deletes standard apps and pages whose files are gone. Do not delete an export folder you still need.
  • A custom app cannot use .ts or .vue files, or packages outside vue, vue-router, pinia and frappe-ui. Export the app if it needs them.
  • In a standard app, Tailwind scans only studio/<studio_app>/. Add a tailwind.config.js with content globs for other paths.
  • The app name must be lowercase with hyphens. It is used in the editor URL and the export folder.

docs.title: Configuration and Operations
docs.text:
Configure sites, deploy to production and upgrade between versions.

Page What it covers Configuration Configure a site with site_config.json and common_site_config.json, read values with frappe.conf, change them with bench set-config, and override them with environment variables. Deployment Run Frappe in production with the bench CLI - processes, Procfile, supervisor or systemd, nginx, workers and queues, socketio, maintenance mode and DNS multitenancy. Upgrading Notable breaking changes from v15 to v16 and from v16 to develop, how deprecations work in deprecation_dumpster, and the steps to upgrade a bench.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Frappe reads its configuration from two JSON files in the sites folder. sites/common_site_config.json holds values for every site on the bench. sites/<site>/site_config.json holds values for one site and overrides the common file. Use configuration for things that differ per server or site: credentials, Redis URLs, ports, feature flags. Use a Single DocType such as System Settings for things that a user changes in the desk.

docs.title: How the values merge
docs.text:
frappe.get_site_config() builds the configuration in this order. A later step wins.

  1. common_site_config.json.
  2. site_config.json of the site.
  3. Environment variables (see Environment variables).
  4. Defaults: db_type = mariadb, db_host = 127.0.0.1, db_port = the default port of the database, db_user = db_name (and the other way round), redis_queue = redis://127.0.0.1:11311, redis_cache = redis://127.0.0.1:13311.
  5. extra_config hooks: if the config has extra_config (a dotted path or a list of paths), Frappe calls each function and merges the dict it returns.

docs.title: Read configuration in code
docs.text:
import frappe

frappe.conf.developer_mode           # current site, merged config. A missing key returns None.
frappe.conf.get("max_file_size", 0)  # with a default

frappe.get_site_config()             # merged config of the current site, read from disk
frappe.get_common_site_config()      # common_site_config.json only
frappe.get_conf("frappe.localhost")  # config of another site
frappe.get_conf()                    # current site, or common config when no site is set

frappe.conf is frappe.local.conf. It is loaded once per request or job by frappe.init. The result is a frappe._dict, so attribute access returns None for a missing key.

Some keys are read with frappe.get_common_site_config() or before a site is set. These keys work only in common_site_config.json. They are marked common in the tables below.

Warning

Site config holds secrets: db_password, encryption_key, mail and Redis passwords. Never send frappe.conf to the browser. frappe.boot gets only developer_mode, socketio_port, socketio_backend, file_watcher_port, max_file_size and file_chunk_size.

docs.title: Change configuration
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config developer_mode 1
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config allow_cors '["https://app.example.com"]' --parse
bench set-config -g scheduler_tick_interval 60        # common_site_config.json
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config pause_scheduler None   # remove the key
bench --site frappe.localhost show-config                       # print the merged config
  • -g, --global: write to common_site_config.json.
  • -p, --parse: read the value as a Python literal (true, false, numbers, lists, dicts).
  • Without --parse, "0" and "1" are saved as integers, and "true" and "false" as booleans. The value None removes the key.

From code, use frappe.installer.update_site_config(key, value). It locks the file, writes it, and clears the cached config. Running processes read the new value on their next request. Restart workers and the Socket.IO server for keys they read at startup (workers, socketio_*, redis_*).

docs.title: Keys by purpose
docs.text: This is the list of keys that you are most likely to set. For every key read by the framework, see the site config reference.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: Key Default Description db_type mariadb mariadb, postgres or sqlite. db_name db_user Database name. Also the Redis key prefix of the site. db_user, db_password db_name, none Database credentials. db_host, db_port, db_socket 127.0.0.1, default port, none Where the database server is. db_ssl_ca, db_ssl_cert, db_ssl_key, db_ssl_check_hostname none TLS for MariaDB. db_schema none Schema for Postgres. read_from_replica off Send read-only requests to a replica. Needs replica_host. replica_host, replica_db_port none Replica server. different_credentials_for_replica, replica_db_name, replica_db_user, replica_db_password off Use other credentials for the replica. max_writes_per_transaction framework limit Raise the limit of writes in one transaction. enable_db_statement_timeout off Stop queries after 1.5 times the request timeout (http_timeout, default 300 s) or the job timeout. rds_db off Grant a reduced set of privileges when making the site database, for managed databases.

docs.title: Redis, queues and workers
docs.text:
Key Default Description redis_cache redis://127.0.0.1:13311 Redis for frappe.cache. redis_queue redis://127.0.0.1:11311 Redis for job queues and realtime events. common redis_cache_sentinel_enabled, redis_cache_sentinels, redis_cache_master_service, ... off Connect to the cache through Redis Sentinel. The same keys exist with the redis_queue_ prefix. workers none Extra queues: {"<queue>": {"timeout": <seconds>}}. common use_rq_auth, rq_username, rq_password off Redis ACL user for the queue. common max_queued_jobs 500 Queue size at which frappe.enqueue fails. rq_job_failure_ttl, rq_results_ttl, rq_failed_jobs_limit 7 days, 600 s, 1000 How long RQ keeps job data. background_process_niceness 10 CPU niceness increment for workers and the scheduler. common client_cache_max_bytes no limit Memory limit of frappe.client_cache per process.

See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Scheduler and maintenance
docs.text:
Key Default Description scheduler_tick_interval 240 Seconds between scheduler checks. common scheduler_interval 240 Interval of all scheduler events, in seconds. pause_scheduler off Pause scheduled jobs. disable_scheduler off Disable scheduled jobs. maintenance_mode off Block writes and stop the scheduler. allow_reads_during_maintenance on In maintenance mode, keep the site open for reads.

See Scheduler.

docs.title: Web server, URLs and realtime
docs.text:
Key Default Description webserver_port none Port of bench serve. Used in URLs when host_name is not set. common host_name (or hostname) none Full site URL, such as https://erp.example.com. Used by frappe.utils.get_url. http_port none Port added to URLs made from the request host. default_site none Site used when no --site is given. common socketio_port 9000 Port of the Socket.IO server. common socketio_backend node node or python. Read by bench socketio. common socketio_uds, socketio_worker_threads none, 4 Socket.IO Unix socket and Python server threads. common live_reload, file_watcher_port off Development asset watcher. common restart_supervisor_on_update, restart_systemd_on_update off Restart services after bench update.

See Realtime and Deployment.

docs.title: Security and requests
docs.text:
Key Default Description encryption_key made at site creation Key for encrypted Password fields and backups. Keep a copy. Without it, encrypted data cannot be read. allow_cors none "*", one origin, or a list of origins allowed to call the API from a browser. allowed_referrers [] Extra referrers accepted by the CSRF check. ignore_csrf off Turn off the CSRF check. Only for development. deny_multiple_sessions off Log out other sessions of a user at login. Also in System Settings. rate_limit none {"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}. Total request time the site may use in each window. Over the limit, requests get HTTP 429. throttle_user_limit 60 Maximum users created in 60 seconds. server_script_enabled off Allow Server Scripts and safe exec. common allow_internal_webhook_urls off Allow webhooks to private network addresses. common notify_admin_access_to_system_manager off Email System Managers when Administrator logs in.

See Security.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Key Default Description max_file_size 25 MB Maximum upload size in bytes. System Settings max_file_size (in MB) wins when set. file_chunk_size 25 MB Chunk size in bytes for uploads from the desk. max_zip_extract_size, max_zip_extract_members 25 MB, 1000 Limits for unzipping a File. System Settings max_zip_extract_size (in MB) wins when set. private_path private Folder of private files, relative to the site folder. storage_v2, storage_driver, storage_driver_config off File Storage v2 (alpha). See Files.

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
These keys make a default outgoing account when mail_server is set and no Email Account exists for sending.

Key Description mail_server, mail_port SMTP server and port. mail_login, mail_password SMTP login. use_tls, use_ssl SMTP encryption. auto_email_id Sender address. Default: mail_login, else notifications@example.com. email_sender_name Sender name. Default Frappe. always_use_account_email_id_as_sender, always_use_account_name_as_sender_name Force the account sender. disable_mail_smtp_authentication Send without SMTP login. mute_emails Do not send emails. email_queue_batch_size Emails sent per queue flush. Default 500. pop_timeout, imap_timeout Timeouts for incoming mail.

docs.title: Development and logging
docs.text: Key Default Description developer_mode off Write DocType and other standard changes to app files. Turns off website cache. allow_tests off Allow bench run-tests on the site. Not needed when CI is set. logging 0 2 logs each SQL query. A true value also shows tracebacks on 404 responses. enable_frappe_logger off Write request logs with frappe.logger. monitor off Record request and job metrics (frappe.monitor). disable_async off The desk does not connect to the Socket.IO server. disable_website_cache off Do not cache rendered website pages. disable_global_search off Do not update the global search index. error_report_email none Recipient of error reports that users send from the desk.

docs.title: Install and backups
docs.text:
Key Default Description admin_password none Administrator password used by bench new-site and tests. install_apps none Apps to install with every new site (after frappe). skip_setup_wizard off Do not open the setup wizard after install. backup none {"includes": [...], "excludes": [...]}: tables for a partial backup. keep_backups_for_hours 23 Hours before temporary backup files in the backup folder are deleted. lang en Language used before a user is known.

Other groups: chromium_* and use_persistent_chromium (PDF with Chromium), flow_* (Flow server), pulse_* (telemetry), cloud_* and fc_* (Frappe Cloud). See the site config reference.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Overrides FRAPPE_DB_TYPE, FRAPPE_DB_HOST, FRAPPE_DB_PORT, FRAPPE_DB_SOCKET, FRAPPE_DB_NAME, FRAPPE_DB_USER, FRAPPE_DB_PASSWORD The matching db_* keys. FRAPPE_REDIS_QUEUE, FRAPPE_REDIS_CACHE redis_queue, redis_cache. FRAPPE_SITE Default site for bench commands. SITES_PATH Sites folder used by frappe.get_conf() without a site. FRAPPE_SENTRY_DSN Send errors from workers to Sentry. FRAPPE_BACKGROUND_WORKERS_NOFORK bench worker-pool runs jobs without fork.

Environment variables win over both JSON files.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A key in site_config.json hides the same key in common_site_config.json for that site.
  • common keys in site_config.json have no effect.
  • frappe.conf is loaded per request. A long-running process (worker, scheduler, Socket.IO) reads some keys only at startup.
  • bench set-config writes valid JSON. Hand edits that break the JSON stop every request with "site_config.json is invalid".
  • Do not commit site_config.json or common_site_config.json to a repository.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: A Frappe bench runs as a set of processes: a web server, background workers, a scheduler, a realtime (socketio) server and two Redis servers. In development, bench start runs them from the Procfile. In production, the bench CLI generates supervisor (or systemd) and nginx configuration. The bench CLI is a separate package (frappe-bench). The commands on this page were checked against bench CLI 5.31.1.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
Process Command Description Web bench serve (development), gunicorn ... frappe.app:application (production) Serves desk, website and API requests. Worker bench worker --queue <queues> Runs background jobs from Redis queues. Scheduler bench schedule Enqueues Scheduled Job Types at their time. It does not run the jobs. Realtime bench socketio Socket.IO server for realtime events. Redis cache redis-server config/redis_cache.conf Cache, locks, rate limit counters, realtime pub/sub. Redis queue redis-server config/redis_queue.conf Background job queues.

All processes serve all sites of the bench. The web process finds the site from the X-Frappe-Site-Name header or from the host name of the request (init_request in frappe/app.py).

docs.title: Workers
docs.text:
bench worker options:

Option Description --queue Queues to consume, comma-separated, for example short,default. Without it, the worker consumes all queues. --burst Stop when the queues are empty. --strategy round_robin or random dequeue order. --quiet Hide log output. -u, --rq-username / -p, --rq-password Redis ACL user and password.

bench worker-pool --queue <queues> --num-workers 2 starts a pool of workers in one process. The standard queues are short, default and long. Add your own queues in common_site_config.json with the workers key. See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: bench socketio reads socketio_backend from common_site_config.json. The value node (default) runs apps/frappe/socketio.js with Node. The value python runs python -m frappe.realtime.server from the bench environment. If the Python server is not available, the command falls back to Node. The desk reads socketio_port from the boot info to connect.

docs.title: Development: Procfile
docs.text:
bench init and bench setup procfile write Procfile in the bench root. bench start runs it with honcho.

redis_cache: redis-server config/redis_cache.conf
redis_queue: redis-server config/redis_queue.conf
web: bench serve --port 8000
socketio: bench socketio
watch: bench watch
schedule: bench schedule
worker: bench worker 1>> logs/worker.log 2>> logs/worker.error.log

Each entry under workers in common_site_config.json adds a line worker_<name>: bench worker --queue <name>.

docs.title: Production setup
docs.text:
Run these commands from the bench root as the bench user. They need sudo.

  1. Turn off developer mode on each site: bench --site <site> set-config developer_mode 0.
  2. Build assets: bench build --production.
  3. Run sudo bench setup production <user>. <user> is the system user that owns the bench.
  4. Check that the processes run: sudo supervisorctl status.

bench setup production <user>:

  1. Installs Ansible, fail2ban, nginx and supervisor if they are missing.
  2. Writes config/supervisor.conf (or systemd units if restart_systemd_on_update is set).
  3. Writes config/nginx.conf.
  4. Links config/supervisor.conf into the supervisor config folder and config/nginx.conf to /etc/nginx/conf.d/<bench-name>.conf.
  5. Reloads supervisor and nginx.

You cannot set both restart_supervisor_on_update and restart_systemd_on_update. bench disable-production removes the links.

docs.title: supervisor
docs.text:
config/supervisor.conf has these programs:

Program Command <bench>-frappe-web gunicorn -b 127.0.0.1:<webserver_port> -w <gunicorn_workers> ... frappe.app:application --preload <bench>-frappe-schedule bench schedule <bench>-frappe-short-worker bench worker --queue short,default <bench>-frappe-long-worker bench worker --queue long,default,short <bench>-frappe-default-worker bench worker --queue default (only if multi-queue consumption is off) <bench>-frappe-<name>-worker bench worker --queue <name>, one per workers entry <bench>-redis-cache, <bench>-redis-queue Redis servers <bench>-node-socketio bench socketio

Groups: <bench>-web (web and socketio), <bench>-workers (scheduler and workers), <bench>-redis.

Bench config keys in common_site_config.json that change this file:

Key Default Description webserver_port 8000 Port of gunicorn. gunicorn_workers CPU count x 2 + 1 gunicorn worker processes. gunicorn_max_requests computed Restart a gunicorn worker after this many requests. http_timeout 120 gunicorn timeout in seconds. background_workers 1 Number of processes for each worker program. workers {} Extra queues: {"<name>": {"timeout": 300, "background_workers": 2}}. socketio_backend node node or python.

After you change a key, run bench setup supervisor and sudo supervisorctl reread && sudo supervisorctl update.

docs.title: nginx
docs.text: config/nginx.conf serves /assets and public files from disk. It sends /socket.io to the socketio server and other requests to gunicorn. It sets X-Frappe-Site-Name on proxied requests. Private files are served through an internal /protected/ location after Frappe checks permission. Run bench setup nginx and sudo bench setup reload-nginx after you add a site or a domain.

docs.title: Multitenancy and DNS
docs.text:
• DNS multitenancy (bench config dns_multitenant on): all sites share port 80. nginx routes by host name. The site folder name must match the domain, for example sites/erp.example.com.
  • Port-based multitenancy (default): each site gets its own port. Set it with bench set-nginx-port <site> <port>.
  • Add more domains to a site with bench setup add-domain <domain> --site <site>.
  • Get TLS certificates with sudo bench setup lets-encrypt <site>, or bench setup wildcard-ssl <domain>.

Run bench setup nginx after each change, then reload nginx.

docs.title: Updates and maintenance
docs.text:
bench update pulls apps, installs requirements, runs migrate on all sites, builds assets and restarts. Options include --pull, --patch, --build, --requirements, --restart-supervisor, --restart-systemd, --no-backup and --reset.

For a manual upgrade of one site:

bench --site erp.example.com set-maintenance-mode on
bench --site erp.example.com ready-for-migration
bench --site erp.example.com migrate
bench --site erp.example.com set-maintenance-mode off
bench restart
  • set-maintenance-mode on sets maintenance_mode in the site config. The scheduler stops enqueuing jobs. Requests can still read: Frappe opens a read-only transaction, or connects to the replica when read_from_replica is set. Set allow_reads_during_maintenance to 0 to stop all requests.
  • ready-for-migration exits with code 1 if the site still has pending background jobs.
  • bench --site <site> scheduler pause and scheduler resume set pause_scheduler. scheduler disable and scheduler enable change the setting in System Settings. scheduler status shows the state.
  • bench doctor shows worker and scheduler status. bench --site <site> show-pending-jobs lists queued jobs.

See Upgrading for version changes.

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
• Raise gunicorn_workers for more parallel requests. Each worker is a process with its own memory.
  • Raise background_workers, or add queues under workers, for more job throughput. Put slow jobs on long so that they do not block short.
  • Run more benches behind a load balancer only with a shared database, shared Redis and shared file storage. All benches must run the same app versions.
  • Point db_host, redis_cache and redis_queue in common_site_config.json to external servers when you move them off the bench host.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not run bench start in production. It runs bench watch and the development server.
  • Do not keep developer_mode on in production. In developer mode, saving a standard DocType writes its files to the app folder.
  • Restart the workers after a code change. They keep the old code in memory.
  • Keep backups of sites/*/site_config.json. They hold the database password and encryption_key.
