docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: This page lists changes that can break an app or a site when you move from v15 to v16, and from v16 to develop (17.0.0-dev). It lists only changes found by comparing the code of the three versions. Read it before you upgrade, and test the upgrade on a copy of the site.

docs.title: Upgrade steps
docs.text:
1. Take a backup with files: bench --site <site> backup --with-files. Keep the encryption_key from site_config.json.
  2. Check the Python and Node versions in the table below. Install the new versions first.
  3. Update each app to the matching branch (version-16 or develop). All apps on a bench must support the same Frappe version.
  4. Run bench setup requirements to install Python and Node dependencies.
  5. Run bench --site <site> migrate for each site.
  6. Run bench build.
  7. Restart the processes: bench restart in production, or start bench start again in development.

In production, turn on maintenance mode before step 5 with bench --site <site> set-maintenance-mode on, and turn it off after step 7. bench update from the bench CLI runs the pull, requirements, migrate, build and restart steps for you.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
v15 v16 develop Python (requires-python) >=3.10,<3.15 >=3.14,<3.15 >=3.14,<3.15 Node (engines.node) >=18 >=24 >=24

v16 needs Python 3.14. A v15 bench on an older Python needs a new virtual environment: bench setup env --python python3.14, then bench setup requirements.

docs.title: Desk route is /desk
docs.text: The desk moved from /app to /desk. Frappe redirects /app/... to /desk/... with the query string (website_redirects in frappe/hooks.py). Update hardcoded links in apps, emails, print formats and external systems. In JavaScript, use frappe.set_route and frappe.utils.get_form_link instead of building /app/ URLs.

docs.title: Modules moved to separate apps
docs.text:
These DocTypes are removed from frappe. Install the app to keep using them.

Feature DocTypes removed App Blog Blog Post, Blog Category, Blogger, Blog Settings blogs Newsletter Newsletter, Newsletter Attachment, Newsletter Email Group newsletter Energy Points Energy Point Log, Energy Point Rule, Energy Point Settings, Review Level eps Offsite backups Dropbox Settings, S3 Backup Settings, Google Drive offsite_backups

Also removed: Changelog Feed, Transaction Log, Marketing Campaign. The hooks leaderboards and get_changelog_feed are no longer read.

docs.title: get_list rejects SQL in fields
docs.text:
frappe.get_list and frappe.get_all now build queries with the query builder (frappe.model.qb_query). SQL functions written as strings in fields raise ValidationError ("SQL functions are not allowed as strings in SELECT"). Use the dict form:

# v15
frappe.get_all("ToDo", fields=["count(name) as count"])

# v16 and develop
frappe.get_all("ToDo", fields=[{"COUNT": "name", "as": "count"}])

For other expressions, write a query with frappe.qb.

docs.title: Default sort is creation
docs.text: The default sort_field of a new DocType is creation, not modified. A v16 patch (MariaDB only) adds an index on creation to the tables of all parent DocTypes, drops the modified index where the DocType does not sort by modified, and changes saved list settings from modified to creation. Code that expects lists sorted by last change must pass order_by="modified desc".

docs.title: Sidebar fixtures
docs.text:
The workspace sidebar of an app moved from <app>/workspace_sidebar/*.json to one Sidebar per module, in <app>/<module>/sidebar/. The old folder is not imported. Until you convert, a module shows a generated sidebar. Convert the files once and commit the result:

bench --site <site> convert-sidebar-fixtures --app sample_app --dry-run
bench --site <site> convert-sidebar-fixtures --app sample_app

The command only reads the old folder and leaves it in place. Without --app, it converts every installed app that still has the old folder.

docs.title: Other changes
docs.text:
• Session IDs are stored as SHA-256 hashes. A patch hashes existing sessions, so users stay logged in. Code that reads tabSessions by the raw cookie value no longer finds the row.
  • Studio is part of frappe. A site that had the separate studio app gets it from frappe after migrate, and studio is removed from the installed apps.
  • frappe.get_version is removed.
  • Test classes: use frappe.tests.UnitTestCase and frappe.tests.IntegrationTestCase. frappe.tests.utils.FrappeTestCase still works with a warning.

docs.title: v16 to develop
docs.text:
• Website search index removed. frappe/search/website_search.py and full_text_search.py are gone. bench migrate --skip-search-index has no effect and shows a warning. bench build-search-index does nothing. Remove them from scripts.
  • Slack Webhook URL renamed. The DocType is now Notification Webhook URL. Notifications with channel Slack change to channel Webhook. Update code and fixtures that use the old names.
  • Sidebar Item Group removed. The DocTypes Sidebar Item Group and Sidebar Item Group Link no longer exist.
  • PDF generator. A patch sets pdf_generator to chrome for Print Formats that used wkhtmltopdf or had no value, and removes the site-wide pdf_generator of Print Settings. Check PDF output of custom print formats after upgrade.
  • OAuth bearer tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes. Existing tokens are hashed by a patch.
  • Classic charts. Sites that finished setup keep the classic charts (use_classic_charts in System Settings). New sites get the new charts.
  • UI tests. bench run-ui-tests runs Playwright. Apps with only a Cypress config still run with a warning. Cypress support is deprecated for removal in v17.
  • frappe.read_doc is new. Use it to load a document for a user, with permission checks and field-level read permissions.
  • rate_limit in @frappe.whitelist. The parameter only accepts None, to mark a guest method that is not rate limited. Any other value raises TypeError. Use the @rate_limit decorator to limit a method.
  • Server Script variables. Server Scripts have a Variables table, read with frappe.env. API scripts with allow_guest must have a rate limit.
  • Removed deprecated functions. frappe.utils.error.get_default_args and frappe.utils.error.raise_error_on_no_output are removed.

docs.title: Deprecations
docs.text:
Frappe keeps deprecated functions in frappe/deprecation_dumpster.py. Each one has the date it was marked and the version from which it is an error.

Warning class Behavior V15FrappeDeprecationWarning An error (subclass of FrappeDeprecationError). V16FrappeDeprecationWarning A warning. V17FrappeDeprecationWarning Ignored by default (PendingFrappeDeprecationWarning).

To see pending warnings, or to turn an error back into a warning in an emergency, set PYTHONWARNINGS, for example PYTHONWARNINGS="default::frappe.deprecation_dumpster.V17FrappeDeprecationWarning".

Functions marked for removal in v17 include:

Deprecated Use instead frappe.tests.utils.FrappeTestCase frappe.tests.UnitTestCase or frappe.tests.IntegrationTestCase frappe.tests.utils.change_settings, patch_hooks, debug_on, timeout The same names from frappe.tests frappe.tests_runner.* frappe.tests.utils functions, or no replacement frappe.get_test_records Test records load lazily frappe.db.is_column_missing frappe.db.is_missing_column frappe.gzip_compress, frappe.gzip_decompress The gzip module frappe.geo.country_info.get_translated_dict frappe.geo.country_info.get_translated_countries User.validate_roles User.populate_role_profile_roles frappe.utils.get_gravatar, get_gravatar_url, has_gravatar frappe.utils.get_identicon. Gravatar is removed. frappe.utils.make_esc, frappe.client.get_js, frappe.utils.print_format.read_multi_pdf No replacement

frappe.utils.data.get_number_format_info is marked for v16. Use NumberFormat.from_string() from frappe.utils.number_format.

In your own app, mark a public function as deprecated with frappe.deprecation_dumpster.deprecation_warning(marked, graduation, msg). Keep it for one major version, then remove it.

docs.title: Reports, Printing and Email
docs.text:
Write script and query reports, print formats and PDFs, and send email and notifications.

Page What it covers Reports Build Script Reports and Query Reports in an app, define filters, return charts and summaries, run reports from code, and use prepared reports and report roles. Print Formats Ship Print Formats in an app, write Jinja print templates, render HTML or PDF with frappe.get_print, choose the PDF engine and add one with the pdf_generator hook. Email and Notifications Send email with frappe.sendmail and the Email Queue, use Email Templates, ship Notifications in an app, log Communications, handle incoming email and create system notifications.

docs.title: Email and Notifications
docs.text: Frappe sends all outgoing email through the Email Queue. Your code calls frappe.sendmail(), and the scheduler sends the queue in the background. Use a Notification to send email, system notifications, SMS or webhooks when a document event happens, without code in the controller. Use Communication to keep an email thread on a document. For setup of email accounts and the desk side, see Email (user guide) and Notifications (user guide).

docs.title: Send email
docs.text:
frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=["user1@example.com"],
    subject="Order SO-00001 is ready",
    message="<p>Your order is ready.</p>",
    reference_doctype="Sample Order",
    reference_name="SO-00001",
    attachments=[
        {
            "print_format_attachment": 1,
            "doctype": "Sample Order",
            "name": "SO-00001",
            "print_format": "Standard",
        }
    ],
)

frappe.sendmail() builds an Email Queue document and returns it. It does not send the email now. The scheduler job frappe.email.queue.flush (event all) sends queued email. A default outgoing Email Account must exist, or Frappe raises frappe.OutgoingEmailError.

Parameter Default Description recipients [] List of addresses, or a comma-separated string. sender "" From address. Empty uses the outgoing Email Account. subject "No Subject" Subject line. message / content "No Message" HTML body. content wins when both are set. as_markdown False Convert the body from Markdown to HTML. template, args None Render templates/emails/<template>.html (and .txt) with args. cc, bcc [] Copy recipients. reply_to None Reply-To address. reference_doctype, reference_name None Link the email to a document. Also doctype and name. attachments None List of attachment dicts. See below. delayed True False sends after the transaction commits. Same as now=True. now None Send after commit instead of waiting for the scheduler. send_after None Do not send before this datetime. send_priority 1 Higher values are sent first. queue_separately False Make one Email Queue per recipient. expose_recipients None "header" shows all To recipients. "footer" adds "This email was sent to ..." text. add_unsubscribe_link 1 Add an unsubscribe link. unsubscribe_method, unsubscribe_params, unsubscribe_message None Customize the unsubscribe link. header None Add a header block to the email. with_container False Wrap the body in a styled container. print_letterhead False Add the letter head to print attachments. inline_images None List of {"filename", "filecontent"}. read_receipt None Ask for a read receipt. x_priority 3 1 highest, 3 normal, 5 lowest. email_headers None Extra headers. Frappe adds X- when it is missing. raw_html False Send the body as a full HTML document. add_css True Add CSS from the email_css hook. redact_message_after_send False Replace the stored body with a placeholder after it is sent. communication None Link the Email Queue to a Communication.

docs.title: Attachments
docs.text:
Shape Description {"fname": "a.txt", "fcontent": b"..."} File content in memory. {"fid": "<File name>"} or {"file_url": "/files/a.pdf"} An existing File. Read when the email is sent. {"print_format_attachment": 1, "doctype": ..., "name": ..., "print_format": ...} A print of a document. Made with frappe.attach_print() when the email is sent.

You can also pass the return value of frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, print_format=...) directly. See Print Formats.

docs.title: Email templates in files
docs.text:
template="sample_order_ready" renders templates/emails/sample_order_ready.html from any app with args as context. A .txt file with the same name gives the plain text part.

{# sample_app/templates/emails/sample_order_ready.html #}
<p>{{ _("Hello") }} {{ customer_name }},</p>
<p>{{ _("Order {0} is ready.").format(order) }}</p>

frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=["user1@example.com"],
    subject="Order ready",
    template="sample_order_ready",
    args={"customer_name": "Customer A", "order": "SO-00001"},
)

docs.title: Email Template
docs.text:
An Email Template is a document with a Jinja subject and response (or response_html when use_html is set). Users pick it in the email dialog. Render it from code with get_formatted_email(doc).

template = frappe.get_doc("Email Template", "Sample Order Ready")
email = template.get_formatted_email(frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001").as_dict())
# {'subject': 'Order SO-00001 is ready', 'message': 'Hello Customer A'}

frappe.sendmail(recipients=["user1@example.com"], **email)

The whitelisted method frappe.email.doctype.email_template.email_template.get_email_template(template_name, doc, sender=None) does the same for the client. It checks read permission on the template.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
A Communication is one email (or comment, call, chat) linked to a document with reference_doctype and reference_name. It shows in the document timeline. The desk email dialog calls frappe.core.doctype.communication.email.make.

from frappe.core.doctype.communication.email import make

make(
    doctype="Sample Order",
    name="SO-00001",
    subject="Order update",
    content="<p>Your order ships today.</p>",
    recipients="user1@example.com",
    send_email=True,
    print_format="Standard",
)

make() only works for system users. It checks email permission on the reference document and create permission on Communication. With send_email=True, it queues the email. Without it, it only saves the Communication.

After a Communication is saved, Frappe calls on_communication_update(communication) on the reference document, if the controller has it. Otherwise it runs the default update (status and response time fields) and calls notify_communication(communication).

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    def on_communication_update(self, communication):
        if communication.sent_or_received == "Received":
            self.db_set("status", "Open")

docs.title: Incoming email
docs.text:
An Email Account with enable_incoming pulls email every 10 minutes (frappe.email.doctype.email_account.email_account.pull). Each email becomes a Communication. To make documents from email:

  1. Set email_append_to on your DocType.
  2. Set subject_field and sender_field on the DocType. Optional: sender_name_field.
  3. In the Email Account, set Append To to your DocType (or set it per IMAP folder).

For a new thread, InboundMail creates a document of that DocType with the subject and sender, with ignore_mandatory, and links the Communication to it. For a reply, it finds the document from the In-Reply-To header, or by subject and sender.

The email_append_to hook lists more DocTypes that can receive email. Frappe sets ["Event", "ToDo", "Communication"].

docs.title: Notifications in an app
docs.text:
A Notification sends a message when a document event happens. A standard Notification (is_standard = 1) is exported to the app when you save it in developer mode.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/notification/sample_order_submitted/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_submitted.json   # the Notification document
├── sample_order_submitted.md     # message (.html or .txt for other message types)
└── sample_order_submitted.py     # get_context(context)

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/notification/sample_order_submitted/sample_order_submitted.py
def get_context(context):
    context.items_count = len(context.doc.items)

<!-- sample_order_submitted.md -->
Order **{{ doc.name }}** for {{ doc.customer_name }} has {{ items_count }} items.

The message, subject and condition get doc, nowdate and a safe frappe namespace. A standard Notification can only be enabled or changed in developer mode.

Field Values channel Email, System Notification, SMS, Webhook event New, Save, Submit, Cancel, Value Change, Method, Days Before, Days After, Minutes Before, Minutes After condition_type Python (a condition expression) or Filters (filters JSON) method Controller method name for the Method event, for example on_payment message_type Markdown, HTML, Plain Text recipients Table of receiver_by_document_field, receiver_by_role, cc, bcc and a condition per row send_to_all_assignees Also send to the users the document is assigned to attach_print, print_format Attach a print of the document send_system_notification Also create a system notification for email recipients set_property_after_alert, property_value Set a field after the notification is sent

How events fire (Document.run_notifications in frappe/model/document.py):

Event Runs on New after_insert Save on_update Submit on_submit Cancel on_cancel Value Change on_change, not during insert or delete Method doc.run_method("<method>") with the method in method Days Before, Days After Daily job trigger_daily_alerts Minutes Before, Minutes After Job trigger_offset_alerts, every 5 minutes

To fire a Method notification from code, call the method with run_method:

doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
doc.run_method("on_payment")

Notifications do not run during install, patches, or imports with mute_emails.

docs.title: System notifications
docs.text:
A system notification is a Notification Log row. Users see it in the bell menu of the desk. Create them with enqueue_create_notification.

from frappe.desk.doctype.notification_log.notification_log import enqueue_create_notification

enqueue_create_notification(
    ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com"],
    {
        "type": "Alert",
        "subject": "Order SO-00001 needs approval",
        "document_type": "Sample Order",
        "document_name": "SO-00001",
        "from_user": frappe.session.user,
    },
)
  • type is a link to Notification Type. Frappe installs Mention, Energy Point, Assignment, Share and Alert.
  • The logs are made in a background job after commit.
  • A user does not get a notification for their own action (for_user == from_user), except for types in the notification_self_notify_types hook (Alert).
  • Pass dedupe_on=["document_type", "document_name"] to skip users who already have a matching log.
  • Notification Settings decide if a log also sends an email. Types in notification_skip_email_types (Alert) never send their own email.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text: Hook Use email_css CSS files added to every email (["email.bundle.css"] in Frappe). make_email_body_message Functions that get the email object before it is sent. Change headers or parts. override_email_send One function (email_queue, sender, recipient, message) that sends instead of SMTP. default_mail_footer HTML added to the footer of every email. email_append_to DocTypes that can receive incoming email. notification_config Function that gives open counts for the desk ("for_doctype", "for_module"). notification_self_notify_types Notification Types that also notify the user who acted. notification_skip_email_types Notification Types that never send their own email.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.sendmail() queues the email in the current transaction. If the transaction rolls back, the email is not sent.
  • now=True sends after commit, in the web request. Use it only for urgent email, like password reset.
  • In tests (frappe.in_test), the queue is built but not sent over SMTP.
  • Set reference_doctype and reference_name so replies link back to the document.
  • Use _() in templates, and send with frappe.translate.print_language when the recipient uses another language.

docs.title: Print Formats
docs.text: A Print Format decides how a document looks when printed, sent as a PDF, or attached to an email. Each Print Format document is linked to a DocType (doc_type) or to a report (print_format_for = "Report"). Users design most formats in the desk (see Printing (user guide)). As a developer you ship formats in your app, render them from code, and extend the PDF pipeline.

docs.title: Kinds of Print Format
docs.text:
Kind Fields Rendered by Standard No Print Format, or "Standard" Layout of the DocType form, frappe/www/printview.py Editor format print_format_builder_beta = 1, format_data (layout JSON) PrintFormatGenerator (frappe/utils/print_format_generator.py) Custom Jinja custom_format = 1, print_format_type = "Jinja", html get_rendered_template() in frappe/www/printview.py Raw printing custom_format = 1, raw_printing = 1, raw_commands Sent to a printer as raw commands

before_save sets print_format_builder_beta = 1 on a new format that is not custom and not standard. Prefer editor formats. Use a custom Jinja format only when the layout cannot be built from editor blocks. The layout JSON keys are described in skills/print-formats/LAYOUT.md in the frappe repository.

docs.title: Print Formats in an app
docs.text:
Set standard to "Yes" and save in developer mode. export_doc() writes the JSON to the module folder. For a Jinja format, put the template in an .html file with the same name. get_print_format() reads that file before the html field.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/
├── sample_order_slip.json
└── sample_order_slip.html

{# sample_app/sample_app/selling/print_format/sample_order_slip/sample_order_slip.html #}
<h2>{{ doc.name }}</h2>
<p>{{ doc.customer_name }}, {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
    {% for row in doc.items %}
    <tr>
        <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
        <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("amount", doc) }}</td>
    </tr>
    {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right"><b>{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</b></p>

Without developer mode, a standard Print Format cannot be saved ("Standard Print Format cannot be updated").

docs.title: Template context
docs.text:
get_rendered_template() renders the template with these variables:

Name Value doc The document. Use doc.get_formatted("<fieldname>") for values in the user's format. meta frappe.get_meta(doc.doctype) layout The form layout in sections and columns (make_layout) no_letterhead 1 when the letter head is off letter_head Rendered letter head HTML footer Rendered letter head footer HTML print_settings Print Settings as a dict trigger_print 1 when the page opens the print dialog

The Jinja globals of Website are also available, for example frappe.db.get_value and _. Methods and filters from the jinja hook work too. validate_template checks the Jinja when you save.

docs.title: Before print
docs.text:
Before it renders, Frappe sets doc.flags.in_print and calls the controller method before_print(settings). Use it to set values that only the print shows.

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
class SampleOrder(Document):
    def before_print(self, settings=None):
        self.print_heading = f"Order {self.name}"

docs.title: Render from code
docs.text:
frappe.get_print() returns HTML, or PDF bytes with as_pdf=True. It checks that the current user has read or print permission on the document (validate_print_permission in frappe/www/printview.py). read alone is enough.

html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Slip", as_pdf=True)

with open("/tmp/so-00001.pdf", "wb") as f:
    f.write(pdf)
Parameter Default Description doctype, name None The document to print. print_format None Print Format name. Empty uses the DocType default, then "Standard". style None Print Style name. Empty uses Print Settings print_style. as_pdf False Return PDF bytes instead of HTML. doc None A document object to print instead of loading it. no_letterhead 0 Leave out the letter head. letterhead None Letter Head name to use. password None Encrypt the PDF with this password. pdf_options None Options for the PDF engine. pdf_generator None "chrome", "PlutoPrint" or "Typst". Overrides the format and Print Settings. output None A pypdf.PdfWriter. Pages are added to it.

frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, print_format=None, ...) returns {"fname": ..., "fcontent": ...} for an email attachment. It returns a PDF when Print Settings send_print_as_pdf is on, else HTML. It skips the print permission check (frappe.local.flags.ignore_print_permissions).

frappe.translate.print_language("de") is a context manager that prints in another language.

docs.title: URLs
docs.text:
URL Returns /printview?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=Sample Order Slip HTML print view /Sample Order/SO-00001 HTML print view (PrintPage renderer) /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=Sample Order&name=SO-00001&format=... PDF download /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_multi_pdf One PDF for many documents

download_pdf takes doctype, name, format, no_letterhead, language, letterhead, pdf_generator, style and settings.

docs.title: PDF engines
docs.text:
pdf_generator on the Print Format picks the engine. Print Settings pdf_generator is the default for formats that do not set one. The field default is PlutoPrint.

Value Description PlutoPrint Default. Renders HTML without a browser process. Falls back to chrome for a format it cannot render (plutoprint_blockers). chrome Renders HTML with a headless Chromium (frappe.utils.chromium). Use it for formats that need scripts, CSS grid or a page range. Typst Editor formats only, without HTML blocks or custom CSS. See frappe/printing/typst_renderer.md.

resolve_pdf_generator() picks the engine in this order: the pdf_generator argument, the format's pdf_generator, Print Settings pdf_generator, then PlutoPrint.

Version

wkhtmltopdf is not used in develop. The patch frappe/patches/v17_0/switch_wkhtmltopdf_to_chrome.py moves formats and Print Settings that used it to chrome.

docs.title: The pdf_generator hook
docs.text:
For an HTML format, get_print(as_pdf=True) renders the HTML and then calls each function in the pdf_generator hook. The first one that returns bytes wins. If none returns a value, Frappe uses frappe.utils.pdf.get_pdf() with Chromium.

# frappe/hooks.py
pdf_generator = [
    "frappe.utils.pdf.get_chrome_pdf",
    "frappe.utils.pdf.get_plutoprint_pdf",
    "frappe.utils.print_format_generator.get_typst_pdf",
]

To add an engine:

  1. Add your engine name to the options of the pdf_generator field of Print Format and Print Settings, for example with a Property Setter in your fixtures.
  2. Add a function to the pdf_generator hook.
  3. In the function, return None when pdf_generator is not your engine.
# sample_app/hooks.py
pdf_generator = ["sample_app.pdf.get_sample_pdf"]

# sample_app/pdf.py
def get_sample_pdf(print_format, html, options, output, pdf_generator=None):
    if pdf_generator != "Sample Engine":
        return None
    return render_with_sample_engine(html, options)  # must return PDF bytes

docs.title: Other print hooks
docs.text: Hook Called with Use on_print_pdf doctype, name, print_format Run code before a PDF is made, for example to log it. get_print_format_template jenv, print_format Return a compiled Jinja template to use instead of the format's HTML. The last app wins. pdf_body_html jenv, template, print_format, args Render the body HTML. Frappe sets frappe.utils.pdf.pdf_body_html. The last app wins. pdf_header_html, pdf_footer_html soup, head, content, styles, html_id, css Build the repeating header and footer.

docs.title: Letter heads
docs.text: get_letter_head() uses, in order: the letterhead argument, the document's letter_head field, then the Letter Head with is_default = 1. When neither argument is passed, Print Settings with_letterhead decides. Frappe renders the letter head content and footer with Jinja and {"doc": doc.as_dict()}, so you can use {{ doc.customer_name }} in a letter head.

docs.title: Print styles
docs.text: Frappe renders templates/styles/standard.css, then adds the css of the selected Print Style, then the Print Settings font_size. A Jinja format can add CSS in its css field. Frappe ships the styles in frappe/printing/print_style/.

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: A raw format sends printer commands (for example ESC/POS or ZPL) instead of HTML. Set raw_printing and write the commands in raw_commands with Jinja. frappe.www.printview.get_rendered_raw_commands(doc, name, print_format) returns the rendered commands. The desk sends them to the printer through QZ Tray when Print Settings enable_raw_printing is on.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A draft document of a submittable DocType prints only when Print Settings allow_print_for_draft is on. A cancelled one needs allow_print_for_cancelled.
  • Fields with print_hide and fields above the user's permission level are not printed.
  • Use get_formatted() instead of raw values. Raw values do not follow the user's date, number and currency format.
  • Render every format and look at the PDF before you ship it. PlutoPrint and Chromium can break pages differently.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
A report is a Report document. Its report_type decides how it gets data. Use a Script Report when you need Python logic, joins or computed columns. Use a Query Report for one SQL query. Report Builder and Custom Report are saved views that users make in the desk. For the desk side, see Reports (user guide).

report_type Data comes from Made by Report Builder A saved list view of ref_doctype (json field) Users, in Report view Query Report The SQL in query Developers or System Managers Script Report execute(filters) in a Python file (standard) or report_script (not standard) Developers Custom Report A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters Users, with "Save As"

docs.title: Script Report in an app
docs.text:
A standard Script Report (is_standard = "Yes") lives in the module folder of the app.

sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_summary.json   # the Report document
├── sample_order_summary.py     # execute(filters)
└── sample_order_summary.js     # filters and client options
  1. Turn on developer_mode in site config.
  2. Log in as Administrator.
  3. Create a Report with report_type "Script Report", ref_doctype "Sample Order" and a module of your app.
  4. Save. In developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to "Yes" and writes the JSON, .py and .js boilerplate.
  5. Fill in the .py and .js files.
  6. Commit the folder. bench migrate syncs the report to other sites.

Frappe finds the module as <app>.<module>.report.<report_name>.<report_name> (get_report_module_dotted_path).

docs.title: The Python file
docs.text:
execute(filters) gets the filter values as a frappe._dict and returns a tuple or list. Frappe reads up to six items, in this order:

Position Name Type Description 0 columns list Column definitions. Dicts or strings. 1 data list Rows. Each row is a dict (keys are column fieldname) or a list in column order. 2 message str HTML shown above the table. 3 chart dict Chart shown above the table. 4 report_summary list Number cards shown above the table. 5 skip_total_row bool Do not add the total row for this run. 
# sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.py
import frappe
from frappe import _


def execute(filters=None):
    filters = frappe._dict(filters or {})
    columns = get_columns()
    data = get_data(filters)
    return columns, data, None, get_chart(data), get_summary(data)


def get_columns():
    return [
        {"label": _("Order"), "fieldname": "name", "fieldtype": "Link", "options": "Sample Order", "width": 140},
        {"label": _("Customer"), "fieldname": "customer_name", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 180},
        {"label": _("Order Date"), "fieldname": "order_date", "fieldtype": "Date", "width": 110},
        {"label": _("Status"), "fieldname": "status", "fieldtype": "Data", "width": 100},
        {"label": _("Total"), "fieldname": "total", "fieldtype": "Currency", "width": 120},
    ]


def get_data(filters):
    conditions = {"docstatus": ["<", 2]}
    if filters.status:
        conditions["status"] = filters.status
    if filters.from_date and filters.to_date:
        conditions["order_date"] = ["between", [filters.from_date, filters.to_date]]

    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters=conditions,
        fields=["name", "customer_name", "order_date", "status", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
    )


def get_chart(data):
    return {
        "data": {
            "labels": [row.name for row in data],
            "datasets": [{"name": _("Total"), "values": [row.total for row in data]}],
        },
        "type": "bar",
    }


def get_summary(data):
    return [
        {"label": _("Orders"), "value": len(data), "datatype": "Int"},
        {"label": _("Total"), "value": sum(row.total for row in data), "datatype": "Currency", "indicator": "Green"},
    ]

A column can also be a string in the form "Label:Fieldtype/Options:Width", for example "Order:Link/Sample Order:150". Frappe converts it to a dict and makes the fieldname from the label.

The chart dict goes to Frappe Charts: data.labels, data.datasets[].name, data.datasets[].values, and type (for example bar, line, pie, percentage, axis-mixed). A summary item has label, value and datatype. It can also have indicator (Green, Red, Blue and other colors) and currency.

The module can also define these functions:

Function Used for execute_snapshot_report(filters) Called instead of execute when the report has snapshot_report set. get_xlsx_styles(metadata) Styles for the Excel export. formatter(value, column, data, default_formatter) Formats cells in PDFs made on the server.

docs.title: The JS file
docs.text:
The .js file sets frappe.query_reports["<Report Name>"]. The key must be the report name.

// sample_app/sample_app/selling/report/sample_order_summary/sample_order_summary.js
frappe.query_reports["Sample Order Summary"] = {
    filters: [
        {
            fieldname: "status",
            label: __("Status"),
            fieldtype: "Select",
            options: ["", "Draft", "Open", "Completed"],
        },
        {
            fieldname: "from_date",
            label: __("From Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.add_months(frappe.datetime.get_today(), -1),
        },
        {
            fieldname: "to_date",
            label: __("To Date"),
            fieldtype: "Date",
            default: frappe.datetime.get_today(),
        },
    ],
    formatter(value, row, column, data, default_formatter) {
        value = default_formatter(value, row, column, data);
        if (column.fieldname === "status" && data && data.status === "Open") {
            value = `<b>${value}</b>`;
        }
        return value;
    },
    onload(report) {
        report.page.add_inner_button(__("Refresh"), () => report.refresh());
    },
};

A filter is a field definition (fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, default, reqd, depends_on, on_change, get_query). Read a value with frappe.query_report.get_filter_value("status"). Set one with frappe.query_report.set_filter_value("status", "Open").

Other keys that the report view reads: onload, formatter, get_datatable_options, after_datatable_render, after_refresh, get_chart_data, tree, parent_field, initial_depth, collapsible_filters, separate_check_filters, export_hidden_cols. A <report_name>.html file in the report folder is the print template of the report.

docs.title: Filters on the server (validate_filters)
docs.text:
The Report has a filters table (Report Filter) with fieldname, label, fieldtype, options, mandatory, default and wildcard_filter. When validate_filters is set:

  • The desk uses these rows as the filters. A JS filter with the same fieldname adds client options, for example get_query. A JS filter without a row logs a warning.
  • Report.get_validated_filters() runs before execute. It rejects unknown keys, applies defaults, checks mandatory, casts values to the fieldtype, and checks Link values against the user's permissions.
  • default can be __user (the current user). An empty default on a Link filter uses the user default for that fieldname.
  • MultiSelectList and DateRange filters need validate_filters.

Frappe's Permitted Documents For User report uses this setup. Its JS file only adds a get_query to the doctype filter.

docs.title: Script Report without a file
docs.text: A Script Report with is_standard = "No" runs report_script with safe_exec. Only a Script Manager can save it, and server scripts must be on (see Server and Client Scripts). The script gets filters. It sets data (a full result like the return value of execute) or result (rows only, with columns from the columns table).

docs.title: Query Report
docs.text:
A Query Report runs query with the filter values as SQL parameters. Write the column definition as the column alias.

select
    name as "Order:Link/Sample Order:150",
    customer_name as "Customer::150",
    total as "Total:Currency:120"
from `tabSample Order`
where docstatus < 2
    and customer_name like %(customer)s

execute_query_report() checks the query with check_safe_sql_query. It runs the query in a read-only transaction and rolls it back after. The filters in the JS file (or the filters table) give the values for %(customer)s. The result rows come back as dicts, with fieldname made from the label (order, customer, total).

docs.title: Run a report from code
docs.text:
frappe.desk.query_report.run is the method that the desk calls. It is whitelisted and read-only.

from frappe.desk.query_report import run

result = run("Sample Order Summary", filters={"status": "Open"})
result["columns"]   # list of column dicts
result["result"]    # list of row dicts, plus a total row (a list) when add_total_row is set

The returned dict has result, columns, message, chart, report_summary, skip_total_row, status, execution_time and add_total_row. For a prepared report, it has prepared_report and doc and the saved result.

curl -b cookies.txt -G "http://<site>/api/method/frappe.desk.query_report.run" \
  --data-urlencode 'report_name=Sample Order Summary' \
  --data-urlencode 'filters={"status": "Open"}'
Parameter Type Default Description report_name str required Name of the Report. filters dict or JSON str None Filter values. ignore_prepared_report bool False Run now, also for a prepared report. custom_columns list None Extra columns from linked DocTypes. is_tree, parent_field bool, str False, None Build the total row for a tree report. are_default_filters bool True Use the saved filters of a Custom Report. js_filters list None Filter definitions from the client, used to check filter permissions when validate_filters is off.

docs.title: Permissions and roles
docs.text:
get_report_doc() checks these before a run:

  1. Report.is_permitted(). The user must have one of the roles in the roles table (or in a Custom Role for the report). An empty table allows all users.
  2. The user has report permission on ref_doctype.
  3. The report is not disabled.

A new report that is not standard gets the permlevel 0 roles of ref_doctype in roles (set_doctype_roles). After the run, get_filtered_data() removes rows with Link values that the user's user permissions do not allow. Still check permissions in execute. Use frappe.get_list, or frappe.only_for("System Manager") for admin reports.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result in a Prepared Report document with a file attachment. Use it for slow reports.

  • Set prepared_report on the Report to always run it in the background.
  • A Script Report that runs for more than 15 seconds turns on prepared_report by itself. Set disable_prepared_report_automation to stop this.
  • The job runs on the long queue. timeout on the Report sets the job timeout. The default is 1500 seconds (REPORT_TIMEOUT).
  • run() returns the last completed result for the same filters and user. Users start a new run with "Generate New Report" (frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report).
  • The user gets a notification when the job is done.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• run() is read-only (@frappe.read_only). Do not write to the database in execute.
  • Use the same fieldname in columns and row dicts. Rows with other keys show empty cells.
  • A Query Report cannot skip a condition when a filter is empty. Use a Script Report for optional filters.
  • add_total_row adds a list row at the end of result. Code that reads result must handle it.
  • The report name, the folder name and the JS key must match. The folder name is the scrubbed report name.

docs.title: Jobs, Realtime and Caching
docs.text:
Run background jobs and scheduled tasks, push realtime events and cache data.

Page What it covers Background Jobs Run code outside the web request with frappe.enqueue, enqueue_doc and enqueue_task, on RQ queues served by bench workers. Scheduler Run functions on a schedule with the scheduler_events hook, Scheduled Job Type records and the bench schedule process. Realtime Push events from the server to browsers with publish_realtime, Socket.IO rooms and frappe.realtime.on, and add custom realtime handlers. Caching Cache data in Redis with frappe.cache, read documents with get_cached_doc and get_cached_value, and use the request_cache, site_cache and redis_cache decorators.

docs.title: Background Jobs
docs.text: Use a background job when work takes longer than a web request should wait: bulk updates, imports, reports, emails, calls to slow external services. Frappe puts the job on a Redis queue (RQ). A worker process (bench worker) takes the job and runs it in a fresh site context. Use frappe.enqueue for plain jobs. Use frappe.enqueue_task when the user must see the job, its progress and its result in the desk.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Queue: a named RQ queue. Frappe has three built-in queues: short, default and long. You can add more in common_site_config.json (see Queues and timeouts).
  • Worker: a process that takes jobs from one or more queues. Start it with bench worker. In production, supervisor or systemd runs the workers (see Deployment).
  • Job ID: every job has an ID. Frappe adds the site name as a prefix, so the ID my_job becomes <site>||my_job. If you do not give an ID, Frappe makes a UUID.
  • RQ Job: a virtual DocType that shows jobs in Redis. Open it at /desk/rq-job. It shows the status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled, canceled), arguments, timeout and exception.
  • Background Task: a normal DocType that frappe.enqueue_task creates. It keeps status, progress, stage, result and exception in the database. It is shown to the user who started it.

docs.title: Enqueue a function
docs.text:
# sample_app/sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist()
def recalculate_rates(category: str):
    frappe.only_for("System Manager")
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.recalculate_item_rates",
        queue="long",
        timeout=1800,
        category=category,  # passed to the job as a keyword argument
    )

# sample_app/sample_app/jobs.py
import frappe


def recalculate_item_rates(category: str):
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Item", {"category": category}, pluck="name"):
        item = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", name)
        item.rate = item.rate * 1.1
        item.save()

You can pass the dotted path as a string or the function object. All extra keyword arguments go to the function. They must be picklable.

What the worker does for each job (execute_job in frappe/utils/background_jobs.py):

  1. Connects to the site and sets the user to the user who enqueued the job (frappe.session.user at enqueue time).
  2. Sets frappe.job with site, method, job_name, kwargs and user.
  3. Runs every before_job hook.
  4. Runs the function.
  5. Commits the transaction if the function returns. Rolls back, writes an Error Log and raises again if it fails.
  6. Runs every after_job hook.

The job does not check permissions for you. The job runs with the roles of the user who enqueued it, so check permissions in the whitelisted method before you enqueue.

docs.title: Retries on deadlock
docs.text: If the function raises a deadlock, a lock wait timeout, or frappe.RetryBackgroundJobError, the worker rolls back and runs the function again. It tries up to 5 more times and waits 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 seconds between attempts. For other retries, pass an rq.Retry object as rq_retry.

docs.title: Enqueue after commit
docs.text:
When the job reads a document that the current request creates, enqueue it after commit. Otherwise the worker can start before the data is in the database.

def on_submit(self):
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.notify_order",
        order=self.name,
        enqueue_after_commit=True,
    )

With enqueue_after_commit=True, frappe.enqueue returns None. If the transaction rolls back, the job is not queued.

docs.title: Deduplicate jobs
docs.text:
Give a job_id and set deduplicate=True to skip the call when the same job is queued or running.

frappe.enqueue(
    "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.rebuild_index",
    queue="long",
    job_id="sample_rebuild_index",
    deduplicate=True,
)

If a job with that ID is queued or started, frappe.enqueue writes a log line and returns None. If a finished or failed job with that ID exists, Frappe deletes it and queues a new one. deduplicate=True without job_id raises an error.

Check a job from code:

from frappe.utils.background_jobs import get_job_status, is_job_enqueued

is_job_enqueued("sample_rebuild_index")  # True while queued or started
get_job_status("sample_rebuild_index")   # rq JobStatus, or None if not found

Pass the ID without the site prefix. These functions add it.

docs.title: Run a controller method in the background
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue_doc loads the document in the worker and calls one of its methods.

frappe.enqueue_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001", "send_reminders", queue="short", timeout=300)

The worker calls frappe.get_doc(doctype, name).<method>(**kwargs). The default timeout of enqueue_doc is 300 seconds.

docs.title: The frappe.task decorator
docs.text:
@frappe.task(...) adds an enqueue attribute to a function. The decorator arguments become frappe.enqueue arguments.

@frappe.task(queue="long", timeout=1800)
def rebuild_index(category=None):
    ...


rebuild_index.enqueue(category="Hardware")

docs.title: User-facing tasks with frappe.enqueue_task
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue_task wraps frappe.enqueue. It also creates a Background Task document, sends task_update realtime events to the user, and stores the result.

task = frappe.enqueue_task(
    "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.export_orders",
    task_name="Export orders",
    queue="long",
    ref_doctype="Sample Order",
    ref_docname="SO-00001",
    customer="Customer A",
)
task.task_id  # UUID, also the RQ job ID unless you pass job_id

Inside the job, get the task with frappe.get_current_task() and report progress:

# sample_app/sample_app/jobs.py
import frappe


def export_orders(customer):
    task = frappe.get_current_task()
    orders = frappe.get_all("Sample Order", {"customer_name": customer}, pluck="name")
    for i, name in enumerate(orders):
        ...
        task.publish_progress(i * 100 / len(orders), stage=f"Order {name}")
    return {"count": len(orders)}  # stored as JSON in Background Task.result

frappe.get_current_task() returns None outside an enqueue_task job.

Background Task methods you can call in the job:

Method Description publish_progress(percent, stage=None) Sends progress (0 to 100). Calls below 100 are throttled to one each 0.2 seconds. update_stage(stage) Sends a stage text without a number. store_result(result) Saves a JSON result now. attach_file(file_name, content, is_private=True, doctype=None, docname=None) Makes a File attached to the reference document or to the task. Returns the file URL.

Status values: Queued, Running, Completed, Failed, Cancelled. Whitelisted methods in frappe/core/doctype/background_task/background_task.py:

  • stop_task(task_id): the owner or a System Manager can cancel a task.
  • retry_task(task_id): retries a Failed or Cancelled task.

The fields allow_user_cancellation and allow_user_retry control what the owner can do. Log Settings deletes Background Task rows after 7 days by default.

docs.title: enqueue_task parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description method str or callable required Function to run. task_name str the method path Name shown to the user. queue str "default" Queue name. timeout int queue timeout Seconds before the job is stopped. ref_doctype, ref_docname str None Document the task belongs to. deduplicate, job_id bool, str False, None Same as frappe.enqueue. enqueue_after_commit bool True Queue the job after the current transaction commits. now bool False Run in the current process. on_success, on_failure callable or str None Called with the arguments the callback accepts from task, result or exception, and the job kwargs. retry_on, max_retries tuple, int (), 0 Retry through RQ when the job raises one of these exceptions. show_progress_bar bool True Show a progress bar in the desk. allow_user_cancellation bool True The owner can stop a running task. allow_user_retry bool True The owner can retry a failed task. at_front, at_front_when_starved bool False Same as frappe.enqueue.

Note

enqueue_task defaults to enqueue_after_commit=True. frappe.enqueue defaults to False.

docs.title: frappe.enqueue parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description method str or callable required Function to run. queue str "default" Queue name. Must be a known queue, or frappe.enqueue raises ValidationError. timeout int queue timeout Seconds before RQ stops the job. event str None Label stored with the job. Used by bench purge-jobs --event. is_async bool True False runs the job in the current process. Deprecated outside tests, use now. now bool False Run the function now with frappe.call, in the current process and transaction. enqueue_after_commit bool False Queue the job only after the current transaction commits. on_success callable None RQ success callback. on_failure callable truncate_failed_registry RQ failure callback. at_front bool False Put the job at the front of the queue. job_id str UUID Job ID. Frappe adds <site>|| before it. deduplicate bool False Do not queue if a job with job_id is queued or started. at_front_when_starved bool False Put the job at the front when more than 16 jobs wait in the queue. rq_retry rq.Retry None RQ retry policy. job_name str None Deprecated. Use job_id. **kwargs Arguments for the function.

Return value: the rq.job.Job. It is None when the job is deduplicated or queued after commit. With now=True, it is the return value of the function.

docs.title: Queues and timeouts
Workers and CLI
docs.text:
Command Description bench worker Start a worker for all queues. bench worker --queue short,default Start a worker for some queues. Other options: --burst (exit when the queues are empty), --strategy round_robin\|random, --quiet, -u/--rq-username, -p/--rq-password. bench worker-pool --num-workers 4 Start a pool of workers (experimental). bench doctor Show scheduler status and the number of workers online. bench --site <site> show-pending-jobs Show jobs that wait in the queues. bench purge-jobs --site <site> [--queue] [--event] Delete pending jobs.

Workers run with a lower CPU priority than web processes. The default niceness increment is 10. Change it with background_process_niceness in common_site_config.json.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key Default Description workers none Extra queues and their timeouts. common_site_config.json only. max_queued_jobs 500 Queue size at which frappe.enqueue fails. rq_job_failure_ttl 7 days Seconds to keep failed jobs in Redis. rq_results_ttl 600 Seconds to keep finished job results in Redis. rq_failed_jobs_limit 1000 Maximum number of failed jobs kept per queue. background_process_niceness 10 CPU niceness increment for workers and the scheduler. use_rq_auth, rq_username, rq_password off Connect to the queue Redis with an ACL user.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not pass documents or open files as arguments. Pass names and load the data in the job.
  • A job that runs with now=True shares the caller's transaction. It does not commit.
  • The worker commits only when the job ends. A long loop holds its writes until then. Commit in batches if you must, with frappe.db.commit().
  • Code changes do not reach running workers. Restart the workers after you deploy.
  • If you call frappe.db.commit() and then read in the same process, MariaDB can show you an old snapshot. Commit or roll back again before you read data that a worker wrote.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text: Use a cache when your code reads the same data many times and the data changes rarely: settings, master records, computed lookups. Frappe has a Redis cache shared by all processes of the bench (frappe.cache), helpers that cache whole documents in it, and decorators that cache function results per request, per process or in Redis. Pick the smallest scope that works, and always plan how the cache gets cleared.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text: Tool Stored in Lives Shared across processes @request_cache frappe.local.request_cache One request or job No @site_cache Process memory Until ttl or clear_cache() No frappe.cache / @redis_cache Redis (redis_cache URL) Until expiry or delete Yes for frappe.cache. @redis_cache builds its key with Python hash(), which differs per process for strings, so calls with string arguments do not share results across workers. frappe.get_cached_doc / get_cached_value Redis 1 hour, or until the document is saved Yes frappe.client_cache Process memory + Redis 10 minutes local, invalidated by Redis Yes (internal use)

docs.title: frappe.cache
docs.text:
frappe.cache is a RedisWrapper (a subclass of redis.Redis). Values are pickled, so you can store dicts, lists and documents.

frappe.cache.set_value("sample_app:rates", {"Hardware": 10}, expires_in_sec=3600)
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates")

# compute and store the value when it is missing
rates = frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates", generator=load_rates)

frappe.cache.delete_value("sample_app:rates")
frappe.cache.delete_keys("sample_app:")  # every key that starts with the prefix

Keys are namespaced by site. frappe.cache.make_key("k") returns <db_name>|k. Options on most methods:

  • user=True adds user:<current user>: to the key. Pass a user ID to use another user.
  • shared=True uses the key as given, with no site prefix. All sites on the bench see it.
Method Description set_value(key, val, user=None, expires_in_sec=None, shared=False) Store a value. Returns the size in bytes. get_value(key, generator=None, user=None, expires=False, shared=False) Read a value. Calls generator on a miss and stores the result. delete_value(keys, user=None, make_keys=True, shared=False) Delete one key or a list of keys. delete_keys(key) Delete all keys that start with key. get_keys(key) List keys that start with key. exists(*names, user=None, shared=None) Count of keys that exist. expire_key(key, time) Set a TTL in seconds. hset(name, key, value), hget(name, key, generator=None), hdel(name, keys), hgetall(name) Hash operations, with the site prefix. lpush, rpush, lpop, rpop, llen, lrange, ltrim, sadd, srem, smembers List and set operations.

get_value also keeps the value in frappe.local.cache for the rest of the request. A second read in the same request does not go to Redis. Pass expires=True for keys with a TTL so the local copy is not kept.

If Redis is not reachable, set_value and get_value do not raise. get_value returns None, or the generator result.

Deprecated

frappe.cache() (called as a function) is deprecated. Use frappe.cache.

docs.title: Cached documents
docs.text:
settings = frappe.get_cached_doc("System Settings")
item = frappe.get_cached_doc("Sample Item", "Laptop")
rate = frappe.get_cached_value("Sample Item", "Laptop", "rate")
values = frappe.get_cached_value("User", "user1@example.com", ["first_name", "user_type"], as_dict=True)
time_zone = frappe.get_single_value("System Settings", "time_zone")
  • get_cached_doc takes the same arguments as frappe.get_doc. It stores the document in Redis for 1 hour under document_cache::<doctype>::<name>.
  • Saving or deleting the document clears its cache entry (Document.clear_cache). The entry is cleared again after commit and after rollback.
  • Clear it yourself with frappe.clear_document_cache(doctype, name). Without name, it clears all cached documents of the DocType.
  • get_cached_value returns None if the document does not exist.
  • frappe.get_single_value(doctype, fieldname) reads a field of a Single DocType through get_cached_value.
  • These functions do not check permissions.

Warning

frappe.db.set_value and frappe.db.set_single_value clear the document cache. Raw SQL (frappe.db.sql) and frappe.qb updates do not. After such writes, call frappe.clear_document_cache.

docs.title: Decorators
docs.text: All three are in frappe.utils.caching. frappe.request_cache and frappe.site_cache are aliases.

docs.title: request_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import request_cache


@request_cache
def get_item_rate(item: str) -> float:
    return frappe.db.get_value("Sample Item", item, "rate")

Calls with the same arguments in one request or job run once. Arguments must be hashable. Unhashable arguments skip the cache.

docs.title: site_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import site_cache


@site_cache(ttl=300, maxsize=128)
def get_category_map() -> dict:
    return dict(frappe.get_all("Sample Item", fields=["name", "category"], as_list=True))


get_category_map.clear_cache()  # clear for all sites in this process

The key includes the site, so sites do not share results. The cache is per process: each web worker and background worker has its own copy, and clear_cache() only clears the current process. frappe.clear_cache() clears all site_cache entries in the current process. When maxsize is reached, the oldest entry is removed.

docs.title: redis_cache
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.caching import redis_cache


@redis_cache(ttl=600)
def get_open_order_count(customer: str) -> int:
    return frappe.db.count("Sample Order", {"customer_name": customer, "status": "Open"})


get_open_order_count.clear_cache()
Argument Default Description ttl 3600 Seconds to keep each result. user None True caches one result for each session user. shared False True shares the results across sites.

The cache key is <module>.<function>::<hash of arguments>. clear_cache() deletes every result of the function. A None result is cached too.

docs.title: http_cache
docs.text: @http_cache(public=False, max_age=None, stale_while_revalidate=None) sets a Cache-Control header on GET responses of a whitelisted method. It does not cache on the server.

docs.title: client_cache
docs.text: frappe.client_cache keeps hot keys in process memory and uses Redis client-side caching to invalidate them. Frappe uses it for hooks, schema and settings. The docstring says it is internal and can change without notice. Use frappe.cache in apps. It has get_value, set_value, delete_value, delete_keys and get_doc. The local TTL is 10 minutes and the default size is 1024 keys. client_cache_max_bytes in site config limits its memory.

docs.title: Clear the cache
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-cache
bench --site frappe.localhost clear-website-cache

frappe.clear_cache()                       # all site keys, site_cache, client_cache
frappe.clear_cache(doctype="Sample Item")  # DocType meta and related caches
frappe.clear_cache(user="user1@example.com")  # user caches (roles, permissions, defaults)

A full frappe.clear_cache() deletes all Redis keys of the site except keys that match the persistent_cache_keys hook. Then it runs every clear_cache hook.

# sample_app/hooks.py
persistent_cache_keys = ["sample_app:rates*"]  # kept by frappe.clear_cache()
clear_cache = "sample_app.cache.clear_sample_cache"  # called by frappe.clear_cache()

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Never cache data that depends on permissions in a key that other users can read. Use user=True.
  • Changes from site_cache do not reach other processes. Do not use it for data that users edit.
  • Cached documents are copies. Changing a cached document does not change the database. Use frappe.get_doc when you will save.
  • Do not cache large values in client_cache. It is sized for values of about 4 KB.

docs.text:

  • Database

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: Use realtime events to push data from the server to open browser tabs: a progress bar, a refresh after a background job, a message to one user. Server code calls frappe.publish_realtime. Frappe publishes the event on the Redis channel events. The Socket.IO server (bench socketio) reads the channel and sends the event to the browsers in the target room. Browser code listens with frappe.realtime.on.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
• Event: a name, such as doc_update or sample_order_ready, and a JSON message.
  • Room: a group of sockets on one site. The server sends each event to one room.
  • Socket.IO server: a separate process. It listens on socketio_port (default 9000). There are two backends: the Node server apps/frappe/socketio.js and the Python server python -m frappe.realtime.server. The bench socketio command picks one from the socketio_backend key in common_site_config.json (node by default, or python).

docs.title: Rooms
docs.text:
Room Who is in it How a socket joins user:<user> All sockets of that user on the site On connect website All sockets on the site, guests too On connect all Sockets of System Users on the site On connect doctype:<doctype> Sockets that show a list of that DocType doctype_subscribe, needs read permission doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that have the form open doc_subscribe, needs read permission open_doc:<doctype>/<name> Sockets that view the form now. Used for doc_viewers. doc_open task_progress:<task_id> Sockets that follow a task task_subscribe

The desk subscribes for you. A form subscribes to its document on load. A list view subscribes to its DocType.

docs.title: Publish from the server
docs.text:
frappe.publish_realtime(
    event="sample_order_ready",
    message={"order": "SO-00001", "status": "Ready"},
    user="user1@example.com",
    after_commit=True,
)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Name Type Default Description event str "task_progress" if a task ID is set, else "global" Event name. message dict {} JSON message. room str see below Room name. Overrides the other targets. user str None Send to the room user:<user>. doctype, docname str None Send to the room doc:<doctype>/<docname>. task_id str frappe.local.task_id Send to the room task_progress:<task_id>. Forces after_commit=False. after_commit bool False Send only after the transaction commits. Dropped on rollback. Duplicate events are sent once.

When room is not given, the first match wins: task_id, then user, then doctype and docname. If none is given, the event goes to the all room (System Users of the site).

Special cases:

  • msgprint without user goes to the current user.
  • list_update always goes to doctype:<doctype>. The DocType comes from doctype or from message["doctype"].
  • docinfo_update always goes to doc:<doctype>/<docname>.

Use after_commit=True when the browser reloads data after the event. Otherwise the browser can read the database before your changes are committed.

docs.title: Named helpers
docs.text:
frappe.realtime has one helper for each room. Each calls publish_realtime and takes after_commit as a keyword-only argument.

from frappe.realtime import (
    publish_task_progress,
    publish_to_all,
    publish_to_doc,
    publish_to_doctype,
    publish_to_room,
    publish_to_user,
    publish_to_website,
)

publish_to_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001", "sample_order_ready", {"status": "Ready"}, after_commit=True)
publish_to_doctype("Sample Order", "sample_orders_changed")
publish_to_room("doc:Sample Order/SO-00001", "sample_order_ready")

publish_task_progress(task_id, message) has no event argument. It sends task_progress.

docs.title: Progress bar
docs.text:
frappe.publish_progress sends the progress event. The desk shows a progress dialog.

def import_items(rows):
    for i, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        ...
        frappe.publish_progress(i * 100 / len(rows), title="Importing items", description=f"Row {i}")

Signature: publish_progress(percent, title=None, doctype=None, docname=None, description=None, task_id=None). With doctype and docname, everyone with the form open sees the progress. Without them, only the current user sees it.

For jobs that the user must follow, use frappe.enqueue_task. It sends task_update events for you (see Background Jobs).

docs.title: Events the framework sends
docs.text:
Event Room When Message doc_update doc:<doctype>/<name> After a document is saved (notify_update), after commit doctype, name, modified list_update doctype:<doctype> Same, for DocTypes that are not single, child or read-only doctype, name, user docinfo_update doc:<doctype>/<name> A Comment or Communication on the document changes varies doc_viewers open_doc:<doctype>/<name> A user opens or closes the form doctype, docname, users msgprint user:<user> frappe.msgprint(..., realtime=True) message progress user or doc room frappe.publish_progress percent, title, description task_update user:<user> Background Task status or progress changes task_id, task_name, status, progress, stage

notify_update does not send events during import, patch, migrate and install. doc.db_set(..., notify=True) also calls it.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
bench --site frappe.localhost publish-realtime sample_event --message '{"status": "Open"}' --user Administrator

Options: --message, --room, --user, --doctype, --docname, --after-commit. The message is sent as a string.

docs.title: Listen in the browser
docs.text:
// sample_app/public/js/sample_order.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {
    refresh(frm) {
        frappe.realtime.off("sample_order_ready");
        frappe.realtime.on("sample_order_ready", (data) => {
            if (data.order === frm.doc.name) {
                frm.reload_doc();
            }
        });
    },
});

Client API (frappe.realtime, also frappe.socketio):

Method Description on(event, callback) Listen for an event. Connects the socket if needed. off(event, callback) Stop listening. Without callback, it removes only one listener for the event, because Frappe passes undefined on to the Socket.IO emitter. emit(event, ...args) Send an event to the server. doctype_subscribe(doctype) / doctype_unsubscribe(doctype) Join or leave doctype:<doctype>. doc_subscribe(doctype, name) / doc_unsubscribe(doctype, name) Join or leave doc:<doctype>/<name>. task_subscribe(task_id) / task_unsubscribe(task_id) Join or leave task_progress:<task_id>.

The client restores its DocType and document subscriptions after a reconnect. If disable_async is set in site config, the client does not connect.

docs.title: Custom handlers (Python backend)
docs.text:
With the Python backend, an app can handle events that the browser emits. Put the handlers in <app>/realtime/handlers.py. The server imports this module for each installed app at startup. A handler runs only for sockets on sites where its app is installed.

# sample_app/sample_app/realtime/handlers.py
from frappe.realtime import Socket, realtime


@realtime.on("sample_order_subscribe")
async def sample_order_subscribe(socket: Socket, order: str) -> dict:
    allowed = await socket.has_permission("Sample Order", order)
    if allowed:
        await socket.join(f"sample_order:{order}")
    return {"subscribed": allowed}

frappe.realtime.emit("sample_order_subscribe", "SO-00001");

Then publish to the same room from server code: publish_to_room("sample_order:SO-00001", "sample_order_ready", {...}).

Rules:

  • The first argument is the Socket. The other arguments are what the client sent.
  • The return value answers the client's acknowledgement callback.
  • @realtime.on(event, frappe_context=False, allow_guest=False). With allow_guest=False, events from guests are dropped.
  • Write handlers as async def. A plain def handler runs in a worker thread and gets a blocking socket with the same methods without await.
  • frappe_context=True opens a site context with a database connection for each event. It needs a plain def handler. Use it only when you must query the database.
  • An import error in handlers.py stops the server at startup.

Socket attributes: site, user, user_type, installed_apps. Methods: join(room), leave(room), emit(event, data=None, room=None), has_permission(doctype, name=None), set(key, value), get(key, default=None). has_permission calls the web process over HTTP.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text:
All keys are in common_site_config.json.

Key Default Description socketio_port 9000 Port of the Socket.IO server. socketio_backend node node or python. Read by bench socketio. socketio_uds none Listen on this Unix socket instead of the port. socketio_worker_threads 4 Threads for blocking work in the Python server. redis_queue redis://127.0.0.1:11311 Redis that carries the events channel.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Events are not stored. A browser that is not connected when you publish misses the event.
  • A user sees events in user:<user> and all without a permission check. Do not put data there that the user must not read.
  • publish_realtime does nothing if Redis is down. It does not raise.
  • In a background job, publish after your writes commit, or use after_commit=True.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: Use the scheduler to run a function at fixed times: each few minutes, hourly, daily, or on a cron expression. You declare the function in the scheduler_events hook of your app. Frappe stores each entry as a Scheduled Job Type record. The bench schedule process checks these records and puts due jobs on a background queue. A worker then runs them.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. bench migrate (and app install) reads scheduler_events from every installed app. It creates or updates one Scheduled Job Type per method, and deletes records whose method is no longer in the hooks.
  2. The bench schedule process wakes up each 4 minutes by default (scheduler_tick_interval).
  3. For each site, it skips the site if the scheduler is inactive (see Enable and disable).
  4. For each Scheduled Job Type that is not stopped, it computes the next run from last_execution and the frequency. If the run is due, it enqueues the job.
  5. The job ID is scheduled_job||<Scheduled Job Type name>. A job that is still queued or running is not queued again.
  6. The worker runs the method, commits, and writes a Scheduled Job Log row (Start, Complete or Failed).

The scheduler only queues jobs. If no worker runs, no scheduled job runs.

docs.title: Declare scheduled events
docs.text:
# sample_app/hooks.py
scheduler_events = {
    "all": [
        "sample_app.tasks.sync_stock",
    ],
    "hourly": [
        "sample_app.tasks.send_reminders",
    ],
    "daily": [
        "sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders",
    ],
    "daily_long": [
        "sample_app.tasks.rebuild_rates",
    ],
    "weekly": [],
    "monthly": [],
    "cron": {
        "*/15 * * * *": ["sample_app.tasks.poll_service"],
        "30 2 * * 1-5": ["sample_app.tasks.weekday_report"],
    },
}

# sample_app/tasks.py
import frappe


def close_old_orders():
    for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Order", {"status": "Open", "docstatus": 0}, pluck="name"):
        frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name).add_comment("Comment", "Checked by scheduler")

The method takes no arguments. It runs as the user Administrator, the user that the scheduler process uses when it enqueues. Run bench migrate after you change scheduler_events.

docs.title: Event keys
docs.text:
The key in scheduler_events sets the frequency of the Scheduled Job Type. Frappe converts daily_long to Daily Long.

Key Frequency Runs Queue all All Each scheduler_interval seconds (default 240, so each 4 minutes) default hourly Hourly At minute 0 of each hour default hourly_long Hourly Long At minute 0 of each hour long hourly_maintenance Hourly Maintenance Each hour, at a minute offset that depends on the site long daily Daily At 00:00 default daily_long Daily Long At 00:00 long daily_maintenance Daily Maintenance Each day, at a minute offset that depends on the site long weekly Weekly Sunday 00:00 default weekly_long Weekly Long Sunday 00:00 long monthly Monthly 1st day of the month, 00:00 default monthly_long Monthly Long 1st day of the month, 00:00 long yearly, annual Yearly, Annual 1 January, 00:00 default cron Cron The cron expression (dict key) default, or the queue field

Times are in the system time zone of the site. The maintenance offset (0 to 59 minutes) comes from a hash of the site name. It spreads the load when many sites share one bench. Use the _maintenance keys for work that must run about once an hour or day but not at an exact time.

Cron expressions use the croniter syntax. An invalid expression fails validation on save with "Bad Cron Expression".

docs.title: Scheduled Job Type
docs.text:
Open the list at /desk/scheduled-job-type. Fields:

Field Description method Dotted path of the function. frequency See the table above. cron_format Cron expression. Required for Cron. queue Queue for Cron jobs. Empty means default. Cleared for other frequencies. stopped Check to stop this job. Migrate keeps this value. create_log Write a Scheduled Job Log for each run. Always on for frequencies other than All and Cron. last_execution Time of the last run. The next run is computed from it. server_script Set for jobs that come from a Server Script of type Scheduler Event.

Actions in the form (System Manager only): Execute queues the job now (execute_event). Skip Next Execution moves last_execution to the next run time (skip_next_execution).

Run a job now from the CLI. This runs it in the current process, not in a worker:

bench --site frappe.localhost trigger-scheduler-event sample_app.tasks.close_old_orders

docs.title: Enable and disable
docs.text:
The scheduler is inactive for a site when one of these is true:

  • maintenance_mode is set in site config.
  • pause_scheduler is set in site config.
  • disable_scheduler is set in site config.
  • System Settings > Enable Scheduler (enable_scheduler) is off.
Command Effect bench --site <site> enable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 1 in System Settings. bench --site <site> disable-scheduler Sets enable_scheduler = 0. bench --site <site> scheduler enable\|disable Same as the two commands above. bench --site <site> scheduler pause\|resume Sets or clears pause_scheduler in site_config.json. bench --site <site> scheduler status [-f json] Prints enabled or disabled. bench --site <site> set-maintenance-mode on\|off Sets maintenance_mode. Scheduled jobs do not run in maintenance mode. bench schedule Starts the scheduler process for all sites of the bench. bench doctor Shows scheduler status per site and workers online.

The whitelisted method frappe.utils.scheduler.activate_scheduler (Administrator only) enables the scheduler and clears pause_scheduler. It fails in maintenance mode.

Note

On Frappe Cloud, a site with no user activity for dormant_days (System Settings) runs scheduled jobs only once each 24 hours. This check is off in developer mode and on other hosts.

docs.title: Configuration keys
docs.text: Key File Default Description scheduler_tick_interval common_site_config.json 240 Seconds between scheduler checks. scheduler_interval site or common 240 Interval of all events, in seconds. Converted to whole minutes. pause_scheduler site unset Pause scheduling for the site. disable_scheduler site unset Disable scheduling for the site. maintenance_mode site unset Stops the scheduler and blocks writes.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A disabled app keeps its Scheduled Job Type rows, but its jobs do not run. See App State.
  • A job that is still running when its next run is due is skipped, not queued twice.
  • Long jobs on default hold up short ones. Use a _long key, or set queue on a cron job.
  • trigger-scheduler-event runs in your shell. Errors show there, not in a worker log.
