docs.title: Permissions and Security
docs.text:
Control access with permissions, authenticate clients and write secure code.

Page What it covers Permissions How the permission engine decides access from role permissions, permission levels, user permissions, sharing and app hooks, and how to check permissions in code. Authentication Authenticate HTTP requests with a session cookie, API key and secret, or an OAuth 2 bearer token, and how CSRF, two-factor login, guests and auth hooks work. Security Write secure Frappe app code - permission checks in whitelisted methods, safe SQL, escaping, private files, rate limits, CSRF, secrets and the risks of ignore_permissions.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Each request to a Frappe site runs as one user. frappe.session.user is that user, or Guest if the request is not authenticated. Frappe sets the user from one of these, in frappe/auth.py:

Method Header or cookie Use it for Session sid cookie Browsers, the desk and portal pages API key and secret Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret> Server-to-server scripts and integrations OAuth 2 Authorization: Bearer <access_token> Third-party apps that act for a user Auth hooks anything Custom schemes in your app

All requests on this page were sent with curl to http://frappe.localhost:8000.

docs.title: Session login
docs.text:
curl -s -c cookies.txt -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"usr": "user1@example.com", "pwd": "Sample-Pass-123!"}'

{"message": "Logged In", "home_page": "desk", "full_name": "User 1"}

The response sets the sid cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax) and the cookies system_user, full_name, user_id and user_lang. Send the cookie with later requests:

curl -s -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

usr is the email. It can also be the user name or the mobile number when System Settings allow_login_using_user_name or allow_login_using_mobile_number is set. Log out with POST /api/method/logout.

Failed logins return HTTP 401 and are written to the Activity Log. Repeated failures lock the user and the IP for a time (LoginAttemptTracker in frappe/auth.py). The login also checks the IP allowlist of the user (restrict_ip) and the login hours (login_after, login_before).

The login runs the before_login and on_login hooks. Logout runs on_logout. Each handler gets login_manager. See Hooks.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
For a cookie session, POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH requests must send the CSRF token of the session in the X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header (or as csrf_token in the form). Otherwise the request fails with frappe.CSRFTokenError (HTTP 400):

{"exception": "frappe.exceptions.CSRFTokenError: Invalid Request", "exc_type": "CSRFTokenError"}
  • The desk gets the token in frappe.csrf_token and frappe.call sends it for you.
  • A session gets a token the first time it is needed (frappe.sessions.get_csrf_token). A session that has no token yet is not checked.
  • Requests with token or bearer authentication have no session token, so the check does not apply.
  • Requests from an origin in the site config key allowed_referrers skip the check.

docs.title: Generate keys
docs.text:
A System Manager generates the keys for a user:

  1. Open the User in the desk.
  2. Open the API Access section.
  3. Click Generate Keys.
  4. Copy the API Secret from the dialog. It is shown only once.

From code or the API, call frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys. It requires the System Manager role and POST:

curl -s -b admin_cookies.txt -X POST \
  "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.core.doctype.user.user.generate_keys" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"user": "user1@example.com"}'

{"message": {"api_key": "1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8", "api_secret": "9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"}}

The API key is created once and does not change. Each call makes a new secret and the old secret stops working. The secret is stored encrypted in the api_secret Password field of the User.

docs.title: Use the keys
docs.text:
curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: token 1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

HTTP Basic with base64(api_key:api_secret) also works:

curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Basic $(printf '1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8:9f8e7d6c5b4a3f2' | base64)"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

A wrong key or secret returns HTTP 401 with "exc_type": "AuthenticationError". The failure is written to the Activity Log, at most once per interval for each user.

  • The request runs with the roles and permissions of that user. There is no separate scope.
  • The user must be enabled.
  • The restrict_ip allowlist of the user also applies.
  • No session is created and no cookie is set.
  • Two-factor authentication does not apply to token requests.

The header Frappe-Authorization-Source: <DocType> makes Frappe look up the key in another DocType instead of User. That DocType needs the fields api_key, api_secret, enabled and user. The request then runs as the value of user.

docs.title: OAuth 2
docs.text:
Frappe is an OAuth 2 and OpenID Connect provider. A third-party app gets an access token for a user and sends it as a bearer token. Set up the provider and clients in the desk. See Integrations.

Endpoint Path Authorization /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize Token /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token Revocation /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token Introspection /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.introspect_token User info (OpenID) /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_profile

The paths are in ENDPOINTS in frappe/integrations/oauth2.py.

docs.title: Authorization code flow
docs.text:
The example uses an OAuth Client with client_id <client_id>, scopes all openid, redirect URI http://localhost:9999/callback, grant type Authorization Code and response type Code.

  1. Send the user to the authorization endpoint. A guest is redirected to /login first.

    curl -s -i -b user_cookies.txt -G "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize" \
  --data-urlencode client_id=<client_id> --data-urlencode response_type=code \
  --data-urlencode scope=all --data-urlencode redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback \
  --data-urlencode state=xyz

    HTTP/1.1 302 FOUND
Location: http://localhost:9999/callback?code=<authorization_code>&state=xyz

    The user sees a Confirm Access page first, unless the client has Skip Authorization set.

  2. Exchange the code for tokens. Authenticate the client with HTTP Basic (client_id:client_secret) for the method Client Secret Basic.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -u "<client_id>:<client_secret>" \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code -d code=<authorization_code> \
  -d redirect_uri=http://localhost:9999/callback

    {"access_token": "<access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<refresh_token>"}

  3. Call the API with the access token.

    curl -s "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.auth.get_logged_user" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
# {"message":"user1@example.com"}

  4. When the token expires, get a new one with the refresh token. The old access token stops working.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token" \
  -u "<client_id>:<client_secret>" -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=<refresh_token>

    {"access_token": "<new_access_token>", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer",
 "scope": "all", "refresh_token": "<new_refresh_token>"}

  5. To end access, revoke the token. The endpoint always returns HTTP 200 with {}.

    curl -s -X POST "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token" \
  -u "<client_id>:<client_secret>" -d token=<new_access_token>

Tokens are stored as OAuth Bearer Token documents with a hash of the token. An unknown, expired or revoked token returns HTTP 401. A token of a disabled user raises frappe.AuthenticationError. The request runs with the roles of the user who approved the token.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
When 2FA applies to a user (System Settings enable_two_factor_auth and a role with Two Factor Authentication set), POST /api/method/login does not log in at once:

  1. The first login request checks the password. The response has tmp_id and a verification object with the method (OTP App, Email or SMS). The user is still Guest.
  2. Send the code: POST /api/method/login with tmp_id and otp. On success the session is created.

The tmp_id expires after 300 seconds for SMS and Email, and after 180 seconds for an OTP App that is set up. The logic is in frappe/twofactor.py.

docs.title: Guests
docs.text:
A request without credentials runs as Guest. The only role of Guest is Guest.

  • A guest can call only methods with @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True). Other methods return HTTP 403 with "Function ... is not whitelisted".
  • A guest can read documents only through permissions given to the Guest role.
  • Guest string arguments are sanitized for HTML unless the method sets xss_safe=True.

See Whitelisted methods.

docs.title: Custom authentication
docs.text:
The auth_hooks hook lists functions that run on every request after the built-in checks. A function can call frappe.set_user(user) to authenticate the request.

# sample_app/hooks.py
auth_hooks = ["sample_app.auth.validate_sample_header"]

# sample_app/auth.py
import frappe


def validate_sample_header():
    token = frappe.get_request_header("X-Sample-Token")
    if not token:
        return
    user = frappe.db.get_value("Sample Device", {"token": token, "enabled": 1}, "user")
    if user:
        form_dict = frappe.local.form_dict
        frappe.set_user(user)
        frappe.local.form_dict = form_dict

frappe.set_user resets frappe.local.form_dict. Save it before the call and put it back after, as the built-in token and OAuth checks in frappe/auth.py do. Without this, the request loses its arguments.

If a request has an Authorization header with two parts and no method sets a user, Frappe raises frappe.AuthenticationError (HTTP 401).

docs.title: Agent attribution
docs.text: A request with a token or a bearer token can send X-Frappe-Agent: <name>. Frappe records the name as the agent that acts for the user, and shows it in the Version log of changed documents. Cookie sessions ignore the header.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• An API secret gives full access as that user. Create a separate user with only the roles the integration needs.
  • generate_keys replaces the secret. Integrations that use the old secret stop working.
  • Do not send API keys in URLs. Use the Authorization header.
  • A cookie session that calls POST from a script must send X-Frappe-CSRF-Token.

docs.text:

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: The permission engine decides if a user can do an action on a DocType or on one document. Use this page when you write server code that reads or changes data for a user, or when your app must add its own access rules. To set up roles and rules in the desk, see Role permissions and User Permissions.

docs.title: How a decision is made
docs.text:
frappe.has_permission (in frappe/__init__.py) calls frappe.permissions.has_permission. The engine evaluates these layers in order:

  1. Administrator gets every permission. No other check runs.
  2. If the DocType is a child table, the check runs on the parent DocType. Pass parent_doctype when you do not pass a document.
  3. If the module of the DocType belongs to a disabled app, access is denied.
  4. Role permissions. The engine collects the DocPerm rows (or Custom DocPerm rows, if the DocType has any) at permission level 0 for the roles of the user. A right is granted if any row grants it.
  5. If you pass a document, the engine also applies:
    1. has_permission hooks. They can only deny.
    2. "If Owner" rules. Some rights apply only when doc.owner is the user.
    3. User Permissions on the document itself and on its Link fields.
  6. If access is still denied, the engine checks document sharing (DocShare). Only the rights read, write, share, submit, email, print and custom permission types can be shared.
  7. select is implied by read.

Without a document, the result answers "can the user do this on at least one document of this DocType". With a document, it answers for that document only.

docs.title: Rights
docs.text:
The standard rights are in frappe.permissions.std_rights:

select, read, write, create, delete, submit, cancel, amend, print, email, report, import, export, share.

A DocType can add custom rights with the Permission Type DocType. frappe.permissions.get_rights(doctype) returns the standard and the custom rights.

submit is always false on a DocType that is not submittable. import is always false when allow_import is off.

docs.title: Automatic roles
docs.text:
frappe.get_roles(user) adds roles based on the user type. You do not assign them:

Role Who has it Guest Everybody, including users who are not logged in All Every logged-in user, including website users Desk User System users (desk users) Administrator The Administrator user 
frappe.get_roles("user1@example.com")
# ['Sample Role', 'All', 'Guest', 'Desk User']

docs.title: frappe.has_permission
docs.text:
frappe.has_permission(
    doctype=None, ptype="read", doc=None, user=None, throw=False,
    *, parent_doctype=None, debug=False, ignore_share_permissions=False,
)
Name Type Default Description doctype str None DocType to check. Optional if you pass doc. ptype str "read" Right to check. doc Document or str None Document or document name. Enables document-level checks. user str current user User to check for. throw bool False Raise frappe.PermissionError instead of returning False. parent_doctype str None Required for a child DocType when you do not pass doc. debug bool False Collect the reason for each step in frappe.local.permission_debug_log. ignore_share_permissions bool False Do not grant access through sharing.

Output on the site, as user1@example.com (role Sample Role, which has read, write, create and delete on Sample Item and no rule on Sample Order):

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read")                  # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "write", doc="Laptop")   # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read")                 # False
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read", throw=True)     # raises frappe.PermissionError

When throw=True and access is denied for the current user, the engine also shows the reason with frappe.msgprint.

docs.title: Document methods
docs.text:
Method Description doc.has_permission(permtype="read", *, debug=False, user=None) Returns bool. Returns True if doc.flags.ignore_permissions is set. doc.check_permission(permtype="read") Raises frappe.PermissionError if not permitted. frappe.get_doc(doctype, name, check_permission="read") Loads the document and runs check_permission. True means "read".

doc.insert(), doc.save(), doc.submit(), doc.cancel() and frappe.delete_doc() check the matching right. Pass ignore_permissions=True, or set doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True, to skip the check. See Controllers.

docs.title: frappe.read_doc
docs.text:
frappe.read_doc(doctype, name=None, /) loads a document for display to the current user:

  1. It raises frappe.PermissionError if the user cannot read the document.
  2. It removes the values of fields at a permission level the user cannot read.
  3. It masks fields that are masked for the user.

The result cannot be saved. doc.save() raises an error that says the document has fields removed for reading. Use frappe.get_doc for documents you change. The REST API uses frappe.read_doc for GET /api/resource/<doctype>/<name> and GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>.

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.read_doc("Sample Order", "SO-00001")   # raises frappe.PermissionError

Version

frappe.read_doc exists only in develop.

docs.title: frappe.only_for
docs.text:
frappe.only_for(roles, message=False) raises frappe.PermissionError if the current user has none of the roles. Administrator always passes. Set message=True to show a "This action is only allowed for ..." message.

frappe.only_for("System Manager")
frappe.only_for(["System Manager", "Sample Role"], message=True)

docs.title: Permission levels
docs.text:
Each field has a permlevel (default 0). A role can read or write fields at level N only if it has a DocPerm row at level N. Level 0 rights decide access to the document itself. Rights at higher levels only control groups of fields.

  • frappe.read_doc and the REST API remove values of fields the user cannot read.
  • frappe.get_list leaves out fields the user cannot read, also when you ask for *.
  • frappe.get_list raises frappe.PermissionError if you filter, sort or group by a field the user cannot read.
  • doc.save() resets fields at a level the user has no access to back to their stored values (Document.validate_higher_perm_levels). Administrator and ignore_permissions skip this.

docs.title: Permissions in list queries
docs.text:
frappe.get_list and frappe.qb.get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False) add conditions to the SQL query. The logic is in Engine.add_permission_conditions in frappe/database/query.py:

  1. The user needs select or read on the DocType, or the query raises frappe.PermissionError.
  2. If no role gives read or select, the query returns only documents shared with the user.
  3. If read is "If Owner" only, the query adds owner = <user>.
  4. Otherwise the query adds User Permission conditions for the DocType and its Link fields.
  5. The query adds the conditions from permission_query_conditions hooks and from Server Scripts of type Permission Query.
  6. If any condition from steps 3 to 5 applies, shared documents are added with OR.

frappe.get_all sets ignore_permissions=True. It skips all of the above.

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.get_list("Sample Order")    # raises frappe.PermissionError
frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="name")
# ['SO-00006', 'SO-00005', 'SO-00004', 'SO-00003', 'SO-00002', 'SO-00001']

After frappe.share.add("Sample Order", "SO-00002", "user1@example.com", read=1):

frappe.get_list("Sample Order", pluck="name")                         # ['SO-00002']
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "read", doc="SO-00002")         # True
frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "write", doc="SO-00002")        # False

docs.title: User Permissions in queries
docs.text:
A User Permission restricts a user to some documents of a DocType. It applies to that DocType and to every Link field that points to it, unless the field has ignore_user_permissions set.

from frappe.permissions import add_user_permission

add_user_permission("Sample Item", "Laptop", "user1@example.com")

frappe.set_user("user1@example.com")
frappe.get_list("Sample Item", pluck="name")                                 # ['Laptop']
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read", doc="Monitor")                  # False
frappe.get_list("Sample Item", pluck="name", ignore_user_permissions=True)   # all items

Helpers in frappe/permissions.py:

Function Description add_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False, applicable_for=None, is_default=0, hide_descendants=0) Creates a User Permission. Raises frappe.DoesNotExistError if the document does not exist. remove_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False) Deletes it. clear_user_permissions_for_doctype(doctype, user=None) Deletes all User Permissions for a DocType. get_user_permissions(user) Returns the User Permissions of a user, grouped by DocType.

docs.title: has_permission hook
docs.text:
Use the has_permission hook to deny access to single documents with Python logic. The hook runs only for document-level checks.

# sample_app/hooks.py
has_permission = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_has_permission",
}

# sample_app/permissions.py
def sample_order_has_permission(doc, ptype=None, user=None, debug=False):
    if ptype == "write" and doc.status == "Completed":
        return False
    return True

Rules:

  • The hook can only deny. It cannot grant a right that role permissions do not give.
  • Return True to allow. Every falsy value denies, including None. A function that ends without return denies access.
  • Handlers for "*" run for every DocType. Handlers run in reverse order, and the first denial stops the check.
  • The hook is called with frappe.call, so it receives only the arguments it declares from doc, ptype, user and debug.

Warning

The hook does not run for list queries. Add a matching permission_query_conditions hook, or frappe.get_list will show documents that has_permission denies.

docs.title: permission_query_conditions hook
docs.text:
Use permission_query_conditions to filter list queries. The function returns a SQL condition string, or a query builder criterion. An empty value adds no condition.

# sample_app/hooks.py
permission_query_conditions = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.permissions.sample_order_query",
}

# sample_app/permissions.py
import frappe


def sample_order_query(user, doctype=None):
    if user == "Administrator" or "System Manager" in frappe.get_roles(user):
        return ""
    return f"`tabSample Order`.`owner_user` = {frappe.db.escape(user)}"

Rules:

  • The function receives user and the keyword argument doctype.
  • The engine wraps a string in parentheses and joins all conditions with AND.
  • The hook also runs for Administrator. Return an empty string for users that must see everything.
  • Escape every value with frappe.db.escape. The string goes into the SQL as it is.

docs.title: Custom permission types
docs.text: The Permission Type DocType adds a right to one DocType. Check it like a standard right: frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "approve", doc=doc). Custom rights can also be shared.

docs.title: Ignore permissions safely
docs.text:
Code Effect frappe.get_all(...) No permission conditions. frappe.get_list(..., ignore_permissions=True) Same as frappe.get_all. doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True), doc.save(ignore_permissions=True) Skips the right check for this call. doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True Skips the right check for all later actions on this object. frappe.db.* methods Never check permissions.

Arguments that come from an HTTP request never reach your function as ignore_permissions or flags. frappe.get_newargs removes them before the call. Make sure you do not read them from frappe.form_dict.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.get_all and frappe.db.* return data the user may not see. In a whitelisted method, use frappe.get_list, or check frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True) first.
  • A has_permission hook that returns None denies access.
  • A permission_query_conditions hook without an Administrator check also filters the list for Administrator.
  • has_permission without doc returns True if the user can access at least one document. It does not apply User Permissions or hooks.
  • Sharing overrides User Permissions and query hooks in list queries.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Every whitelisted method is an HTTP endpoint. Any logged-in user, and with allow_guest any visitor, can call it with any arguments. This page lists the rules that keep app code safe. The rules come from code_review.md and AGENTS.md in the frappe repository, and each one is checked against the code.

docs.title: Check permissions in whitelisted methods
docs.text:
Frappe checks that the method is whitelisted. It does not check permissions on the documents that your method reads or changes. Do it yourself, before you read data.

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["GET"])
def get_order(name: str):
    doc = frappe.read_doc("Sample Order", name)
    return doc.as_dict()


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def close_order(name: str):
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    doc.check_permission("write")
    doc.status = "Closed"
    doc.save()
API Checks frappe.read_doc(doctype, name) Raises PermissionError without read permission. Removes fields the user cannot read. The returned document cannot be saved. frappe.get_doc(doctype, name) No check on load. doc.save(), doc.insert(), doc.submit() and doc.delete() check permission, unless ignore_permissions is set. doc.check_permission(ptype) Raises PermissionError. frappe.has_permission(doctype, ptype, doc=None, user=None, throw=False) Returns True or False. Raises with throw=True. frappe.only_for(roles) Raises PermissionError if the user has none of the roles. frappe.get_list(...) Applies role permissions, user permissions and permission query conditions. frappe.get_all(...) No permission check. Use it only for internal queries. frappe.db.get_value(...), frappe.db.sql(...) No permission check.
  • Take the user from frappe.session.user. Never take the user ID from an argument.
  • Restrict methods for each endpoint. Use GET for reads and POST for writes. A GET endpoint that writes can be triggered by a link.
  • Put validation in the controller (validate, on_update, on_trash), not in one endpoint. Bulk actions, Data Import, the REST API and doc.save() skip a check that lives in one endpoint.

See Permissions for the permission engine.

docs.title: ignore_permissions
docs.text: doc.insert(ignore_permissions=True), doc.flags.ignore_permissions = True and frappe.get_all skip permission checks. Use them only for writes that the system makes, such as a log record, never for a value that comes from the request. Do not use ignore_permissions=True or a blanket role grant to fix a workflow. Give the user the right permission instead.

docs.title: SQL injection
docs.text:
Use the ORM or the query builder. They escape values.

# Good
frappe.get_list("Sample Order", filters={"customer_name": customer}, fields=["name"])

Order = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Order")
frappe.qb.from_(Order).select(Order.name).where(Order.customer_name == customer).run()

# Good: values as parameters
frappe.db.sql("select name from `tabSample Order` where customer_name = %s", (customer,))

# Bad: value in the string
frappe.db.sql(f"select name from `tabSample Order` where customer_name = '{customer}'")
  • Pass values in the second argument of frappe.db.sql, never with f-strings or % formatting.
  • A field name or sort order from the request is not a value. Check it against frappe.get_meta(doctype).get_valid_columns() or a fixed list.
  • frappe.get_list rejects SQL functions as strings in fields. Use the dict form, for example {"COUNT": "*"}.
  • In Server Scripts, frappe.db.sql allows only read queries.

docs.title: XSS
docs.text:
Escape at render time, for the context of the output. Do not strip HTML from data at storage, because that loses data.

  • In Jinja templates, values are not escaped by default. Use {{ value | e }} for user data in HTML.
  • In Python, use frappe.utils.escape_html(text) for text in HTML, and frappe.utils.sanitize_html(html) for HTML that users write.
  • In desk JavaScript, use frappe.utils.escape_html(value) before you put a value into HTML.
  • For a guest method, Frappe sanitizes the arguments in frappe.form_dict unless the method is whitelisted with xss_safe=True. Use xss_safe=True only when the method escapes its output.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
• A file with is_private set is served from /private/files/. Frappe checks read permission on the File record, and logs the access. Guests always get 403.
  • The File permission allows Administrator, the owner, users the file is shared with, and users who can read the document that the file is attached to.
  • A public file (/files/...) is readable by anyone who knows the URL. Make uploads private when they hold personal or business data.
  • Frappe forces download, not display, for file types such as .html, .svg and .xml, so they cannot run scripts on the site domain.
  • Do not open a file path that comes from the request. Look up the File document and check its permission.

See Files.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text:
Every guest endpoint needs a rate limit. Use the rate_limit decorator below @frappe.whitelist:

# sample_app/api.py
import frappe
from frappe.rate_limiter import rate_limit


@frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True, methods=["POST"])
@rate_limit(limit=5, seconds=60 * 60)
def contact(email: str, message: str):
    ...

rate_limit(key=None, limit=5, seconds=86400, methods="ALL", ip_based=True, endpoint=None, user_based=False):

Name Default Description key None A form field name. Its value becomes part of the counter, for example an email address. limit 5 Requests allowed in the window. Can be a callable. seconds 86400 Window length. methods "ALL" HTTP methods to limit. ip_based True Count per client IP. user_based False Count per logged-in user. Guests are counted by IP. endpoint None Counter name. Default is the dotted path of the function.

Over the limit, Frappe raises RateLimitExceededError (HTTP 429). Counters are in Redis cache. Calls outside a request, such as tests and background jobs, are not limited.

For a guest method that must not be limited, write @frappe.whitelist(allow_guest=True, rate_limit=None). This marks the choice. Any other value for rate_limit raises TypeError.

The site-wide limit in site_config.json ("rate_limit": {"limit": <seconds>, "window": <seconds>}) is different. It limits the total request time of the site in each window, not the number of requests.

docs.title: CSRF
docs.text:
For a logged-in session, Frappe checks the CSRF token on POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH requests (validate_csrf_token in frappe/auth.py). The check runs only when the session holds a CSRF token. The desk sends the token in the X-Frappe-CSRF-Token header, or a form sends it as csrf_token. Requests whose Referer or Origin matches the allowed_referrers config also pass.

Do not set ignore_csrf in production. It turns the check off for all requests.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Store passwords and API secrets in Password fields. Frappe encrypts them with the site's encryption_key and stores them in __Auth. Read them with doc.get_password("fieldname") or frappe.utils.password.get_decrypted_password(doctype, name, fieldname).
  • Keep a copy of encryption_key from site_config.json. Without it, a restored backup cannot decrypt the passwords.
  • Never return a secret from an endpoint. Return a masked value or a boolean.
  • Put bench-wide secrets in site_config.json or common_site_config.json, not in the app repository. Read them with frappe.conf.<key>.
  • Do not log secrets or full request bodies with frappe.log_error.

docs.title: Other rules
docs.text:
• Fail loudly. Catch the specific exception. Do not wrap code in a blanket try/except.
  • Never destroy data in silence. Disable records instead of deleting them, and confirm bulk actions.
  • Server Scripts run restricted Python. Allow the Script Manager role only to trusted users. See Server Scripts and Client Scripts.

docs.title: Testing and Performance
docs.text:
Test apps and make them fast.

Page What it covers Testing Write and run tests for Frappe apps with UnitTestCase and IntegrationTestCase, test records, context managers, run-tests, run-parallel-tests and run-ui-tests. Performance Keep Frappe apps fast with indexes, cached reads, fewer queries, bulk operations and background jobs, and find slow code with the Recorder, the monitor log and query profiling.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Write code for tables with 100,000 rows or more. Most slow Frappe code makes too many queries, filters on columns without an index, or does long work inside a web request. This page shows the fixes and the tools to find the slow code. Measure before you change code, and measure again after.

docs.title: Keep work out of the hot path
docs.text:
Code that runs on every request, every save or every desk load affects all users.

  • Keep boot_session, before_request, doc_events on "*" and permission hooks fast. Do not query per record in them.
  • Read values the client needs on page load from frappe.boot, not with a server call on each form load.
  • Load JavaScript that few users need on first use, not in the main bundle.

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
• Set Index (search_index) on fields that you filter or sort by. Frappe adds the index on migrate.
  • Add a composite index in code with frappe.db.add_index(doctype, fields, index_name=None). Call it from a patch or after_migrate.
  • Add a unique constraint with frappe.db.add_unique(doctype, fields, constraint_name=None).
  • Sort by an indexed column. Every table of a parent DocType has an index on creation, and new DocTypes sort by creation.
# sample_app/patches/v1_0/add_order_indexes.py
import frappe


def execute():
    frappe.db.add_index("Sample Order", ["customer_name", "order_date"])

docs.title: Cached reads
docs.text:
API Use for frappe.get_cached_doc(doctype, name) Documents that change rarely, such as settings or masters. Cleared when the document is saved. frappe.get_cached_value(doctype, name, fieldname) One or more fields of such a document. frappe.db.get_single_value(doctype, fieldname) Values of a Single DocType. cache=True is the default. It caches the value on the database connection. frappe.db.get_value(doctype, name, fieldname, cache=True) Caches the value on the database connection, for a name given as a string.

Do not edit and save a document from get_cached_doc. Load it with frappe.get_doc. See Caching for frappe.cache, site_cache and redis_cache. Add a cache only when you measured the cost it removes, and know how it is cleared.

docs.title: Avoid N+1 queries
docs.text:
Do not call frappe.get_doc or frappe.db.get_value inside a loop over records. Get all rows in one query.

# Slow: one query per order
for name in frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="name"):
    order = frappe.get_doc("Sample Order", name)
    total += order.total

# Fast: one query
total = sum(frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="total"))

# Fast: aggregate in the database
frappe.get_all("Sample Order", fields=[{"SUM": "total", "as": "total"}])
  • Ask only for the fields you need. fields=["*"] reads all columns.
  • Use pluck="field" for a list of one field.
  • Set a limit for lists. frappe.get_list and frappe.get_all have no default limit and return all matching rows.
  • Get the rows of a child table in one query with frappe.get_all("Sample Order Item", filters={"parent": ["in", names]}).

docs.title: Bulk operations
docs.text:
API Description frappe.db.set_value(doctype, filters, field, value, update_modified=True) Updates all matching rows in one query. No controller events. frappe.db.bulk_update(doctype, doc_updates, *, chunk_size=100, update_modified=True) Updates many records with different values. doc_updates maps names to dicts of values. frappe.db.bulk_insert(doctype, fields, values, ignore_duplicates=False, *, chunk_size=1000) Inserts many rows. No controller events, no naming, no validation. frappe.qb.update(...) Query builder UPDATE with any condition.

These skip validate, on_update and doc_events. Use them in patches and imports where you control the data. Do not use frappe.db.delete in place of frappe.delete_doc for normal deletes, because it skips the link checks and hooks.

In patches, commit in batches when you change many rows, so that one transaction does not hold locks for a long time.

docs.title: Background jobs
docs.text:
Move work that takes more than a few seconds, calls to third-party services, and bulk operations to a background job.

frappe.enqueue(
    "sample_app.tasks.rebuild_totals",
    queue="long",
    enqueue_after_commit=True,
    order_name=doc.name,
)

See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Recorder
docs.text:
The Recorder captures requests and background jobs, with every SQL query, its call stack, EXPLAIN output and the document events that ran. Only Administrator can use it.

  1. Open /desk/recorder.
  2. Start the Recorder. Set the request path filter if you need only some requests.
  3. Do the slow action in another tab.
  4. Stop the Recorder and open the captured request.

The Recorder stops after 10 minutes. It stores data in Redis cache. For a captured request, the Recorder can suggest indexes, and Administrator can add them from the same page.

RecorderConfig options: record_requests, record_jobs, record_sql, capture_stack, capture_doc_events, profile (cProfile), explain, request_filter, jobs_filter.

docs.title: Monitor log
docs.text: Set "monitor": 1 in site_config.json. Frappe then records each request and job: path or method, duration in microseconds, status code, and the wait time of jobs. The scheduler writes the records from Redis to logs/monitor.json.log in the bench every few minutes (frappe.monitor.flush runs on the all event). Add your own keys to the current record with frappe.monitor.add_data_to_monitor(**kwargs).

docs.title: Query profiling
docs.text:
• frappe.db.sql(query, values, debug=True) prints the query and its time.
  • frappe.db.sql(query, values, explain=True) prints the EXPLAIN output.
  • bench --site frappe.localhost execute sample_app.tasks.rebuild_totals --profile runs a function with cProfile.
  • bench --site frappe.localhost run-tests --module ... --profile profiles tests.

docs.title: Guard performance in tests
docs.text:
IntegrationTestCase has context managers that fail when code gets slower:

from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase


class IntegrationTestSampleOrder(IntegrationTestCase):
    def test_list_query_count(self):
        with self.assertQueryCount(3):
            frappe.get_list("Sample Order", limit=20)

        with self.assertRowsRead(100):
            frappe.get_list("Sample Order", limit=20)

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A filter on an unindexed column scans the whole table. Check with explain=True.
  • frappe.get_all with no limit reads every row.
  • A site_cache is per process and is not cleared when data changes. Use it only for data that never changes while the process runs.
  • Long requests that write hold row locks until the commit. Other users then wait. Move long writes to a background job.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Frappe runs Python tests with the standard unittest module, through bench run-tests. Tests run against a real site and a real database. Use a separate test site, because integration tests write records to the database. UI tests run with Playwright through bench run-ui-tests.

docs.title: Test classes
docs.text:
Import the classes from frappe.tests:

Class Use for Database UnitTestCase Code that does not need the database, or needs it only to read Not rolled back IntegrationTestCase Code that reads and writes documents Connected to the site, test records created, rolled back after the class MockedRequestTestCase Code that makes HTTP requests. It mocks them with the responses library Same as IntegrationTestCase 
# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/test_sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase


class IntegrationTestSampleItem(IntegrationTestCase):
    def test_rate_is_saved(self):
        item = frappe.get_doc(
            {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Test Bolt", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 10}
        ).insert()
        self.assertEqual(item.rate, 10)

UnitTestCase adds these assertions: assertDocumentEqual(expected, actual), assertQueryEqual(first, second), assertSequenceSubset(larger, smaller). In setUpClass it sets cls.doctype (from the folder of the test file) and sets the user to Administrator.

IntegrationTestCase adds:

Name Description assertQueryCount(count, query_type=None) Context manager. Fails if more than count SQL queries run. assertRowsRead(count) Context manager. Fails if queries read more than count rows. assertRedisCallCounts(count, exact=False) Context manager. Fails if more Redis calls run. primary_connection(), secondary_connection() Context managers. Switch between two database connections to test concurrency. globalTestRecords Read-only map of the test records made so far. SHOW_TRANSACTION_COMMIT_WARNINGS Class attribute. Set True to print a warning when code commits.

If you override setUpClass, call super().setUpClass().

frappe.tests.utils.FrappeTestCase is deprecated for removal in v17. Use UnitTestCase or IntegrationTestCase.

docs.title: Context managers
docs.text:
Import them from frappe.tests. Each context manager also works as a decorator. Most are also attributes of UnitTestCase, so you can use self.<name>. change_settings and switch_site are attributes of IntegrationTestCase only.

Name Description set_user(user) Run as another user, then switch back. change_settings(doctype, settings_dict=None, /, commit=False, **settings) Change a Single DocType for the block, then restore. patch_hooks(overridden_hooks) Replace hook values for the block. freeze_time(time_to_freeze, is_utc=False) Freeze the clock with freezegun. enable_safe_exec() Turn on server scripts for the block. switch_site(site) Connect to another site for the block. debug_on(*exceptions) Start pdb on the given exceptions. timeout(seconds=30) Decorator. Fail if the function runs longer. Not a class attribute. timeout_context(seconds=30) Context manager form of timeout. trace_fields(doc_class, ...) Trace changes to fields of a document class. 
from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase, set_user


class IntegrationTestSampleOrder(IntegrationTestCase):
    def test_user_cannot_read_other_orders(self):
        with set_user("user1@example.com"):
            names = frappe.get_list("Sample Order", pluck="name")
        ...

    @IntegrationTestCase.change_settings("System Settings", {"float_precision": 3})
    def test_precision(self):
        ...

docs.title: Test records
docs.text:
When an IntegrationTestCase class starts, Frappe creates test records for its DocType and, recursively, for the DocTypes of its Link fields. It commits them. Frappe looks for records in this order (frappe/tests/utils/generators.py):

  1. A _make_test_records() function in the test module.
  2. A test_records attribute in the test module.
  3. A test_records.json file next to the DocType.
  4. A test_records.toml file next to the DocType.
# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/test_records.toml
[["Sample Item"]]
item_name = "_Test Sample Item"
category = "Hardware"
rate = 100

Control the dependencies with module variables:

EXTRA_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES = ["User"]
IGNORE_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES = ["Sample Role"]

The old names test_dependencies and test_ignore still work but show a deprecation warning. Records are loaded lazily. --skip-test-records is deprecated and has no effect.

docs.title: Run tests
docs.text:
Tests are off by default. Turn them on for the site once:

bench --site test.localhost set-config allow_tests true

run-tests also runs when the CI environment variable is set.

bench --site test.localhost run-tests --app sample_app
bench --site test.localhost run-tests --doctype "Sample Item"
bench --site test.localhost run-tests --module sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.test_sample_item
bench --site test.localhost run-tests --module sample_app.tests.test_api --test test_get_count
Option Description --app Run all tests of an app. --doctype Run the tests of a DocType. --module-def Run the tests of all DocTypes in a Module Def. --doctype-list-path Path to a .txt file with DocType names. --module Dotted path of a test module. --case Run one TestCase class of the module. --test Run one test method. Repeat for more. --test-category unit, integration or all (default). --test-service Run only tests that declare a required service, for example web-server. --failfast Stop at the first failure. --debug Disable output buffer and start pdb on errors. --profile Run with cProfile. --coverage Collect coverage. --junit-xml-output Write a JUnit XML report to this file. --skip-before-tests Do not run before_tests hooks. --lightmode Skip the full test setup.

--doctype, --doctype-list-path, --module-def and --module cannot be combined.

Frappe finds test files whose names start with test_ and end with .py. It groups tests into unit and integration by their class and runs unit tests first. Before integration tests, it runs the before_tests hooks of the app and creates records for global_test_dependencies.

# sample_app/hooks.py
before_tests = "sample_app.tests.setup.before_tests"

Detailed logs are written to a log file. run-tests prints its path at the start.

docs.title: Parallel tests in CI
docs.text:
bench --site test.localhost run-parallel-tests --app sample_app --build-number 1 --total-builds 4
Option Default Description --app frappe The app to test. --build-number 1 Number of this build. --total-builds 1 Number of builds that share the tests. --with-coverage off Write a coverage file. Also read from CAPTURE_COVERAGE. --use-orchestrator off Get tests from an orchestrator service. --dry-run off List tests, do not run them. --lightmode off Skip the test setup. --failfast off Stop at the first failure.

docs.title: UI tests
docs.text:
bench run-ui-tests <app> runs Playwright if the app has a Playwright config file. It installs @playwright/test and the browser on first use.

bench --site test.localhost run-ui-tests sample_app --headless
bench --site test.localhost run-ui-tests sample_app --headless --browser firefox --spec tests/ui/sample_item.spec.js
Option Description --headless Run without the Playwright UI. --browser chromium (default), firefox or webkit. --spec One spec file. --parallel-site Another site to run tests on. Repeat for more. Each site gets a worker.

Frappe sets BASE_URL to the site URL, and ADMIN_PASSWORD when the site has admin_password. Extra arguments go to playwright test. Apps with only a Cypress config still run with Cypress, with a warning. Cypress support is deprecated for removal in v17.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Do not run tests on a site with real data. Test records are committed.
  • Test as a normal user, not Administrator. Permission bugs do not show as Administrator. Use frappe.get_list in permission tests, not frappe.get_all.
  • Use example.com addresses for test users and emails.
  • Do not add if frappe.in_test branches to app code. Use patch_hooks, change_settings or mocks in the test.
  • A test that calls frappe.db.commit() makes its records permanent. The class rollback cannot undo them.

docs.title: Website and Portal
docs.text:
Build website pages, portal pages, routes and web forms.

Page What it covers Website Serve web pages from an app with www/ files, route rules, redirects, base templates, DocTypes with a web view, page renderers and Jinja hooks. Web Forms Ship standard Web Forms in an app, add a client script and Python context, control access and list settings, and use Web Form Request keys.

docs.title: Web Forms
docs.text: A Web Form shows fields of one DocType as a form on the website. Guests or website users fill it in, and Frappe saves a document of that DocType. Use a Web Form for sign-ups, requests and portal edit forms. For a page with your own layout, write a www page instead. The desk side of Web Forms is in Website (user guide).

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
WebFormPage serves each published Web Form (published = 1) at its route. These paths are matched (get_page_info_from_web_form in frappe/website/router.py):

Path Mode /<route> Redirects to /<route>/list if show_list is set, else to /<route>/new /<route>/new New document /<route>/list List of the user's documents /<route>/<name> Read view. Redirects to /edit if allow_edit is set /<route>/<name>/edit Edit view

A Web Form of a module that is disabled (see App State) is not served.

docs.title: Standard Web Forms in an app
docs.text:
A Web Form with is_standard = 1 is exported to the app when you save it in developer mode. on_update() writes the JSON and creates a .js and a .py stub the first time.

sample_app/sample_app/<module>/web_form/sample_order_request/
├── __init__.py
├── sample_order_request.json   # the Web Form document
├── sample_order_request.js     # client script (runs on the page)
├── sample_order_request.py     # get_context and get_list_context
└── sample_order_request.css    # optional styles
  1. Turn on developer_mode in site config.
  2. Create the Web Form in the desk and set Is Standard.
  3. Set module to a module of your app.
  4. Save. The files appear in the module folder.
  5. Commit the files. bench migrate syncs them to other sites.

Without developer mode, a standard Web Form cannot be changed. Only published can be toggled.

docs.title: Python context
docs.text:
Frappe calls get_context(context) of the module before it renders a standard form. Change context or return a dict.

# sample_app/sample_app/selling/web_form/sample_order_request/sample_order_request.py
import frappe


def get_context(context):
    context.introduction_text = f"Hello {frappe.utils.get_fullname()}"

get_list_context(context) in the same module changes the list at /<route>/list (frappe/www/list.py). For a custom DocType in a module that is not custom, the webform_list_context hook gives the list context. Frappe calls it with the module name.

docs.title: Client script
docs.text:
The .js file runs after the form is built. Frappe renders it with Jinja first, so you can use {{ }} values from the context. The client_script field of the Web Form also runs, through frappe.init_client_script. Both get the form as frappe.web_form.

// sample_app/sample_app/selling/web_form/sample_order_request/sample_order_request.js
frappe.ready(function () {
    frappe.web_form.on("customer_name", (field, value) => {
        frappe.web_form.set_value("status", value ? "Open" : "Draft");
    });

    frappe.web_form.validate = () => {
        if (!frappe.web_form.get_value("order_date")) {
            frappe.msgprint(__("Set the order date"));
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    };

    frappe.web_form.after_save = () => {
        frappe.show_alert(__("Request sent"));
    };
});
Member Description frappe.web_form.on(fieldname, handler) Run handler(field, value) when the field changes. frappe.web_form.get_value(fieldname) Get the current value. frappe.web_form.set_value(fieldname, value) Set a value. Returns a promise. frappe.web_form.set_df_property(fieldname, prop, value) Change a field property, for example hidden or reqd. frappe.web_form.validate Function that runs before save. Return false to stop the save. frappe.web_form.after_load Function that runs after the form is built. frappe.web_form.after_save Function that runs after a successful save. frappe.web_form.doc The document values.

The form extends frappe.ui.FieldGroup, so the other FieldGroup methods also work. Save calls frappe.website.doctype.web_form.web_form.accept with POST. That method is rate limited (rate_limit(key="web_form", limit=10, seconds=60)).

docs.title: Scripts and styles from hooks
docs.text:
Add JS or CSS to the Web Forms of any DocType, also forms from other apps:

# sample_app/hooks.py
webform_include_js = {"Sample Order": "public/js/sample_order_webform.js"}
webform_include_css = {"Sample Order": "public/css/sample_order_webform.css"}

Use "*" as the key in webform_include_js to add a script to every Web Form. These files are only added to standard Web Forms that have a .js (or .css) file.

docs.title: Access settings
docs.text:
Field Effect login_required Guests see a login prompt and cannot submit. allow_edit A user can edit a document they submitted. allow_multiple A user can submit more than one document. allow_delete A user can delete their documents. show_list Show /<route>/list with the user's documents. anonymous Save the document as Guest, also when a user is logged in. apply_document_permissions Check read and write with the DocType permissions instead of document ownership. allow_incomplete Save without mandatory fields. key_required Only holders of a Web Form Request key can open the form. allowed_embedding_domains Domains that may show the form in an iframe. Sent as Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors. max_attachment_size Upload limit in MB. success_url, success_message, success_title What the user sees after save.

set_access_flags() runs on validate. When neither login_required nor key_required is set, it clears allow_multiple, allow_edit, allow_delete and show_list. When allow_multiple is set without login_required, it clears allow_delete.

docs.title: List settings
docs.text: When show_list is set, /<route>/list shows the documents of the user. Set the columns in the list_columns table (Web Form List Column). Set list_title for the heading. condition_json holds the list filters. The list loads rows from frappe.website.doctype.web_form.web_form.get_web_form_list.

docs.title: Web Form Request keys
docs.text:
A Web Form Request gives one person access to a form with a secret key, without a login. Use it to ask a customer to fill in or correct one document.

  1. Set key_required on the Web Form. Set allow_edit too if the key must edit an existing document.
  2. Create a Web Form Request with web_form set. Frappe creates key on insert.
  3. Optional: set expires_on.
  4. Optional: set web_form_values (JSON, fills the form) and doc_values (JSON, set on the document on save).
  5. Share /<route>/new?web_form_request_key=<key>.

To edit one document, call frappe.website.doctype.web_form_request.web_form_request.create_for_document with web_form, docname and an optional expires_on. It checks write permission on the document and returns the edit URL.

from frappe.website.doctype.web_form_request.web_form_request import create_for_document

url = create_for_document("sample-order-request", "SO-00001")
# http://<site>/<route>/SO-00001/edit?web_form_request_key=...

After a key creates a document, it cannot create another one unless the Web Form has allow_multiple. The key stops working after expires_on.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Without apply_document_permissions, a user can open a document when they own it or when frappe.has_website_permission allows it. Review login_required, allow_edit and apply_document_permissions before you publish.
  • Link fields on a Web Form only show options the user may read, unless allow_read_on_all_link_options is set on the field.
  • The Web Form page is never cached (website = frappe._dict(no_cache=1) on the controller).
  • Frappe ships standard Web Forms you can read as examples: frappe/core/web_form/edit_profile and frappe/website/web_form/request_data.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Website
  • Form Scripts
  • Permissions
  • Website (user guide)

docs.title: Website
docs.text: Every request that is not /api/*, /assets/*, /files/* or /desk is a website request. Frappe resolves the path to a page and renders it with Jinja. Use the website layer for public pages, portal pages for website users, and pages that show documents of a DocType. For a form that guests fill in, use a Web Form. For desk screens, use Desk Pages.

docs.title: How a path is resolved
docs.text:
frappe.website.serve.get_response() creates a PathResolver for the request path. PathResolver.resolve() does these steps in order:

  1. If the path is desk or starts with desk/, it renders the desk.
  2. If the URL is in the cached 404 list, it returns the 404 page.
  3. It applies redirects from the website_redirects hook and from Website Settings (route_redirects).
  4. It maps the path to an endpoint. If an app sets the website_path_resolver hook, that function does this. Otherwise resolve_path() uses the home page for an empty path, removes .html, and applies website_route_rules.
  5. It tries each renderer in this order and uses the first whose can_render() returns true.
Order Renderer Renders 1 Classes from the page_renderer hook Anything your app decides 2 StaticPage Binary files (images, fonts, PDF) in an app www/ folder 3 WebFormPage Published Web Forms at their route 4 DocumentPage A document of a DocType with has_web_view, or a Web Page with a dynamic route 5 TemplatePage A .html or .md file in www/ or templates/pages/ 6 PrintPage /<DocType>/<name>, the print view of a document 7 ListPage /<DocType>, the portal list of a DocType

If no renderer matches, Frappe shows NotFoundPage. frappe.Redirect, frappe.PermissionError and frappe.PageDoesNotExistError raised during rendering show the redirect, "not permitted" and 404 pages.

docs.title: Pages in www/
docs.text:
Put a file in <app>/<app>/www/. The file path is the route. TemplatePage looks for these names, in this order: <path>, <path>.html, <path>.md, <path>/index.html, <path>/index.md. It looks in www/ first, then templates/pages/. Apps are checked from the last installed app to the first, so a later app can replace a page of an earlier app.

sample_app/sample_app/www/
├── orders.html        -> /orders
├── orders.py          -> context for /orders
├── orders.js          -> added to the page (no {% block script %} in orders.html)
├── orders.css         -> added to the page (no {% block style %} in orders.html)
└── help/
    ├── index.md       -> /help
    └── shipping.md    -> /help/shipping

docs.title: Context with get_context
docs.text:
A .py file with the same name (hyphens become underscores) is the page controller. Frappe calls its get_context(context) function before it renders the template. Change context in place or return a dict.

# sample_app/sample_app/www/orders.py
import frappe
from frappe import _

no_cache = 1


def get_context(context):
    if frappe.session.user == "Guest":
        frappe.throw(_("Log in to see your orders"), frappe.PermissionError)

    context.title = _("My Orders")
    context.orders = frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Order",
        filters={"owner_user": frappe.session.user},
        fields=["name", "order_date", "status", "total"],
        order_by="order_date desc",
    )

{# sample_app/sample_app/www/orders.html #}
{% extends "templates/web.html" %}

{% block page_content %}
<h1>{{ title }}</h1>
{% for order in orders %}
    <p>{{ order.name }}: {{ frappe.format(order.total, {"fieldtype": "Currency"}) }}</p>
{% endfor %}
{% endblock %}

If the template does not contain {% extends %} and does not contain </body>, Frappe wraps it in the base template inside {% block page_content %}. So a plain .html or .md file also gets the navbar and footer.

These module-level variables in the controller set page properties:

Name Effect no_cache Set to 1 to never cache the rendered HTML. sitemap Set to 1 to add the page to /sitemap.xml. base_template_path Use another base template for this page. template Render another template instead of the file. condition_field Read by the router for page info.

docs.title: Frontmatter
docs.text:
A .md or .html file can start with YAML frontmatter. The keys go into context.

---
title: Shipping
add_breadcrumbs: 1
show_sidebar: 1
---

# Shipping

Orders ship in 2 days.

Useful context keys: title, no_cache, sitemap, add_breadcrumbs, parents, show_sidebar, website_sidebar, sidebar_items, no_header, no_breadcrumbs, http_status_code, base_template_path, safe_render.

docs.title: Context that every page gets
docs.text: init_context() starts the context from get_website_settings() (navbar, footer, theme, web_include_js, web_include_css) and from website_context in site_config.json. After get_context, Frappe adds metatags, the base template, the title prefix, the update_website_context hook output, path, pathname, canonical and the current user (user, fullname, user_image).

docs.title: Templates and blocks
docs.text:
templates/base.html is the HTML document. templates/web.html extends it and is the usual parent for pages. These are the blocks you override most:

Template Blocks templates/base.html meta_block, title, favicon, head, head_include, style, banner, navbar, content, footer, base_scripts, script, body_include templates/web.html hero, breadcrumbs, page_container, header, header_actions, page_content, page_footer, page_sidebar

To change the base template for all pages, set base_template in hooks.py. The last app wins. To change it for some routes only, use base_template_map. The longest matching regex wins.

# sample_app/hooks.py
base_template = "sample_app/templates/sample_base.html"

base_template_map = {
    r"orders.*": "sample_app/templates/orders_base.html",
}

docs.title: Web Templates
docs.text: A Web Template is a reusable block for Web Pages and Website Settings (navbar, footer). A standard Web Template lives in <module>/web_template/<name>/ with <name>.html and <name>.json. Set standard to 1 in developer mode to export it. See frappe/website/web_template/ for the templates that Frappe ships.

docs.title: Route rules and redirects
docs.text:
website_route_rules maps a URL pattern to an endpoint. The syntax is the Werkzeug rule syntax. Matched parts go into frappe.form_dict, and a match with arguments turns off the page cache.

# sample_app/hooks.py
website_route_rules = [
    {"from_route": "/orders/<name>", "to_route": "order"},
    {"from_route": "/shop/<path:rest>", "to_route": "shop", "defaults": {"view": "grid"}},
]

With this rule, /orders/SO-00001 renders www/order.html, and frappe.form_dict.name is SO-00001. Frappe itself uses this hook, for example {"from_route": "/profile", "to_route": "me"}.

website_redirects sends a redirect. source is a regex that must match the full path. target can use groups.

# sample_app/hooks.py
website_redirects = [
    {"source": "/old-orders", "target": "/orders"},
    {"source": r"/catalog/(.*)", "target": r"/shop/\1", "redirect_http_status": 302},
    {"source": r"/app/(.*)", "target": r"/desk/\1", "forward_query_parameters": True},
]
Key Default Description source required Regex for the path, without the leading /. target required URL or path. Can use \1 for regex groups. redirect_http_status 301 HTTP status of the redirect. forward_query_parameters False Add the request query string to the target. match_with_query_string False Match source against path?query.

Users can also add redirects in Website Settings > Route Redirects. Resolved redirects are cached in the website_redirects cache key.

docs.title: DocTypes with a web view
docs.text:
A DocType can show each document as a web page.

  1. Set has_web_view on the DocType.
  2. Set route on the DocType, for example orders. This is also the URL of the list.
  3. Optional: set allow_guest_to_view so that guests can see published documents.
  4. Optional: set is_published_field to a Check field, for example published.
  5. Make the controller extend WebsiteGenerator.
# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe.website.website_generator import WebsiteGenerator


class SampleItem(WebsiteGenerator):
    website = frappe._dict(
        condition_field="published",
        page_title_field="item_name",
    )

    def get_context(self, context):
        context.related = frappe.get_all(
            "Sample Item",
            filters={"category": self.category, "name": ("!=", self.name)},
            fields=["item_name", "route"],
            limit=5,
        )

WebsiteGenerator.validate() sets route when the document is published and route is empty. The route is <DocType route>/<scrubbed title>. DocumentPage renders the document with templates/<doctype>.html in the DocType folder. The list at /<DocType route> uses templates/<doctype>_row.html for each row.

sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/templates/
├── sample_item.html       # one document
└── sample_item_row.html   # one row in the list

DocumentPage shows a document when one of these is true: the DocType has allow_guest_to_view, the user has read permission, or frappe.has_website_permission(doc) returns true. Use the has_website_permission hook or a has_website_permission controller method for portal access rules.

# sample_app/hooks.py
has_website_permission = {
    "Sample Order": "sample_app.portal.order_has_website_permission",
}

# sample_app/portal.py
def order_has_website_permission(doc, ptype, user, verbose=False):
    return doc.owner_user == user

docs.title: Portal list pages
docs.text:
ListPage renders /<DocType> with www/portal.html (frappe/www/list.py). It renders for DocTypes with has_web_view, and for standard DocTypes whose module has a get_list_context(context) function. Return a dict to change the list.

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_order/sample_order.py
def get_list_context(context=None):
    return {
        "title": "My Orders",
        "show_sidebar": True,
        "row_template": "sample_app/templates/includes/order_row.html",
    }

Add portal menu items for website users with the standard_portal_menu_items hook. Portal Settings syncs them into its menu.

# sample_app/hooks.py
standard_portal_menu_items = [
    {"title": "Orders", "route": "/orders", "reference_doctype": "Sample Order", "role": "Sample Role"},
]

docs.title: Home page
docs.text:
get_home_page() picks the page for /, in this order:

  1. The home_page of the user's roles (logged-in users).
  2. Portal Settings default_portal_home (logged-in users).
  3. The get_website_user_home_page hook, then website_user_home_page, then role_home_page, then home_page.
  4. Website Settings home_page.
  5. login for guests, me for others. System users go to desk.
# sample_app/hooks.py
role_home_page = {"Sample Role": "orders"}

docs.title: Custom page renderers
docs.text:
Add a class to the page_renderer hook to render paths your own way. It runs before all built-in renderers. The class gets (path, http_status_code) and must have can_render() and render(). Extend BaseRenderer or BaseTemplatePage.

# sample_app/hooks.py
page_renderer = ["sample_app.renderers.FeedRenderer"]

# sample_app/renderers.py
import frappe
from frappe.website.page_renderers.base_renderer import BaseRenderer


class FeedRenderer(BaseRenderer):
    def can_render(self):
        return self.path == "orders.json"

    def render(self):
        data = frappe.as_json(frappe.get_all("Sample Order", fields=["name", "status"], limit=20))
        return self.build_response(data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})

Frappe uses this hook for Studio apps (frappe.studio.doctype.studio_app.studio_app.StudioAppRenderer).

docs.title: Jinja
docs.text:
frappe.render_template(template, context) renders a template string or a template path. Website pages, print formats, email templates and notifications all use it.

frappe.render_template("Hello {{ name }}", {"name": "Customer A"})
# 'Hello Customer A'

frappe.render_template("{{ '2026-01-15' | global_date_format }}", {})
# 'January 15, 2026'

frappe.render_template("templates/includes/footer/footer_powered.html", {})

Frappe guesses that the string is a path when it looks like one. Pass is_path=True to be sure. With safe_render=True (the default), a template string that contains .__ raises "Illegal template".

Templates run in a sandboxed Jinja environment. The globals come from render_safe_globals() in frappe/utils/safe_exec.py. They include frappe.format, frappe.get_doc, frappe.get_list, frappe.get_all, frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_single_value, frappe.db.exists, frappe.db.count, frappe.session.user, frappe.form_dict, frappe.utils (date and number helpers) and _. frappe.get_list and frappe.db.get_value apply the user's permissions.

docs.title: Add methods and filters
docs.text:
Use the jinja hook. Each value is a module path or a function path. For a module path, Frappe adds every function defined in that module (not imported into it).

# sample_app/hooks.py
jinja = {
    "methods": [
        "sample_app.jinja.methods",
        "sample_app.utils.get_order_total",
    ],
    "filters": [
        "sample_app.jinja.filters",
    ],
}

# sample_app/jinja/filters.py
def as_order_code(value):
    return f"ORD/{value}"

{{ doc.name | as_order_code }}
{{ get_order_total(doc.name) }}

docs.title: Change context for all pages
docs.text:
update_website_context runs for every page after get_context. Return a dict to merge it into the context.

# sample_app/hooks.py
update_website_context = ["sample_app.website.update_context"]
website_context = {"favicon": "/assets/sample_app/images/favicon.png"}

# sample_app/website.py
def update_context(context):
    return {"support_email": "support@example.com"}

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
TemplatePage and DocumentPage cache the HTML in Redis per path and per language for 30 minutes (cache_html in frappe/website/utils.py). The response gets Cache-Control: private,max-age=300,stale-while-revalidate=10800 and X-From-Cache. Frappe does not cache when one of these is true:

  • developer_mode or disable_website_cache is set in site config.
  • The request has a query string.
  • The page sets no_cache, or a route rule matched with arguments.
  • The request sends Cache-Control: no-cache.

WebsiteGenerator.clear_cache() clears the cache for the document route after commit. Run frappe.website.utils.clear_cache(path) to clear one path, or bench --site <site> clear-website-cache for all.

docs.title: Sitemap
docs.text:
/sitemap.xml (frappe/www/sitemap.py) lists:

  • www/ pages whose controller or frontmatter sets sitemap = 1.
  • Published documents of DocTypes with has_web_view, allow_guest_to_view and a condition field. Routes blocked in Website Settings robots_txt are left out.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A .py file in www/ is not a page. Only .html and .md files are pages. The .py file only gives context.
  • Pages are cached for guests and users alike. Set no_cache = 1 on pages that show user data.
  • get_context runs as the current user. Check permissions in it, for example with frappe.get_list or frappe.has_permission.
  • website_route_rules and the DocType route map are cached. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache after you change them on a running site.
  • website_path_resolver replaces route rules and home page handling. The last function in the hook list wins.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Install Frappe, learn how it works and build a first app.

Topic What it covers Installation Install the bench CLI, create a bench with Frappe develop, create a site and start the development server. Architecture How a Frappe bench, its sites and apps fit together, how a request is handled, and which processes run beside the web server. Quickstart Build a small Frappe app end to end with a DocType, a controller validation, a whitelisted method, a form script, a list view setting and a test. Glossary Short definitions of the terms used in the Frappe Framework and its documentation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Read this page before you build an app. It explains the parts of a Frappe installation, the path of one HTTP request, and the processes that run beside the web server. The details of each part are in the developer guide.

docs.title: Bench, site and app
docs.text:
Term What it is On disk Bench One installation folder. It holds the code, the Python environment and all sites. frappe-bench/ with apps/, sites/, env/, config/, logs/, Procfile App A Python package that adds DocTypes, pages, APIs and hooks. Frappe itself is an app. apps/<app_name>/ Site One tenant: one database, one set of files and one site_config.json. sites/<site_name>/

The apps available to the bench are listed in sites/apps.txt. Each site installs a subset of them, in order. frappe is always the first app.

docs.title: Multi-tenancy
docs.text:
One bench serves many sites from the same processes. For each request, init_request() in frappe/app.py picks the site in this order:

  1. The site given to bench serve (for example with bench --site <site> serve).
  2. The X-Frappe-Site-Name request header.
  3. The host name of the request, without the port (get_site_name() in frappe/utils/__init__.py).

Then frappe.init(site) loads the site config and frappe.connect() opens the site database. State for the request lives in frappe.local, which is local to the thread.

Configuration is merged from sites/common_site_config.json (all sites) and sites/<site>/site_config.json (one site). See Configuration.

docs.title: Request lifecycle
docs.text:
The WSGI entry point is application() in frappe/app.py. Gunicorn runs it in production. bench serve runs it with the Werkzeug server in development.

  1. init_request() finds the site, connects to the database and builds frappe.form_dict from the query string and body. It loads the session from the session cookie (HTTPRequest in frappe/auth.py). Then it runs the before_request hooks.
  2. validate_auth() reads the Authorization header. It sets the user from an API token or an OAuth bearer token.

  3. The request path picks the handler:

    Path Handler /api/* frappe.api.handle(). Routes /api/v1/* (also /api/*) and /api/v2/*. /backups/* frappe.utils.response.download_backup() /private/files/* frappe.storage.serve.serve_private_file() (permission check) /files/* frappe.storage.serve.serve_public_file() /.well-known/* security.txt and other well-known files any other GET, HEAD, POST frappe.website.serve.get_response() (website and desk pages)

  4. If no exception occurs, sync_database() commits for POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH. It rolls back for other methods, unless frappe.local.flags.commit is set.

  5. If an exception occurs, Frappe makes an error response and rolls back the transaction.
  6. The after_request hooks run. Then the response gets its headers and cookies.
  7. Callbacks added to frappe.request.after_response run after the response is sent.

Note

A request with a cmd form value still goes to frappe.handler.handle(). This is deprecated in develop. Call /api/method/<dotted.path> instead.

docs.title: Whitelisted methods
docs.text: /api/method/<dotted.path> resolves the Python function and calls frappe.handler.execute_cmd(). This checks that the function has the @frappe.whitelist() decorator and that the HTTP method is allowed. Then it calls the function with frappe.form_dict as keyword arguments. The return value is sent as message in the JSON response. See Whitelisted methods and REST API.

docs.title: Desk, website and API
docs.text:
One process serves three kinds of clients:

Area Route Who uses it Built from Desk /desk and /desk/<path> Logged-in System Users frappe/www/desk.html and the JS bundle desk.bundle.js. Routing inside the desk is done in the browser. Website and portal all other routes, for example /login, /me, web forms, www/ pages Guests and Website Users Page renderers in frappe/website/page_renderers/ API /api/v1/*, /api/v2/* Scripts, mobile apps, the desk itself frappe/api/

The hook website_route_rules in frappe/hooks.py maps /desk/<path:app_path> to the desk page. The hook website_redirects sends /app, /app/* and /apps to /desk. A Guest who opens /desk gets a redirect to /login. A Website User gets a permission error.

For website routes, PathResolver in frappe/website/path_resolver.py tries the page renderers in this order: renderers from the page_renderer hook, then StaticPage, WebFormPage, DocumentPage, TemplatePage, PrintPage and ListPage. See Website.

docs.title: Processes
docs.text:
bench start (development) or the process manager (production) runs these processes:

Process Command Job Web bench serve / Gunicorn Runs frappe.app.application for HTTP requests. Worker bench worker Runs background jobs from Redis queues. Scheduler bench schedule Every tick, enqueues the due scheduled jobs of each site. Realtime bench socketio Socket.IO server for live updates in the browser. Redis cache redis-server config/redis_cache.conf Cache store (redis_cache). Redis queue redis-server config/redis_queue.conf Job queues and realtime pub/sub (redis_queue).

docs.title: Background workers
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue() puts a job in a Redis queue (RQ). A worker process takes jobs from one or more queues and runs each job in the context of its site. The built-in queues and their default timeouts (get_queues_timeout() in frappe/utils/background_jobs.py) are:

Queue Default timeout short 300 seconds default 300 seconds long 1500 seconds

Add more queues with the workers key in common_site_config.json. See Background jobs.

docs.title: Scheduler
docs.text: bench schedule runs start_scheduler() in frappe/utils/scheduler.py. On each tick it reads the Scheduled Job Type records of every site and enqueues the jobs that are due. The workers run them. Apps add jobs with the scheduler_events hook. See Scheduler.

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text:
Server code calls frappe.publish_realtime(). This publishes the event to the Redis channel events on the redis_queue server. The realtime server reads the channel and sends the event to the browser sockets in the right room (user, document or DocType). The browser receives it with frappe.realtime.on().

bench socketio starts one of two servers, set by socketio_backend in common_site_config.json:

  • node (default): apps/frappe/socketio.js.
  • python: python -m frappe.realtime.server, a Python Socket.IO server on asyncio and uvicorn. It calls back to the web process to authenticate sockets and check permissions.

Both listen on socketio_port (default 9000). See Realtime.

docs.title: Metadata-driven model
docs.text:
Frappe stores the data model as data. A DocType is a document that describes a table: its fields, permissions, naming and form layout.

  • Each DocType has one table named tab<DocType>, for example tabToDo.
  • Each field of a DocType is a column. Standard columns (name, owner, creation, modified, modified_by, docstatus, idx) are added to every table.
  • A child DocType (istable) stores its rows in its own table, with parent, parenttype and parentfield columns.
  • A Single DocType (issingle) has no table. Its values are stored in tabSingles.
  • The form, list view, REST API, permissions and reports all read the same DocType metadata (frappe.get_meta()).

A standard DocType belongs to an app. Its definition is a JSON file in the app, for example frappe/desk/doctype/todo/todo.json. bench migrate syncs these files to the database. A custom DocType (custom = 1) exists only in the site database. See DocTypes.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
A module groups DocTypes, reports, pages and workspaces inside an app. Each module is a Module Def record and a Python package in the app:

apps/sample_app/sample_app/        # Python package of the app
├── hooks.py
├── modules.txt                    # list of module names
└── sample_app/                    # module folder "Sample App"
    ├── .frappe                    # marks the folder as a module
    └── doctype/
        └── sample_item/
            ├── sample_item.json
            ├── sample_item.py
            └── sample_item.js

A new app gets one module with the same name as the app title. bench new-app writes both modules.txt and the .frappe marker file. See Apps.
