docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Use this page to look up a Frappe term. Each entry has a short definition and a link to the page with the details. Names in backticks are exact DocType names, fieldnames, hook keys or Python names.

docs.title: Installation and structure
docs.text: Term Definition Bench A folder that holds the apps, the Python environment and the sites. Also the name of the bench CLI. See Architecture. App A Python package in apps/ that adds DocTypes, pages, APIs and hooks. Frappe is also an app. See Apps. Site One tenant of a bench: one database, one sites/<site>/ folder and one site_config.json. Module A group of DocTypes, reports, pages and workspaces inside an app. Stored as a Module Def record and listed in the app's modules.txt. Site config The JSON settings of a site (site_config.json), merged with common_site_config.json. Read in code with frappe.conf. See Configuration. Developer mode The site config key developer_mode. When on, DocTypes and other standard records are saved as files in the app. Hook A variable in an app's hooks.py that Frappe reads to extend the framework, for example doc_events or scheduler_events. See Hooks. Fixture Records that an app exports as JSON (in <app>/fixtures/) with the fixtures hook. Frappe imports them on install and migrate. See Fixtures and patches. Patch A Python function listed in the app's patches.txt that bench migrate runs once per site. Sections [pre_model_sync] and [post_model_sync] set when it runs. Migrate bench --site <site> migrate. Runs patches, syncs DocType JSON to the database and imports fixtures.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: Term Definition DocType The definition of a data type: fields, permissions, naming and layout. Each DocType has a table named tab<DocType>. See DocTypes. Document One record of a DocType. In Python, an instance of frappe.model.document.Document. DocField One field of a DocType. Has a fieldname, a fieldtype, options and other properties. See Field types. Standard fields Columns in every table: name, owner, creation, modified, modified_by, docstatus, idx. Child Table A DocType with istable = 1. Its rows belong to a parent document through the parent, parenttype and parentfield columns. Single A DocType with issingle = 1. It has one record and no table of its own. Its values are stored in tabSingles. Used for settings. Tree A DocType with is_tree = 1. Its records form a hierarchy. The controller uses NestedSet. Virtual DocType A DocType with is_virtual = 1. It has no table. The controller loads and saves the data. Custom DocType A DocType with custom = 1. It exists only in the site database, not in an app. Standard A record that belongs to an app and is saved as a file in it, for example a standard DocType or report. Controller The Python class of a DocType (<doctype>.py). Its methods, such as validate and on_submit, run during the document lifecycle. See Controllers. Submittable A DocType with is_submittable = 1. Its documents can be submitted and cancelled. docstatus The state of a document: 0 Draft, 1 Submitted, 2 Cancelled. See frappe.model.docstatus.DocStatus. Amend Make a new draft copy of a cancelled document. The copy links to the original in amended_from. Naming How the name (primary key) of a document is set, for example with autoname. See Naming. Link field A field of type Link that stores the name of a document of another DocType, set in options. Custom Field A field added to a DocType for one site, stored in Custom Field. See Customize Form. Property Setter A record that changes one property of a DocType or field for one site.

docs.title: Desk and UI
docs.text: Term Definition Desk The admin UI for System Users, served at /desk. See Desk. Workspace A desk page with shortcuts, links, charts and number cards. Stored in Workspace. See Workspaces, sidebar and dock. Sidebar The navigation of a module in the desk. An app can ship it as a Sidebar record. Otherwise Frappe computes it from the module's workspaces, DocTypes, reports and pages. Dock The rail of links of one app in the desk. Stored in Dock. Each Dock Item links to a sidebar, a workspace or a URL. Desktop Icon An icon on the desk home page (/desk). Stored in Desktop Icon. Form view The page that shows one document. See Form view. List view The page that shows the documents of a DocType. See List view. Form script JavaScript for a DocType form, in <doctype>.js, with frappe.ui.form.on. See Form scripts. Client Script A form or list script saved as a record on the site, not in an app. See Server and client scripts. Server Script Python code saved as a record on the site. Runs in a restricted environment. Report A saved report. report_type is Report Builder, Query Report, Script Report or Custom Report. See Reports. Page A custom desk page with its own JS, stored in Page. See Desk pages. Web Form A form on the website for Guests or Website Users that makes or edits documents. See Web forms. Print Format A template that makes the print and PDF output of a document. See Print formats.

docs.title: Users and permissions
docs.text: Term Definition Administrator The built-in super user of a site. Guest The user of a request that is not logged in. System User A user who can use the desk. Website User A user who can use only the website and portal, not the desk. Role A named set of permissions given to users, for example System Manager. See Users and roles. Role permission A row in a DocType's permissions: a role, a permission level and rights such as read, write, create, submit and delete. See Permissions. Permission Level The permlevel of a field (default 0). Roles get rights per level, so you can restrict groups of fields. User Permission A User Permission record that limits a user to documents linked to one value, for example one company. See User permissions. Share Access to one document given to one user, outside the role permissions.

docs.title: Server and API
docs.text: Term Definition Whitelisted method A Python function with the @frappe.whitelist() decorator. It can be called over HTTP at /api/method/<dotted.path>. See Whitelisted methods. REST API The HTTP API under /api/v1/ (also /api/) and /api/v2/. See REST API. frappe.local Request-local state: site, database connection, user, form data. frappe.form_dict The parameters of the current request, from the query string and body. Background job A function that a worker runs outside the request, put in a queue with frappe.enqueue. See Background jobs. Queue A Redis job queue. Built-in queues: short, default, long. Worker A process (bench worker) that runs background jobs. Scheduler The process (bench schedule) that enqueues scheduled jobs. Jobs are set with the scheduler_events hook. See Scheduler. Realtime Live events from the server to the browser over Socket.IO, sent with frappe.publish_realtime. See Realtime. Cache The Redis cache of the site, used with frappe.cache. See Caching.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Use this page to set up a local development environment for Frappe develop (17.0.0-dev). You install the bench CLI, create a bench folder that holds Frappe, create a site, and start the processes. For production servers, see Deployment.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Software Version Source of the requirement Python 3.14 (>=3.14,<3.15) requires-python in pyproject.toml Node.js 24 or newer engines.node in package.json Yarn any current version bench runs yarn install for app assets (yarn.lock) MariaDB 10.6 to 11.8 check_compatible_versions() in frappe/database/mariadb/setup_db.py warns outside this range PostgreSQL supported, experimental bench new-site --db-type postgres SQLite supported, experimental bench new-site --db-type sqlite Redis a current Redis server Used for cache, job queue and realtime events Git any current version bench new-app makes a Git repository for the new app bench CLI the frappe-bench package Creates benches, gets apps and runs processes

MariaDB is the default database. For PostgreSQL and SQLite, bench new-site prints a note that the support is experimental.

docs.title: Install the bench CLI
docs.text:
1. Install the frappe-bench package as a tool:

    uv tool install frappe-bench

  2. Make sure the command works:

    bench --version

docs.title: Create a bench
docs.text:
A bench is a folder that holds the apps, a Python virtual environment (env/), the sites (sites/), the Redis configuration (config/) and a Procfile.

  1. Create the bench with the develop branch of Frappe and Python 3.14:

    bench init frappe-bench --frappe-branch develop --python python3.14

  2. Go into the bench folder:

    cd frappe-bench

Useful bench init options:

Option Description --frappe-branch (alias --version) Branch of Frappe to clone. --python Path to the Python executable for env/. --frappe-path Clone Frappe from this path or URL. --skip-assets Do not build JS and CSS assets. --no-procfile Do not make a Procfile. --dev Turn on developer mode and install development dependencies.

docs.title: Create a site
docs.text:
A site is one database plus one folder in sites/. One bench can serve many sites.

  1. Create the site. Give the MariaDB root password and a password for Administrator:

    bench new-site sample.localhost --db-root-password <root-password> --admin-password <admin-password>

  2. Make the new site the default site of the bench:

    bench use sample.localhost

  3. If you develop apps on this site, turn on developer mode:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config developer_mode 1

Common bench new-site options:

Option Default Description --db-type mariadb mariadb, postgres or sqlite. --db-name generated Database name. --db-host, --db-port from config Database server address. --db-root-username root Root user that makes the database and the user. --db-root-password prompt Root password for MariaDB or PostgreSQL. --admin-password prompt Password of the Administrator user. --install-app none App to install after the site is made. Use more than once for more apps. --set-default off Make the site the default site. --source-sql none Start the database from an SQL file. --force off Replace a site or database that already exists.

docs.title: Start the bench
docs.text:
1. Start all processes from the Procfile:

    bench start

  2. Open http://sample.localhost:8000 in the browser.

  3. Log in as Administrator with the admin password.

The desk opens at /desk. The old route /app redirects to /desk.

bench start runs these processes:

Process Command Purpose redis_cache redis-server config/redis_cache.conf Cache (redis_cache in common_site_config.json). redis_queue redis-server config/redis_queue.conf Job queue and realtime pub/sub (redis_queue). web bench serve --port 8000 Python web server for all sites. socketio bench socketio Realtime (Socket.IO) server. watch bench watch Rebuilds JS and CSS when files change. schedule bench schedule Scheduler that enqueues scheduled jobs. worker bench worker Background job worker.

The site is found from the Host header of the request. A name that ends in .localhost points to your computer in most browsers. For other names, run bench --site <site> add-to-hosts.

docs.title: Realtime server backend
docs.text:
Frappe develop ships two realtime servers: the Node.js server (socketio.js) and a Python Socket.IO server (frappe.realtime.server). bench socketio reads the socketio_backend key in common_site_config.json. The value is node (default) or python.

To use the Python server, set the key and restart the bench:

bench set-config -g socketio_backend python

The realtime server listens on socketio_port (default 9000).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Python 3.13 and older do not work. pyproject.toml requires Python 3.14.
  • A MariaDB version outside 10.6 to 11.8 shows a warning during bench new-site. The site can still be made, but the version is not tested.
  • bench new-site prompts for passwords when you do not give them. Give --db-root-password and --admin-password in scripts.
  • Without developer_mode, you cannot make a standard (non-custom) DocType. You get the error "Not in Developer Mode".

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: This page builds a small app, sample_app, with one DocType, Sample Item. You add a server validation, a whitelisted method, a form button, a list indicator and a test. Before you start, set up a bench and a site as shown in Installation. The examples use the site sample.localhost.

docs.title: 1. Create the app
docs.text:
1. In the bench folder, create the app:

    bench new-app sample_app

  2. Answer the prompts:

    Prompt Default Note App Title Sample App Also the name of the first module. App Description none App Publisher none App Email none Must be a valid email address. App License mit Create GitHub Workflow action for unittests False Adds .github/workflows/ci.yml and linter.yml. Branch Name branch of frappe Initial Git branch.

bench new-app runs bench make-app apps sample_app. Then it installs the app into the bench Python environment and adds it to sites/apps.txt. Use --no-git to skip the Git repository.

The new app has this layout:

apps/sample_app/
├── .editorconfig
├── .eslintrc
├── .gitignore
├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
├── README.md
├── license.txt
├── pyproject.toml
└── sample_app/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── hooks.py
    ├── modules.txt
    ├── patches.txt
    ├── config/
    ├── patches/
    ├── public/
    │   ├── css/
    │   └── js/
    ├── templates/
    │   ├── includes/
    │   └── pages/
    ├── www/
    └── sample_app/          # module "Sample App"
        ├── __init__.py
        └── .frappe

The generated hooks.py turns on two options for the app:

  • export_python_type_annotations = True: Frappe writes field type hints into the controller when you save the DocType.
  • require_type_annotated_api_methods = True: every whitelisted method of the app must have type annotations.

docs.title: 2. Install the app on the site
docs.text:
1. Install the app:

    bench --site sample.localhost install-app sample_app

  2. Turn on developer mode, so that DocTypes you make are saved as files in the app:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config developer_mode 1

  3. Start the bench:

    bench start

docs.title: 3. Create the DocType
docs.text:
1. Open http://sample.localhost:8000/desk/doctype/new.
  2. Set Name to Sample Item.
  3. Set Module to Sample App.
  4. Leave Custom? cleared.

  5. Add these fields:

    Label Fieldname Type Options Mandatory Item Name item_name Data Yes Category category Select Hardware, Software, Service (one per line) Yes Rate rate Currency No Disabled disabled Check No Description description Text Editor No

  6. In the Permissions tab, keep the row for System Manager.

  7. In the Naming tab, set Auto Name to field:item_name.
  8. Save.

Frappe makes the table tabSample Item and writes these files to apps/sample_app/sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/:

File Content sample_item.json DocType definition. sample_item.py Python controller. sample_item.js Form script. test_sample_item.py Test class. __init__.py Package marker.

docs.title: 4. Add a validation and a whitelisted method
docs.text:
Edit the controller. Keep the generated type block as it is.

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe import _
from frappe.model.document import Document
from frappe.utils import flt


class SampleItem(Document):
    # begin: auto-generated types
    # This code is auto-generated. Do not modify anything in this block.

    from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        from frappe.types import DF

        category: DF.Literal["Hardware", "Software", "Service"]
        description: DF.TextEditor | None
        disabled: DF.Check
        item_name: DF.Data
        rate: DF.Currency
    # end: auto-generated types

    _DOCTYPE_NAME = "Sample Item"

    def validate(self):
        if flt(self.rate) <= 0:
            frappe.throw(_("Rate must be greater than zero."), title=_("Invalid Rate"))


@frappe.whitelist()
def get_items_by_category(category: str) -> list[dict]:
    return frappe.get_list(
        "Sample Item",
        filters={"category": category, "disabled": 0},
        fields=["name", "item_name", "rate"],
        order_by="rate desc",
    )
  • validate() runs before each insert and save. frappe.throw() raises frappe.ValidationError and stops the save.
  • get_items_by_category() is callable at /api/method/sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category.
  • frappe.get_list() applies the read permissions of the current user.

Test the method with curl. Log in first and keep the session cookie in the file jar:

curl -c jar -X POST http://sample.localhost:8000/api/method/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"usr":"Administrator","pwd":"<admin-password>"}'
curl -b jar "http://sample.localhost:8000/api/method/sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category?category=Hardware"

The response has this shape:

{"message": [{"name": "Laptop", "item_name": "Laptop", "rate": 900.0}]}

docs.title: 5. Add a form script
docs.text:
The form script runs in the desk when a Sample Item form opens.

// sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item.js
frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Item", {
    refresh(frm) {
        if (frm.is_new()) return;

        frm.add_custom_button(__("Same Category"), () => {
            frappe.call({
                method: "sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item.get_items_by_category",
                args: { category: frm.doc.category },
                callback(r) {
                    frappe.msgprint(r.message.map((d) => d.item_name).join(", "));
                },
            });
        });
    },
});

After you change JS files, reload the page. bench watch (part of bench start) rebuilds the assets.

docs.title: 6. Add a list view setting
docs.text:
Make a file <doctype>_list.js next to the controller. The desk loads it for the list view.

// sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/sample_item_list.js
frappe.listview_settings["Sample Item"] = {
    add_fields: ["disabled"],
    get_indicator(doc) {
        if (doc.disabled) {
            return [__("Disabled"), "gray", "disabled,=,1"];
        }
        return [__("Enabled"), "green", "disabled,=,0"];
    },
};

get_indicator returns [label, color, filter]. A click on the indicator applies the filter. Open /desk/sample-item to see the list.

docs.title: 7. Write a test
docs.text:
Edit the generated test file:

# sample_app/sample_app/doctype/sample_item/test_sample_item.py
import frappe
from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase


class IntegrationTestSampleItem(IntegrationTestCase):
    def test_rate_must_be_positive(self):
        doc = frappe.get_doc(
            {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Test Item", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 0}
        )
        self.assertRaises(frappe.ValidationError, doc.insert)

    def test_get_items_by_category(self):
        from sample_app.sample_app.doctype.sample_item.sample_item import get_items_by_category

        frappe.get_doc(
            {"doctype": "Sample Item", "item_name": "Test Mouse", "category": "Hardware", "rate": 20}
        ).insert()
        names = [d.name for d in get_items_by_category("Hardware")]
        self.assertIn("Test Mouse", names)

  1. Allow tests on the site:

    bench --site sample.localhost set-config allow_tests true

  2. Run the tests of the DocType:

    bench --site sample.localhost run-tests --doctype "Sample Item"

IntegrationTestCase rolls back the database changes of the test class when the class is done.

docs.title: 8. Install the app on another site
docs.text:
1. Commit the app code to Git.
  2. On the other bench, get the app with bench get-app <git-url>.

  3. Install the app:

    bench --site <site> install-app sample_app

install-app makes the tables of all DocTypes in the app and runs the after_install hooks. After you pull new code, run bench --site <site> migrate.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Without developer_mode, saving a DocType with Custom? cleared fails with "Not in Developer Mode".
  • In this app, a call to a whitelisted method without type annotations fails, because require_type_annotated_api_methods is on.
  • The dotted path of a DocType module repeats the app name: sample_app.sample_app.doctype.... The first part is the app package. The second part is the module folder.
  • Do not edit the DocType JSON by hand. Change it in the desk, so Frappe updates the JSON, the table and the type hints together.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: This page lists every bench command that the frappe app adds, in this version. The list and the options come from the click definitions in frappe/commands/ and the Studio and Flow command modules. Commands of the bench tool itself (init, get-app, new-app, start, setup ...) are not on this page. Run all commands from the bench root (frappe-bench/).

docs.title: How commands find the site
docs.text:
bench loads frappe.commands.commands and the commands list of every other app (<app>/commands/__init__.py or <app>/commands.py). It wraps them in one group that takes these options before the command name:

Option Description --site <site> Site to run on. --site all runs on every site, for commands that loop over sites. --verbose Verbose output. --force Force flag. Some commands read it (for example run-patch, reload-doc). --profile Run the command under cProfile and print the top 100 lines.

When --site is not given, bench uses the FRAPPE_SITE environment variable, then default_site from common_site_config.json (set with bench use <site>).

bench --site frappe.localhost migrate
bench --site all clear-cache
bench --site frappe.localhost execute frappe.client.get_count --args '["ToDo"]'

In the tables below, "Needs site" means:

  • Yes: the command runs on the site from --site (or the default site). Without one, it fails with "Please specify --site sitename".
  • Optional: the command also works without a site, or takes --site after the command name.
  • No: the command does not use a site.

Run bench <command> --help to see the same options on your bench. Commands in a group (flow-server) take the subcommand next: bench flow-server status.

docs.title: Sites and apps
docs.text:
Defined in frappe/commands/site.py.

Command Needs site Description add-system-manager Yes Add a new system manager to a site. add-user Yes Add user to a site. add-database-index Yes Adds a new DB index and creates a property setter to persist it. describe-database-table Yes Show the schema, indexes and row count of a DocType table as JSON. With --column, also show distinct value counts. backup Yes Make a database backup of the site. Optionally include files and config. drop-site No (<site> argument) Remove a site from database and filesystem. disable-app Yes Disable an app on site, keeping its schema and data intact. enable-app Yes Enable an app that was disabled on site. install-app Yes Install a new app to site, supports multiple apps. list-apps Yes List apps in site. migrate Yes Run patches, sync schema and rebuild files/translations. migrate-to No Move a site to a hosting provider (Frappe Cloud). Interactive. new-site No (<site> argument) Create a new site. reinstall Yes Reinstall site ie. wipe all data and start over. reload-doc Yes Reload schema for a DocType. reload-doctype Yes Reload schema for a DocType. remove-from-installed-apps Yes Remove app from site's installed-apps list. restore Yes Restore site database from an sql file. run-patch Yes Run a particular patch. set-password Yes Set password for a user on a site. set-admin-password Yes Set Administrator password for a site. uninstall-app Yes Remove app and linked modules from site. disable-user Yes Disable a user account on site. use No (<site> argument) Set a default site. set-last-active-for-user Yes Set users last active date to current datetime. publish-realtime Yes Publish realtime event from bench. browse Optional Open the site in a web browser, logged in as a user. start-recording Yes Start Frappe Recorder. stop-recording Yes Stop Frappe Recorder. add-to-hosts Yes Add the site name to /etc/hosts (uses sudo). ngrok Yes Start a ngrok tunnel to your local development server. build-search-index Yes Does nothing. Kept for old scripts. Website search indexing is removed. partial-restore Yes Restore some tables from a partial backup file (made with backup --only). Not supported on SQLite. trim-tables Yes Remove columns from tables where fields are deleted from doctypes. trim-database Yes Remove database tables for deleted DocTypes. clear-log-table Yes Shrink a large log table. Recent rows are copied to a new table, which replaces the old one. bypass-patch Yes Bypass a patch permanently instead of migrating using the --skip-failing flag. sync-desktop-icons Yes Import the desktop icon fixtures again for the site.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Put global options before the command: bench --site s1 migrate, not bench migrate --site s1. Only commands that define their own --site (for example doctor, show-pending-jobs, build-studio-app) accept it after the name.
  • bench execute evaluates --args and --kwargs as Python literals. Quote them for the shell.

docs.title: Hooks Reference
docs.text: This page lists every key in an app's hooks.py that the framework reads in this version. Use it to look up the shape of a hook value and the code that reads it. For how hooks work and how values from many apps merge, see Hooks.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• frappe.get_hooks("key") collects the key from all active apps and returns a list. A single string value becomes a one-item list.
  • A dict value is merged key by key. Each inner value also becomes a list. For example, doc_events["*"]["on_update"] is a list of dotted paths from all apps.
  • "Last wins" means the framework uses only the last item ([-1]). Apps load in install order, so the app installed last wins.
  • "All run" means the framework calls every dotted path in the list, in app order.
  • "Per app" means the framework reads the key with app_name=<app> and uses only that app's value.
  • Paths in the "Read in" column are relative to apps/frappe.

The Audit System Hooks report (frappe/custom/report/audit_system_hooks) shows the merged value of each hook on a site. In code, check a value from the console:

frappe.get_hooks("calendars")   # ['Event']

Per app. app_logo_url str frappe/boot.py, frappe/core/doctype/navbar_settings/navbar_settings.py, frappe/utils/change_log.py Logo of the app. The navbar uses the second logo when exactly two apps set one. app_home str frappe/boot.py Route of the app home, for example /desk/build. Per app. <branch>_version str frappe/utils/change_log.py Version label for a branch, for example develop_version. Shown when the app is not on master. add_to_apps_screen list of dict frappe/apps.py, frappe/boot.py, frappe/desk/doctype/desktop_icon/desktop_icon.py, frappe/desk/doctype/dock/dock.py Adds the app to the apps screen. ]

docs.title: App lifecycle (install, migrate, enable, build, tests)
docs.text:
All keys in this table are lists of dotted paths. "Per app" keys run only the hooks of the app that the event is about.

Key Read in Called with Description before_install frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs before the app is installed. If a function returns False, the install stops. after_install frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs after the app's DocTypes and fixtures sync. after_sync frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs at the end of install_app. before_app_install frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs before any app is installed. after_app_install frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs after any app is installed. before_uninstall frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs before the app is removed. after_uninstall frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Runs after the app is removed. before_app_uninstall frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs before any app is removed. after_app_uninstall frappe/installer.py app_name All apps. Runs after any app is removed. before_enable, after_enable frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Run when a disabled app is enabled again. Frappe commits after after_enable. before_disable, after_disable frappe/installer.py nothing Per app. Run when an app is disabled on a site. before_migrate frappe/migrate.py nothing Per app. Runs at the start of bench migrate. after_migrate frappe/migrate.py nothing Per app. Runs at the end of bench migrate. after_build frappe/commands/utils.py nothing Per app. Runs after bench build for the apps that were built. after_app_build frappe/commands/utils.py list of built apps Per app, for every app on the bench. Runs after a build. before_tests frappe/testing/environment.py, frappe/parallel_test_runner.py nothing Per app. Runs before the tests of the app. never_skip_patches frappe/modules/patch_handler.py not called Patch paths (or prefixes) that bench migrate --skip-failing cannot skip. A failure in one stops the migrate. fixtures frappe/utils/fixtures.py, frappe/translate.py not called Records to export with bench export-fixtures and import on migrate. Items are DocType names or dicts with doctype, filters, or_filters. fixture_auto_order frappe/utils/fixtures.py not called True adds a numeric prefix to exported fixture files, in the order of fixtures. Per app. importable_doctypes frappe/model/sync.py not called Extra DocTypes whose records in module folders (<module>/<doctype>/<name>/<name>.json) import on migrate. 
# sample_app/hooks.py
after_install = "sample_app.setup.install.after_install"
after_migrate = ["sample_app.setup.install.sync_defaults"]
fixtures = [{"doctype": "Custom Field", "filters": [["module", "=", "Sample App"]]}]

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A key with a typo does nothing and gives no error. Check the value with frappe.get_hooks("<key>").
  • Merged hooks are cached. Run bench --site <site> clear-cache after you change hooks.py.
  • For "last wins" keys, the app install order decides which app wins.

docs.title: Site Config Reference
docs.text: This page lists every key in site_config.json and common_site_config.json that the framework reads in this version. For how the two files merge, how to set keys and how environment variables override them, see Configuration.

docs.title: How to read this page
docs.text:
• Frappe reads sites/common_site_config.json first, then sites/<site>/site_config.json. A site key overrides a common key with the same name. The result is frappe.conf (same object as frappe.local.conf).
  • Scope "Common" means the key is read without a site (through frappe.get_common_site_config(), or frappe.get_conf() outside a site). Set it in common_site_config.json. "Site" keys work in either file.
  • "Default" is the value the code uses when the key is missing. An empty cell means the feature is off or the value is empty.
  • Set a key with bench --site <site> set-config <key> <value>, or bench set-config -g <key> <value> for the common file. Add -p to parse the value as JSON or a Python literal.
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config developer_mode 1
bench set-config -g redis_cache "redis://127.0.0.1:13000"
bench --site frappe.localhost set-config -p allow_cors '["https://app.example.com"]'

In code, read a key from frappe.conf. A missing key returns None.

frappe.conf.developer_mode      # 1 or None
frappe.conf.get("max_file_size")

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.conf is cached for up to 60 seconds in long-running processes. Restart workers after you change Redis or database keys.
  • A key in site_config.json hides the same key in common_site_config.json.
  • The auth_method key for the site config email account is not read. The code passes ("auth_method"), a string, not a tuple, so it looks up each character.

docs.title: Data Model Reference
docs.text:
Every field type, every DocField property and every DocType shipped with Frappe.

Page What it covers Field Types Every DocField fieldtype with its database column type on MariaDB, Postgres and SQLite, what Options means, and validation rules. DocField Properties Every DocField property from docfield.json with its type, default, the fieldtypes it applies to, its effect, and whether Customize Form and Custom Field can set it. DocTypes Reference Every DocType shipped with the frappe app, grouped by module, with flags and a one-line description.

docs.title: DocField Properties
docs.text: A DocField is one row in the fields table of a DocType. This page lists every DocField property. Use it to look up a property name, its type and default, and the fieldtypes that use it. For how the main properties behave on the desk and on the server, read Field Properties.

docs.title: How this table is made
docs.text:
A script reads frappe/core/doctype/docfield/docfield.json in field_order and skips Section, Column and Tab Breaks. Type, Default and Label come from the JSON. Applies to comes from the depends_on of each property in the JSON, which controls when the DocType form shows it. Some rows add rules from the code. Customize Form is "Yes" when the property is a key of docfield_properties in frappe/custom/doctype/customize_form/customize_form.py. Custom Field is "Yes" when frappe/custom/doctype/custom_field/custom_field.json has a field with that name. Effect was written by hand from the code.

"Fields with a column" means all fieldtypes except the no-value fieldtypes in frappe.model.no_value_fields: Section Break, Column Break, Tab Break, Attachment Gallery, HTML, Table, Table MultiSelect, Button, Image, Fold, Heading and Vue Component.

See Field Types. fieldname Data Name All Yes Column name and document key. Lowercase, at most 64 characters (63 on Postgres), no special characters. length Int Length Data, Link, Dynamic Link, Password, Select, Read Only, Attach, Attach Image, Int, Float, Currency, Percent Yes Yes Size of the varchar column and the maximum length checked on save. docs.title: Customize Form
docs.text:
Customize Form saves each changed property of a standard field as one Property Setter. It saves only the keys of docfield_properties. These DocField properties are not in that list, so Customize Form cannot change them: fieldname, search_index, not_nullable, show_on_timeline, sticky, in_filter, max_height, documentation_url, show_description_on_click, oldfieldname, oldfieldtype.

docfield_properties also has idx (the row order) and auto_repeat, which are not DocField properties in docfield.json.

Customize Form also blocks these changes on standard fields (allow_property_change):

Property Rule fieldtype Only inside one group of ALLOWED_FIELDTYPE_CHANGE, for example Currency, Float, Percent. Virtual fields can change freely. length A smaller length fails when saved values are longer. reqd You cannot clear it when the standard field is mandatory. read_only You cannot clear it when the standard field is read-only. allow_on_submit You cannot set it when the standard field does not have it. in_list_view Not allowed for fieldtypes from get_fields_not_allowed_in_list_view. options Only for Read Only, HTML and Data fields (ALLOWED_OPTIONS_CHANGE).

A blocked change shows a message and is skipped. A wrong fieldtype change raises an error.

docs.title: Custom Field and Property Setter
docs.text:
• A Custom Field adds a new field. It has its own copy of most DocField properties (see the Custom Field column), plus dt (the DocType) and insert_after.
  • A Property Setter stores one property value for one field (doctype_or_field = DocField). It does not check the property name, so code can set any property with frappe.make_property_setter. After an update it runs the same field checks as a DocType save (validate_fields_for_doctype).
frappe.make_property_setter(
    {
        "doctype": "ToDo",
        "fieldname": "description",
        "property": "documentation_url",
        "value": "https://example.com/help",
        "property_type": "Data",
    }
)

docs.title: DocTypes Reference
docs.text:
This page lists every DocType that the frappe app ships, grouped by module. Use it to find the exact DocType name and its module. The list is generated from frappe/*/doctype/*/*.json. It has 339 DocTypes, the same as the count of non-custom DocTypes on a develop site.

Flags come from the DocType JSON:

Flag JSON property Meaning single issingle One record only. Values are in tabSingles. child istable Child table. Rows belong to a parent document. submittable is_submittable Has Submit and Cancel (docstatus). tree is_tree Nested set tree with lft and rgt. virtual is_virtual No table. The controller supplies the data.

For child tables, the description names the parent DocType and the Table field. See DocTypes for how DocTypes work.

docs.title: Field Types
docs.text: The fieldtype of a DocField sets the database column, the desk control and the validation of a field. Use this page to choose a fieldtype and to set its options. The list of fieldtypes comes from the fieldtype options in frappe/core/doctype/docfield/docfield.json. Column types come from setup_type_map() of each database class.

docs.title: Groups of fieldtypes
docs.text:
frappe/model/__init__.py defines these groups:

Constant Fieldtypes Meaning data_fieldtypes All types with a column, from Currency to JSON in the table below Each field of these types gets a column in tab<DocType>. no_value_fields Section Break, Column Break, Tab Break, Attachment Gallery, HTML, Table, Table MultiSelect, Button, Image, Fold, Heading, Vue Component No column in the parent table. display_fieldtypes no_value_fields minus Table and Table MultiSelect Layout and display only. table_fields Table, Table MultiSelect Rows are stored in the child DocType table. numeric_fieldtypes Currency, Int, Long Int, Float, Percent, Check Numeric values. float_like_fields Float, Currency, Percent Decimal values with precision. datetime_fields Datetime, Date, Time Date and time values. attachment_fieldtypes Attach, Attach Image Values are file URLs. data_field_options Email, Name, Phone, URL, Barcode, IBAN Allowed options of a Data field.

docs.text:
VARCHAR_LEN is 140 (frappe/database/database.py).

The control has a country code picker. Int int(11) int int Not used. Long Int bigint(20) bigint bigint Not used. Not in the DocField fieldtype list. An Int field with length above 11 gets this column. Check tinyint(4) smallint integer Not used. Value is 0 or 1. Float decimal(21,9) decimal(21,9) real Not used. Set precision for decimals. docs.title: Fieldtypes without a column
docs.text: Fieldtype Options Notes Table Required. A child DocType (istable = 1). Rows are stored in the child table with parent, parenttype and parentfield. A virtual DocType needs a virtual child table. Table MultiSelect Required. A child DocType with at least one Link field. Shows the rows as pills of the first Link field. Section Break Not used. Starts a section. Column Break Not used. Starts a column in a section. Tab Break Not used. Starts a tab. Fold Not used. Hides the rest of the form behind a "Show more details" link. Only one per form, and it must be before a Section Break. Heading Not used. Shows the label as a heading. HTML HTML to show. Form scripts can set the content with frm.get_field(fieldname).$wrapper.html(...). Image Fieldname that holds the image URL. Shows the image of that field. Button Optional. Name of a controller method. A click runs the form script event of the field. If there is none and options is set, it calls the controller method through run_doc_method. The source marks this path as deprecated. Attachment Gallery Not used. Shows attachments of the document. Its link_filters must target File. Vue Component Required. Name of a UI island on the site. Mounts the island in the form. See Islands.

docs.title: How a column is built
docs.text:
get_definition() in frappe/database/schema.py turns a DocField into a column type:

  • Currency, Float and Percent get decimal(length, precision) on MariaDB and Postgres. The default is decimal(21,9). precision must be from 1 to 6. precision cannot be greater than length.
  • A length on a varchar field changes the size. Values below 64 become 64.
  • An Int field with length above 11 becomes Long Int (bigint). On MariaDB, a length below 11 sets int(length).
  • A Link to a DocType with autoname = "UUID" gets a uuid column.
  • Check, Int, Currency, Float and Percent are NOT NULL. Their default is 0 if none is set.
  • not_nullable = 1 makes other columns NOT NULL.
  • unique = 1 adds a unique constraint, except for text and longtext columns.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
validate_fields() in frappe/core/doctype/doctype/doctype.py checks these rules when you save a DocType:

Rule Fieldtypes Options must be a valid DocType Link, Table, Table MultiSelect Options must be a child table Table, Table MultiSelect Can be unique Data, Link, Read Only, Int only Cannot have search_index Text, Long Text, Small Text, Code, Text Editor Cannot be mandatory no_value_fields except Table and Table MultiSelect Not allowed in_list_view no_value_fields. In a child table, Button and HTML are allowed. Not allowed in_global_search no_value_fields Default must be 0 or 1 Check Precision from 1 to 6 Float, Currency, Percent Options from 3 to 10 Rating Hidden and mandatory needs a default All

docs.title: Desk controls
docs.text: Each fieldtype has a control class frappe.ui.form.Control<Fieldtype> without spaces, for example ControlDynamicLink. The files are in frappe/public/js/frappe/form/controls/. Dialogs and web forms use the same controls. Some controls exist only for dialogs and filters: MultiCheck, MultiSelect, MultiSelectList, MultiSelectPills, DateRange, Switch and Comment.

docs.title: HTTP API
docs.text:
Every REST endpoint and whitelisted method route, with methods and permission checks.

Page What it covers REST Endpoints Reference Every route under /api in Frappe (v1, v2, discovery, MCP) and the most used whitelisted methods, with HTTP methods and permission checks.

docs.title: REST Endpoints Reference
docs.text: This page lists every route that Frappe serves under /api, and the core whitelisted methods that clients call most. For how to authenticate, filter and page, see REST API and Authentication.

docs.title: Route maps
docs.text:
frappe/api/__init__.py mounts three route sets:

Prefix Rules from Response key /api/ frappe/api/v1.py message for methods, data for resources /api/v1/ frappe/api/v1.py (same rules) same as /api/ /api/v2/ frappe/api/v2.py data for all routes. Errors are in errors

Trailing slashes are optional. When System Settings log_api_requests is on, each call writes an API Request Log. All routes run as the session user. Permission checks are those of the called function.

docs.title: API v1
API v2
docs.text:
Route HTTP methods Does Permission check /api/v2/method/login any Does not log in. LoginManager logs in only on the path /api/method/login. This route returns {} and the session stays Guest. Use /api/method/login. none /api/v2/method/logout POST Log out the session. none /api/v2/method/ping any Returns "pong". none /api/v2/method/upload_file POST Upload a file. Same as frappe.handler.upload_file. see Files /api/v2/method/bulk_delete POST Delete docs: a list of {"doctype", "name"}. delete per document /api/v2/method/bulk_update POST Update docs: a list of {"doctype", "name", ...fields}. write per document /api/v2/method/run_doc_method GET, POST, QUERY Run a whitelisted method on an unsaved document dict. Args: method, document, kwargs. read (GET), write or create (POST) /api/v2/method/<dotted.path> any allowed by the method Calls a whitelisted function or API Server Script. Applies override_whitelisted_methods. @frappe.whitelist rules /api/v2/method/<doctype>/<method> any allowed by the method Calls a whitelisted module function in the DocType's controller file. @frappe.whitelist rules /api/v2/document/<doctype> GET, QUERY List records. Returns data and has_next_page. query permission rules /api/v2/document/<doctype> POST Insert a document from the JSON body. create /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> GET Read one document. fields picks fields, also from child tables. read /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> PATCH, PUT Update fields and save. write /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name> DELETE Delete. Returns HTTP 202 and "ok". delete /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/copy GET A copy of the document without name and other private properties, ready to insert. The route keeps no_copy fields. read /api/v2/document/<doctype>/<name>/method/<method> GET, POST, QUERY Call a whitelisted controller method. The saved document goes in docs. read (GET, QUERY), write (POST) /api/v2/document/<doctype>/bulk_delete POST Delete names (a list) of one DocType. delete per document /api/v2/document/<doctype>/bulk_update POST Update docs (list of {"name", ...fields}) of one DocType. write per document /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/meta GET DocType meta. logged-in user (frappe.only_for("All")) /api/v2/doctype/<doctype>/count GET, QUERY Count with optional filters. frappe.desk.reportview.get_count rules

List parameters for GET /api/v2/document/<doctype>: fields, filters (list or dict), order_by, group_by, start (default 0), limit (default 20), as_dict (default true), debug. A controller can change the list query with a static get_list(query) method that returns a query builder object.

Bulk routes run in the request when the list has up to bulk_operation_async_threshold items (site config, default 20, a number or a dict per DocType with "*"). For longer lists they enqueue a job and return HTTP 202 with {"job_id": ...}. Each item runs in its own savepoint. The result has deleted or updated, failed, total, success_count and failure_count.

curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/document/ToDo \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"description": "Sample REST todo"}'
curl -b cookies.txt -X PATCH http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/document/ToDo/rhs7if2b7m \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status": "Closed"}'
curl -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/doctype/ToDo/count"

{"data": 5}

docs.title: API discovery
docs.text:
All discovery routes need the Desk User role. They are GET only.

Route Returns /api/v2/discovery Counts of methods and DocType methods, and links to the routes below. /api/v2/discovery/search?q=<text> Up to 50 methods whose text has every word of q. /api/v2/discovery/method All whitelisted methods the user can call. /api/v2/discovery/method/<dotted.path> One method: parameters, HTTP methods, docstring, and source when the app sets expose_discovery_source. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype> Whitelisted controller methods of a DocType. /api/v2/discovery/doctype/<doctype>/method/<method> One controller method.

The discovery index is built in a background job after bench migrate. Until it is ready, the routes return HTTP 503 DiscoveryCacheUnavailable. Try again after a few seconds. See MCP and Discovery.

docs.title: MCP
docs.text:
Route HTTP methods Does /api/v2/mcp POST (GET and DELETE return 405) Model Context Protocol server over streamable HTTP with JSON responses.

The route returns 404 unless System Settings enable_mcp is on. It needs a logged-in user with the Desk User role, Content-Type: application/json, and an Accept header that allows application/json. Tools: search_doctypes, get_doctype_schema, search_methods, get_method_schema, list_document_methods, list_documents, get_document, count_documents, create_document, update_document, delete_document, call_method, call_document_method. Each tool runs with the permissions of the user.

docs.title: Login, logout and files
docs.text:
These work on /api/method/... (v1). In v2, use the routes in the v2 table.

Method path HTTP methods Guest Description login POST yes Log in. Args: usr, pwd. Returns message, home_page, full_name and sets the sid cookie. logout POST yes Log out the current session. frappe.handler.web_logout POST yes Log out and show a "Logged Out" web page. frappe.auth.get_logged_user any no Returns the user name of the session. frappe.ping GET, POST yes Returns "pong". upload_file (frappe.handler.upload_file) POST yes Upload a file as multipart form data (file, doctype, docname, fieldname, is_private, folder, file_url). frappe.handler.download_file GET, POST yes Download a file by file_url, with session or token auth. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.reset_password POST yes Send a password reset link. Arg: user. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.update_password POST yes Set a new password with key or old_password. frappe.core.doctype.user.user.sign_up POST yes Website sign up. Args: email, full_name, redirect_to.

Short names such as logout and upload_file resolve to frappe.handler and are deprecated. Use the full dotted path in new code.

curl -c cookies.txt -X POST http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/method/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"usr": "Administrator", "pwd": "password"}'

{"message": "Logged In", "home_page": "desk", "full_name": "Administrator"}

docs.title: frappe.client methods
docs.text:
Call them as /api/method/frappe.client.<name> or /api/v2/method/frappe.client.<name>. Defined in frappe/client.py. "any" means GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and QUERY.

Method HTTP methods Arguments Description get_list any doctype, fields, filters, or_filters, group_by, order_by, limit_start, limit_page_length (20), parent, as_dict, expand, debug List records with permission checks. get_count any doctype, filters, cache, debug Count records. get any doctype, name or filters, parent Get one document as a dict. get_value any doctype, fieldname (str or list), filters, as_dict, parent Get field values of one record. get_single_value any doctype, field Get a field of a Single DocType. set_value POST, PUT doctype, name, fieldname (str or dict), value Set values and save the document. insert POST, PUT doc Insert a document. A child row needs parenttype, parent, parentfield. insert_many POST, PUT docs Insert many documents. save POST, PUT doc Save an existing document. rename_doc POST, PUT doctype, old_name, new_name, merge Rename a document. submit POST, PUT doc Submit a document. cancel POST, PUT doctype, name Cancel a submitted document. delete DELETE, POST doctype, name Delete a document. bulk_update POST, PUT docs Update many documents. Each item has doctype, docname and fields. has_permission any doctype, docname, perm_type (read) Returns {"has_permission": bool}. get_doc_permissions any doctype, docname Returns {"permissions": {...}}. Empty when the user cannot read the document. get_password any doctype, name, fieldname Returns a decrypted Password field. System Manager only. get_time_zone GET, POST (guest) none Returns the system time zone. attach_file POST, PUT filename, filedata, doctype, docname, folder, decode_base64, is_private (1), docfield Attach file content to a document. is_document_amended any doctype, docname True when an amended copy exists. validate_link_and_fetch GET, POST doctype, docname, fields_to_fetch, query, filters Check a Link value and fetch fields from the linked record. 
curl -b cookies.txt "http://frappe.localhost:8000/api/v2/method/frappe.client.get_value?doctype=User&filters=%22Administrator%22&fieldname=%5B%22full_name%22%5D"

{"data": {"full_name": "Administrator"}}

docs.title: Other core methods
docs.text:
The desk calls these. They are useful for clients too.

Method HTTP methods Description frappe.desk.reportview.get any List view data. Args like get_list (doctype, fields, filters, order_by, start, page_length). frappe.desk.reportview.get_count any Count for list view. frappe.desk.reportview.export_query any Export Report Builder data as CSV or Excel. frappe.desk.reportview.delete_items POST, DELETE Delete selected records. frappe.desk.form.load.getdoc any Load a document with docinfo for the form. frappe.desk.form.load.getdoctype any Load DocType meta and scripts for the form. frappe.desk.form.save.savedocs POST, PUT Save, submit or update a document from the form. Args: doc, action. frappe.desk.form.save.cancel POST, PUT Cancel from the form. frappe.desk.search.search_link any Results for a Link field dropdown. frappe.desk.query_report.run any Run a Query or Script Report. Args: report_name, filters. frappe.rename_doc POST, PUT Rename and update links.

frappe has about 740 whitelisted methods in this version. To list them, call /api/v2/discovery/method as a desk user. App developers make new ones with @frappe.whitelist(). See Whitelisted Methods.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A method without methods= in @frappe.whitelist accepts all HTTP verbs. Write methods should set methods=["POST"].
  • v1 PUT /api/resource/... and v2 PATCH call doc.save(). They do not submit. Use the submit method or a document method.
  • v2 list returns 20 records by default. Check has_next_page and raise start.
  • frappe.client.get_list and /api/resource return 20 rows by default. limit_page_length=0 removes the limit. Use it with care on large tables.
