docs.title: Error checks
docs.text:
Use these in an except block to test a database error without engine-specific codes. Each takes the exception and returns a bool.

Method True when is_deadlocked(e) The transaction was a deadlock victim. is_timedout(e) A lock wait timed out. is_statement_timeout(e) A statement ran longer than the statement timeout. is_read_only_mode_error(e) The transaction or server is read-only. is_table_missing(e) The table does not exist. is_missing_table(e) Same as is_table_missing. MariaDB and Postgres only. is_missing_column(e) The column does not exist. is_missing_table_or_column(e) Either of the two above. is_duplicate_entry(e) A unique or primary key was violated. is_primary_key_violation(e) The primary key was violated. is_unique_key_violation(e) A unique key was violated. is_duplicate_fieldname(e) A column with that name exists. is_data_too_long(e) A value is too long for the column. is_data_truncated(e) A value is out of range or of the wrong type. MariaDB and Postgres only. is_db_table_size_limit(e) The row size is above the limit. is_syntax_error(e) The SQL has a syntax error. is_access_denied(e) The database user has no access. cant_drop_field_or_key(e) A column or key to drop does not exist. is_interface_error(e) The connection is unusable. is_nested_transaction_error(e) A transaction is already active. SQLite only. 
try:
    frappe.db.sql("insert into `tabSample Item` (name) values ('Laptop')")
except Exception as e:
    if not frappe.db.is_duplicate_entry(e):
        raise

FROM STDIN, default chunk_size=10_000. Uses INSERT when ignore_duplicates=True Multi-row INSERT add_index Skips the index when using is set. Ignores where and include Supports using (gin_trgm, gin_fulltext, btree, hash, gist, gin, brin, spgist), partial (where) and covering (include) indexes. Index names include the table Skips the index when using is set. docs.title: Document
docs.text:
frappe.model.document.Document is the base class of every controller. frappe.get_doc, frappe.new_doc and the other loaders in frappe namespace return instances of it. This page lists every public method and property, the order of controller hooks for each operation, and the flags that change behavior. For the how-to and controller examples, see Controllers.

BaseDocument was merged into Document. frappe.model.document.BaseDocument and frappe.model.base_document.BaseDocument are aliases of Document.

docs.title: Construction
docs.text:
Call Result Document(doctype, name) Load the document and its child rows. Raises DoesNotExistError. Pass for_update=True to lock the rows (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, not on SQLite). Document(doctype) Load a Single DocType. Uses defaults if no row exists. Document(dict) or Document(**fields) Make a new unsaved document. Raises ValueError without arguments.

Controller code uses frappe.get_doc and frappe.new_doc, which pick the right controller class with get_controller(doctype). A custom DocType (custom = 1) uses Document, or NestedSet when is_tree is set.

Function in frappe.model.document Description get_controller(doctype) Return the controller class. Cached per site in frappe.controllers. Applies override_doctype_class (last entry wins, must subclass the original) and extend_doctype_class hooks. import_controller(doctype) Import the controller class without the cache. get_lazy_controller(doctype, *, site=None, meta=None, controller=None) Return a subclass that loads child tables on first access. Used by frappe.get_lazy_doc. get_doc_permission_check(doc, check_permission=None) -> Document Call doc.check_permission(check_permission), or "read" when it is True. bulk_insert(doctype: str, documents: Iterable[Document], ignore_duplicates: bool = False, chunk_size=1000, commit_chunks=False) Insert documents and their child rows with frappe.db.bulk_insert. Runs no hooks, no validation, no naming. Sets owner, creation, modified. execute_action(__doctype, __name, __action, **kwargs) Worker side of queue_action. On error, rolls back and adds a comment "Action Failed". unlock_document(doctype: str, name: str) Remove the lock of a queued document. Needs write. Whitelisted: POST.

A controller that sets _DOCTYPE_NAME gets a docs collection. The controller boilerplate that Frappe writes for a new DocType sets it. Access it on the class, not on an instance.

docs.text:

Setting a plain int converts it. flags _dict Per-document flags. See Flags. meta Meta Cached frappe.get_meta(self.doctype). permitted_fieldnames set[str] Fields the session user may read. docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
Method Description insert(ignore_permissions=None, ignore_links=None, ignore_if_duplicate=False, ignore_mandatory=None, set_name=None, set_child_names=True) -> Self Insert a new document and its child rows. Checks create permission (and submit if docstatus is 1). Runs the insert hooks. The first three ignore_* arguments set the matching flags. set_name forces a name. save(ignore_permissions=None, ignore_version=None) -> Self Insert if new, else update. Checks write permission. Runs the save hooks. ignore_version defaults to frappe.in_test. Throws if the document came from frappe.read_doc. submit() -> Self Set docstatus to 1 and save(). Checks submit permission. Whitelisted. cancel() -> Self Set docstatus to 2 and save(). Checks cancel permission. Whitelisted. discard() Set docstatus of a draft to 2 with db_set. Checks write permission. Runs no validation. Whitelisted. delete(ignore_permissions=False, force=False, *, delete_permanently=False) Call frappe.delete_doc with this document's flags. See delete_doc. rename(name: str \| int, merge: bool = False, force: bool = False, validate_rename: bool = True) Check write permission, call frappe.model.rename_doc.rename_doc, then reload. Whitelisted. validate_rename is not passed on. reload() -> Self Load all values again from the database. load_from_db() -> Self Same as reload. Called by the constructor. load_children_from_db() Load all child tables again. db_set(fieldname, value=None, update_modified=True, notify=False, commit=False) Set a value on the object and in the database without the save cycle. See db_set. db_get(fieldname) Return the stored value with frappe.db.get_value. get_db_value(key) Same as db_get. db_insert(ignore_if_duplicate=False) Raw INSERT of this row only. Names the document if name is empty. Raises DuplicateEntryError or UniqueValidationError. Retries up to 5 times for a hash name collision. db_update() Raw UPDATE of this row only. Calls db_insert for a new row. Clears frappe.db.value_cache for the DocType. db_update_all() db_update of the parent and every child row. No validation, no hooks. update_modified() Set modified to now and write only that column. update_single(d) Replace the rows of a Single DocType in tabSingles with d. update_children() Write all child tables: delete removed rows, update or insert the others. update_child_table(fieldname: str, df=None) Write one child table. Skips DocTypes in flags.ignore_children_type. deferred_insert() -> None Push the row to Redis. A scheduled job inserts it later. Insertion is not guaranteed. queue_action(action, **kwargs) Lock the document and enqueue action (or _action if it exists, such as _submit) for a worker. enqueue_after_commit defaults to True. Other kwargs go to frappe.enqueue. lock(timeout=None) Make a lock file for the document. Raises DocumentLockedError if a lock younger than 3 hours exists. With timeout, retry once per second. unlock() Delete the lock file. check_if_locked() Throw DocumentLockedError if is_locked. After 30 minutes the message offers a "Force Unlock" action.

Whitelisted methods run through run_doc_method. The desk calls /api/method/run_doc_method with dt and dn, which loads the document with check_permission=True (read). See REST Endpoints for /api/v2/method/run_doc_method and the document method routes.

docs.title: db_set
docs.text:
Parameter Default Description fieldname Fieldname, or a dict of fieldnames and values. value None New value. Ignored when fieldname is a dict. update_modified True Set modified and modified_by. Not changed while the document is in frappe.flags.currently_saving, for example inside on_update. notify False Call notify_update(). commit False Call frappe.db.commit().

db_set loads get_doc_before_save() if it is not loaded, runs before_change, writes with frappe.db.set_value (or set_single_value), then runs on_change. It skips validation, permission checks, mandatory checks, Link checks and Version.

docs.title: Hooks and triggers
docs.text:
Method Description run_method(method: str, *args, **kwargs) Run the controller method, doc_events handlers for the DocType, then for "*". Then run Notifications, Webhooks, DocType Event Server Scripts and automations for method. Raises if method starts with _. Returns the combined return value. run_trigger(method, *args, **kwargs) Alias of run_method. run_notifications(method) Evaluate enabled Notifications of the DocType for the event of method. Document.hook(f) Static decorator. Makes f extensible by doc_events. Dict return values are merged. frappe.db.commit() and rollback() do nothing inside handlers. run_before_save_methods() Run before_validate and the before_* methods for the current action. run_post_save_methods() Run the on_* methods, clear cache, notify, update global search, save Version, run on_change.

A doc_events handler gets (doc, method, *args). A handler that does not accept a method argument gets (doc) when the event has no extra arguments.

Flag Effect ignore_permissions has_permission returns True. Skips permlevel resets. Set by insert(ignore_permissions=True) and save(ignore_permissions=True). ignore_links Skip Link validation and the back link check on cancel. Set by insert(ignore_links=True). ignore_mandatory Skip the mandatory field check. Set by insert(ignore_mandatory=True). ignore_validate Skip validate, before_save, before_submit, before_cancel, before_update_after_submit and set_title_field. before_validate and the standard checks still run. ignore_validate_update_after_submit Allow changes to fields without allow_on_submit on a submitted document. ignore_version Do not save a Version. Function Description rename_doc(doctype=None, old=None, new=None, force=False, merge=False, ignore_permissions=False, ignore_if_exists=False, show_alert=True, rebuild_search=True, doc=None, validate=True) -> str Rename a document. Pass doctype, old, new, or doc, new. See the steps below. validate_rename(doctype, old, new, meta, merge, force=False, ignore_permissions=False, ignore_if_exists=False, save_point=False, old_doc=None) -> str Check a rename and return the validated new name. update_document_title(*, doctype: str, docname: str, title=None, name=None, merge=False, enqueue=False, **kwargs) -> str Change the title, the name, or both. With enqueue, the rename runs in the long queue. Needs write. Whitelisted: POST. bulk_rename(doctype: str, rows=None, via_console: bool = False) -> list[str] \| None Rename from rows of (old, new, merge). Commits after each row. Max 500 rows unless via_console. get_link_fields(doctype: str) -> list[dict] Return Link fields in all DocTypes, Custom Fields and Property Setters that point to doctype. update_link_field_values, rename_dynamic_links, update_user_settings, update_attachments, rename_versions, update_assignments, update_customizations, rename_doctype, rename_parent_and_child, update_autoname_field, update_child_docs, update_options_for_fieldtype, get_select_fields, update_select_field_values, update_parenttype_values, update_sequence_name Steps of rename_doc.

rename_doc steps:

  1. With validate, run before_rename(old, new, merge). A returned string, or a dict with new, changes the new name.
  2. With validate, check: not a Single, old exists, new is different, new exists only with merge (unless ignore_if_exists), write permission on both, and allow_rename unless force or ignore_permissions.
  3. Rename the row and child rows, or move assignments with merge.
  4. Update Link and Dynamic Link values, user settings, attachments and versions.
  5. Run after_rename(old, new, merge) and add an "Edit" comment.
  6. With merge, delete the old document.
  7. Clear the cache, enqueue the global search rebuild, show an alert, and publish doc_rename after commit.

This page lists the public functions for outgoing email, files, print output and Jinja templates. Use it to look up a signature, a default or a side effect. For how-to guides, read Email and Notifications, Files and Print Formats.

Whitelisted means the function is callable at /api/method/<dotted.path>. "any" means the default set: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY.

docs.title: frappe.sendmail
docs.text:
frappe.sendmail is frappe.email.sendmail. It makes an Email Queue record. The scheduler sends queued emails (frappe.email.queue.flush).

frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=None, sender="", subject="No Subject", message="No Message", as_markdown=False, delayed=True,
    reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, unsubscribe_method=None, unsubscribe_params=None,
    unsubscribe_message=None, add_unsubscribe_link=1, attachments=None, content=None, doctype=None, name=None,
    reply_to=None, queue_separately=False, cc=None, bcc=None, message_id=None, in_reply_to=None, send_after=None,
    expose_recipients=None, send_priority=1, communication=None, retry=None, now=None, read_receipt=None,
    is_notification=False, inline_images=None, template=None, args=None, header=None, print_letterhead=False,
    with_container=False, email_read_tracker_url=None, x_priority: Literal[1, 3, 5] = 3, email_headers=None,
    raw_html=False, add_css=True, redact_message_after_send=False, wrapper=None,
) -> EmailQueue | None
Parameter Default Description recipients, cc, bcc None List, or a comma-separated string. Duplicates are removed. Unsubscribed addresses and .invalid addresses are dropped. sender "" Empty or "Administrator" uses the default_sender of the outgoing Email Account. subject "No Subject" message, content "No Message", None HTML body. content wins over message. as_markdown False Convert the body from Markdown. template, args None Render templates/emails/<template>.html (and .txt if it exists) with args. Replaces message. delayed True False sets now=True. now None Send after the current transaction commits, not on the next scheduler run. reference_doctype, reference_name None Link the queue to a document. doctype and name are aliases. Also used to pick the Email Account. attachments None List of dicts. See below. reply_to, message_id, in_reply_to None Headers. in_reply_to is a Communication name. Its message_id becomes In-Reply-To. send_after None Datetime. An integer means that many days from today. expose_recipients None "header" shows all To addresses. "footer" adds a "sent to" line. None hides To recipients from each other. queue_separately False One Email Queue per To recipient, made in a long queue job. Always on for more than 100 recipients. Then the function returns None. send_priority 1 Higher is sent first. x_priority 3 X-Priority header: 1 highest, 3 normal, 5 lowest. add_unsubscribe_link, unsubscribe_method, unsubscribe_params, unsubscribe_message 1, None, None, None The link is added only with a reference DocType and an unsubscribe_message (or for Newsletter). Default method /api/method/frappe.email.queue.unsubscribe. communication None Communication name to link. Needs at least one recipient. read_receipt None Add Disposition-Notification-To. is_notification False Mark as a notification email. inline_images None List of {"filename", "filecontent"}. src values are replaced with Content-IDs. header None Header block added to the body. with_container, wrapper False, None Wrap in a styled container. wrapper defaults to templates/emails/standard.html. print_letterhead False Letterhead for print attachments. email_read_tracker_url None URL for read tracking. email_headers None Extra headers. X- is added when missing. raw_html, add_css False, True Use the template as a full HTML file. Add CSS from the email_css hook. redact_message_after_send False Replace the stored body after it is sent. retry None Deprecated.

Return value: the Email Queue document. An empty list when no recipient is left. None when queue_separately applies. Raises frappe.OutgoingEmailError when no outgoing Email Account exists.

Attachment dicts:

Shape Description {"fid": "<File name>"} or {"file_url": "/private/files/a.pdf"} An existing File. Read when the email is sent. {"print_format_attachment": 1, "doctype": ..., "name": ..., "print_format": ..., "lang": ...} A print rendered when the email is sent. lang defaults to the current language. {"fname": "a.pdf", "fcontent": b"..."} Content in memory, for example from frappe.attach_print. 
frappe.sendmail(
    recipients=["user1@example.com"],
    subject="Order SO-0001",
    template="sample_order",
    args={"customer": "Customer A"},
    reference_doctype="Sample Order",
    reference_name="SO-0001",
    attachments=[frappe.attach_print("Sample Order", "SO-0001", file_name="SO-0001")],
)

docs.title: get_print
docs.text:
frappe.get_print(
    doctype=None, name=None, print_format=None, style=None, as_pdf=False, doc=None, output=None,
    no_letterhead=0, password=None, pdf_options=None, letterhead=None,
    pdf_generator: Literal["chrome", "PlutoPrint", "Typst"] | None = None, settings=None,
)

frappe.get_print is frappe.utils.print_utils.get_print. It returns the print HTML (str), or PDF bytes with as_pdf=True.

  • print_format empty or "Standard" uses the default print format of the DocType. A missing Print Format falls back to Standard.
  • doc renders a document object instead of loading doctype/name.
  • password encrypts the PDF.
  • output is a pypdf.PdfWriter. Pages are added to it and it is returned.
  • The PDF engine is picked by resolve_pdf_generator: the pdf_generator argument, then the Print Format setting, then Print Settings pdf_generator (default PlutoPrint). PlutoPrint falls back to chrome when it cannot render the format.
  • on_print_pdf hooks run before a PDF. pdf_generator hooks can return the PDF.
  • Permission: the user needs read or print on the document, or website permission, or a valid share key. Submittable drafts and cancelled documents need the Print Settings that allow them.

docs.title: Jinja templates
docs.text:
All in frappe.utils.jinja. frappe.render_template, frappe.get_template, frappe.get_jenv and frappe.get_email_from_template are aliases.

Function Description render_template(template, context=None, is_path=None, safe_render=True, *, restrict_globals=None) -> str Render a template path or a template string. Returns "" for an empty template. get_template(path, *, restrict_globals=None) Return a compiled template from the templates folders of the apps. App templates win over frappe templates. get_jenv(*, restrict_globals=None) Return the sandboxed Jinja environment for the request. get_email_from_template(name, args) -> tuple Render templates/emails/<name>.html and .txt. Returns (html, text or None). validate_template(html, restrict_globals=None) Raise ValidationError on a Jinja syntax error. guess_is_path(template) -> bool True for a one-line string that ends in .html, .css, .scss, .py, .md, .json, .js, .xml or .txt. get_jinja_hooks() (methods, filters) from the jinja hook. get_jloader(), set_filters(jenv), safe_render_flags() Internal helpers.

render_template behavior:

  • The environment is a sandbox. restrict_globals=None means True: the template gets render_safe_globals(). False gives the full safe-exec globals.
  • With safe_render=True, a template string that contains .__ raises "Illegal template".
  • An undefined variable renders as its source, for example {{ missing }}.
  • A syntax error raises ValidationError. An error while rendering raises the original exception class. Users allowed to see tracebacks get the traceback as the message.
frappe.render_template("Hello {{ name }}", {"name": "Customer A"})  # "Hello Customer A"
frappe.render_template("templates/emails/new_user.html", {"link": "/login"})

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.sendmail does not send in the request. Use now=True only when the user waits for the email. It still sends after commit.
  • attach_print skips the print permission check. Check permission before you attach a document the user asked for.
  • File.get_content() returns str for text files and bytes for binary files.
  • Template strings from users are rendered in the sandbox. Do not pass restrict_globals=False for them.

docs.title: frappe namespace
docs.text: This page lists every public name on the frappe module on develop (frappe.__version__ == "17.0.0-dev"). Use it to look up an exact signature, default or side effect. The list comes from dir(frappe) and the _LAZY_IMPORTS table in frappe/__init__.py, with signatures read by inspect.signature on a develop site. For the Document class, see Document. For frappe.db, see Database. For frappe.utils, see Utilities.

docs.title: How names are loaded
docs.text:
• Names in _LAZY_IMPORTS load their module on first access through frappe.__getattr__, then stay in globals(). Examples: frappe.get_doc, frappe.enqueue, frappe.sendmail.
  • Names marked with a Defined in module other than frappe are re-exports. Import them from either place.
  • Request-scoped objects (frappe.db, frappe.session, frappe.form_dict ...) are LocalProxy objects on frappe.local. They are valid only after frappe.init() and, for db, frappe.connect().
  • frappe.* re-exports every class from frappe/exceptions.py (from .exceptions import *).

docs.title: delete_doc
docs.text:
frappe.delete_doc calls frappe.model.delete_doc.delete_doc. For each name it does this:

  1. Return False if the record does not exist and ignore_missing=True. Raise DoesNotExistError if ignore_missing=False.
  2. Lock the row with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT. Throw QueryTimeoutError or QueryDeadlockError if another transaction holds it.
  3. Check delete permission and throw if the document is submitted. Skipped with for_reload=True.
  4. Run on_trash and on_change (with doc.flags.in_delete). Skipped with ignore_on_trash=True.
  5. Check that no document links to it. Skipped with force=True. Raises LinkExistsError.
  6. Delete the row and child rows, run after_delete, delete attachments, passwords, global search entries and tags.
  7. Add a Deleted Document unless delete_permanently=True or for_reload=True.
  8. Enqueue delete_dynamic_links after commit, publish doc_update and list_update, and insert a feed entry.
Parameter Default Description doctype None DocType. If empty, read dt and dn from frappe.form_dict. name None Name, or a list of names. force False Skip the link check. Also allows deleting a standard DocType. ignore_doctypes None Child DocTypes whose rows are not deleted. for_reload False Used when a DocType is reloaded. Runs before_reload, skips permission and on_trash, deletes permanently. ignore_permissions False Skip the delete permission check. flags None Dict copied to doc.flags. doc.delete() passes its own flags. ignore_on_trash False Skip on_trash and on_change. ignore_missing True Return False instead of raising for a missing record. delete_permanently False Do not keep a Deleted Document copy.

Warning

With a list of names, delete_doc returns False at the first missing name. Names after it in the list are not deleted.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
frappe.get_list and frappe.get_all call frappe.model.qb_query.DatabaseQuery(doctype).execute(). For filter syntax, see Database. For frappe.db.get_value and other database methods, see Database.

Function Description get_list(doctype, *args, **kwargs) Return rows as a list of _dict. Applies role permissions, user permissions and sharing of user (default session user). No default row limit. get_all(doctype, *args, **kwargs) Same as get_list with ignore_permissions=True. Sets limit_page_length=0 if not given. get_value(*args, **kwargs) Alias of frappe.db.get_value. No permission check. get_cached_value(doctype: str, name: str \| dict, fieldname: str \| Iterable[str] = 'name', as_dict: bool = False) -> Any Return field values from get_cached_doc. Returns None if the document does not exist. as_dict=True needs a list of fieldnames. get_single_value(setting: str, fieldname: str, /, *, as_dict: bool = False) Return a cached value of a Single DocType. set_value(doctype, docname, fieldname, value=None) Call frappe.client.set_value: load the document, update it, run save() with all validations and permission checks. fieldname can be a dict. Throws if only standard fields are given. get_query(*args, **kwargs) -> QueryBuilder Build a query from table, fields, filters and other options. Defined in frappe.query_builder.utils. See Query Builder. get_query_builder(type_of_db: str) Return the query builder class for mariadb, postgres or sqlite. build_match_conditions(doctype, as_condition=True) Return the user permission conditions of a DocType as SQL, or as a list.

docs.title: get_list arguments
docs.text:
Argument Type Default Description fields list \| tuple \| str [pluck or "name"] Columns. Use the dict form for SQL functions, for example {"COUNT": "*"}. Child fields as "items.qty". filters dict \| list None AND conditions. or_filters dict \| list None OR conditions. group_by str None Group by fields. order_by str DocType sort_field and sort_order Order by fields. limit int None Maximum rows. None or 0 returns all rows. offset int None Rows to skip. as_list bool False Return tuples, not dicts. pluck str None Return a flat list of one field. distinct bool False SELECT DISTINCT. ignore_permissions bool False Skip permission checks. get_all sets it. ignore_user_permissions bool False Skip only User Permissions. user str session user Check permissions of this user. parent_doctype str None Parent DocType, needed to query a child table with permissions. reference_doctype str None DocType whose link field context applies to user permissions. with_comment_count bool False Add _comment_count to each row. update dict None Merge this dict into each row. run bool True False returns the query object, not rows. debug bool False Print the query. save_user_settings, save_user_settings_fields, user_settings False, False, None Save list settings of the user. Used by the list view. ignore_ddl bool False Return [] if the table does not exist. limit_start, limit_page_length, start, page_length int 0, None, None, None Deprecated aliases of offset and limit. They warn when set. with_childnames, join, ignore_ifnull, strict Accepted for compatibility. They do nothing.

The first two arguments are swapped when fields looks like filters (a dict, or a list of lists).

frappe.get_list("Sample Order", filters={"status": "Draft"}, fields=["name", "total"], order_by="creation desc", limit=20)
frappe.get_all("Sample Item", filters={"disabled": 0}, pluck="name")
frappe.get_list("Sample Order", fields=["status", {"COUNT": "*", "as": "count"}], group_by="status")

docs.text:
Parameter Default Description msg String, list (with as_list) or list of lists (with as_table). title "Message" Dialog title. raise_exception False True raises ValidationError. An exception class or instance raises that exception with msg. as_table, as_list False Render a list of lists as a table, or a list as a bullet list. indicator None blue, green, orange, red or yellow. Red if raise_exception is set. alert False Show a toast, not a dialog. primary_action None Dict for a button: label, and server_action or client_action, args, hide_on_success. is_minimizable, wide False Dialog options. realtime False Publish the message at once with the msgprint realtime event, not in the response. allow_dangerous_html False Skip clean_html on the message.

frappe.throw(_("Rate must be positive"), title=_("Invalid Rate"))

docs.title: log_error
docs.text:
• title is the method field. message is the error field. Without message, Frappe logs the current traceback.
  • If title contains a newline and message is set, the two are swapped.
  • Inserts with ignore_permissions=True. Uses deferred_insert when defer_insert=True, in read-only mode, or in a read-only transaction.
  • Errors while writing the log go to the site log file. The function returns None then.
  • Returns None if no database connection exists.

Warning

frappe.log_error(message="...") without title raises TypeError on develop. Always pass title.

All classes are in frappe/exceptions.py and on frappe. The HTTP status comes from http_status_code. A class without one inherits it from its base, or gives 500.

docs.title: Whitelisting and calls
docs.text:
See Whitelisted Methods and REST Endpoints.

Function Description whitelist(allow_guest=False, xss_safe=False, methods=None, force_types=None, rate_limit=None) Decorator. Makes a function callable at /api/method/<dotted.path>. See below. is_whitelisted(method) Raise PermissionError if method is not whitelisted, or is not guest-allowed for Guest. Raise AppDisabledError if its app is disabled on the site. For Guest and non-xss_safe methods, sanitize string values in form_dict. override_whitelisted_method(original_method: str) -> str Return the last path from the override_whitelisted_methods hook, or the original path. validate_and_sanitize_search_inputs(fn) Decorator for custom Link search query functions. Validates doctype, txt, searchfield, start, page_len, filters. Defined in frappe.desk.search. read_only() Decorator. With read_from_replica in site config, run the function on the replica connection. Also marks it read-only for Flow. write_only() Decorator. Switch to the primary connection while the function runs, if a replica is active. call(fn: str \| Callable, *args, **kwargs) Call a function, or a dotted path, with only the keyword arguments it accepts. get_newargs(fn: Callable, kwargs: dict) -> dict Return kwargs without keys fn does not accept. Always removes ignore_permissions and flags. get_attr(method_string: str) Return the object at a dotted path. Defined in frappe.utils.

@frappe.whitelist details:

  • methods: None allows GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and QUERY. A string or list limits the methods. QUERY is added when GET is in the list.
  • allow_guest=True lets Guest call it. Guest arguments are HTML-sanitized unless xss_safe=True.
  • force_types: True requires type annotations on every argument. None reads the require_type_annotated_api_methods hook of the function's app.
  • Arguments are converted and checked against the annotations in a request or in tests (frappe.utils.typing_validations.validate_argument_types).
  • rate_limit accepts only None. Any other value raises TypeError. To rate limit, put @frappe.rate_limiter.rate_limit(...) below @frappe.whitelist().
# sample_app/api.py
import frappe

@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def set_rate(item: str, rate: float) -> float:
    doc = frappe.get_doc("Sample Item", item, check_permission="write")
    doc.rate = rate
    doc.save()
    return doc.rate

docs.title: Jobs, Cache and Realtime API
docs.text:
This page lists the public functions of the background job, scheduler, Redis cache and realtime modules. Use it to look up a signature, a default or a side effect. For how-to guides, read Background Jobs, Scheduler, Caching and Realtime.

Whitelisted means the function is callable at /api/method/<dotted.path>. "any" means the default set: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY.

docs.title: frappe.enqueue
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue is frappe.utils.background_jobs.enqueue.

frappe.enqueue(
    method: str | Callable, queue: str = "default", timeout: int | None = None, event: str | None = None,
    is_async: bool = True, job_name: str | None = None, now: bool = False, enqueue_after_commit: bool = False,
    *, on_success: Callable | None = None, on_failure: Callable | None = None, at_front: bool = False,
    job_id: str | None = None, deduplicate=False, at_front_when_starved=False, rq_retry: Retry | None = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> Job | Any
Parameter Default Description method Dotted path or function. The worker calls it with **kwargs. queue "default" short, default, long, or a queue in the workers key of common_site_config.json. Other names raise ValidationError. timeout None Seconds. None uses the queue timeout: 300 for short and default, 1500 for long. event None Stored on the job. Used by the scheduler. is_async True False in tests runs the job in the same process through RQ. False outside tests calls the method directly and shows a deprecation warning. Use now. job_name None Deprecated. Use job_id. now False Call the method directly with frappe.call and return its result. enqueue_after_commit False Add the job only after the current transaction commits. Returns None. on_success, on_failure None RQ callbacks. on_failure defaults to truncate_failed_registry. at_front False Put the job at the front of the queue. job_id None Your ID. Stored as <site>\|\|<job_id>, with : replaced by \|. deduplicate False Needs job_id. Returns None if a job with that ID is queued or started. A finished job with the ID is deleted first. at_front_when_starved False Use at_front when the queue has more than 16 jobs. rq_retry None rq.Retry object to retry a failed job. **kwargs Arguments for method. async is read as is_async.

Side effects and behavior:

  • The job runs as the user who enqueued it, on the same site.
  • The worker commits after the method returns. On an exception it rolls back, writes an Error Log, and commits the log.
  • On a deadlock, lock timeout or frappe.RetryBackgroundJobError, the worker retries up to 5 times.
  • before_job and after_job hooks run around the method. frappe.local.job holds site, method, job_name, kwargs, user and after_job.
  • If the queue has max_queued_jobs jobs (default 500, plus 50 for each site), it raises frappe.QueueOverloaded.
  • If Redis is down during bench migrate, the method runs directly.
# sample_app/sample_app/api.py
import frappe


@frappe.whitelist(methods=["POST"])
def rebuild_totals(order: str):
    frappe.has_permission("Sample Order", "write", order, throw=True)
    frappe.enqueue(
        "sample_app.sample_app.jobs.rebuild_totals",
        queue="long",
        job_id=f"rebuild_totals::{order}",
        deduplicate=True,
        enqueue_after_commit=True,
        order=order,
    )

docs.title: frappe.enqueue_task
docs.text:
frappe.enqueue_task is frappe.utils.task_queue.enqueue_task. It makes a Background Task document that users can follow, cancel and retry in the desk.

frappe.enqueue_task(
    method: str | Callable, *, task_name: str | None = None, queue: str = "default", timeout: int | None = None,
    ref_doctype: str | None = None, ref_docname: str | None = None, deduplicate: bool = False,
    job_id: str | None = None, enqueue_after_commit: bool = True, now: bool = False,
    on_success: Callable | None = None, on_failure: Callable | None = None,
    retry_on: tuple[type[Exception], ...] = (), max_retries: int = 0, show_progress_bar: bool = True,
    allow_user_cancellation: bool = True, allow_user_retry: bool = True, at_front: bool = False,
    at_front_when_starved: bool = False, **kwargs,
) -> BackgroundTask
  • Inserts the Background Task (status Queued) with ignore_permissions, then enqueues. enqueue_after_commit is True by default.
  • task_name defaults to the dotted method path. job_id defaults to the task ID (a UUID).
  • The worker sets status Running, then Completed (with result as JSON) or Failed (with the traceback). It commits each status change and sends a task_update realtime event to the user.
  • retry_on with max_retries > 0 retries on those exceptions through RQ.
  • on_success and on_failure get the keyword arguments they declare from task, result or exception, and the job kwargs.
Function Description frappe.get_current_task() -> BackgroundTask \| None Return the Background Task of the running job. frappe.utils.task_queue.get_task_status(task_id: str) -> dict \| None Return status, progress, stage, result, exception, started_at, ended_at, with cached progress applied.

BackgroundTask methods:

Method Description publish_progress(percent: int \| float, stage: str \| None = None) -> None Send progress. Calls under 100 percent are throttled to one each 0.2 seconds. update_stage(stage: str) -> None Send a stage text without a number. store_result(result) -> None Save result as JSON with db_set. attach_file(file_name: str, content: bytes, is_private: bool = True, doctype=None, docname=None) -> str Make a File attached to the reference document (or the task). Returns its URL.

Whitelisted endpoints in frappe.core.doctype.background_task.background_task: get_recent_tasks(limit: int = 15) (any), get_cached_task_status(task_id: str) (any), stop_task(task_id: str) (any, owner or System Manager), retry_task(task_id: str) (POST, owner or System Manager).

# sample_app/sample_app/jobs.py
import frappe


def export_orders():
    task = frappe.get_current_task()
    names = frappe.get_all("Sample Order", pluck="name")
    for i, name in enumerate(names, 1):
        ...
        task.publish_progress(i * 100 / len(names))

docs.title: frappe.cache
docs.text:
frappe.cache is a frappe.utils.redis_wrapper.RedisWrapper, a subclass of redis.Redis connected to redis_cache. Values are pickled. frappe.cache() (called) is deprecated.

Key rules (make_key(key, user=None, shared=False)):

  • The key becomes <db_name>|<key> (bytes). So each site has its own keys.
  • user=True adds user:<session user>:. A user name adds user:<name>:.
  • shared=True uses the key as given. All sites see it.

Most methods also keep the value in frappe.local.cache for the rest of the request. Most methods ignore redis.exceptions.ConnectionError.

Method Description set_value(key, val, user=None, expires_in_sec=None, shared=False) -> int Store a value. Returns the pickled size in bytes. get_value(key, generator=None, user=None, expires=False, shared=False, *, use_local_cache=True) Read a value. On a miss, call generator() and store the result. With expires=True, the generator is not called and the value is not kept locally. delete_value(keys, user=None, make_keys=True, shared=False) Delete one key or a list. make_keys=False takes full keys. delete_key(*args, **kwargs) Same as delete_value. delete_keys(key, user=None, shared=False) Delete keys that start with key. get_keys(key, user=None, shared=False) Full keys that start with key. get_all(key) Meant to return values of keys that start with key. See the warning below. exists(*names, user=None, shared=None) -> int Count of keys that exist. expire_key(key, time, *, user=None, shared=False) Set a TTL in seconds. hset(name, key, value, shared=False, *args, **kwargs) Set a field of a hash. Does nothing when key is None. hget(name, key, generator=None, shared=False) Read a field. On a miss, call generator() and store. hgetall(name) -> dict All fields, unpickled. Raises on connection errors. hexists(name, key, shared=False) -> bool True if the field exists. hdel(name, keys, shared=False, pipeline=None) Delete one field or a list. hdel_names(names, key) Delete one field from many hashes in one pipeline. hdel_keys(name_starts_with, key) Delete one field from hashes whose names start with a prefix. hkeys(name) Field names. lpush(key, value, user=None, shared=False), lpop(key, user=None, shared=False), blpop(key, timeout=0, user=None, shared=False) List operations. rpush(key, value), rpop(key), llen(key), lrange(key, start, stop), ltrim(key, start, stop) List operations. No user or shared argument. sadd(name, *values), srem(name, *values), sismember(name, value), spop(name), smembers(name), srandmember(name, count=None) Set operations. Values are not pickled. ft(index_name="idx") RediSearch client with prefixed keys (sugadd, suglen, sugdel, sugget). connected() -> bool True if Redis answers PING.

Warning

get_all(key) returns {key: None}, not the values. srandmember(name, count) ignores count and returns one member.

frappe.cache.set_value("sample_app:rates", {"Hardware": 10}, expires_in_sec=3600)
frappe.cache.get_value("sample_app:rates", expires=True)
frappe.cache.hset("sample_app:rate_by_item", "Laptop", 1200)
frappe.cache.hget("sample_app:rate_by_item", "Laptop")  # 1200
frappe.cache.delete_keys("sample_app:")

Module functions: setup_cache() -> RedisWrapper (makes frappe.cache, with Sentinel when redis_cache_sentinel_enabled is set) and get_sentinel_connection(sentinels, sentinel_username=None, sentinel_password=None, master_username=None, master_password=None).

docs.text:
frappe.client_cache is a ClientCache: process memory in front of Redis, with Redis client tracking for invalidation. It is internal to Frappe and can change without notice. Use frappe.cache in apps.

Member Description ClientCache(maxsize=1024, ttl=600, monitor=None, maxsize_bytes=0) maxsize_bytes defaults to the client_cache_max_bytes config key. get_value(key, *, shared=False, generator=None) Read from memory, else Redis. Misses are not cached locally. set_value(key, val, *, shared=False) Write to Redis and memory. delete_value(key, *, shared=False), delete_keys(pattern) Delete. get_doc(doctype: str, name: str \| None = None) Cached frappe.get_doc. docs.title: Caching decorators
docs.text:
All in frappe.utils.caching. frappe.request_cache and frappe.site_cache are aliases.

Decorator Description request_cache(func) Cache results in frappe.local.request_cache for the request or job. Unhashable arguments skip the cache. Outside a request, calls the function. site_cache(ttl: int \| None = None, maxsize: int \| None = None) Cache results in process memory per site. All entries clear when ttl passes. maxsize removes the oldest entry. Adds func.clear_cache(). Works with or without parentheses. redis_cache(ttl: int \| None = 3600, user: str \| bool \| None = None, shared: bool = False) Cache results in Redis under <module>.<qualname>::<hash of arguments>. A None result is cached too. Adds func.clear_cache(). Works with or without parentheses. http_cache(*, public: bool = False, max_age: int \| None = None, stale_while_revalidate: int \| None = None) Set Cache-Control on GET responses of a whitelisted method. Does not cache on the server. deprecated_local_cache(namespace, key, generator, regenerate_if_none=False) The function behind the deprecated frappe.local_cache.

Warning

redis_cache builds the key with Python hash(). String hashes change between processes, so a result cached in one worker is not found by another worker for the same string arguments. Use frappe.cache.get_value with an explicit key when workers must share the result.

docs.title: Realtime
docs.text: All in frappe.realtime. frappe.publish_realtime and frappe.publish_progress are aliases. Events go to the Redis channel events of redis_queue. Connection errors are ignored.

docs.title: publish_realtime
docs.text:
frappe.publish_realtime(
    event: str | None = None, message: dict | None = None, room: str | None = None, user: str | None = None,
    doctype: str | None = None, docname: str | None = None, task_id: str | None = None, after_commit: bool = False,
)

The room is picked in this order:

  1. Event list_update always uses doctype:<doctype> (from doctype or message["doctype"]). Event docinfo_update always uses doc:<doctype>/<docname>. These replace a room you pass.
  2. room, when given.
  3. task_id (or frappe.local.task_id) uses task_progress:<task_id>. Adds task_id to the message and sets after_commit=False.
  4. user uses user:<user>. Event msgprint without user goes to the session user.
  5. doctype and docname use doc:<doctype>/<docname>.
  6. Else the site room all (System Users of the site).

event=None becomes task_progress with a task, else global. With after_commit=True, events are queued and sent after commit, and dropped on rollback. The same event, message and room are sent once.

docs.title: Python Socket.IO handlers
docs.text: For the Python Socket.IO backend, frappe.realtime.realtime is a Registry. realtime.on(event: str, *, frappe_context: bool = False, allow_guest: bool = False) registers a handler. Frappe imports <app>/realtime/handlers.py of each installed app. The handler gets a frappe.realtime.Socket with site, user, user_type, installed_apps, join(room), leave(room), emit(event, data=None, room=None), get(key, default=None), set(key, value), participants(room), user_of(sid) and has_permission(doctype, name=None). See Realtime.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A job that reads data from the current request needs enqueue_after_commit=True. Else the worker can start before the commit.
  • frappe.enqueue(..., now=True) runs in the same transaction. The worker commit and retry rules do not apply.
  • get_queues_timeout is cached for the process. Restart workers after you change workers in config.
  • site_cache is per process. func.clear_cache() clears only the current process.
  • frappe.cache keeps a request-local copy. A value changed by another process in the same request is not seen. Pass use_local_cache=False to read Redis.

docs.title: Permissions and Sessions API
docs.text:
This page lists the public functions and classes of the permission, sharing, session, login, user and defaults modules. Use it to find an exact signature, default or side effect. For the permission model (roles, permlevels, User Permissions, has_permission hooks), read Permissions. For login, API keys and OAuth, read Authentication.

The wrappers on the frappe namespace (frappe.has_permission, frappe.get_roles, frappe.only_for, frappe.set_user, frappe.get_user) are in frappe namespace.

Whitelisted means the function is callable at /api/method/<dotted.path>. "any" means the default set: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, QUERY.

docs.title: frappe.permissions: constants
docs.text: Name Value std_rights, rights ("select", "read", "write", "create", "delete", "submit", "cancel", "amend", "print", "email", "report", "import", "export", "share") GUEST_ROLE "Guest" ALL_USER_ROLE "All". Website users have it too. SYSTEM_USER_ROLE "Desk User" ADMIN_ROLE "Administrator" AUTOMATIC_ROLES (GUEST_ROLE, ALL_USER_ROLE, SYSTEM_USER_ROLE, ADMIN_ROLE). Frappe gives these by user type. They are not stored in Has Role.

docs.title: has_permission
docs.text:
frappe.permissions.has_permission(
    doctype, ptype="read", doc=None, user=None, *,
    parent_doctype=None, print_logs=True, debug=False, ignore_share_permissions=False,
) -> bool

Return True if user (default: session user) has ptype on the DocType, or on doc when given. This function does not raise. frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True) is the raising wrapper.

The checks run in this order:

  1. Administrator gets True.
  2. ptype="share" gets False when System Settings disable_document_sharing is set.
  3. If doctype is a document, it is used as doc.
  4. A child DocType is checked on its parent with has_child_permission.
  5. A DocType of a disabled app gets False.
  6. With doc (a document, or a name that is loaded with frappe.get_lazy_doc), get_doc_permissions decides. Without doc, role permissions at permlevel 0 decide. submit on a non-submittable DocType and import on a DocType without allow_import get False.
  7. If still denied and ignore_share_permissions is not set, a share (DocShare) can grant read, write, share, submit, email, print and custom permission types. email and print are checked as read shares. Without doc, one shared document of the DocType is enough.
  8. select falls back to read.

With print_logs=True and the user checking their own access, the reasons for a denial are sent with frappe.msgprint. With debug=True, the steps are collected in frappe.local.permission_debug_log.

docs.title: Other checks
docs.text: Function Description get_doc_permissions(doc, user=None, ptype=None, debug=False) -> dict Return the evaluated rights for a document, for example {"read": 1, "write": 0, ...}. Runs has_controller_permissions first. If a hook denies, returns {ptype: 0}. Applies if_owner rules and User Permissions. Sets submit and import to 0 when the DocType does not allow them. get_role_permissions(doctype_meta, user=None, is_owner=None, debug=False) -> dict Return rights from role rules at permlevel 0, with an if_owner sub-dict and has_if_owner_enabled. doctype_meta can be a DocType name. Cached per request in frappe.local.role_permissions. has_user_permission(doc, user=None, debug=False, *, ptype=None, strict=True) -> bool Return False if User Permissions block the document, or a Link field value in the document or its child rows. Applies apply_strict_user_permissions from System Settings when strict is true. has_controller_permissions(doc, ptype, user=None, debug=False) -> bool Call the has_permission hooks for the DocType and "*". A hook can deny only. Returns True when no hook denies. has_child_permission(child_doctype, ptype="read", child_doc=None, user=None, parent_doctype=None, *, debug=False, print_logs=True) -> bool Check a child DocType on its parent. Needs parent_doctype or a child_doc with parenttype. Checks that the table field exists and its permlevel is readable. check_doctype_permission(doctype: str, ptype: str = "read") -> None Raise frappe.PermissionError if the user has no ptype on the DocType. Ignores shares. Sets frappe.flags.disable_traceback. handle_does_not_exist_error(fn) Decorator for exception handlers. Turns a DoesNotExistError into a PermissionError when the user cannot read the DocType, so a missing record does not leak. is_system_user(user: str \| None = None) -> bool Return True if user_type is System User. Reads the cached User value. validate_desk_user() -> None Raise frappe.PermissionError for Website Users and Guest. check_app_permission() Return True if the session user is a System User with the System Manager role. push_perm_check_log(log, debug=False) Add a message to the denial log that has_permission prints. print_has_permission_check_logs(func) Decorator used on has_permission. Prints the denial log with msgprint.

docs.title: frappe.permissions: change rules
docs.text:
These functions write Custom DocPerm rows. They do not commit.

Function Description add_permission(doctype, role, permlevel=0, ptype=None) Add a rule with ptype (default read) set. Copies DocPerm to Custom DocPerm first if needed. A session is a row in tabSessions and an entry in the Redis hash session. Both use the SHA-256 hash of the sid as key. The client cookie sid holds the raw sid. All guests share the sid "Guest".

docs.title: frappe.defaults
docs.text:
Defaults are DefaultValue rows keyed by parent: a user name, __default (global) or __global. A key can hold more than one value. Then the read value is a list. Reads use frappe.client_cache under defaults::<parent>.

Function Description get_defaults(user=None) -> dict Global defaults updated with the user's defaults, plus user and owner. Default user is the session user. get_defaults_for(parent="__default") -> dict All defaults of one parent. get_user_default(key, user=None) The first value for key from get_defaults(user). For a DocType key (for example "Company"), User Permissions decide the value. Returns None if User Permissions do not allow the value. get_user_default_as_list(key, user=None) -> list All values for key, filtered by User Permissions. set_user_default(key, value, user=None, parenttype=None) Replace the value for the user. add_user_default(key, value, user=None, parenttype=None) Add one more value for the user. clear_user_default(key, user=None) Delete the key for the user. get_global_default(key) The first value from get_defaults(). A session user's own value wins over the global one. set_global_default(key, value), add_global_default(key, value) Same as the user forms, with parent __default. set_default(key, value, parent, parenttype="__default") Replace the value. value=None deletes it. Locks the row with FOR UPDATE. Clears the defaults cache. add_default(key, value, parent, parenttype=None) Insert a row. Clears the cache of the parent (frappe.clear_cache). clear_default(key=None, value=None, parent=None, name=None, parenttype=None) Delete rows that match. Raises Exception when no filter is given. get_user_permission_default(key, defaults, user=None) The User Permission marked is_default, or the one that matches the stored default. is_a_user_permission_key(key) True when key has no : and is not in snake case. not_in_user_permission(key, value, user=None) True when User Permissions exist for key and value is not one of them. get_user_permissions(user=None) Kept for old code. Same as the User Permission function. 
import frappe.defaults

frappe.defaults.set_user_default("sample_key", "A", "user1@example.com")
frappe.defaults.add_user_default("sample_key", "B", "user1@example.com")
frappe.defaults.get_user_default("sample_key", "user1@example.com")          # "A"
frappe.defaults.get_user_default_as_list("sample_key", "user1@example.com")  # ["A", "B"]

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• frappe.permissions.has_permission does not raise and has no throw argument. Use frappe.has_permission(..., throw=True).
  • has_permission hooks can only deny. They cannot grant a right that roles do not give.
  • frappe.utils.user.is_system_user and frappe.permissions.is_system_user return different things.
  • delete_session, Session.start and Session.update commit the transaction.
  • get_roles is cached in Redis. After you change Has Role rows with SQL, call frappe.clear_cache(user=...).

docs.title: frappe.qb
docs.text:
frappe.qb builds SQL from Python objects. It is a PyPika 0.51 dialect with Frappe additions. Use this page to look up a class, function or argument. For a guided introduction with joins, subqueries and updates, see Query Builder.

All SQL on this page was made on a develop site with MariaDB. Values are shown inline for reading. run() sends them as bound parameters.

Warning

Queries built with frappe.qb skip permissions, validations, controller methods and doc_events. UPDATE, INSERT and DELETE do not set modified and do not clear the document cache. Only frappe.qb.get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False) checks permissions.

docs.title: The builder classes
docs.text:
frappe.qb is frappe.local.qb. frappe.connect() sets it to the class for db_type in the site config:

db_type Class PyPika base mariadb frappe.query_builder.builder.MariaDB MySQLQuery postgres frappe.query_builder.builder.Postgres PostgreSQLQuery sqlite frappe.query_builder.builder.SQLite SQLLiteQuery

frappe.db.qb is the class for the dialect of that connection. Use it when the connection can be a replica or another database. frappe.query_builder.get_query_builder(type_of_db: str) returns the class for a db_type.

Class attributes and methods:

Name Description DocType(table_name: str, *args, **kwargs) -> Table Return the table tab<table_name>. Raises frappe.ValidationError ("Invalid DocType") if the name has characters other than letters, digits, _, space and -. Table(name, schema=None, alias=None) Return a PyPika table with the exact name, for tables such as __Auth or tabSingles. Schema(name) Return a schema. frappe.qb.Schema("information_schema").tables is a table in it. On Postgres, information_schema.tables maps to pg_stat_all_tables. Field(name, table=None, alias=None) Return a field. On Postgres, table_name maps to relname and table_rows to n_tup_ins. from_(table) Start a SELECT. A string is passed to DocType(). into(table) Start an INSERT. A string is passed to DocType(). update(table) Start an UPDATE. A string is passed to DocType(). select(*terms) Start a SELECT without a table. with_(table, name, recursive=False) Start a query with a WITH (CTE). recursive=True renders WITH RECURSIVE. get_query(...) Build a query from fields and filters. See get_query. max(dt, fieldname, filters=None, **kwargs) Return MAX(fieldname) for the filters, or 0. kwargs go to run(). min(dt, fieldname, filters=None, **kwargs) Return MIN(fieldname), or 0. avg(dt, fieldname, filters=None, **kwargs) Return AVG(fieldname), or 0. sum(dt, fieldname, filters=None, **kwargs) Return SUM(fieldname), or 0. functions(name: str, *args, **kwargs) -> Function Return the SQL function name with the arguments. terms A frappe._dict of all public names in pypika.terms. asc, desc Order.asc and Order.desc. validate_doctype(doctype) The name check that DocType() runs. Tables(*names), create_table, drop_table, create_index, drop_index, drop_database, drop_user, drop_view, load Inherited from PyPika Query. 
frappe.qb.max("Sample Item", "rate")                                     # 900.0
frappe.qb.sum("Sample Item", "rate", filters={"category": "Hardware"})   # 1195.0

frappe.qb.from_(frappe.qb.Table("__Auth")).select("name").get_sql()
# SELECT `name` FROM `__Auth`

docs.title: The frappe.query_builder module
docs.text:
frappe.query_builder exports everything from pypika (with from pypika import *) and these Frappe names:

Name Description DocType(*args, **kwargs) Calls frappe.qb.DocType. Table(*args, **kwargs) Calls frappe.qb.Table. get_query(*args, **kwargs) Calls frappe.database.query.Engine().get_query. Same as frappe.qb.get_query. get_query_builder(type_of_db: str) Return the builder class for a db_type. Interval Frappe's Interval. It replaces PyPika's and also renders on SQLite. Field, Column PyPika Field and Column. ParameterizedValueWrapper, ParameterizedFunction Frappe classes that replace PyPika's ValueWrapper and Function, so values become bound parameters. patch_all() Apply the Frappe patches to PyPika. Runs on import.

Common PyPika names from the same module: Case, Criterion, EmptyCriterion, Order, Not, NULL, Tuple, Array, JSON, JoinType, CustomFunction, Parameter, Index, Rollup, Schema, AliasedQuery, Query.

Importing frappe.query_builder patches PyPika:

  • table.field_name and table["field name"] return a Field bound to the table.
  • query.run() and query.walk() are added to every query and union.
  • .like() and .not_like() render ILIKE and NOT ILIKE on Postgres.
  • .regex() renders REGEXP on MariaDB and SQLite, and ~* on Postgres.

docs.title: Criteria
docs.text:
Python SQL Item.rate == 10, !=, <, >, <=, >= =, <>, <, >, <=, >= (a) & (b), (a) \| (b) AND, OR ~(a), Not(a) NOT Item.category.isin([...]), .notin([...]) IN, NOT IN. The value can be a subquery. Item.name.like("L%"), .not_like("L%") LIKE, NOT LIKE (ILIKE on Postgres) Item.name.ilike("l%") ILIKE Item.name.regex("^L") REGEXP (MariaDB, SQLite), ~* (Postgres) Item.description.isnull(), .isnotnull() IS NULL, IS NOT NULL Item.rate[50:150], Item.rate.between(50, 150) BETWEEN 50 AND 150 Tuple(Item.category, Item.disabled).isin([("Hardware", 0)]) (category, disabled) IN (('Hardware', 0)) Criterion.all([a, b]), Criterion.any([a, b]) a AND b, a OR b. An empty list gives an EmptyCriterion that adds nothing.

Put parentheses around each side of & and |. Python binds & before ==.

frappe.database.query.RawCriterion(sql_string) is a criterion from a raw SQL string. It supports &, | and ~. Never put user input in it.

docs.title: Query methods
docs.text:
These come from PyPika. Each returns a new query.

Method SQL .select(*terms) SELECT. A string is a column name. "*" is all columns. .where(criterion) WHERE. Many calls are joined with AND. .join(table, how=JoinType.inner).on(criterion) JOIN ... ON. .left_join(table), .inner_join(table), .right_join(table), .outer_join(table), .cross_join(table) Join of that type. .groupby(*terms), .having(criterion) GROUP BY, HAVING .orderby(*terms, order=None) ORDER BY. Without order, no direction is written, so the database sorts ASC. .limit(n), .offset(n) LIMIT, OFFSET .distinct() SELECT DISTINCT .for_update(nowait=False, skip_locked=False, of=()) FOR UPDATE, with NOWAIT or SKIP LOCKED .delete() DELETE (after from_) .set(field, value) SET (after update) .columns(*names), .insert(*rows) Columns and rows (after into) .ignore() Ignore duplicate rows. frappe.db.bulk_insert uses it on MariaDB and SQLite. .on_duplicate_key_update(field, value) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (MariaDB) .on_conflict(*fields).do_nothing(), .do_update(field, value=None) ON CONFLICT (Postgres, SQLite) query1 + query2, query1 * query2 UNION, UNION ALL .get_sql(), str(query) The SQL with values inline. Use it to read the query only. 
Item = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Item")
(
    frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name).where(Item.rate > 500)
    + frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name).where(Item.rate < 50)
).run(pluck=True)
# ['Laptop', 'Keyboard']

docs.title: run() and walk()
docs.text:
query.run(*args, **kwargs) runs the query on frappe.local.db. To run on another connection, pass the query to that connection: db.sql(query).

run() takes the keyword arguments of frappe.db.sql:

Argument Result none Tuple of tuples as_dict=True List of frappe._dict as_list=True List of lists pluck=True List of the first column update={...} Dict merged into each row. Needs as_dict. debug=True Logs the query and its run time run=False Returns the SQL with placeholders. The values are not returned. as_iterator=True Generator of rows. See frappe.db.unbuffered_cursor.

After the query runs, run() also:

  • runs the child queries of get_query and adds their rows (only with as_dict=True),
  • masks the values of masked fields when the query came from get_query(..., ignore_permissions=False),
  • removes a name column that get_query added only for child queries.

query.walk() returns (sql, params). The SQL has %(paramN)s placeholders. frappe.db.sql(query) calls walk() on a query object.

frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Item", filters={"category": "Hardware"}).walk()
# ('SELECT `name` FROM `tabSample Item` WHERE `category`=%(param1)s', {'param1': 'Hardware'})

In a Server Script, run() raises frappe.PermissionError for a query that is not SELECT or EXPLAIN.

docs.title: Custom functions and constants
docs.text:
Name Description CustomFunction(name, ["arg1", ...]) Make a function class. From frappe.query_builder. frappe.qb.functions("UPPER", Item.name) Call any SQL function by name. frappe.query_builder.custom.ConstantColumn(value) A column with the same string in every row. Its default alias is the value. frappe.query_builder.terms.SubQuery(query, alias=None) (also subqry) Wrap a query as a criterion term, for > or = against a subquery. 
from frappe.query_builder import CustomFunction
from frappe.query_builder.custom import ConstantColumn
from frappe.query_builder.functions import Count, GroupConcat

Item = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Item")
DateOnly = CustomFunction("DATE", ["value"])

frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(
    Item.category,
    Count(Item.name).as_("count"),
    GroupConcat(Item.name, "; ").as_("names"),
).groupby(Item.category).get_sql()
# SELECT `category`,COUNT(`name`) `count`,GROUP_CONCAT(`name` SEPARATOR '; ') `names`
# FROM `tabSample Item` GROUP BY `category`

frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(DateOnly(Item.creation).as_("d"), ConstantColumn("Sample Item").as_("doctype")).get_sql()
# SELECT DATE(`creation`) `d`,'Sample Item' `doctype` FROM `tabSample Item`

docs.title: Case, Order and Interval
docs.text:
Name Use Case().when(criterion, value).else_(value) CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END. Chain more .when() calls. Order.asc, Order.desc The order argument of .orderby(). Also frappe.qb.asc and frappe.qb.desc. Interval(years=0, months=0, days=0, hours=0, minutes=0, seconds=0, microseconds=0, quarters=0, weeks=0, dialect=None) A date interval. Add it to or subtract it from a date term. 
from frappe.query_builder import Case, Interval, Order
from frappe.query_builder.functions import Now

Item = frappe.qb.DocType("Sample Item")
band = Case().when(Item.rate >= 200, "High").else_("Low")

frappe.qb.from_(Item).select(Item.name, band.as_("band")).where(
    Item.creation > Now() - Interval(days=7)
).orderby(Item.rate, order=Order.desc).get_sql()
# SELECT `name`,CASE WHEN `rate`>=200 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END `band` FROM `tabSample Item`
# WHERE `creation`>NOW()-INTERVAL '7' DAY ORDER BY `rate` DESC

docs.title: get_query
docs.text:
frappe.qb.get_query(
    table: str | Table,
    fields: str | list | tuple | set | None = None,
    filters: dict | str | int | bool | list | Criterion | None = None,
    order_by: str | None = None,
    group_by: str | None = None,
    limit: int | None = None,
    offset: int | None = None,
    distinct: bool = False,
    for_update: bool = False,
    update: bool = False,
    into: bool = False,
    delete: bool = False,
    *,
    validate_filters: bool = False,
    skip_locked: bool = False,
    wait: bool = True,
    ignore_permissions: bool = True,
    ignore_user_permissions: bool = False,
    user: str | None = None,
    parent_doctype: str | None = None,
    reference_doctype: str | None = None,
    or_filters: dict | list | None = None,
    db_query_compat: bool = False,
) -> QueryBuilder

Build a query from the fields and filters syntax of frappe.get_all. The returned query is immutable. Each method you chain, such as .where(), returns a new query. frappe.db.get_value, get_values, count, set_value and delete use it.

frappe.database.query.Engine(db=None).get_query(...) is the class behind it. Pass db to build for a connection other than frappe.local.db.

Argument Default Description table DocType name or a Table. fields ["name"] Fields to select. See Fields. filters None Conditions joined with AND. See Filters. order_by None No ORDER BY when empty. "KEEP_DEFAULT_ORDERING" uses the sort settings of the DocType. See Order and group. group_by None Comma-separated fields. limit None Non-negative int. Another type raises TypeError. offset None Non-negative int. Without limit, MariaDB gets LIMIT 18446744073709551615 and SQLite gets LIMIT -1. distinct False SELECT DISTINCT. On Postgres, an order_by field that is not selected is dropped with a UserWarning. for_update False Add FOR UPDATE. skip_locked False With for_update, add SKIP LOCKED. wait True With for_update, False adds NOWAIT. update False Return an UPDATE with the filters. Chain .set(). fields is ignored. into False Return an INSERT INTO. Chain .columns() and .insert(). delete False Return a DELETE with the filters. ignore_permissions True False checks select or read permission, field permlevels, user permissions, permission_query_conditions and shares. Raises frappe.PermissionError when the user has no access. ignore_user_permissions False With permissions on, skip User Permission conditions. user frappe.session.user User for the permission checks. parent_doctype None For a child DocType: check permissions on this parent and join it. reference_doctype None DocType of a link field. Applies User Permissions with "Applicable For" this DocType. or_filters None Conditions joined with OR, then added to filters with AND. db_query_compat False True makes a field in order_by without a direction sort ASC, as in frappe.get_list. It also turns None in in and not in into ("",). validate_filters False Deprecated. Not used.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Form Example SQL Field name "rate" `rate` Comma-separated string "name, rate as price" `name`,`rate` `price` Alias "rate as price" `rate` `price` All columns "*" * (with permissions on: all permitted fields) Table-qualified "`tabSample Item`.`rate`" `tabSample Item`.`rate` Link field "item.category" (in Sample Order Item) LEFT JOIN on the linked DocType with an alias such as `tab_Sample Item_1` Child table field "items.item" (in Sample Order) LEFT JOIN on the child table with parent, parenttype and parentfield Child query {"items": ["item", "qty"]} A second query per run. Rows go in a list under items. Needs run(as_dict=True). Function {"COUNT": "*", "as": "n"}, {"SUM": "rate"}, {"IFNULL": ["description", "''"]} COUNT(*)n`,SUM(rate),IFNULL(description,'')` Arithmetic {"MUL": ["rate", 2], "as": "double"} `rate`*2 `double` Query builder term Count(Item.name), Item.rate as built

Function keys are COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN, ABS, EXTRACT, LOCATE, TIMESTAMP, IFNULL, CONCAT, NOW, NULLIF, MONTHNAME, QUARTER, MONTH, YEAR. Arithmetic keys are ADD, SUB, MUL and DIV, with exactly two operands. Functions and operators can nest. A string argument is a field name, a number, "*" (COUNT only), or a quoted literal such as "'text'". An alias must be a simple identifier.

A function written as a string, such as "count(name) as c", raises frappe.ValidationError. Any other field string that is not a plain, backticked, table-qualified or aliased name raises frappe.PermissionError.

frappe.qb.get_query(
    "Sample Item",
    fields=["category", {"COUNT": "*", "as": "n"}, {"SUM": "rate", "as": "total"}],
    group_by="category",
    order_by="total desc",
).run(as_dict=True)

frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Order", fields=["name", {"items": ["item", "qty"]}], limit=1, order_by="name asc").run(as_dict=True)
# [{'name': 'SO-00001', 'items': [{'item': 'Laptop', 'qty': 2.0}, {'item': 'Monitor', 'qty': 2.0}]}]

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Form Example SQL Name "Laptop" name='Laptop' List of names ["Laptop", "Monitor"] name IN ('Laptop','Monitor') Dict {"category": "Hardware", "rate": [">", 100]} category='Hardware' AND rate>100 List of conditions [["rate", "between", [10, 100]], ["item_name", "like", "%a%"]] joined with AND Condition with DocType [["Sample Order Item", "item", "=", "Laptop"]] joins the child table Nested [["category", "=", "Hardware"], "or", [["rate", "<", 50], "and", ["disabled", "=", 0]]] category='Hardware' OR (rate<50 AND disabled=0) Criterion Item.rate > 800 as built

A condition is [field, value], [field, operator, value] or [doctype, field, operator, value]. A field can be a link or child table field ("items.qty"). A field that is not in the DocType but is in one of its child tables is looked up there, and the child table is joined.

Operators:

Operator Value Notes =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, =<, => value None with = gives IS NULL. None with != compares with the empty value of the field type. in, not in list, tuple, or comma-separated string An empty list with in gives 1=0. An empty list with not in gives 1=1. "" or None in an in list also matches NULL. like, not like, ilike pattern like is ILIKE on Postgres. regex pattern between [from, to] Dates on a Datetime field become the start and end of the day. is "set" or "not set" Compares with NULL and the empty value of the field type. timespan "this month", "last week" and others Becomes between. previous, next "1 week" and others Becomes between. ancestors of, descendants of, not ancestors of, not descendants of, descendants of (inclusive) document name For tree DocTypes. Uses lft and rgt. +, -, *, / value Python arithmetic operators. Custom Operators from the filters_config hook. See Hooks.

A filter field name with characters other than letters, digits and _ raises frappe.ValidationError. On _assign and _liked_by, = and != become like and not like with %value%.

frappe.qb.get_query(
    "Sample Item",
    filters={"disabled": 0},
    or_filters={"category": "Hardware", "rate": [">", 200]},
).get_sql()
# SELECT `name` FROM `tabSample Item` WHERE `disabled`=0 AND (`category`='Hardware' OR `rate`>200)

docs.title: Order and group
docs.text:
order_by and group_by take comma-separated fields: plain names, select aliases, result positions ("1"), link and child table fields, or backticked table-qualified names.

Warning

In order_by, a field without a direction sorts DESC. frappe.get_list sorts it ASC. Pass db_query_compat=True or write the direction.

frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Item", fields=["name"], order_by="rate").get_sql()
# SELECT `name` FROM `tabSample Item` ORDER BY `rate` DESC
frappe.qb.get_query("Sample Item", fields=["name"], order_by="KEEP_DEFAULT_ORDERING").get_sql()
# SELECT `name` FROM `tabSample Item` ORDER BY `modified` DESC

On Postgres with group_by or an aggregate, an order_by field that is not grouped or aliased is wrapped in MAX().

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
With ignore_permissions=False, get_query:

  1. Checks select permission on the DocType (or on parent_doctype) for user. Raises frappe.PermissionError if missing.
  2. Removes fields above the permlevels the user can read. "*" becomes the permitted fields.
  3. Adds the if_owner condition, or the User Permission conditions.
  4. Adds the conditions of permission_query_conditions hooks.
  5. Adds shared documents with OR. With no role permission, only shared documents match.
frappe.qb.get_query("ToDo", fields=["name"], ignore_permissions=False, user="user1@example.com").get_sql()
# SELECT `name` FROM `tabToDo` WHERE ((`tabToDo`.allocated_to = 'user1@example.com'
#   or `tabToDo`.assigned_by = 'user1@example.com' or `tabToDo`.owner = 'user1@example.com'))

See Permissions.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: Name Use instead get_query(..., validate_filters=...) Leave it out. It does nothing. frappe.query_builder.functions.Ifnull IfNull

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• get_query does not check that a field exists. A wrong field name fails when the query runs.
  • get_query applies no ORDER BY by default. frappe.get_list sorts by the DocType settings.
  • run(run=False) returns the SQL without its values. Use walk() to get both.
  • str(query) and get_sql() put values in the SQL. Do not run that string with frappe.db.sql. Pass the query object.
  • query.run() always uses frappe.local.db, even for a query from frappe.db.qb of a replica. Use db.sql(query) for another connection.
