docs.title: Testing API
docs.text:
This page lists the public classes and helpers in frappe.tests. Use it to look up a signature or a side effect. For how to write and run tests, read Testing. For bench run-tests options, read CLI: run-tests.

frappe.tests exports UnitTestCase, IntegrationTestCase, MockedRequestTestCase and the context managers below.

docs.title: Test classes
docs.text:
Class Base Description UnitTestCase unittest.TestCase For code that does not write to the database. Sets the user to Administrator. No rollback. IntegrationTestCase UnitTestCase Connects to the site, makes test records, commits them, and rolls back at the end of the class. MockedRequestTestCase IntegrationTestCase Starts a responses.RequestsMock in each setUp as self.responses. Outgoing requests calls fail unless you register a mock. frappe.tests.test_api.FrappeAPITestCase IntegrationTestCase HTTP helpers for REST tests. It is in a test module, not in frappe.tests.

If you override setUpClass, call super().setUpClass().

docs.title: UnitTestCase
docs.text: Member Description setUpClass() Sets cls.doctype from the test file folder (.../doctype/<name>/test_<name>.py), cls.module, and the user Administrator. Restores Administrator after the class. doctype DocType name read from the JSON file next to the test, or None. assertDocumentEqual(expected: dict \| Document, actual: Document) -> None Compare only the fields in expected. Child tables must have the same length. Floats use the field precision. Integers and booleans are compared with cint. Dates are compared as strings. assertQueryEqual(first: str, second: str) -> None Compare SQL after normalize_sql. assertSequenceSubset(larger: Sequence, smaller: Sequence, msg=None) -> None Assert that smaller is a subset of larger. normalize_html(code: str) -> str Static. Format HTML with BeautifulSoup for string comparison. normalize_sql(query: str) -> str Static. Format SQL with sqlparse. Backticks become double quotes on Postgres and SQLite. registerAs(_as) Class method. Used to attach the context managers to the class.

docs.title: IntegrationTestCase
FrappeAPITestCase
docs.text:
frappe.tests.test_api.FrappeAPITestCase sends requests to the site through a Werkzeug test client in another thread.

Member Description version "" (v1), "v1" or "v2". Picks the path prefix. site_url get_url(). sid Cached property. Logs in as Administrator and returns the sid. Pass it as a cookie or ?sid=. resource(*parts), method(*parts), doctype_path(*parts), get_path(*parts) Build URLs such as /api/resource/... or /api/v2/document/.... get(path, params=None, **kwargs), post(path, data, **kwargs), put(path, data, **kwargs), patch(path, data, **kwargs), delete(path, **kwargs), query(path, data, **kwargs) Send a request with a JSON body. Return a TestResponse. tearDown() Rolls back after each test.

On SQLite, make_request commits before the request so the request thread can write.

docs.title: Context managers
docs.text:
Each one is a context manager and also works as a decorator. Import them from frappe.tests. Most are also attributes of UnitTestCase (self.set_user(...)). change_settings and switch_site are attributes of IntegrationTestCase only. timeout is not a class attribute.

Name Description set_user(user: str) Call frappe.set_user(user), then switch back to the previous user. change_settings(doctype, settings_dict=None, /, commit=False, **settings) Set fields on a Single DocType, save with ignore_permissions, and restore the old values after the block. With commit=True, commits both saves. When settings_dict is given, **settings is ignored. patch_hooks(overridden_hooks: dict) Make frappe.get_hooks(hook) return the given value for the listed hooks. freeze_time(time_to_freeze, is_utc: bool = False, *args, **kwargs) Freeze the clock with freezegun. The time is read in the system time zone unless is_utc=True. enable_safe_exec() Set server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json for the block, then restore it. Writes the file. switch_site(site: str) Connect to another site for the block, then connect back. debug_on(*exceptions) Print the traceback and start pdb.post_mortem on the exceptions (default AssertionError), then raise. timeout_context(seconds=30, error_message="Operation timed out.") Raise Exception(error_message) after seconds. Uses SIGALRM: Unix and the main thread only. timeout(seconds=30, error_message="Operation timed out.") Decorator form of timeout_context. Works as @timeout or @timeout(60). trace_fields(doc_class, field_name=None, forbidden_values=None, custom_validation=None, **field_configs) Replace fields of a document class with traced properties for the block. Assigning a forbidden value, or a value that fails custom_validation, raises. 
from frappe.tests import IntegrationTestCase, set_user


class IntegrationTestSampleItem(IntegrationTestCase):
    @IntegrationTestCase.change_settings("System Settings", {"float_precision": 4})
    def test_precision(self):
        ...

    def test_user_cannot_delete(self):
        with set_user("user1@example.com"):
            self.assertRaises(frappe.PermissionError, frappe.delete_doc, "Sample Item", "_Test Sample Item")

docs.title: Test records
docs.text:
frappe.tests.utils re-exports these from frappe.tests.utils.generators.

Function Description make_test_records(doctype, force=False, commit=False) -> list Make test records for the DocType and, depth first, for the DocTypes it links to. Returns [(doctype, count), ...]. force=True makes them again. make_test_records_for_doctype(doctype, force=False, commit=False) -> list Make records for one DocType only. Returns names. make_test_objects(doctype=None, test_records=None, reset=False, commit=False) -> list Insert the given records (a list, or {doctype: [records]}), or load them from the DocType folder. Returns names. load_test_records_for(index_doctype) -> dict Read test_records.json, else test_records.toml, from the DocType folder. get_missing_records_doctypes(doctype, visited=None, _parent=None) -> list[str] DocTypes that still need records, in dependency order. get_missing_records_module_overrides(module) -> [list, list] (to_add, to_remove) from EXTRA_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES and IGNORE_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES of a test module. get_modules(doctype) (module, test_module) of a DocType. Cached. print_mandatory_fields(doctype, initial_doctype) Log the mandatory fields of a DocType that has no test records. TestRecordManager Keeps a log of made records in sites/<site>/.test_records.jsonl, so a second run does not make them again.

Where the records come from, for each DocType:

  1. _make_test_records() in the test module. It must yield (tag, document) pairs.
  2. test_records in the test module.
  3. test_records.json, then test_records.toml, in the DocType folder.

Test module variables: EXTRA_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES (DocTypes to add) and IGNORE_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES (DocTypes to skip). The old names test_dependencies and test_ignore still work with a warning. IGNORE_TEST_RECORD_DEPENDENCIES works only in a test module inside a DocType folder.

Warning

If you delete a record listed in .test_records.jsonl, the next run raises ValueError ("had been deleted resulting in inconsistent global state"). Delete the file to start again.

docs.title: Other helpers
docs.text:
All in frappe.tests.utils unless noted.

Function Description whitelist_for_tests(**whitelist_kwargs) Decorator. Same as @frappe.whitelist(...), but the method works only in tests, under CI, or on bench start with the allow_tests site config. toggle_test_mode(enable: bool) Set frappe.in_test and frappe.local.flags.in_test. wait_for_job(job_id: str, wait_timeout: float = 10) Wait until the job is no longer queued or started. Skips the test when the TestService is not available. bench run-tests --test-service selects these tests. frappe.tests.utils.test_capabilities.is_test_service_available(service) -> bool True if the service is available to this test process. frappe.tests.global_test_dependencies ["User"].

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Test records are committed. They stay in the site database after the run.
  • A test that commits (frappe.db.commit()) breaks the class rollback. Set SHOW_TRANSACTION_COMMIT_WARNINGS = True to find commits.
  • enable_safe_exec writes common_site_config.json. Other processes on the bench see the change during the block.
  • change_settings restores values with a second save. Without commit=True, both saves roll back with the class.

docs.title: frappe.utils
docs.text:
frappe.utils holds helpers for type conversion, dates, numbers, strings, URLs, HTML, paths and files. Use this page to look up the exact signature, default, return value and side effect of a helper. Most helpers live in frappe/utils/data.py. frappe/utils/__init__.py imports all of frappe.utils.data with from frappe.utils.data import *, so import them from frappe.utils:

from frappe.utils import add_days, cint, flt, getdate, nowdate

Helpers in submodules (frappe.utils.file_manager, frappe.utils.password and others) are not re-exported. Import them from the submodule.

Signatures come from the code. DateTimeLikeObject means str | datetime.date | datetime.datetime. NumericType means int | float. A function marked "Whitelisted" can be called over HTTP at /api/method/<dotted.path>. "All methods" means GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and QUERY.

Note

The star import also re-exports names that frappe/utils/data.py imports, such as relativedelta, parser, slug, get_date_format and NumberFormat. Import those from their own modules. This page does not list them, except NumberFormat.

docs.title: Example output
docs.text:
These results come from the develop site. The site has date format dd-mm-yyyy, number format #,##,###.##, time zone Asia/Kolkata and no currency precision.

from frappe.utils import (
    add_days, add_to_date, cint, comma_and, date_diff, flt, fmt_money, format_duration,
    get_last_day, getdate, rounded,
)

cint("12.7")                            # 12
cint("1,234")                           # 0
cint(None, 5)                           # 5
flt("1,234.567", 2)                     # 1234.57
flt(1.005, 2)                           # 1.0  (banker's rounding, legacy)
rounded(2.5)                            # 2.0
getdate("2026-01-15")                   # datetime.date(2026, 1, 15)
getdate("")                             # today, as datetime.date
add_days("2026-01-31", 1)               # '2026-02-01'  (string in, string out)
add_days(getdate("2026-01-31"), 1)      # datetime.date(2026, 2, 1)
add_to_date("2026-01-31", months=1)     # '2026-02-28'
date_diff("2026-03-01", "2026-02-01")   # 28
get_last_day("2024-02-03")              # datetime.date(2024, 2, 29)
fmt_money(1234567.891)                  # '12,34,567.89'
format_duration(93784)                  # '1d 2h 3m 4s'
comma_and(["a", "b", "c"])              # "'a', 'b', and 'c'"

docs.title: Type conversion and JSON
docs.text: Function Description cint(s: NumericType \| str \| None, default: int = 0) -> int Convert to int. A float string is truncated ("12.7" gives 12). A string with commas gives default. Returns default when conversion fails. flt(s: NumericType \| str \| None, precision: int \| None = None, rounding_method: str \| None = None) -> float Convert to float. Removes commas from strings. Returns 0.0 when conversion fails. Rounds with rounded() when precision is set. cstr(s, encoding="utf-8") -> str Convert to str. None gives "". Decodes bytes with encoding. sbool(x: str \| Any) -> bool \| str \| Any "true" and "1" give True. "false" and "0" give False. Case does not matter. Other values come back unchanged. cast(fieldtype, value=None) Cast to the Python type of a Frappe fieldtype. Float, Currency, Percent use flt. Int, Check use cint(sbool(value)). Text and link types use cstr. An empty Date gives date(1, 1, 1). An empty Datetime gives datetime(1, 1, 1). Time gives a timedelta. Other fieldtypes return value. parse_json(val: Any) Parse a JSON string with orjson. A dict result becomes frappe._dict. Other values come back unchanged. parse_val(v) Convert SQL result values to simple types. date and datetime become str. timedelta becomes "h:mm". orjson_dumps(obj, default=None, option=None, decode=True) orjson.dumps with OPT_PASSTHROUGH_DATETIME and OPT_NON_STR_KEYS. Returns str if decode is true, else bytes. Dates need a default such as frappe.utils.response.json_handler. safe_json_loads(*args) Parse each argument as JSON. Keep an argument as it is if it does not parse. One argument gives one value, more give a list. dictify(arg) Convert dicts, also dicts inside lists, to frappe._dict. Changes lists in place. encode(obj, encoding="utf-8") Encode a str to bytes. Other values come back unchanged. safe_encode(param, encoding="utf-8") Encode a str to bytes. Ignores errors. safe_decode(param, encoding="utf-8", fallback_map: dict \| None = None) Decode bytes to str. Returns param unchanged on failure. fallback_map maps an unknown encoding to a known one. as_unicode(text, encoding: str = "utf-8") -> str bytes are decoded, None gives "", other values go through str(). encode_dict(d, encoding="utf-8") Encode every str value of d to bytes. Changes d in place. decode_dict(d, encoding="utf-8") Does nothing. Its condition is always false. Returns d.

docs.title: Current date and time
docs.text:
All values use the system time zone from System Settings.

Function Description now() -> str Current datetime, for example "2026-11-22 17:16:59.229329" (with microseconds). now_datetime() -> datetime.datetime Current datetime as a naive datetime. nowdate() -> str Current date as yyyy-mm-dd. today() -> str Same as nowdate(). nowtime() -> str Current time, for example "17:16:59.229439" (with microseconds). get_timestamp(date: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None) -> float Unix timestamp of the start of the date in the server local time. None gives today. get_eta(from_time: DateTimeLikeObject, percent_complete) -> str Estimated time left as a timedelta string, from the start time and the percent done.

docs.title: Parse and convert dates
docs.text: Function Description getdate(string_date: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None, parse_day_first: bool = False) -> datetime.date \| None Convert to date. None or "" gives today. "0000-00-00" and "0001-01-01" give None. A string that does not parse raises frappe.ValidationError. get_datetime(datetime_str: DateTimeLikeObject \| None \| tuple \| list = None) -> datetime.datetime \| None Convert to datetime. None gives now. A date gives midnight. "" gives None. A timedelta comes back unchanged. A tuple or list raises TypeError. get_time(time_str: str \| datetime.datetime \| datetime.time \| datetime.timedelta) -> datetime.time Convert to time. get_timedelta(time: str \| datetime.timedelta \| None = None) -> datetime.timedelta \| None Convert a time string such as "10:20:30" to timedelta. to_timedelta(time_str: str \| datetime.time) -> datetime.timedelta Convert a string or time to timedelta. get_date_str(date_obj: DateTimeLikeObject) -> str Date as yyyy-mm-dd. get_datetime_str(datetime_obj: DateTimeLikeObject) -> str Datetime as yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss.ffffff. "2026-01-15" gives "2026-01-15 00:00:00.000000". get_time_str(timedelta_obj: datetime.timedelta \| str) -> str Time as h:m:s with no zero padding. 1:02:03 gives "1:2:3". Drops days. guess_date_format(date_string: str) -> str strftime format of a date string, for example "%d-%m-%Y". is_invalid_date_string(date_string: str) -> bool True if the value is not a string, is empty, or starts with 0001-01-01 or 0000-00-00. It does not check the format.

docs.title: Date arithmetic
docs.text:
A string input gives a string output. A date or datetime input gives the same type.

Function Description add_to_date(date: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None, years=0, months=0, weeks=0, days=0, hours=0, minutes=0, seconds=0, as_string=False, as_datetime=False) -> DateTimeLikeObject Add any mix of units with relativedelta. None uses now. Month ends clamp: 2026-01-31 plus one month is 2026-02-28. See the pitfalls for strings. add_days(date: DateTimeLikeObject, days: NumericType) -> DateTimeLikeObject Add days. add_months(date: DateTimeLikeObject, months: NumericType) -> DateTimeLikeObject Add months. add_years(date: DateTimeLikeObject, years: NumericType) -> DateTimeLikeObject Add years. 2024-02-29 plus one year is 2025-02-28. date_diff(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> int Days from start to end. Negative if end is before start. days_diff(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> int Same as date_diff. month_diff(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> int Months between two dates, counting both partial months. month_diff("2026-03-01", "2026-01-15") is 3. time_diff(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> datetime.timedelta Difference as timedelta. time_diff_in_seconds(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> float Difference in seconds. time_diff_in_hours(string_ed_date: DateTimeLikeObject, string_st_date: DateTimeLikeObject) -> float Difference in hours.

docs.title: Week, month, quarter and year
docs.text:
Functions with as_str return a yyyy-mm-dd string when as_str=True, else a date. The first day of the week comes from System Settings (first_day_of_the_week), Sunday by default.

Function Description get_first_day(dt, d_years: int = 0, d_months: int = 0, as_str: bool = False) -> str \| datetime.date First day of the month of dt, after moving d_years and d_months. get_last_day(dt) Last day of the month as date. is_last_day_of_the_month(dt) True if dt is the last day of its month. get_first_day_of_week(dt: DateTimeLikeObject, as_str=False) -> datetime.date \| str First day of the week of dt. get_last_day_of_week(dt: DateTimeLikeObject, as_str=False) -> datetime.date \| str Last day of the week of dt. get_quarter_start(dt: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None, as_str: bool = False) -> str \| datetime.date First day of the quarter. None uses today. get_quarter_ending(date: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None, as_str=False) -> str \| datetime.date Last day of the quarter. get_year_start(dt: DateTimeLikeObject, as_str=False) -> str \| datetime.date 1 January of the year. get_year_ending(date: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None, as_str=False) -> datetime.date \| str 31 December of the year. get_timespan_date_range(timespan: TimespanOptions) -> tuple[datetime.date, datetime.date] \| None (start, end) for a timespan filter value: "last week", "last month", "last quarter", "last 6 months", "last year", "yesterday", "today", "tomorrow", "this week", "this month", "this quarter", "this year", "next 7 days", "next 14 days", "next 30 days", "next week", "next month", "next quarter", "next 6 months", "next year". get_weekday(datetime: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None) -> str English weekday name, for example "Sunday". None uses now. get_weekdays() -> list[str] Weekday names from "Monday" to "Sunday". get_month(datetime: DateTimeLikeObject \| None = None) -> str English month name, for example "January". get_start_of_week_index() -> int Index of the first day of the week, 0 for Sunday. get_normalized_weekday_index(dt: datetime.date \| datetime.datetime) -> int Weekday index with Sunday as 0. get_week_start_offset_days(dt: datetime.date \| datetime.datetime) -> int Days from the first day of the week to dt. Weekday Enum from Sunday = 0 to Saturday = 6.

docs.title: Time zones
docs.text: Function Description get_system_timezone() -> str System time zone name from System Settings, for example "Asia/Kolkata". get_timezone_utc_offset(timezone: str) -> str Current UTC offset as ±HH:MM, for example "+05:30". get_datetime_in_timezone(time_zone: str) -> datetime.datetime Current datetime in a time zone. The result is aware. convert_utc_to_timezone(utc_timestamp: datetime.datetime, time_zone: str) -> datetime.datetime Convert a UTC datetime to an aware datetime in time_zone. convert_utc_to_system_timezone(utc_timestamp: datetime.datetime) -> datetime.datetime Convert a UTC datetime to an aware datetime in the system time zone. validate_time_zone(time_zone: str) -> None Raise frappe.ValidationError if the name is not in zoneinfo.available_timezones().

docs.title: Format for display
docs.text:
These use the format of the current user and System Settings. To format a value by fieldtype, use frappe.format_value.

Function Description format_date(string_date=None, format_string: str \| None = None, parse_day_first: bool = False) -> str Format a date with Babel in the user date format. format_string uses Babel patterns, for example "dd MMM yyyy". None gives "". formatdate Alias of format_date. format_time(time_string=None, format_string: str \| None = None) -> str Format a time in the user time format. format_datetime(datetime_string: DateTimeLikeObject, format_string: str \| None = None) -> str Format a datetime in the user date and time format. No time zone conversion. global_date_format(date: DateTimeLikeObject, format="long") -> str Localized date in the current language. "long" gives "January 15, 2026", "short" gives "1/15/26". pretty_date(iso_datetime: datetime.datetime \| str, mini=False) -> str Relative time, for example "2 hours ago". mini=True gives "2h". get_user_date_format() -> str Date format of the current user, for example "dd-mm-yyyy". Cached in frappe.local for the request. get_user_format Alias of get_user_date_format. get_user_time_format() -> str Time format of the current user, for example "HH:mm:ss". Cached in frappe.local.

docs.title: Durations and timedelta
docs.text: Function Description format_duration(seconds: float \| int, hide_days: bool = False) -> str 93784 gives "1d 2h 3m 4s". hide_days=True gives "26h 3m 4s". duration_to_seconds(duration: str) -> int "1d 2h 3m 4s" gives 93784. validate_duration_format(duration: str) -> None Raise frappe.ValidationError if the string is not in the d h m s format. format_timedelta(o: datetime.timedelta \| str) -> str Format as h:mm:ss. Hours can be more than 23 ("25:01:02"). Used for Time values in JSON. parse_timedelta(s: str) -> datetime.timedelta Parse str(timedelta) output such as "1 day, 2:03:04".

docs.title: Numbers and money
docs.text:
Rounding uses the rounding_method from System Settings. The default is "Banker's Rounding (legacy)". The other values are "Banker's Rounding" and "Commercial Rounding". Another value raises frappe.InvalidRoundingMethod.

Function Description rounded(num, precision=0, rounding_method=None) Round with the given or system rounding method. rounded(2.5) is 2.0, rounded(3.5) is 4.0. ceil(s: NumericType \| str) -> int Round up. floor(s: NumericType \| str) -> int Round down. safe_div(numerator: NumericType, denominator: NumericType, precision: int = 2) -> float Divide and round. A 0 denominator gives 0.0. remainder(numerator: NumericType, denominator: NumericType, precision: int = 2) -> NumericType Remainder of the division, rounded. get_currency_precision() -> int \| None currency_precision from System Settings, or None if not set. round_based_on_smallest_currency_fraction(value, currency, precision=2) Round to the smallest_currency_fraction_value of the Currency. fmt_money(amount: str \| float \| int \| None, precision: int \| None = None, currency: str \| None = None, format: str \| None = None) -> str Format with the number format of the user or format. Adds the currency symbol when currency is set. None or an invalid string gives "0.00". money_in_words(number: str \| float \| int, main_currency: str \| None = None, fraction_currency: str \| None = None) Amount in words, for example "USD One Thousand, Two Hundred And Fifty and Fifty Cent only.". The default currency is the currency default, else INR. A negative or invalid number gives "". in_words(integer: int, in_million=True) -> str Integer in words. in_million=False uses lakh and crore. NumberFormat(precision: int, decimal_separator: str, thousands_separator: str, string: str) Parsed number format. Make one with NumberFormat.from_string("#,###.##"). Defined in frappe.utils.number_format.

docs.title: Strings
docs.text: Function Description scrub(txt: str) -> str Lowercase and replace spaces and hyphens with _. "Sales-Order 2" gives "sales_order_2". unscrub(txt: str) -> str Replace _ and - with spaces and title-case. "sales_order" gives "Sales Order". strip(val: str, chars: str \| None = None) -> str Remove all \ufeff and \u200b characters, then strip whitespace or chars from both ends. None gives "". get_abbr(string: str, max_len: int = 2) -> str First letters of up to max_len words. Keeps the case. "Example Corp" gives "EC". random_string(length: int) -> str Random letters and digits from secrets. generate_hash(*args, **kwargs) -> str Same as frappe.generate_hash. Hex string of 56 characters by default. Pass length. sha256_hash(input: str \| bytes) -> str SHA-256 hex digest. is_sha256_hash(value: str) -> bool True if the value has 64 hex characters. comma_and(some_list: list \| tuple, add_quotes=True) -> str "'a', 'b', and 'c'". Translates each item except the last. comma_or(some_list: list \| tuple, add_quotes=True) -> str "'a', 'b', or 'c'". comma_sep(some_list: list \| tuple, pattern: str, add_quotes=True) -> str Join all items but the last with commas, then join with the last using pattern, for example "{0} or {1}". new_line_sep(some_list: list \| tuple) -> str Join with "\n " (new line and a space). filter_strip_join(some_list: list[str], sep: str) -> str Drop empty items, strip each, then join with sep. list_to_str(seq, sep=", ") Convert each item to str, strip it, then join with sep. get_string_between(start: str, string: str, end: str) -> str Text between start and end. These are regex patterns. Returns string if there is no match. esc(s, esc_chars) Put a backslash before each of esc_chars in s. unesc(s, esc_chars) Remove the backslash before each of esc_chars. bold(text: str \| int \| float) -> str Wrap in <strong>. Same as frappe.bold. sanitize_column(column_name: str) -> str Raise frappe.ValidationError if a column name or expression has unsafe SQL. Returns the name. get_table_name(table_name: str, wrap_in_backticks: bool = False) -> str "ToDo" gives "tabToDo". Names that start with __ stay the same.

docs.title: Lists and dicts
docs.text: Function Description unique(seq: Sequence[T]) -> list[T] Remove duplicates and keep the order. has_common(l1: Hashable, l2: Hashable) -> bool Common items as a set. The set is truthy when there is a match. is_subset(list_a: list, list_b: list) -> bool True if every item of list_a is in list_b. create_batch(iterable: Iterable, size: int) -> Generator[Iterable] Yield slices of at most size items. The input must support len() and slicing. dict_with_keys(dict, keys) New dict with only keys. remove_blanks(d: dict) -> dict Remove all falsy values, also 0. Changes d in place. dict_to_str(args: dict[str, Any], sep: str = "&") -> str URL query string. None values become empty. groupby_metric(iterable: dict[str, list], key: str) Regroup {category: [records]} as {record[key]: {category: [records]}}. squashify(what) Return the only item of a one-item sequence. Other values come back unchanged. recursive_defaultdict() defaultdict that makes nested defaultdicts on access.

docs.title: Filters and comparison
docs.text:
These evaluate Frappe filters in Python, without a database query.

Function Description evaluate_filters(doc: Mapping, filters: FilterSignature) True if doc matches all filters. doc must have a doctype key, else Filters raises ValueError. Supports descendants of and the other tree operators. compare(val1: Any, condition: str, val2: Any, fieldtype: str \| None = None) -> bool Compare with a filter operator. Casts with cast() when fieldtype is set. An unknown operator returns False. get_filter(doctype: str, filters: FilterSignature, filters_config=None) -> frappe._dict Normalize the first filter to {doctype, fieldname, operator, value, fieldtype}. make_filter_tuple(doctype, key, value) [doctype, key, "=", value], or [doctype, key, op, val] when value is [op, val]. make_filter_dict(filters) Convert [[doctype, key, op, value], ...] to {key: (op, value)}. sql_like(value: str, pattern: str) -> bool Python version of SQL LIKE with % at the start, the end or both. No % matches a substring. filter_operator_is(value: str \| None, pattern: str) -> bool pattern is "set" or "not set". Another value raises frappe.ValidationError. filter_operator_timespan(value: str, pattern: str) -> bool True if the date is in get_timespan_date_range(pattern). filter_operator_between(value: Any, pattern: list \| tuple) -> bool True if pattern[0] <= value <= pattern[1]. None gives False. convert_type_for_between_filters(value: DateTimeLikeObject, set_time: datetime.time) -> datetime.datetime Make a datetime from a date with set_time. A datetime comes back unchanged. get_safe_filters(filters) Parse a JSON filter string. Keeps the string if it does not parse or parses to a number. operator_map Dict of operator to function, used by compare: ^, in, not in, =, !=, >, <, >=, <=, not None, None, like, not like, is, Timespan, between, Between. 
from frappe.utils import compare, evaluate_filters

evaluate_filters({"doctype": "ToDo", "status": "Open", "priority": "High"},
    {"status": "Open", "priority": ["in", ["High", "Low"]]})          # True
compare("2026-01-02", ">", "2026-01-01", "Date")                     # True
compare(5, "between", [1, 10])                                        # True

docs.title: Email addresses and phone numbers
docs.text: Function Description validate_email_address(email_str, throw=False) Return the valid addresses in the string, joined with ", ". Invalid ones are dropped. throw=True raises frappe.InvalidEmailAddressError on an invalid one. split_emails(txt) Split a string of addresses on commas. Keeps quoted names with commas intact. A new line does not split (see the pitfalls). parse_addr(email_string) (name, email) from "Name <email>". name falls back to the email. Gives (None, email) when no valid address is found. extract_email_id(email: str) -> str Only the address part. "" for an empty value. check_format(email_id) Simple check: an @, a . after it, and more than four characters after @. get_name_from_email_string(email_string, email_id, name) Name part of an address string, with unsafe characters removed. sanitize_email(emails) Keep valid addresses and format each as Name <email>, joined with ", ". validate_phone_number(phone_number, throw=False) True if the value has only digits, spaces and + _ - , . * # ( ), up to 20 characters. throw=True raises frappe.InvalidPhoneNumberError. validate_phone_number_with_country_code(phone_number: str, fieldname: str \| None = None, label: str \| None = None) -> None Check with the phonenumbers library. Raise frappe.InvalidPhoneNumberError if not valid. Needs fieldname or label, else raises TypeError. validate_name(name, throw=False) True if a person name has only letters, digits, ' and -, with single spaces. throw=True raises frappe.InvalidNameError.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
These read the User DocType. They do not check permissions.

Function Description get_fullname(user=None) First and last name. Falls back to the user ID. Defaults to the session user. Cached in frappe.local.fullnames. get_email_address(user=None) Email of the user from the document cache. get_formatted_email(user, mail=None) "Full Name <email>". Uses the get_sender_details hook if an app defines it. "" if there is no email. get_user_display_id(user: str \| None = None) -> str Email of the user for display. Administrator, Guest and missing users give the ID. get_email_addresses(users: Iterable[str]) -> set[str] Emails of the users. Leaves out Guest, missing users and users without email. get_user_by_email(email: str, *, include_standard_users: bool = False, enabled: bool \| None = None) -> str \| None User ID with this email, or None. Leaves out Administrator and Guest by default. enabled filters on the enabled field. get_user_info_for_avatar(user_id: str) -> _UserInfo {"email", "image", "name"} of a user. A missing user gives the ID as email and name. add_user_info(user: str \| list[str] \| set[str], user_info: dict[str, _UserInfo]) -> None Add fullname, image, name, email and time_zone to user_info for each user ID or email not in it yet.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: Function Description validate_url(txt: str, throw: bool = False, valid_schemes: str \| Container[str] \| None = None) -> bool True if the text has a scheme and a host or path, or starts with /. valid_schemes limits the scheme. throw=True raises frappe.ValidationError. has_unsafe_url_scheme(txt: str) -> bool True for javascript:, vbscript: and data:. validate_egress_url(url: str) -> None Resolve the host and raise ValueError for loopback, link-local, private or reserved addresses, or a scheme other than http and https. Use it before a server-side HTTP request to a user URL. validate_iban(iban: str, throw: bool = False) -> bool Check the IBAN checksum. throw=True raises frappe.ValidationError. is_valid_iban(iban: str) -> bool IBAN checksum check. Ignores spaces. validate_json_string(string: str) -> None Raise frappe.ValidationError if the string is not valid JSON. validate_python_code(string: str, fieldname: str \| None = None, is_expression: bool = True) -> None Compile the code. Raise frappe.ValidationError with the line on a syntax error. is_expression=False checks a script. is_git_url(url: str) -> bool True for git, ssh, http and https repository URLs.

docs.title: URLs and links
docs.text:
get_url reads host_name from site config first. Without it, it uses the request host, then the site name. The desk routes use /desk.

Function Description get_url(uri: str \| None = None, full_address: bool = False, allow_header_override: bool = True, *, for_dev_server: bool = False) -> str Absolute site URL with uri joined. Tree DocTypes use the nested set model with lft, rgt and a parent Link field. Set nsm_parent_field on the DocType. Without it, the parent field is parent_<scrubbed doctype>. See DocTypes.

NestedSet.get_children() -> Iterator[NestedSet] Child documents. Uses get_list, so read permission applies. NestedSet.validate_one_root() Raise NestedSetMultipleRootsError if there is more than one root. NestedSet.validate_ledger(group_identifier="is_group") Raise if a leaf node has children. get_root_of(doctype) Name of the root node. get_ancestors_of(doctype, name, order_by="lft desc", limit=None) Names of the ancestors. Uses get_all, so no permission check. get_descendants_of(doctype, name, order_by="lft desc", limit=None, ignore_permissions=False) Names of the descendants. Uses get_list, so read permission applies. rebuild_tree(doctype: str) -> None Compute lft and rgt again for the whole tree. rebuild_tree_for_doctype(doctype: str) -> None Whitelisted, all methods. Only System Manager. Calls rebuild_tree. remove_subtree(doctype: str, name: str, throw=True) Delete a node and its descendants with SQL. Checks DocType delete permission. Runs no controller methods. update_nsm(doc) Update lft and rgt after a node is added or moved. update_add_node(doc, parent, parent_field) Insert a node into the tree. update_move_node(doc: Document, parent_field: str) Move a node to a new parent. rebuild_node(doctype, parent, left, parent_field) Set lft and rgt for a node and its children. restore_nsm_fields(doc, old_parent_field) Reset lft, rgt and the old parent to the saved values. validate_loop(doctype, name, lft, rgt) Raise NestedSetRecursionError if the node is its own ancestor. NestedSetRecursionError, NestedSetMultipleRootsError, NestedSetChildExistsError, NestedSetInvalidMergeError Subclasses of frappe.ValidationError.

docs.title: frappe.utils.caching
docs.text:
For details and Redis cache methods, see Jobs, Cache and Realtime and Caching.

Function Description redis_cache(ttl: int \| None = 3600, user: str \| bool \| None = None, shared: bool = False) -> Callable Cache return values in Redis for ttl seconds. user=True caches per session user. shared=True shares across sites. Use with or without parentheses. Adds fn.clear_cache(). site_cache(ttl: int \| None = None, maxsize: int \| None = None) -> Callable Cache in process memory per site. Not shared between workers. Adds fn.clear_cache(). request_cache(func: Callable) -> Callable Cache in frappe.local.request_cache until the request ends. http_cache(*, public: bool = False, max_age: int \| None = None, stale_while_revalidate: int \| None = None) -> Callable Set the Cache-Control header on GET responses of a whitelisted method. deprecated_local_cache(namespace, key, generator, regenerate_if_none=False) Backs the deprecated frappe.local_cache.

docs.title: frappe.utils.jinja
docs.text:
For templates and email, see Email, Files and Printing.

Function Description render_template(template, context=None, is_path=None, safe_render=True, *, restrict_globals=None) Render a template string or path with the sandboxed Jinja environment. With safe_render, a string with .__ raises frappe.ValidationError. Also frappe.render_template. get_template(path, *, restrict_globals=None) Load a template from an app path. Also frappe.get_template. get_jenv(*, restrict_globals=None) Jinja environment with Frappe globals, filters and the jinja hook. restrict_globals defaults to True. Cached in frappe.local. validate_template(html, restrict_globals=None) Raise frappe.ValidationError on a Jinja syntax error. get_email_from_template(name, args) (html, text) from templates/emails/<name>.html and .txt. text is None if missing. guess_is_path(template) True for one line that ends with .html, .css, .scss, .py, .md, .json, .js, .xml or .txt. get_jinja_hooks() (methods, filters) dicts from the jinja hook. get_jloader() Template loader for all installed apps. set_filters(jenv) Add the json, len, int, str and flt filters. safe_render_flags() Context manager that counts nested safe renders in frappe.flags.in_render_safe_exec. 
from frappe.utils.jinja import render_template

render_template("Hi {{ name }} {{ frappe.utils.flt('2.5') }}", {"name": "Customer A"})
# 'Hi Customer A 2.5'

docs.title: frappe.utils.print_format
docs.text:
Print and PDF endpoints. For print formats, see Print Formats.

Function Description download_pdf(doctype: str, name: str, format: str \| None = None, doc: Document \| None = None, no_letterhead: bool \| int = 0, language: str \| None = None, letterhead: str \| None = None, pdf_generator: str \| None = None, style: str \| None = None, settings: str \| None = None) Whitelisted, GET and POST, guests allowed. Rate limit 30 per 60 seconds per user. Checks print permission. Sends <name>.pdf. attach_pdf(doctype: str, name: str, format: str \| None = None, no_letterhead: bool \| int = 0, language: str \| None = None, letterhead: str \| None = None, pdf_generator: str \| None = None, style: str \| None = None, settings: str \| None = None) -> dict Whitelisted, POST. Needs print and write permission. Attaches the PDF as a private file in Home/Attachments/Printed PDFs. Replaces the file this method attached before for the same format. download_multi_pdf(doctype: str \| dict[str, list[str]], name: str \| list[str], format: str \| None = None, no_letterhead: bool = False, letterhead: str \| None = None, options: str \| None = None) Whitelisted, all methods. Needs bulk_actions on the User. Sends one PDF for many documents. Limited by get_max_bulk_print_docs(). download_multi_pdf_async(...) Whitelisted, all methods. Same arguments. Builds the PDF in a background job and returns a task ID. Rate limited per user. report_to_pdf(html: str, orientation: str = "Landscape", print_format: str \| None = None) Whitelisted, all methods. Render report HTML to report.pdf. Adds an Access Log. download_report_pdf(report_name: str, filters=None, orientation="Landscape", print_format=None, letterhead=None, no_letterhead=0, columns=None, visible_idx=None, custom_columns=None, applied_filters=None, ignore_prepared_report=False, in_background=False) -> None Whitelisted, POST. Run a report on the server and send it as PDF. in_background emails a link instead. render_report_jinja(print_format: str, data=None, columns=None, filters=None, letterhead=None, no_letterhead=0) -> dict Whitelisted, all methods, read-only. Render a Jinja Report print format with the given data. render_letterhead_for_print(letterhead: str \| None = None, doc: dict \| str \| None = None) -> dict Whitelisted, all methods. {"header", "footer"} HTML of a Letter Head. {} without read permission on Letter Head. print_by_server(doctype: str, name: str \| int, printer_setting: str, print_format: str \| None = None, doc: Document \| None = None, no_letterhead: bool \| int = 0, file_path: str \| None = None, style: str \| None = None, settings: str \| None = None, letterhead: str \| None = None) Whitelisted, all methods. Send the PDF to a CUPS printer from Network Printer Settings. Needs pycups. get_max_bulk_print_docs() -> int max_bulk_print_docs from Print Settings or site config, else 100. get_max_concurrent_bulk_exports() -> int max_concurrent_bulk_exports from Print Settings or site config, else 5. get_document_print_language(doctype: str, name: str, print_format: str \| None = None) -> str \| None The language of the document, else the default language of the print format. page_settings(pdf_options) -> dict Page size of the bulk print dialog as Print Settings values. classic_page_options(pdf_options) -> dict Same page size as HTML pipeline options. publish_failure(task_id: str, error: Exception) Send a task_complete realtime event with the error of a bulk export.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: Name Use instead cast_fieldtype(fieldtype, value, show_warning=True) cast(). Prints a warning. get_number_format_info(format: str) NumberFormat.from_string() from frappe.utils.number_format. frappe.utils.data.number_format_info frappe.utils.number_format.NUMBER_FORMAT_MAP. get_gravatar(email) get_identicon(). Now returns an identicon. get_gravatar_url(email, default="mm") get_identicon(). Returns "". has_gravatar(email) Returns "". make_esc(esc_chars) esc(). gzip_compress(data, compresslevel=5), gzip_decompress(data) Python gzip module. frappe.utils.print_format.read_multi_pdf(output) PdfWriter.write(). frappe.utils.html_utils.clean_script_and_style(html) sanitize_html() or clean_html(). deprecated Decorator from frappe/deprecation_dumpster.py that marks a function as deprecated.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• add_to_date with a date string and only minutes or seconds drops the time. add_to_date("2026-01-31", minutes=30) gives "2026-01-31". Pass a datetime string, or use hours.
  • add_to_date with a date object and a time unit returns a datetime.
  • getdate("") and getdate(None) return today, not None. Check for empty values before you call it.
  • cint("1,234") gives 0. Use cint(flt("1,234")).
  • flt(1.005, 2) gives 1.0 with the default rounding method. Pass rounding_method="Commercial Rounding" to round half away from zero.
  • compare needs the exact operator name. "Timespan" works, "timespan" returns False.
  • evaluate_filters needs a doctype key in doc.
  • orjson_dumps raises TypeError for date values. Pass default=json_handler or use frappe.as_json.
  • split_emails does not split on new lines. It changes them to spaces first. validate_email_address handles new lines.
  • frappe.utils.markdown sanitizes. frappe.utils.data.markdown does not.
  • get_ancestors_of ignores permissions. get_descendants_of and NestedSet.get_children apply them.
  • NestedSet.get_parent, get_children and validate_one_root read self.nsm_parent_field. That attribute is set only when the DocType sets nsm_parent_field.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
Use and administer the desk: navigation, users and permissions, customization, automation, reports, website, settings and system administration.

Topic What it covers Desk Basics Move around the desk and work with lists, views, forms, fields, search and collaboration tools. Users and Permissions Manage users and roles, role permissions and user permissions. Customization Change forms and fields without code, and define document workflows. Automation and Email Automate work with rules, notifications, email and automation flows. Data, Reports and Printing Import and export data, run reports, build dashboards and print documents. Website and Integrations Publish web pages and web forms, and connect Frappe to other services. AI and App Builder Use Flow AI agents and build apps in Studio. Settings Every settings page in Frappe: what each field does, its default and where it takes effect. System Administration Take backups and monitor logs and jobs.

docs.title: AI and App Builder
docs.text:
Use Flow AI agents and build apps in Studio.

Page What it covers Flow Chat with AI agents that work on your Frappe site, connect a model provider, and set up agents, tools, skills, knowledge, memories and triggers. Studio Build web apps on a Frappe site with Studio, a visual editor with drag and drop components, data sources, variables, scripts and one-click publish.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
Flow is an AI assistant inside your Frappe site. You chat with an agent. The agent uses tools to read and change records, run reports, call APIs and search the web, with your permissions. Use Flow to ask questions about your data, do repeated work in plain language, or run an agent on a schedule or when a document changes. Flow needs a model provider, such as Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, and an API key from that provider.

Warning

Flow is in beta and can make mistakes. Flow sends your messages and the data its tools read to the model provider you connect.

docs.title: Open Flow
docs.text:
• Go to /flow for the full page. Guests are sent to the login page.
  • In the desk or in Studio, press Ctrl+I (Cmd+I on macOS) to open Flow in a side panel. The panel shows only to users who can use Flow.

The left sidebar has New chat, Search and your earlier chats. The Flow menu at the top has Apps, Settings (Cmd+,) and Log out.

docs.title: Connect a provider
docs.text:
Before anyone can chat, a System Manager connects a provider and picks a model.

  1. Open /flow.
  2. Under Choose a provider, select Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. Click More providers for OpenRouter, Grok, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral, Cerebras and Custom provider.
  3. Create a key at the provider and paste it in API key.
  4. Click Connect. Flow checks the key with the provider. A wrong key saves nothing.
  5. Pick the model that chats start with.

Custom provider connects any server that speaks the OpenAI API, such as vLLM, LM Studio or a LiteLLM proxy. Enter its address, starting with http:// or https://. The key is optional. When Ollama runs on the same server at localhost:11434, Flow also offers its models.

The first enabled model also makes the built-in agent Flow (frappe/Flow), which knows the site and the built-in tools.

docs.title: What the setup saves
docs.text:
Flow Provider (one per provider):

Field Default Description provider openai, anthropic, gemini, openrouter, xai, groq, deepseek, mistral, cerebras, custom_openai (OpenAI-compatible endpoint) or litellm_proxy. enabled 1 Turn off to stop all its models. api_key Password field. Stored encrypted. base_url For a custom endpoint or proxy.

Flow Model (one per model):

Field Default Description title Name shown in the model picker, for example "Claude Sonnet 4.6". provider Link to Flow Provider. model_id The id of the model at the provider. enabled 1 embedding 0 The model makes embeddings for knowledge search. context_window Number of tokens the model accepts. api_key, base_url Only when the model has no provider. extra_params JSON passed to the model call. roles Only users with one of these roles can use the model.

docs.title: Chat
docs.text:
1. Click New chat.
  2. Select an agent in the agent picker. The default agent is Flow.
  3. Type a request, for example "List open Sample Orders for Customer A".
  4. Attach files if the agent needs them.
  5. Send the message. Flow shows each tool call as it runs.

Pick how Flow asks before it changes data:

Mode Description Auto Default. A helper model decides which tool calls need approval. Ask for approval Asks you before each change. Auto-approve Runs everything without asking.

To use a skill in a message, type /skill:<name> or pick it in the skill picker. Only skills with User Invocable on show there.

To share a chat, click Share. Set General access to "Only people you add" or "Every Flow user", or add members. People you share with can read the chat. Only the owner can send messages.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open Flow > Settings.

Tab What you set General Theme, Show each step separately, Helper model, Web search service, Guest messages per hour. Models Providers and models. Add a model, change a key, or delete a provider. Agents The agents users can chat with. Skills Instructions agents can load for specific tasks. Tools Actions agents can take. Triggers Run an agent when a document changes or on a schedule. Knowledge Knowledge bases and their sources. Memories What agents remember.

Flow Settings fields:

Field Default Description small_model (Helper model) Does side jobs such as chat titles and approvals in Auto mode. A cheaper model saves credits. search_provider DuckDuckGo DuckDuckGo, Brave, Tavily or Exa. search_api_key Needed for every search provider except DuckDuckGo. guest_messages_per_hour 0 Messages one address can send to public agents in an hour. 0 uses the default of 30.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
An agent is a Flow Agent record.

Field Default Description title Agent name. model Flow Model the agent uses. instructions The system prompt. tools Flow Tool records the agent can call. sub_agents Other agents this agent can hand work to. skills Flow Skill records the agent can load. knowledge_bases Knowledge bases the agent can search. max_iterations 100 Most model turns in one run. token_budget Most tokens in one run. roles Only users with one of these roles can chat with the agent. public 0 Guests can chat with the agent without a login.

Records with System Generated set come from an app. Their greyed-out fields cannot be changed.

docs.title: Tools, skills and knowledge
docs.text:
• Tools (Flow Tool): the built-in tools have names such as frappe/read_records, frappe/create, frappe/update, frappe/run_report and frappe/web_search. A Script tool runs sandboxed Python with a main(...) function. An Imported tool points to a Python function in Import Path. Turn on Requires Confirmation to always ask before it runs.
  • Skills (Flow Skill): a name, a one-line Description of when it applies, and Instructions. Available to All Agents offers it to every agent.
  • Knowledge (Flow Knowledge Base with Flow Knowledge Source rows): a source is Text, File, URL or DocType. A DocType source can Auto Sync when records change. Set the Embedding Model in Flow Knowledge Settings first. Search is Hybrid by default, with chunk size 1000 and overlap 200.
  • Memories (Flow Agent Memory): notes an agent keeps, for the agent or for one user.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
A trigger runs an agent without a chat.

  1. Open Settings > Triggers and add a trigger.
  2. Select the Agent.
  3. Set Event to DocType Event or Scheduled.
  4. For DocType Event, select the Target DocType and the Doc Event (after_insert, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel or on_trash).
  5. For Scheduled, enter a Cron Expression. Flow checks due triggers every 5 minutes.
  6. Optional: enter a Python Condition. It gets doc and utils.
  7. Write the Prompt Template. It is Jinja with doc and now.
  8. Save.
A new Sample Order {{ doc.name }} came in from {{ doc.customer_name }}.
Check the items and add a comment if a rate is missing.

The trigger runs as the Run As user, or as its owner. It skips documents that user cannot read. Trigger chats approve tool calls on their own. Each run is a Flow Run with status Running, Paused, Completed, Denied or Failed.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
Role Can do System Manager Connect providers, manage models, agents, tools, skills and triggers. See trigger and guest chats. Flow User Chat with agents they may use, read models and skills, and manage their own triggers.

Chats, runs and personal memories are private to their owner. Roles on an agent or a model limit who can use it.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Define agents, tools and triggers in Python with frappe.flow.Agent and the @tool decorator, and register them with the flow_agents, flow_tools and flow_triggers hooks. See Flow Development.
  • Agents run in the Flow server daemon. Manage it with bench flow-server setup, start, serve, stop, restart and status.
  • Flow adds its launcher to the desk, to Studio and to apps with a route in add_to_apps_screen.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Without an enabled model, /flow shows only the provider setup. Users who cannot connect a provider see "An admin needs to connect a provider first."
  • Auto-approve lets the agent change data without asking. Use it only with agents and tools you trust.
  • A public agent answers guests. Give it only read tools and limit Guest messages per hour.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Flow Development
  • Automation Flow
  • Studio
  • Users and Roles

docs.title: Studio
docs.text: Studio is a visual app builder in Frappe. You build pages from components with drag and drop, connect them to Frappe data, and publish them as a web app on your site. Use Studio for a portal, an internal tool or a small app that needs its own UI, without a separate frontend project. Studio is in beta.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Name DocType What it is App Studio App A web app served at /<app route>. It has one or more pages. Page Studio Page One screen of the app, at /<app route>/<page route>. Holds the block tree, data sources, variables and a page script. Component Studio Component A reusable part of the UI that you make in the app. Data source Studio Page Resource Data a page loads: a list of documents, one document, or an API call. Variable Studio Page Variable Page state of type String, Number, Boolean or Object.

An app is Custom (stored in the database, edited on any site) or Standard (exported to files in a Frappe app, edited in developer mode).

docs.title: Open Studio
docs.text: Go to /studio. The home page lists your apps. Filter them with All, Standard and Custom, or search by name.

docs.title: Make an app
docs.text:
1. Click New App.
  2. Enter a Title, for example "Sample Orders App".
  3. Optional: enter an App Route and an App Name. By default both come from the title, for example sample-orders-app.
  4. Click Create.

Studio makes the app and a first page, and opens the editor at /studio/app/<app>/<page>.

docs.title: The editor
docs.text: Area What it does Top bar Page title and route. Click it to change Page Title, Page Route, Tab Title and Allow Guest Access. Preview and Publish Page are at the right. Left rail Pages, Add Component, Layers, Data, Code and AI Assistant. Canvas The page. Switch between desktop, tablet and mobile, and zoom. Right panel Properties, Styles and Events of the selected block. For a text block, the props are in Styles. Containers have no Properties tab.

docs.title: Add components
docs.text:
1. Click Add Component in the left rail.
  2. Find a component in Standard or Custom. Standard groups include Core (Text Block, Repeater, Variants, HTML, Header, Image View) and Frappe UI (Button, Alert, Badge, charts, List and more).
  3. Drag the component onto the canvas.
  4. Select it and set its props in the right panel.

Use Layers to see and select blocks in a tree. Use Visibility Condition in the right panel to show a block only when an expression is true.

docs.title: Connect data
docs.text:
1. Click Data in the left rail.
  2. Click Add Data Source.
  3. Enter a Data Source Name.
  4. Select the Type: Document List, Document or API Resource.
  5. For a document type, select the Document Type, the fields and filters.
  6. For API Resource, enter the URL, the method and the parameters.
  7. Save the data source. Bind block props to it.

Click Add Variable to add page state. Read and set variables in events and in the page script.

docs.title: Scripts
docs.text: Click Code to write the page script and app files. A custom app can use .js, .json and .css files and import vue, vue-router, pinia and frappe-ui.

docs.title: Preview and publish
docs.text:
• Preview opens the page at /dev/<app route>/<page route>. It shows your draft and needs a login.
  • Publish Page publishes the current page and opens it at /<app route>/<page route>.
  • The arrow next to Publish Page has Revert Changes (shows when a published page has a draft), Publish App (all pages), Unpublish Page and Unpublish App.

An app is live when at least one page is published. Published apps also show on the apps screen of the desk. A guest can open a page only when it is published and Allow Guest Access is on. Other guests go to the login page.

docs.title: AI Assistant
docs.text: The AI Assistant in the left rail builds or changes pages from a prompt. It needs an OpenRouter API key in Studio Settings (ai_api_key). Set the key at /desk/studio-settings. The Studio settings dialog has no AI tab. When Flow is set up, the panel can also open Flow.

docs.title: Access
docs.text: Users with the System Manager or Studio User role can create and edit Studio apps. A user needs write permission on Studio App and Studio Page to edit an app.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Export an app with Export App (developer mode only) to make it standard. The files go to <frappe_app>/studio/<studio_app>/.
  • Run bench --site <site> watch-studio beside bench start to sync file changes of a standard app.
  • Add boot data for an app with the studio_app_boot hook. Frappe serves Studio apps through the page_renderer hook.
  • See Studio Development and skills/studio-app-building/SKILL.md in the frappe repo.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A standard app can be saved only in developer mode.
  • A custom app cannot use .ts or .vue files or npm packages. Export the app if you need them.
  • Editor changes are saved as a draft (draft_blocks). Publishing copies the draft to blocks, which the live page shows.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Studio Development
  • Website
  • Flow

docs.title: Automation and Email
docs.text:
Automate work with rules, notifications, email and automation flows.

Page What it covers Automation Assign documents with Assignment Rule, repeat documents with Auto Repeat, set Reminders, track Milestones, and name documents with Document Naming Rule and Document Naming Settings. Automation Flow Run a series of actions when a document changes, on a date, on a schedule or on a custom event, with Automation Flow, runs and Automation Settings. Notifications Send email, in-app, SMS or webhook alerts when documents change, with the Notification DocType, Notification Log and Notification Settings. Email Set up Email Account and Email Domain, watch the Email Queue, reuse text with Email Template, schedule Auto Email Report, and handle unsubscribes.

docs.title: Automation Flow
docs.text:
An Automation Flow runs a list of steps when a trigger fires: a document is created, a field changes, a date comes near, a cron schedule is due, or an app sends an event. Steps can set fields, create documents, assign users, send notifications, call webhooks and run server scripts. Use it for multi-step automation without code. For one simple rule, an Assignment Rule or a Notification can be enough.

Version

Automation Flow is new in develop and is marked Experimental in the desk. Only System Managers can create flows.

docs.title: How a flow runs
docs.text:
1. A trigger fires. Frappe checks the trigger, the match fields and the advanced condition.
  2. If they match, Frappe adds a row to Automation Trigger Queue. The save that fired the trigger does not wait.
  3. A background job takes rows from the queue and runs the flow.
  4. Each run is saved as an Automation Run with one row for each step.

Because steps run in the background, an error in a step does not block the save that fired the trigger.

docs.title: Create a flow
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/automation-flow/new.
  2. Enter a Title and select the Document Type.
  3. Select the Trigger Type and fill in its fields.
  4. Optional: add match fields or an advanced condition.
  5. Add rows in Actions.
  6. Save.
  7. Select Enabled and save again.

A flow can only be enabled when it has at least one action.

docs.title: Triggers
docs.text:
Trigger Type Fires when Fields Doc Created A document is inserted. Doc Updated A document is saved, but not on insert. Field Value Changed A saved document has a new value in a field. Trigger Field, optional From Value and To Value (empty means any value). Doc Deleted A document is deleted. Doc Submitted A document is submitted. Doc Cancelled A document is cancelled. Date Based A date field is a number of days before or after today. Checked every hour. Each document fires once a day. Date Field, Date Offset (Days), Date Direction Scheduled A cron expression is due. Checked every 5 minutes. Cron Expression, for example 0 9 * * 1 Custom Event An app sends an event with this name. Custom Event Manual Started from code with run_manually.

Document triggers and Date Based need a Document Type. A child table DocType is not allowed.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
• Match Fields: field rules made with the filter editor. All rules must match.
  • Advanced Expression using Python (condition): an expression with doc, for logic the match fields cannot express, such as OR groups. The match fields and the expression must all be true.
  • Revalidate on Run: check the match fields and the expression again in the background job before the steps run.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
Each row in Actions is one step. Steps run in order.

Field Description Step Type Action, Wait, WaitForEvent or If. Default Action. Action Type For Action steps. See the table below. Parameters (params) JSON with the values for the action. Target The record alias the step acts on. Default trigger, the document that fired the flow. Output Alias A name for the record that this step creates, for later steps. Step Condition Python expression. The step runs only when it is true. Required for If steps. Parent Step / Parent Step Branch Put a step inside an earlier If step, in its If or Else branch.

Built-in actions:

Action Type Label Parameters SetFieldValue Set Field Value field and value, or values (a map of field to value). Saves the document. IncrementFieldValue Increment Field Value field (a numeric field), amount. CreateDocument Create Document doctype, values. AssignToUser Assign to User assign_to (list of users), description. SendNotification Send Notification channel (Email or System), recipients, subject, message, or email_template. Use @owner and @assignees as recipients. CallWebhook Call Webhook url, method, headers, payload, timeout (seconds). RunScript Run Script server_script (a Server Script of type API) or script, not both.

Text values in parameters are Jinja templates with doc, for example "Order {{ doc.name }} completed".

Other step types:

  • Wait: pause the run. Parameters: value and unit (Seconds, Minutes, Hours or Days).
  • WaitForEvent: pause until an app sends an event, or until a timeout. Parameters: event_name, correlation_key, timeout_value, timeout_unit.
  • If: run the child steps in the If branch when Step Condition is true, else the Else branch.

Example parameters for a Set Field Value step:

{"values": {"status": "Completed", "owner_user": "user1@example.com"}}

docs.title: Settings of a flow
docs.text: Field Default Description Run As Automation User Triggering User, Document Owner or Automation User. The steps run with this user's permissions. Automation User Administrator The user for Automation User. Must be enabled. Stop on Error 1 Stop the run at the first failed step.

docs.title: Test a flow
docs.text: Click Test Run on a saved flow. Select a document in Run against and click Run. The flow runs for real against this document, then Frappe rolls back everything it did. The result shows each step and its status. CallWebhook steps do not send requests in a test run, and Wait steps do not pause.

docs.title: Runs and history
docs.text:
• Automation Run (/desk/automation-run): one record for each run, with status Running, Waiting, Success, Partially Failed, Failed or Skipped. The Steps table has the status, duration, detail and error of each step.
  • Automation Trigger Queue (/desk/automation-trigger-queue): rows waiting to run, with status Pending, Scheduled, Running, Done, Failed or Skipped.

After a number of failures in a row (Failure Threshold, default 10), Frappe disables the flow. It sets Disabled Reason, skips the waiting rows, and sends a notification to the owner of the flow.

docs.title: Automation Settings
docs.text:
Go to /desk/automation-settings.

Field Default Description Disable Automations 0 Stop all flows on the site. Queued rows stay. Maximum Recursion Depth 3 How many times a flow can trigger another flow in one chain. Failure Threshold 10 Failures in a row before a flow is disabled. Stale Running Minutes 30 A row that stays Running longer is queued again. Maximum Attempts 3 Retries for a row that fails outside its steps. Queue Retention Days 7 Days to keep Failed and Skipped queue rows. Step Output Limit 65536 Bytes of output a step can pass to later steps. Event Payload Limit 65536 Bytes an event payload can have. Allow Unregistered Events 0 Accept events that no app registered.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Flows do not run during install, patches or migrate.
  • A flow changes data with the Run As user. With the default Automation User (Administrator), steps can change any document.
  • When a flow saves a document, that save can trigger other flows. The recursion depth limit stops long chains and logs an error.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Send a custom event from code with emit(event, doc=None, payload=None, correlation_key=None) in frappe/automation_engine/events.py.
  • Register events, actions and record relationships with the automation_events, automation_actions and automation_relationships hooks.
  • Start a Manual flow with frappe.automation_engine.api.run_manually(automation, docname=None).
  • See Automation Engine for the developer guide.

docs.text:
