docs.title: Automation
docs.text: Frappe has small, rule-based tools that act on documents without code. This page covers Assignment Rule, Auto Repeat, Reminder, Milestone Tracker, Document Naming Rule and Document Naming Settings. For multi-step flows with triggers and actions, see Automation Flow.

docs.title: Assignment Rule
docs.text:
An Assignment Rule assigns a document to a user when a condition is true. The assignment is a ToDo, the same as a manual assignment. Use it to share incoming work in a team.

  1. Go to /desk/assignment-rule/new.
  2. Enter a name, and select the Document Type.
  3. Enter the Assign Condition.
  4. Select the Rule and add Users.
  5. In Assignment Days, add the days the rule is active.
  6. Save.

Field Description Document Type The DocType to assign. ToDo is not allowed. Priority Rules with a higher priority are tried first. Disabled Stop the rule. Description The ToDo text. Jinja with the document fields, for example {{ name }}. Default "Automatic Assignment". Assign Condition Python expression. Assign when true. Example: status == "Open". Unassign Condition Python expression. Remove the assignment made by this rule when true. Close Condition Python expression. Close the open ToDos of the document when true. Rule Round Robin, Load Balancing, Based on Field or Weighted Distribution. Users The users for Round Robin and Load Balancing. Field For Based on Field: a field that holds a user or the email address of a user. Users (weighted_users) For Weighted Distribution: users with a Weight. Due Date Based On A date field. Its value becomes the ToDo date, and the ToDo date follows it when it changes. Assignment Days The rule runs only on these weekdays.

Conditions use the document fields by name, without doc..

How the rules choose a user:

  • Round Robin: the next user in the list after the last one assigned.
  • Load Balancing: the user with the fewest open ToDos for this DocType.
  • Based on Field: the user in the selected field.
  • Weighted Distribution: users in turn, in proportion to their weight. A user with weight 2 gets two documents for each one a user with weight 1 gets.

Frappe runs the rules after each save, cancel and update after submit. It tries the unassign conditions first. It assigns only when the document has no assignment from these rules, and stops at the first rule that assigns. If an expression has an error, Frappe shows "Auto assignment failed" and saves the document.

To apply the rules to existing documents, select them in the list view and use Actions > Apply Assignment Rule.

docs.title: Auto Repeat
docs.text:
Auto Repeat makes a copy of a document on a schedule, for example a monthly order. The DocType must allow it.

  1. Open Customize Form for the DocType.
  2. Select Allow Auto Repeat and save. Frappe adds an auto_repeat field to the DocType.
  3. Open the document to repeat.
  4. Select Repeat from the menu.
  5. Enter the Frequency and Start Date in the dialog, and confirm.

You can also create the record at /desk/auto-repeat/new and select the Reference Document Type and Reference Document.

Field Description Start Date / End Date The schedule period. End Date cannot be today or the start date. Frequency Daily, Weekly, Fortnightly, Monthly, Quarterly, Half-yearly or Yearly. Repeat on Days Weekdays, for Weekly. Repeat on Day / Repeat on Last Day of the Month The day of the month, for monthly and longer frequencies. Next Schedule Date The date of the next copy. Read only. Submit on Creation Submit each new copy. Only for submittable DocTypes. Assignee / Generate Separate Documents For Each Assignee Assign the copy to these users, or make one copy for each user. Notify by Email Email the Recipients with Subject and Message, or an Email Template. Attach Print / Print Format Attach a PDF of the new document. Status Active, Disabled or Completed. Set by Frappe.

A daily job (make_auto_repeat_entry) makes the copies in the background. Each copy keeps the field values of the reference document, except fields marked No Copy. Required Date fields get the schedule date. A document can be linked to only one Auto Repeat.

docs.title: Reminder
docs.text:
A Reminder is a personal note that appears as a notification at a time you choose.

  1. Open a saved document.
  2. Select Remind Me from the menu, or press Shift+R.
  3. Select Remind Me In (30 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, or custom).
  4. Enter a Description and click Create.

Frappe checks reminders every 15 minutes and creates a Notification Log for the user. The time cannot be in the past. Reminders more than one hour late are not sent.

docs.title: Milestone Tracker
docs.text:
A Milestone Tracker records each change of one field, for example the status of an order. Each change makes a Milestone record with the document, the field and the new value.

  1. Go to /desk/milestone-tracker/new.
  2. Select the Document Type to Track and the Field to Track.
  3. Save.

Open /desk/milestone to see the records. Use them in reports, for example to count how many orders reached "Completed" each week.

docs.title: Document Naming Rule
docs.text:
A Document Naming Rule gives a document a name from a prefix and a counter, when the document matches conditions. Use it to name documents of one type by category, for example HW-2026-001 for hardware items.

Field Default Description Document Type The DocType to name. Prefix The name before the counter. It can use naming series parts such as .YYYY., .MM. and {fieldname}. Digits (prefix_digits) 5 The length of the counter, padded with zeros. Conditions Field, operator (=, !=, >, <, >=, <=) and value. All must match. Priority 0 Higher priority rules are tried first. Disabled 0 Stop the rule.

Frappe tries the rules before the autoname method and the DocType naming option. The first matching rule sets the name. The counter is kept per resolved prefix in the Series table, so HW-2026- and HW-2027- count on their own.

Prefix: HW-.YYYY.-    Digits: 3    Condition: category = Hardware
Result: HW-2026-001

Naming rules do not apply to Single DocTypes, log DocTypes, or DocTypes with autoincrement or UUID naming. An amended document uses the rules only when its amendment naming is Default Naming.

docs.title: Document Naming Settings
docs.text:
Go to /desk/document-naming-settings. This page has two parts.

Naming Series (for DocTypes that use a naming_series field):

  1. Select the DocType in Select Transaction.
  2. Edit Series List for this Transaction, one series on each line.
  3. Select User must always select to make the user pick a series.
  4. Click Update.
  5. To change a counter, select a Prefix, enter the Current Value and click Update Series Number.

Enter a series in Try a Naming Series to see a preview of the names.

Amended Documents: an amended document gets a name from the cancelled one.

Option Result Amend Counter (default) SO-00001 becomes SO-00001-1, then SO-00001-2. Default Naming The amended document gets a new name from the normal naming rules.

Set Default Amendment Naming, and override it per DocType in Amendment Naming Override. Then click Update Amendment Naming.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Assignment Rule runs from doc_events for * in frappe/hooks.py: assignment_rule.apply and assignment_rule.update_due_date.
  • Auto Repeat calls on_recurring(reference_doc, auto_repeat_doc) on the new document before insert. Define it in your controller to change the copy.
  • Set allow_auto_repeat in the DocType JSON to allow Auto Repeat without Customize Form.
  • Create a reminder from code: frappe.automation.doctype.reminder.reminder.create_new_reminder(remind_at, description, reminder_doctype=None, reminder_docname=None).
  • Add your own naming series parts with the naming_series_variables hook. See Naming.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Automation Flow
  • Collaboration
  • Customize Form
  • Naming

docs.title: Email
docs.text: Frappe sends and receives email through Email Accounts. Every outgoing email first goes to the Email Queue, and a scheduler job sends it. Use this page to connect a mailbox, check sent and failed emails, reuse message text, and email reports on a schedule.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: DocType Purpose Email Account One mailbox. It can send (SMTP), receive (IMAP or POP3), or both. Email Domain Server settings shared by all accounts of one domain. Email Queue One outgoing email and its status. Email Template A reusable subject and body with Jinja. Auto Email Report A report that Frappe emails on a schedule. Email Unsubscribe An address that does not want more email for one document, or for all email (global_unsubscribe). Communication A sent or received email linked to a document. It shows in the form timeline.

docs.title: Email Account
docs.text:
Go to /desk/email-account/new.

  1. Enter the Email Address.
  2. Select a Service (for example GMail or Outlook.com) or a Domain. Use one, not both. A service or domain fills in the server settings.
  3. Select Enable Incoming, Enable Outgoing, or both.
  4. In Authentication, select the Method: Basic (password) or OAuth (a Connected App).
  5. Enter the password, or authorize API access for OAuth.
  6. Save.

docs.title: Outgoing (SMTP)
docs.text: Field Default Description Outgoing Server / Port SMTP host and port. Use TLS / Use SSL 0 Connection security. Default Outgoing 0 Send system emails and notifications from this account. Always use this email address as sender address 0 Replace the sender of every email with this address. Always use this name as sender name 0 Use the account name as the sender name. Send unsubscribe message in email 1 Add an unsubscribe link to emails sent from this account. Track Email Status 1 Track if the recipient opened the email. Disable SMTP server authentication 0 Send without login. Always BCC Address Copy every email to this address. Add Signature / Signature 0 Add a signature. Footer Content Add a footer.

docs.title: Incoming (IMAP or POP3)
docs.text:
Field Default Description Incoming Server / Port IMAP or POP3 host. Use IMAP 0 Use IMAP. When on, add folders in IMAP Folder. Use SSL / Use STARTTLS 0 Connection security. Append To Create or update a document of this DocType for each new email (POP3). The DocType must allow it in its settings. Default Incoming 0 Replies to system emails come to this inbox. Email Sync Option UNSEEN ALL or UNSEEN (IMAP). Initial Sync Count 250 Emails to fetch on the first sync (IMAP). Attachment Limit (MB) Skip larger attachments. Create Contacts from Incoming Emails 1 Make a Contact for new senders. Enable Automatic Linking in Documents 0 Link emails to the documents named in the recipient address. Notify if unreplied 0 Email the addresses in Send Notification to when an email has no reply after Notify if unreplied for (in mins) (default 30). Enable Auto Reply 0 Reply to every new email with Auto Reply Message.

Frappe pulls incoming email every 10 minutes. Click Pull Emails on a saved account to pull now.

Without an Email Account record, Frappe can send email with the SMTP settings in site_config.json (mail_server, mail_port, mail_login, mail_password, use_tls, use_ssl, auto_email_id). See Site Config.

docs.title: Email Domain
docs.text: Create an Email Domain when many accounts use the same mail server. Enter the Domain Name, the incoming and outgoing servers, ports and security options. Then select this domain in each Email Account.

docs.title: Email Queue
docs.text:
Go to /desk/email-queue. Each row is one email with a status: Not Sent, Sending, Sent, Partially Sent or Error.

  • Frappe sends queued emails on every scheduler run (frappe.email.queue.flush). It takes up to 500 emails each time, highest priority first. Set email_queue_batch_size in site config to change this.
  • An email in Sending for more than 15 minutes is retried, up to the Email Retry Limit in System Settings (default 3).
  • Open an email and click Send Now to send it now. Click Retry Sending on a failed email.
  • In the list, select failed emails and use Actions > Retry Sending.
  • A System Manager can click Suspend Sending in the list to stop all sending, and Resume Sending to start again.

Emails are not sent when mute_emails is set in site config.

docs.title: Email Template
docs.text:
An Email Template holds a Subject and a Response. Both are Jinja templates. Select Use HTML to write the body as HTML code. Set Reference DocType to show the template only for that DocType.

The document fields are available by name:

Order {{ name }} for {{ customer_name }} is ready.

Use a template in these places:

  • The email dialog of a form: click Use template. Templates with no Reference DocType or with the form's DocType show.
  • A Notification, in the Email Template field.
  • A Workflow state, in Next Action Email Template.
  • An Auto Repeat, in Template.

docs.title: Auto Email Report
docs.text:
An Auto Email Report emails the output of a report on a schedule. To create one, open a report and select Setup Auto Email from the menu, or go to /desk/auto-email-report/new.

Field Default Description Report The report to send. Based on Permissions For User (user) current user Run the report as this user. Email To Addresses, one on each line. Frequency Daily, Weekdays, Weekly or Monthly. Day of Week Monday For Weekly. Format HTML, XLSX, CSV or PDF. Send only if there is any data 1 Skip empty reports. No of Rows 100 Row limit for Report Builder reports. Only Send Records Updated in Last X Hours Report Builder reports. 0 means all records. Filters Filters for Query and Script reports. From Date Field / To Date Field / Period Set date filters to the current period. Sender The Email Account to send from.

Click Download to get the file now, or Send Now to send it now. A user can have up to 20 enabled reports. Change this with Max auto email report per user in System Settings. You can only use another user's permissions if you are a System Manager or have the impersonate permission on User.

docs.title: Unsubscribe
docs.text: When Send unsubscribe message in email is on, emails get an unsubscribe link. When a recipient clicks it, Frappe creates an Email Unsubscribe record for that address and document. Frappe then skips that address for emails about the same document. A record with Global Unsubscribe skips the address for all emails. Frappe also skips addresses that end in .invalid.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Send email from code with frappe.sendmail(...). It adds rows to the Email Queue. See Email and Notifications.
  • Render a template from code: frappe.get_doc("Email Template", name).get_formatted_email(doc) returns {"subject", "message"}.
  • Add your DocType to the Append To list: set email_append_to in the DocType JSON, or select Allow document creation via Email in Customize Form.
  • Scheduler jobs in frappe/hooks.py: frappe.email.queue.flush (all), email_account.pull (every 10 minutes), email_account.notify_unreplied (every 15 minutes), auto_email_report.send_daily (daily), auto_email_report.send_monthly (monthly).

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Notifications
  • Reports
  • System Settings
  • Form View

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text: A Notification sends a message when something happens to a document: it is created, saved, submitted, cancelled, a field changes, or a date comes near. Use it to tell people about a document without code. The message can go by email, as an in-app (system) notification, by SMS, or to a chat service through a webhook.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: DocType Purpose Notification The rule: which document, which event, which condition, who gets it, and the message. Notification Log One in-app notification for one user. It shows in the bell menu in the desk. Notification Settings Per-user preferences. The name of the record is the user. Notification Type A category for in-app notifications, for example Alert. Used for filters and email preferences. Notification Webhook URL A saved webhook for the Webhook channel. Services: Google Chat, Matrix (Hookshot), Mattermost, Rocket.Chat, Slack, Teams, Discord, Ntfy, Raven.

docs.title: Create a notification
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/notification/new.
  2. Optional: enter a name. If you do not, Frappe uses the subject as the name.
  3. Select the Channel.
  4. Select the Document Type and Send Alert On.
  5. Optional: add a condition.
  6. Add rows in Recipients.
  7. Enter the Subject and Message.
  8. Make sure that Enabled is selected. It is on by default.
  9. Save.

Use the Preview button to render the subject and message for an existing document and to check if it meets the condition.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel Sends Needs Email An email through the Email Queue. An outgoing Email Account. Optional Sender. System Notification A Notification Log for each recipient user. Recipients that resolve to users. SMS A text message through the SMS gateway. SMS settings and recipients with a mobile number. Webhook The rendered message to a Notification Webhook URL. Notification Webhook URL. Recipients are hidden.

For the Email channel, select Send System Notification to also create an in-app notification.

Version

The Slack channel is replaced by Webhook in develop. When a Notification with channel Slack is imported from a fixture or JSON file, Frappe changes it to Webhook.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
Send Alert On When it runs New After a document is inserted (after_insert). Save After every save (on_update). Submit After submit (on_submit). Cancel After cancel (on_cancel). Value Change After save, when the field in Value Changed has a new value. Not on insert. Method When the controller method in Trigger Method runs, for example before_insert. Days Before / Days After Once a day, for documents whose Reference Date field is the given number of days from today. Minutes Before / Minutes After Every 5 minutes, for documents whose Reference Datetime is the given number of minutes away. The offset must be 10 minutes or more.

Date-based events also work on child table DocTypes. Other events do not. You cannot create a notification on Email Queue.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Set Condition Type to one of these:

  • Python: an expression in Condition. The notification is sent only when it is true.
  • Filters: build the condition with the filter editor. Frappe stores it as JSON in filters.

The Python expression gets doc, nowdate and a safe frappe object.

doc.status == "Open" and doc.total > 500

docs.title: Recipients
docs.text:
Each row in Recipients can add people in these ways:

Field Description Receiver By Document Field owner, or a field of the document (or of a child table) that holds a user, an email address or a mobile number. Receiver By Role All users with this role. CC / BCC Email addresses, one on each line. Jinja is allowed. Email channel only. Condition A Python expression. The row is used only when it is true.

Select Send To All Assignees to also email every user the document is assigned to (Email channel).

docs.title: Message
docs.text:
Subject and Message are Jinja templates. The context has doc, nowdate, frappe and comments (the latest comments and communications on the document).

<h3>Order {{ doc.name }}</h3>
<p>{{ doc.customer_name }} placed an order of {{ doc.total }}.</p>

For the Email channel, you can select an Email Template instead of a subject and message. Email Template content uses field names directly, for example {{ name }}, not {{ doc.name }}.

Other options:

Field Description Attach Print / Print Format Attach a PDF of the document. Attach Files From Field (one Attach field) or All (all attachments). Set Property After Alert / Value To Be Set Set a field on the document after the notification is sent. Notification Type The type of the in-app notification. Default Alert.

docs.title: Notification Log and the bell menu
docs.text:
Each in-app notification is a Notification Log for one user (for_user). The bell icon in the desk lists them. A user can only read their own logs. Frappe does not create a log when the recipient is the user who made the change, except for types in the notification_self_notify_types hook (Alert in Frappe).

When a log is created, Frappe also emails it to the user if the user has email notifications on for that type. Types in the notification_skip_email_types hook (Alert in Frappe) do not send this extra email, because the Notification rule sends its own email.

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text:
Each user can open their settings from the gear icon in the bell menu, or at /desk/notification-settings/<user>.

Field Default Description Enable System Notification (enabled) 1 Turn off all in-app notifications for this user. Enable Email Notifications 1 Receive notification emails. Email me for these notification types Types that send an email. Mentions / Assignments / Document Share / Event Reminders 1 Email for these events. Email Threads on Assigned Document 1 Email when a reply arrives on a document assigned to you. Open Documents (subscribed_documents) DocTypes to follow in the notifications panel.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Notifications do not run during data import with emails muted, during patches, or during install.
  • If the Value Changed field is removed from the DocType, Frappe disables the notification and logs an error.
  • A Standard notification (is_standard) can only be edited in developer mode. To change one, disable it and duplicate it.
  • An error in the template stops the save that triggered it, with "Error in Notification".

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Ship a notification with an app: set Is Standard and a Module in developer mode. Frappe exports it to <module>/notification/<name>/ with the JSON, the message file (.md, .html or .txt by Message Type) and a .py file with get_context(context).
  • Send a notification from code: frappe.get_doc("Notification", name).queue_send(doc). It runs in a background job after commit.
  • trigger_daily_alerts (daily) and trigger_offset_alerts (every 5 minutes) run from scheduler_events in frappe/hooks.py.
  • Create an in-app notification from code with enqueue_create_notification(users, doc_dict) in frappe/desk/doctype/notification_log/notification_log.py.
  • See Email and Notifications for the developer guide.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Email
  • Workflow
  • Automation
  • Collaboration

docs.title: Desk Basics
docs.text:
Move around the desk and work with lists, views, forms, fields, search and collaboration tools.

Page What it covers Desk Find your way around the Frappe desk - login, apps screen, dock, sidebar, workspaces, search, notifications, user menu and keyboard shortcuts. List View Find, filter, sort and select documents in the desk list view, run bulk actions, and set list settings and saved layouts. Views Show the documents of a DocType as a report, kanban board, calendar, gantt chart, tree, dashboard, image grid, map or email inbox. Form View Read and change one document in the desk form - layout, save, submit, cancel and amend, timeline, attachments, sharing, print, email, links, duplicate, rename and form shortcuts. Fields Fill each kind of field in a desk form - text, numbers, check boxes, selects, links, dates, child tables, attachments, editors, signature, map, rating, duration, color and phone. Search Find pages and documents with the awesomebar, global search, list filters and tags, and control what global search indexes. Collaboration Work on documents with other users - assignments and ToDo, sharing, comments and mentions, likes, follow, tags, activity and the notification log.

docs.title: Collaboration
docs.text: The desk has tools to work on documents with other users. Assign a document to a user, share it, comment on it, mention users, follow it and tag it. Each action can send a notification. Most tools are in the form sidebar and timeline. Some also work on many documents from the list view.

docs.title: Assignments
docs.text:
An assignment gives a document to a user as a task. Each assignment is a ToDo document for that user.

To assign a document:

  1. Open the document.
  2. In the sidebar, click + next to Assign.
  3. In Assign To, select one or more users. Select Assign to me to add yourself. Select a user group in Assign To User Group to add all its users.
  4. Optional: set Complete By, Priority (Low, Medium or High) and a Comment.
  5. Click Add.

To assign many documents, select them in the list view and click Actions > Assign To.

When you assign a document, Frappe:

  • Creates a ToDo with allocated_to, reference_type, reference_name, description, priority and date. The default date is today. The default description is "Assignment for ".
  • Adds the user to the _assign field of the document. The list view shows the user's avatar on the row.
  • Shares the document with the user (read only) if the user cannot read it. If document sharing is turned off in System Settings, it shows an error.
  • Sends an Assignment notification to the user.
  • Makes the user follow the document if Auto follow documents that are assigned to you is on for the user.

    • If the user already has an open ToDo for the document, Frappe does not make a second one.

    Click the assigned users under Assign to open the Assignments dialog. In this dialog:

    • Click the check icon (Done) next to your own assignment to complete it. This sets the ToDo to Closed. Only the assignee can do this.
    • Click the cross icon (Cancel) to remove an assignment. You can remove your own assignment, or any assignment if you can write the document. This sets the ToDo to Cancelled.

    In the list view, Actions > Clear Assignment removes all assignments of the selected documents.

docs.title: The ToDo list
docs.text:
Open the ToDo list to see your assignments. Click Open on a row to go to the assigned document. A user without a ToDo role permission sees only ToDos allocated to, assigned by or created by them.

Calendar and Kanban views are also available for ToDo. Refer to Views.

For developers

Assign from code with frappe.desk.form.assign_to.add({"assign_to": ["user1@example.com"], "doctype": "Sample Order", "name": "SO-00001", "description": "Check the items"}). Remove with frappe.desk.form.assign_to.remove(doctype, name, assign_to). If the DocType has a field named assigned_to, Frappe also sets it. Use an Assignment Rule to assign documents automatically.

docs.title: Sharing
docs.text:
Sharing gives one user access to one document, even if the user's role has no access to the DocType.

  1. Open the document.
  2. In the sidebar, click + next to Share.
  3. In Share With, select a user.
  4. Select the rights: Read, Write, Submit and Share.
  5. Click Add.

Select Everyone to share the document with all users. You can share only if you have the share right on the document. You can only give the rights that you have yourself. The user gets a Share notification.

Each share is a DocShare document. A System Manager can turn off sharing for the site in System Settings.

For developers

Share from code with frappe.share.add(doctype, name, user, read=1, write=0, submit=0, share=0, everyone=0, notify=0). Read shares with frappe.share.get_users(doctype, name). Refer to Permissions.

docs.title: Comments and mentions
docs.text:
Every user who can read a document can comment on it.

  1. Type in the comment box below the form.
  2. To mention a user, type @ and select the user.
  3. Click Comment.

The comment shows in the activity of the document. You can edit your own comments. Administrator can edit all comments. You can delete a comment if you can delete Comment and you wrote it or have the System Manager role.

A mentioned user gets a Mention notification. A user gets mentions only if Allowed In Mentions is on for the user and the user is an enabled System User.

For developers

A comment is a Comment document with comment_type = Comment. The desk calls frappe.desk.form.utils.add_comment. Mentions are handled by frappe.desk.notifications.notify_mentions.

docs.title: Likes
docs.text: Click the heart in the form sidebar or on a list row to like a document. Click it again to remove the like. The list view header has a heart that shows only the documents you liked. Likes are stored in the _liked_by field and show in the activity.

docs.title: Follow
docs.text:
Follow a document to get emails about its changes.

  1. Turn on Send Notifications For Documents Followed By Me in your User, in the Document Follow section.
  2. Select a Frequency: Hourly, Daily or Weekly.
  3. Open a document and select Follow in the form menu.

Follow shows only for DocTypes with Track Changes. Administrator cannot follow documents. Each follow is a Document Follow document. Select Unfollow to stop.

You can also follow documents automatically. Turn on these options in your User:

  • Auto follow documents that you create
  • Auto follow documents that you comment on
  • Auto follow documents that you Like
  • Auto follow documents that are shared with you
  • Auto follow documents that are assigned to you

For developers

The scheduler sends the follow emails with frappe.desk.form.document_follow.send_hourly_updates, send_daily_updates and send_weekly_updates. Follow from code with frappe.desk.form.document_follow.follow_document(doctype, doc_name).

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
A tag is a label on a document, for example urgent.

  • In the form sidebar, click + next to Tags and type a tag.
  • In the list view, select documents and click Actions > Add Tags.

To find tagged documents, type # and the tag in the awesomebar, or use a Tags quick filter in the list view. To show tags on list rows, turn on Show Tags in list settings.

Tags are stored in the _user_tags column of the document, and in Tag and Tag Link documents.

docs.title: Activity
docs.text: The Activity section of a form shows the history of the document: creation, changes, attachments, likes, assignments, emails and comments. Field changes show only if the DocType has Track Changes. Refer to Form view.

docs.title: Notification log
docs.text:
Each notification for a user is a Notification Log document. The notification types are Alert, Share, Assignment, Mention and Energy Point (DocType Notification Type).

To read notifications:

  1. Click the bell in the dock.
  2. Click a notification to open the document. This marks it as read.
  3. Click the check icon to mark all as read.
  4. Click View Full Log to open the Notification Log list.

docs.title: Notification settings
docs.text:
Click the gear icon in the notifications panel to open your Notification Settings.

Field Label Default What it does enabled Enable System Notification 1 Shows notifications in the desk. enable_email_notifications Enable Email Notifications 1 Also sends notifications by email. enable_email_mention Mentions 1 Emails for mentions. enable_email_assignment Assignments 1 Emails for assignments. enable_email_share Document Share 1 Emails for shares. enable_email_event_reminders Event Reminders 1 Emails for event reminders. enable_email_threads_on_assigned_document Email Threads on Assigned Document 1 Emails for email threads on documents assigned to you.

Refer to Notifications to send your own notifications with the Notification DocType.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Form view

  • Automation
  • Permissions
  • Email

docs.title: Desk
docs.text: The desk is the back-office user interface of a Frappe site. System Users use it to read, create and change documents. It opens at /desk. Use this page to learn the parts of the desk screen and how to move between them.

docs.title: Log in
docs.text:
1. Open <site>/login in the browser.
  2. Type your email (or username) and password.
  3. Click Login.

After login, a System User goes to /desk. A default app, a role home page or a default workspace can change this target. A Website User does not get desk access and goes to the website instead. The logic is in frappe/auth.py (LoginManager.set_user_info).

docs.title: The apps screen
docs.text:
/desk shows the apps screen. It has one icon for each installed app that you can open. On a site with only Frappe installed, there is one icon: Framework. The text under the icon names the other apps in the same group: Studio and Flow.

The top bar of the apps screen has:

  • Search with the Ctrl+K hint. It opens the awesomebar.
  • The notification bell.
  • Your avatar. Click it to open a menu with My Settings, Toggle Theme, About, Frappe Support and Logout.

Click an app icon to open the app at its landing page.

For developers

An app adds its icon with the add_to_apps_screen hook in hooks.py (keys name, logo, title, route, has_permission). The Single DocType Desktop Settings has the field desktop_page (Apps or Desktop Icons). It selects which grid /desk shows. Apps add items to the avatar menu with frappe.pages["desktop"].desktop_page.add_menu_item({label, icon, onclick, order}). See Workspaces, sidebar and dock.

docs.title: Desk layout
docs.text:
Inside an app, the screen has three columns.

Part Where What it does Dock Narrow column on the far left Switches between the modules of the current app. Also holds search, notifications, Flow, background tasks and your user menu. Sidebar Column next to the dock Shows the links of the current module: a workspace (Home), DocTypes, reports and pages, grouped in sections. Page Main area Shows the workspace, list, form, report or page that you opened.

docs.title: Dock
docs.text:
The dock has three groups of buttons:

  1. Utilities at the top: Search, Notifications, Flow (only if you can use Flow) and Background Tasks (only while a background task runs).
  2. One tile for each module of the current app, for example Build, Users, Email and Printing.
  3. Your avatar at the bottom. It opens the user menu.

The dock has two modes. Set the mode in My Settings > Appearance > Dock.

Mode Behavior Pinned (default) The dock is always visible as a column. Floating The dock is hidden. Move the pointer to the left edge of the window to show it.

Press Ctrl+Shift+/ to open the dock from the keyboard. To change the order of the tiles, drag a tile, or select Manage Dock in the user menu.

docs.title: Sidebar
docs.text:
The sidebar header shows the name of the current module. Click the header to open its menu:

Item What it does All apps Goes back to the apps screen at /desk. Edit Sidebar Opens the sidebar editor. You can add, remove and move items. Help Shows the help links for the current page and the help items of the site.

When the dock is not available, the menu also shows Modules and Apps to switch module or app. Items from Navbar Settings also show in this menu.

Click a section name in the sidebar to expand it. Press Ctrl+/ to collapse or expand the sidebar.

docs.title: Workspaces
docs.text:
A workspace is a page with shortcuts, link cards, charts and number cards. The Home item at the top of a module sidebar opens the workspace of that module, for example /desk/build.

Click the ... button at the top right of a workspace to open the workspace menu:

Item Shows when What it does Edit You can edit this workspace Makes the blocks editable. Drag blocks to move them. New You can create workspaces Creates a new workspace. Manage You can manage at least one workspace Opens the workspace manager. Reset to Standard The workspace was customized and you have access Removes the customizations.

A new workspace has an Access setting: Only to you, To a group of users or To everyone. Only a user with the Workspace Manager role can make a workspace for a group or for everyone. Private workspaces open at /desk/private. To show a My Space link to them in the user menu, turn on Show My Space in My Settings.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Click Search in the dock, or press Ctrl+K, to open the awesomebar. Type a DocType name, a report name or new <DocType>. Press Ctrl+G to open global search. Refer to Search.

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
Click the bell in the dock to open the notifications panel. A dot on the bell shows that you have unread notifications.

The panel has two tabs:

  • All: your notifications, for example assignments, mentions and shares.
  • Events: your upcoming events.

At the top of the panel, click the gear icon to open your Notification Settings. Click the check icon to mark all notifications as read. Click View Full Log to open the Notification Log list. Refer to Collaboration.

docs.title: User menu
docs.text:
Click your avatar at the bottom of the dock.

Item What it does My Space Opens your private workspaces. Shows only if Show My Space is on. My Settings Opens the settings dialog for your user. Manage Dock Opens the dock editor. Not shown on phones. Reload Clears the cache and reloads the desk. Logout Logs you out.

docs.title: My Settings
docs.text:
My Settings opens a dialog with these tabs: Profile, Email, Appearance, Preferences, Lists, Forms, Reports, Session Defaults and Keyboard Shortcuts.

On Appearance, set the theme (light, dark or system), the form width (Compact or Full Width) and the dock mode. Press Ctrl+Shift+G to open the theme switcher from anywhere.

docs.title: Desk settings of a user
docs.text:
These check fields on the User DocType turn parts of the desk on or off for one user. A System Manager sets them in the Desk Settings section of the User form. The user can change some of them in My Settings.

Field Label Default Effect search_bar Show search bar 1 Shows the awesomebar. notifications Allow notifications 1 Shows the notification bell. show_my_space Show My Space 0 Shows My Space in the user menu. dock_mode Dock Pinned Pinned or Floating. bulk_actions Allow bulk actions 1 Shows bulk actions in list views. The server also checks it. view_switcher Show view switcher 1 Shows the view switcher in list views. form_sidebar Show sidebar 1 Shows the sidebar in forms. timeline Show timeline 1 Shows the activity timeline in forms. dashboard Show dashboard 1 Shows the connections dashboard in forms. form_navigation_buttons Show navigation buttons 1 Shows the previous and next buttons in forms. report_split_view Split view in reports 1 Uses the split view in reports.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
Press Shift+/ (the ? key) to see the shortcuts for the current page. On macOS, Cmd works in place of Ctrl.

These shortcuts work on every desk page:

Shortcut Action Ctrl+S Do the primary action of the page, for example Save. Ctrl+K Open the awesomebar. Ctrl+G Open global search. Shift+/ Show keyboard shortcuts. Ctrl+Shift+R Clear cache and reload. Shift+T Open the System Console. Only for users who can write System Console. Ctrl+/ Collapse or expand the sidebar. Ctrl+Shift+G Switch theme. Ctrl+Shift+/ Open the app dock. Esc Close the open dialog or the open child table row.

On a workspace page, type any letter to open the awesomebar with that letter.

Hold Alt to see underlined letters in menus and buttons. Press Alt and the letter to click that item. On macOS, this does not work while the cursor is in a text field.

Shortcuts for lists and forms are on List view and Form view.

For developers

Add a shortcut with frappe.ui.keys.add_shortcut({shortcut, action, description, page, condition, ignore_inputs}) (frappe/public/js/frappe/ui/keyboard.js). Pass page to limit the shortcut to one page. Only shortcuts with a description show in the dialog. A menu item gets a shortcut through the shortcut argument of page.add_menu_item().

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• List view
  • Form view
  • Search
  • Collaboration
  • Workspaces, sidebar and dock
  • Users and roles

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: A form shows the fields of a document. Each field has a type, and the type sets how you enter the value. This page tells you how to fill each kind of field. For the form itself (save, submit, tabs and sections), refer to Form View.

docs.title: Field labels and states
docs.text:
What you see Meaning Red * after the label Mandatory field. If it is empty when you save, a Missing Fields message lists it, and the form does not save. Gray text under the field The description of the field. Info icon after the label Click it to see the description or a View Documentation link. Value without an input box The field is read-only. You cannot change it. Field not shown The field is hidden, or it shows only when another field has a value. Red border The value is not valid, for example a wrong email address.

If System Settings has Hide Empty Read-Only Fields on (the default), read-only fields with no value are not shown.

Hold Alt and move the pointer over a field to see its fieldname.

docs.title: Text fields
docs.text:
• Data: Type one line of text. The field has a maximum length, usually 140 characters. If you paste a longer value, a Data Clipped message shows.
  • Data with an email, phone, URL or name format: The field shows a red border if the value has the wrong format. A URL field shows an Open Link icon when the value is a valid URL.
  • Small Text, Text and Long Text: Type more lines of text. Drag the bottom right corner to make the box taller.
  • Text Editor: Use the toolbar to format text. It has headings, font size, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, colors, quote, code block, text direction, link, image, lists, check lists, alignment, indent and tables.
  • Markdown Editor: Type Markdown. Click Preview to see the result and Edit to go back.
  • Code, HTML Editor and JSON: Type in a code editor.
  • Password: The value shows as dots. A bar under the field shows the strength: Weak, Average, Strong or Excellent.

docs.title: Number fields
docs.text:
• Int: Type a whole number.
  • Float, Currency and Percent: Type a number. After you leave the field, it shows in the number format of the system or the currency, for example 1,250.00.
  • Check: Click the box to turn it on or off.
  • Rating: Click a star to set the rating. Click the left half of a star to set a half star.
  • Duration: Click the field to open a small panel with Days, Hours, Minutes and Seconds. Type a number in each box. The field shows the total, for example 1h 30m.

docs.title: Select fields
docs.text:
• Select: Click the field and select one option from the list.
  • Autocomplete: Type to filter the options, then select one. Values that are not in the list are not kept.

docs.title: Link fields
docs.text:
A Link field stores the name of another document, for example a User.

  1. Click the field. A dropdown shows documents you can select.
  2. Type part of the name or title to filter the list.
  3. Click a document, or use the arrow keys and press Enter.

At the end of the dropdown:

  • Create a new ... opens a new document of the linked type. This shows only if you can create that type. After you save it, the new document is set in the field.
  • Advanced Search opens a dialog with filters to find the document.
  • Gray text shows the filters that limit the list, if the field has filters.

When the field has a value, move the pointer over it. An arrow icon (Open Link) opens the linked document. If System Settings has Allow Clearing Link Fields on, an x icon (Clear Link) also shows.

If you type a value that does not exist and leave the field, the field becomes empty.

Dynamic Link: The document type comes from another field of the form, usually a Link to DocType. Fill that field first. Then the Dynamic Link field searches documents of that type.

Table MultiSelect: Select more than one document. Each value shows as a pill in the field. Click the x on a pill to remove it. Press Backspace in the empty input to remove the last pill.

docs.title: Date and time fields
docs.text:
• Date: Click the field to open the calendar. Click a day, or click Today. You can also type the date in your date format.
  • Datetime: The calendar also has a time selector, and the button is Now. The time zone of the system shows under the field.
  • Time: Select the time, or click Now.

Press T in a Date, Datetime or Time field to set the current date or time.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
A Table field shows child rows in a grid, for example the Items of a Sample Order.

Task Steps Add a row Click Add row under the grid. Edit a cell Click the cell and type. Use the arrow keys and Tab to move between cells. Open the row form Click the edit icon at the end of the row. The row form shows all fields of the row. Delete rows Select the check boxes of the rows, then click Delete row or Delete {n} rows. Duplicate rows Select the rows, then click Duplicate row. Move a row Drag the row by its number. Or open the row form and click Move.

In the row form:

  • Insert Above and Insert Below add a new row next to this row.
  • Duplicate copies the row.
  • Delete removes the row.
  • Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down open the previous or next row. Esc closes the row form.

Keys in a grid cell:

Keys Action Ctrl+Down / Ctrl+Up Add a row below or above. Ctrl+Shift+Down / Ctrl+Shift+Up Add a row at the end or at the start. Shift+Alt+Down Duplicate the row. Tab in the last cell of the last row Add a row. Esc Remove a new row that you did not change.

On macOS, use Cmd in place of Ctrl. If the DocType allows bulk edit, Edit, Download and Upload buttons also show.

docs.title: Attachments and images
docs.text:
• Attach and Attach Image: Click Attach. The Upload dialog opens. Drag files into it, or upload from My Device, Library (files already on the site), Link (a URL) or Camera. Click Upload. To remove the file, click Clear.
  • Attach Image also shows a preview of the image.
  • Signature: Draw your signature with the mouse or with a finger. Click the reset icon to clear it.
  • Barcode: Type the barcode value. The field shows the barcode image.
  • Geolocation: The field shows a map. Use the tools at the side of the map to draw a marker, line, polygon, rectangle or circle. Click Show me where I am to go to your location.

docs.title: Other fields
docs.text:
• Color: Click the field to open the color picker.
  • Icon: Click the field to select an icon.
  • Phone: Click the flag to select the country. The field adds the country code in front of the number.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Form View
  • Customize Form
  • System Settings
  • Controls

docs.title: Form View
docs.text: The form view shows one document. Use it to read, change, save and submit the document, and to work with other users on it. Open a form from the list view, or at /desk/<doctype-slug>/<name>, for example /desk/sample-order/SO-00001. For a new document, click Add in the list view or press Ctrl+B.

docs.title: Parts of the form
docs.text: Part What it shows Title bar The DocType, the document title and a status indicator, for example Draft or Not Saved. Previous and next buttons Open the previous or next document of the list. Turn them off with Show navigation buttons on your User. ... menu More actions. Refer to Form menu. Primary button The next action, for example Save, Submit, Update, Cancel or Amend. Fields The fields of the document in tabs, sections and columns. Sidebar Title, name, print and like icons, Assign, Attachments, Tags, Share, and who created and last changed the document. Comments and Activity The comment box and the timeline.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
The DocType defines the layout with layout fields:

  • A Tab Break starts a tab. The tabs show at the top of the form.
  • A Section Break starts a section. A section can have a label. A collapsible section opens when you click its label.
  • A Column Break starts a new column in the section.

A Table field shows a child table, for example Items in Sample Order. Click Add row to add a row. Click the edit icon at the end of a row to open the row as a form.

Hold Alt and move the pointer over a field to see its fieldname. Click to copy the fieldname.

Set the width of forms in My Settings > Appearance > Layout (Compact or Full Width).

docs.title: Save, submit, cancel and amend
docs.text:
Each document has a docstatus:

docstatus Status Can you edit it? 0 Draft Yes. 1 Submitted Only fields with Allow on Submit. 2 Cancelled No.

A normal DocType has only drafts. Click Save or press Ctrl+S to save. If a mandatory field is empty, a Missing Fields message lists the fields.

A submittable DocType (Is Submittable set) has the full cycle:

  1. Click Save. The document is a draft.
  2. Click Submit. Confirm Permanently Submit SO-00001?. The document is now submitted.
  3. To change an Allow on Submit field, change it and click Update.
  4. To stop a submitted document, click Cancel. Confirm Permanently Cancel SO-00001?.
  5. To fix a cancelled document, click Amend. A new draft opens with Amended From set.

When you cancel a document that other submitted documents link to, the Cancel All Documents dialog lists them. Click Cancel All to cancel them together.

By default, an amended document gets the name of the original with a counter, for example SO-00001-1. Change this in Document Naming Settings with Default Amendment Naming (Amend Counter or Default Naming) or Amendment Naming Override for one DocType.

To delete a draft without saving it as a record, select Discard in the menu. This sets docstatus to 2. Discard shows only for submittable DocTypes without a workflow.

The buttons need permissions: Submit needs the submit right, Cancel the cancel right, and Amend the amend right. If the DocType has a workflow, the workflow actions replace Submit and Cancel.

docs.title: Comments and activity
docs.text:
Below the fields, the form shows:

  • Comments: type in the box and click Comment. Type @ to mention a user. Refer to Collaboration.
  • Activity: a timeline of events. It shows who created and changed the document, attachments, likes, assignments, emails and comments. If the DocType has Track Changes, it also shows each field change.
  • Show all activity: turn it off to see only comments and emails.
  • New Email: writes an email about the document. The email shows in the timeline. If the DocType has Allow events in timeline, there is also a New Event button.

Turn off the timeline for your user with Show timeline (timeline).

docs.title: Sidebar
docs.text:
Item What it does Edit icon next to the title Opens the Rename dialog. Shows if you can change the title or the name. Print icon Opens the print view. Paperclip icon Attaches a PDF of the print to the document. Heart Likes the document. Assign Assigns the document to users. Refer to Collaboration. Attachments Click + to upload a file or add a link. Click a file to preview it. Max Attachments on the DocType sets a limit. Tags Adds tags. Share Shares the document with users.

Turn off the sidebar for your user with Show sidebar (form_sidebar).

docs.title: Connections
docs.text:
If other DocTypes link to this DocType, the form shows a Connections section with the linked document counts. Click a DocType to open its list with a filter for this document. Click + to create a linked document.

Select Show Links in the menu to see all documents that link to this one.

docs.title: Form menu
docs.text:
Click ... in the title bar. The menu shows only the items that apply.

Item Shortcut What it does Print Ctrl+P Opens the print view. Refer to Printing. On a wide screen, use the print icon in the sidebar. Attach PDF Attaches a PDF of the print. Save the document first. On a wide screen, use the paperclip icon in the sidebar. Discard Discards a draft. Toggle Sidebar Shows or hides the sidebar. Email Ctrl+E Opens the email composer. Rename Changes the name of the document. Needs Allow Rename on the DocType and write permission. Reload Loads the document again. Delete Ctrl+Shift+D Deletes the document. Not for submitted documents. Duplicate Shift+D Opens a new document with the same values. Hidden if Hide Copy is set on the DocType. New Sample Order Ctrl+B Opens a new document of this DocType. Jump to field Ctrl+J Finds a field and moves to it. Show Links Lists the documents that link to this document. Copy to Clipboard Copies the document as JSON. Remind Me Shift+R Sets a reminder for this document. Follow / Unfollow Follows the document. Refer to Collaboration. Undo / Redo Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y Undoes or redoes a field change. Repeat Creates an Auto Repeat. Needs Allow Auto Repeat on the DocType. View Audit Trail Compares amended versions. Shows for amended documents of a DocType with Track Changes. Templates Saves the form values as a template, or applies a template. Settings Opens the settings dialog of the DocType. Customize Opens Customize Form. Edit DocType Opens the DocType. Only in developer mode.

docs.title: Rename
docs.text:
1. Click the edit icon next to the title in the sidebar, or select Rename in the menu.
  2. Change the title, the name or both.
  3. To merge this document into an existing document with that name, select Merge with existing.
  4. Click Rename.

The rename also changes the links in other documents. A rename can run in the background. A message tells you when it is queued.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text: For a new document, a Templates button shows next to the primary button. For a saved document, Templates is in the menu. In the dialog, type a Template Name and click Save to save the current values. Click a template to apply its values to the form. Templates are saved as Document Template documents. Select Private to keep a template for yourself.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
Shortcut Action Ctrl+S Save, or do the primary action. Ctrl+Shift+> Go to the next record. Ctrl+Shift+< Go to the previous record. Ctrl+P Print. Ctrl+E Email. Ctrl+J Jump to field. Ctrl+B New document. Shift+D Duplicate. Ctrl+Shift+D Delete. Shift+R Remind me. Ctrl+Z Undo. Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo. Alt + pointer on a field Show the fieldname. Click to copy it.

In a child table:

Shortcut Action Up / Down Move to the row above or below. Tab / Shift+Tab Move to the next or previous column. Tab in the last column of the last row adds a row. Ctrl+Up / Ctrl+Down Add a row above or below the current row. Ctrl+Shift+Up / Ctrl+Shift+Down Add a row at the top or at the bottom. Shift+Alt+Down Duplicate the current row. Esc Close the open row.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Form behavior comes from <doctype>.js with frappe.ui.form.on("Sample Order", {...}). Other apps add form scripts with the doctype_js hook. Refer to Form scripts.
  • Add a menu item with frm.page.add_menu_item(label, action, standard, shortcut) and a button with frm.add_custom_button().
  • The DocType properties is_submittable, allow_rename, allow_copy (Hide Copy), track_changes, max_attachments, allow_auto_repeat and image_field control the items above. Refer to DocTypes.
  • The Connections section comes from the links table of the DocType and from get_data() in <doctype>_dashboard.py (Meta.get_dashboard_data in frappe/model/meta.py). Other apps change it with the override_doctype_dashboards hook.
  • The server runs before_submit, on_submit, before_cancel, on_cancel, before_discard and on_discard on the controller. Refer to Controllers.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• List view
  • Collaboration
  • Printing
  • Workflow
  • Form scripts
  • Controllers
  • Fields

docs.title: List View
docs.text: The list view shows the documents of one DocType as rows. Use it to find documents, filter and sort them, and change many documents at the same time. Open it from the sidebar, from the awesomebar, or at /desk/<doctype-slug>, for example /desk/sample-order.

docs.title: Parts of the list view
docs.text:
Part What it shows Title The DocType name, for example Sample Order. View switcher (List View) Changes to another view. Refer to Views. Reload button Loads the list again. ... menu List and DocType settings. Refer to List menu. Add Sample Order Creates a document. The arrow next to it shows more ways to create, for example Import. Quick filters Fields under the title bar, for example ID, Customer Name and Status. Filter Adds filters on any field. Sort button Sets the sort field and the sort order. Rows One row for each document. The right side of the row shows the assigned users, the time of the last change, the comment count and a heart (like). Count For example 6 of 6: rows loaded and total rows that match the filters. Page size 20, 100, 500 or 2500 rows, and Load More.

Click the title of a row to open the document in the form view.

docs.title: Quick filters
docs.text:
Quick filters show above the list. Type or select a value to filter at once. These fields show as quick filters:

  • ID (name) and the title field of the DocType.
  • Fields with In Standard Filter (in_standard_filter) checked.
  • Fields that you add with Customize Quick Filters.

A text quick filter has a match button next to it. Select Equals for an exact match or Like for a partial match. The desk saves your choice for each field.

To add quick filters:

  1. Click ... > Customize Quick Filters.
  2. Select the fields. You can also select Assigned To, Created By and Tags.
  3. Click Save. The page reloads.

Assigned To, Created By and Tags show as dropdowns. Each value in the dropdown shows the number of matching documents.

docs.title: Filter button
docs.text:
1. Click Filter.
  2. Select a field, a condition (for example Equals) and a value.
  3. To add one more condition, click Add filter.
  4. To remove all conditions, click Clear all.

You can also click a value in a row, for example a status indicator, to filter by that value.

Filters show in the URL as query parameters, for example /desk/sample-order?status=Open. Share the URL to share the filtered list. The desk also remembers your last filters for each DocType.

Large tables

The desk treats a table as large when it has more than 100,000 rows (estimated) and a document was created in the last 30 days. On a large table with no filters, the list adds a filter for documents created in the last 90 days. A message tells you about it. Turn this off with Disable Automatic Recency Filters in List settings.

docs.title: Sort
docs.text:
Click the field name on the sort button to select the sort field. Click the icon on its left to change between ascending and descending order.

The sort options are Last Updated On, Created On, ID, Most Used (idx), the title field, the default sort field of the DocType, and every field that is mandatory, bold or in the list view. The default sort is the Default Sort Field and Default Sort Order of the DocType, or Created On descending.

docs.title: Select rows and run bulk actions
docs.text:
Select the check box of a row to select it. Select the check box in the header to select all loaded rows. When you select rows, the Add button changes to Actions.

Action Shows when What it does Copy to Clipboard Always Copies the selected rows. Edit The DocType has editable fields Sets one field to one value on all selected documents. Export You can export the DocType Exports the selected rows. Assign To Always Assigns the documents to users. Refer to Collaboration. Clear Assignment Always Removes all assignments. Apply Assignment Rule Always Runs the assignment rules on the documents. Add Tags Always Adds tags to the documents. Print You can print the DocType Prints all selected documents in one PDF. Submit Submittable DocType, you can submit, no workflow Submits the documents. Cancel You can cancel, no workflow Cancels the documents. Delete You can delete Deletes the documents after you confirm.

All actions except Copy to Clipboard need Allow bulk actions (bulk_actions) on your User. If the DocType has a workflow, Edit and Delete need Allow Bulk Editing in list settings, and the workflow actions show in the menu.

Large jobs run in the background:

Action Runs in the background when Edit, Submit, Cancel 20 or more documents. More than 500 documents is not allowed. Delete More than 10 documents.

The background tasks panel in the dock shows the progress.

docs.title: Like, comments and assignments in rows
docs.text:
• Click the heart on a row to like the document. Click the heart in the header to show only documents that you liked.
  • The comment icon shows the number of comments.
  • The avatars show the assigned users. Click an avatar to filter by that user.

docs.title: Paging and refresh
docs.text:
The list loads 20 rows. On a screen taller than 1180 pixels, it loads 100 rows. Select a page size at the bottom, or click Load More.

The list updates when another user changes a document. It also reloads every 5 minutes while it is open. Turn off live updates with Disable Auto Refresh in list settings.

docs.title: List menu
docs.text:
Click ... to open the list menu.

Item Shows for What it does Customize Quick Filters All users Selects the quick filter fields. List Settings System Manager Opens List settings. Settings - Sample Order Users who can create Custom Field and Property Setter Opens a settings dialog for the DocType, for example naming, workflow, print formats and roles. Not shown for core DocTypes. Customize (Ctrl+Y) Same as above Opens Customize Form, or the DocType form for a custom DocType. Edit DocType System Manager in developer mode Opens the DocType form. User Permissions System Manager Opens the User Permission list for this DocType. Role Permissions Manager System Manager Opens the permissions of this DocType.

docs.title: List settings
docs.text:
List Settings changes the list for all users of the DocType. It saves a List View Settings document named after the DocType.

Field Label What it does fields Fields The columns of the list. Click + Add / Remove Fields to change them, up to 50. You can also set the width of a column. disable_count Disable Count Hides the total count. disable_comment_count Disable Comment Count Hides the comment count in rows. disable_sidebar_stats Disable Sidebar Stats The list view in this version does not read this field. disable_auto_refresh Disable Auto Refresh Stops live updates of the list. allow_edit Allow Bulk Editing Allows bulk Edit and Delete when the DocType has a workflow. disable_automatic_recency_filters Disable Automatic Recency Filters Stops the 90 day filter on large tables. disable_scrolling Disable Scrolling Turns off scrolling inside the list. show_tags Show Tags Shows the tags of each document in its row.

To resize a column, you can also drag the column border in the list.

docs.title: Saved layouts
docs.text:
A layout saves the filters, the sort and the columns of a list with a name.

  1. Click the view switcher (List View).
  2. Move to List View to open its submenu.
  3. Click Create Layout.
  4. Type a Layout name. Select Available to all users to share it.
  5. Set the filters, sort and columns. Click Create.

The submenu shows Default Layout, Global Layouts and Your Layouts. Click a layout to apply it. The view switcher then shows the layout name. Click Manage Layouts to edit, copy or delete layouts. Layouts are saved as List Filter documents.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+B Create a new document. Down / Up Move to the next or previous row. Shift+Down / Shift+Up Select rows while you move. Space Select the current row. Enter Open the current row. Ctrl+Y Open Customize.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Change the list of a DocType in <doctype>_list.js next to the DocType JSON. It sets frappe.listview_settings["Sample Order"] with keys such as add_fields, get_indicator, onload, button, formatters, primary_action and hide_name_column. Another app extends it with the doctype_list_js hook. frappe/desk/form/meta.py loads both. Refer to List view settings.
  • The columns come from fields with in_list_view. Quick filters come from fields with in_standard_filter. The default sort comes from sort_field and sort_order on the DocType.
  • The list gets its rows from frappe.desk.reportview.get. Bulk delete calls frappe.desk.reportview.delete_items. Bulk submit, cancel and edit call frappe.desk.doctype.bulk_update.bulk_update.submit_cancel_or_update_docs.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: The desk has three ways to search. Use the awesomebar to open a page or start a new document. Use global search to find text in documents of many DocTypes. Use the list view filters to find documents of one DocType.

docs.title: Awesomebar
docs.text:
Press Ctrl+K, or click Search in the dock, to open the awesomebar. Type at least two characters. Use Up and Down to select a result and Enter to open it. Hold Ctrl while you select a result to open it in a new tab.

You type You get A DocType name, for example sample order Sample Order List and other matching DocTypes. new and a DocType, for example new sample New Sample Order. It opens a new document. A text, in and a DocType, for example customer a in sample order Find customer a in Sample Order. It opens the list filtered by name. A report, page, workspace or dashboard name Report ..., Open ..., Open ... Workspace or ... Dashboard. A calculation, for example = 12 * 4 or 12*4 The result. Text with random Generate Random Password. # and a tag, for example #urgent Documents with that tag. Any other text Search for .... It opens global search.

On a list view, the awesomebar also offers Find ... in ... for the current DocType. It filters by the title field.

With an empty box, the awesomebar shows your recent pages and your most used links.

Turn off the awesomebar for a user with Show search bar (search_bar) on the User.

For developers

Add results with the awesomebar_search hook. Each method gets txt and returns a list of dicts with label, route and optional description, index and route_options. The desk calls frappe.desk.search.awesomebar_search and shows the first 20 results of each method. A JavaScript function can show as a result with frappe.search.utils.make_function_searchable(fn, label).

docs.title: Global search
docs.text:
Global search finds text in the fields of many DocTypes at the same time.

  1. Press Ctrl+G. You can also type a text in the awesomebar and select Search for ....
  2. Type the text.
  3. Click a DocType above the results to see results of that DocType only. Click More to see all DocTypes. Pin a DocType to keep it in the row.
  4. Click a result to open the document.

To match more than one term, join the terms with &, for example Customer A&Laptop. Start with # to search by tag.

Global search shows only documents that you can read. Press Ctrl+K to go back to the awesomebar.

docs.title: What global search finds
docs.text:
• Only DocTypes in Global Search Settings > Search Priorities. The order of the table is the order of the results. A System Manager opens the settings from the gear icon in the global search dialog.
  • Only fields with In Global Search (in_global_search) set. Set it in the DocType or in Customize Form. Fields of child tables also count.
  • The document name too, if the DocType has Make "name" searchable in Global Search (show_name_in_global_search).
  • Not cancelled documents, and not documents with disabled set or enabled not set.

When you save a document, the desk puts its text in a queue. A scheduled job (frappe.utils.global_search.sync_global_search) writes the queue to the __global_search table every 15 minutes. A new or changed document can take up to 15 minutes to show in the results.

For developers

An app adds its DocTypes to the default search priorities with the global_search_doctypes hook. Set disable_global_search in site_config.json to stop indexing. The search API is frappe.utils.global_search.search(text, start, limit, doctype). Refer to Site config.

docs.title: Search in a list
docs.text:
In the list view, type in the quick filters at the top. The ID filter and text filters match a part of the value by default (Like). Click the match button next to the filter to change to Equals. Click Filter to search in any field.

In Link fields, type to search the linked DocType. The search uses the name, the title field and the Search Fields of the linked DocType.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Tags are labels that users add to documents. To find documents by tag:

  • Type # and the tag in the awesomebar or in global search.
  • In the list view, add Tags with Customize Quick Filters, then select a tag.

Refer to Collaboration.

docs.title: Full-text search for apps
docs.text: Frappe also has a full-text search framework based on SQLite FTS5 in frappe/search/sqlite_search.py. The desk search does not use it. An app makes a subclass of SQLiteSearch, lists it in the sqlite_search hook, and builds its own search UI and API on it. The scheduler runs frappe.search.sqlite_search.index_docs_in_queue to keep the index current.

docs.title: Views
docs.text: A view shows the documents of one DocType in a different form. The list view is the default view. Other views show the same documents as a table, a board, a calendar and more.

docs.title: Switch view
docs.text:
1. Open the list of a DocType.
  2. Click the view switcher at the top right. It shows the name of the current view, for example List View.
  3. Click a view.

Some views have a submenu, for example kanban boards, saved reports, calendars and saved layouts. Move the pointer to the view to open its submenu.

The URL of a view is /desk/<doctype-slug>/view/<view>, for example /desk/sample-item/view/report.

The switcher shows only the views that the DocType supports:

View Shows when List View Always. Report View You have report access to the DocType. Dashboard View Always. Kanban View Always, except for File. Calendar View, Gantt View The DocType has calendar settings in <doctype>_calendar.js, or Is Calendar and Gantt is set. Image View The DocType has an Image Field. Tree View The DocType is a tree (Is Tree), or has tree settings in <doctype>_tree.js. Map View The DocType has a Geolocation field named location, or fields named latitude and longitude. get_coords_method in list settings only adds Map to the view switcher. The map still needs those fields. Inbox View DocType Communication, and you have an email account.

If Show view switcher (view_switcher) is off on your User, the switcher does not show.

docs.title: Report View
docs.text:
Report View shows documents in a table, like a spreadsheet. Use it to pick columns, edit values in cells, group rows and export data.

  • Filters and sort work the same as in the list view.
  • Double-click a cell to edit the value. The change saves at once. You can edit a cell only if you have write permission, the field is not read only, and the document is not submitted or cancelled. A field with Allow on Submit stays editable after submit.
  • Click a column header menu to sort, remove or move the column, or to add a column before it.
  • Click Add Group to group rows by a field. Select an aggregate: Count, Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum.

The ... menu of Report View has these items:

Item What it does Show Totals Adds a row with column totals. Print Prints the rows as shown. Toggle Chart Shows or hides a chart of the data. Pick Columns Selects columns, also from child tables. Export Exports the rows. Shows if you can export the DocType. Setup Auto Email Sends the saved report by email on a schedule. Save the report first. Save Saves changes to the current saved report. Shows if you own it or can write Report. Save As Saves the current columns, filters and sort as a new report. Delete Deletes the saved report.

A saved report is a Report document of type Report Builder. It shows under Saved Reports in the Report View submenu. Refer to Reports.

docs.title: Kanban View
docs.text:
A kanban board shows documents as cards in columns. Each column is one value of a Select field. Drag a card to another column to change the value.

To create a board:

  1. Open the view switcher and move to Kanban View.
  2. Click Create Board.
  3. Type a Kanban Board Name.
  4. In Columns based on, select a Select field, for example Category.
  5. Click Save.

If the DocType has no Select field, the dialog asks you to add one with Customize Form. Boards for Note and ToDo are private.

On the board:

  • Click + at the top of a column, or Add Sample Item, to create a document in that column.
  • Click a card to open the document.
  • Right-click a card, or use its menu, for Open in New Tab, Copy Link, Move to, Assign, Select and Delete.
  • Select cards to show the selection bar with Edit, Assign, Tags, Delete and Clear. Press Esc to clear the selection.
  • Click Filter to filter the cards. Click ... > Save Filters to save them in the board. Only users who can write the board see Save Filters.
  • Click Group to split the board into swimlanes by a second field.
  • Click Settings to change the board: name, title field, image field, footer date, columns and their colors, card fields, preview fields and swimlanes.

A board is a Kanban Board document. A standard board (is_standard = Yes) comes from an app. Outside developer mode, a standard board shows Duplicate in place of Settings. Copy it to change it.

Classic boards

New boards use the new kanban (use_kanban_v2 = 1). Boards made before it keep the classic kanban until you set Use Kanban v2 (New Experience) on the board.

docs.title: Calendar View
docs.text:
Calendar View shows documents on a calendar by their date fields. Frappe has calendars for Event and ToDo.

  • Click Month, Week or Day to change the range. Click Today to go to today.
  • Select or drag across time slots to create a new document.
  • Drag an event to change its dates.
  • Click Hide Weekends or Show Weekends at the bottom.

To make one more calendar for a DocType, create a Calendar View document. Set the Reference Document Type, Subject Field, Start Date Field and End Date Field. The calendar shows in the Calendar View submenu. The Default calendar uses the calendar settings of the DocType.

docs.title: Gantt View
docs.text: Gantt View shows documents as bars on a timeline. It uses the same start and end fields as the calendar. Drag a bar to change the dates.

docs.title: Tree View
docs.text:
Tree View shows a tree DocType as nested nodes. Click a node to expand it.

  • Expand/Collapse expands or collapses all nodes.
  • The node menu has Add Child, Move to..., Rename and Delete. You cannot rename or delete the root node.
  • Change the order with Default Order, Name A to Z or Name Z to A.

docs.title: Dashboard View
docs.text:
Dashboard View shows charts and number cards for the DocType, for example /desk/sample-item/view/dashboard. At first it shows the public Dashboard Chart (type Count, Sum or Group By) and Number Card documents of the DocType.

  1. Click Customize to add, remove or move charts and cards.
  2. Click Save Customizations to keep the changes, or Discard to drop them.

Your layout is saved in your user settings. To go back to the default, click ... > Reset Dashboard Customizations. Refer to Dashboards.

docs.title: Image View
docs.text: Image View shows documents as a grid of images from the Image Field of the DocType. For example, open /desk/user/view/image to see users with their photos.

docs.title: Map View
docs.text: Map View shows documents as markers on a map. It reads the location Geolocation field, or the latitude and longitude fields.

docs.title: Inbox View
docs.text: Inbox View shows Communication documents of your email account as an inbox. Select the email account in the Inbox View submenu. Refer to Email.
