docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Change forms and fields without code, and define document workflows.

Page What it covers Customize Form Change the fields, layout and properties of a standard DocType from the desk with Customize Form, Custom Field and Property Setter. Workflow Move documents through approval states with Workflow, Workflow State, transitions, conditions and Workflow Action.

docs.title: Customize Form
docs.text: Use Customize Form to change a standard DocType on one site without editing the app code. You can add fields, hide or reorder fields, change labels and other field properties, and change DocType settings such as the title field or the sort order. Your changes survive app updates, because Frappe stores them in two separate DocTypes: Custom Field and Property Setter.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
Record DocType What it stores Name format New field Custom Field A field that you add to a DocType. Frappe adds a column to the database table. <DocType>-<fieldname>, for example ToDo-custom_sample_ref Changed property Property Setter One changed property of a DocType, a field, a link, an action or a state. <DocType>-<field or row or "main">-<property>, for example ToDo-priority-reqd
  • When you add a field and do not give a fieldname, Frappe makes one from the label and adds the prefix custom_. A label "Sample Ref" gives custom_sample_ref.
  • Property Setter doctype_or_field ("Applied On") is one of DocField, DocType, DocType Link, DocType Action or DocType State.
  • Frappe merges Custom Fields and Property Setters into the DocType meta when it loads the meta (frappe.get_meta).
  • Only users with the System Manager role can use Customize Form.

docs.title: What you cannot customize
docs.text:
Customize Form rejects these DocTypes:

  • Core DocTypes in frappe.model.core_doctypes_list, for example DocType, User, Role, Report, Print Format, Custom Field and Property Setter. The error is "Core DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Single DocTypes. The error is "Single DocTypes cannot be customized."
  • Custom DocTypes (DocTypes with custom set, such as Sample Item). For these, the desk opens the DocType form instead, where you edit the DocType directly.

docs.title: Open Customize Form
docs.text:
1. Open the list or a form of the DocType, for example ToDo.
  2. Open the menu (the ... button).
  3. Select Customize. In the list view the shortcut is Ctrl+Y.

You can also go to /desk/customize-form and select the DocType in Enter Form Type (doc_type).

The form has two tabs:

  • Details shows the DocType properties, the Fields table, and the Document Actions, Document Links and Document States tables.
  • Form shows the form builder. Drag fields, sections, columns and tabs to change the layout. Click a field to edit its properties in the right panel. Click Add field to add a Custom Field.

Click Update to save. Frappe then creates or updates the Custom Fields and Property Setters, updates the database table if a column changed, and clears the cache of the DocType.

docs.title: Add a field
docs.text:
1. Open Customize Form for ToDo.
  2. In the Form tab, click Add field in the column where you want the field.
  3. Select the field type and enter the label, for example "Sample Ref".
  4. Set other properties in the right panel, for example Mandatory or In List View.
  5. Click Update.

To delete a Custom Field, remove it in the form builder and click Update. You cannot delete a standard field. Hide it instead.

docs.title: Change a standard field
docs.text:
You can change properties of standard fields, for example the label, Hidden, Mandatory, Read Only, In List View, Default, Depends On and the permission level. Each changed property becomes one Property Setter.

Frappe limits field type changes. You can change the type only inside a group of compatible types (ALLOWED_FIELDTYPE_CHANGE in frappe/custom/doctype/customize_form/customize_form.py). If the new type is shorter and saved values are too long, Frappe shows "Data Too Long" and lists the documents.

docs.title: DocType properties
docs.text:
These properties are in the Details tab. The list is not complete.

Label Fieldname Description Change Label (via Custom Translation) label Shows another name for the DocType. Frappe saves it as a Translation record. Search Fields search_fields Fields that Link field search also looks in. Title Field title_field Field shown as the document title. Show Title in Link Fields show_title_field_in_link Shows the title, not the name, in Link fields. Image Field image_field Field used as the document image. Quick Entry quick_entry Opens a small dialog for new documents. Track Changes track_changes Saves a Version record for each change. Track Views track_views Logs who opened a document. Allow Import (via Data Import Tool) allow_import Allows Data Import for this DocType. Allow Auto Repeat allow_auto_repeat Adds an auto_repeat Custom Field so documents can repeat. Max Attachments max_attachments Maximum number of attachments per document. Hide Sidebar, Menu, and Comments hide_toolbar Hides the form sidebar, menu and comments. Naming Rule / Auto Name naming_rule, autoname How new documents get a name. Default Print Format default_print_format Print format used by default. Default View default_view View that opens from the sidebar, for example List or Report. Sort Field / Sort Order sort_field, sort_order Default sort of the list view. Allow document creation via Email email_append_to Creates documents from incoming email.

docs.title: Actions menu
docs.text:
The Actions button has these items:

Item What it does Go to {DocType} List Opens the list view. Not shown for child tables. Set Permissions Opens the Role Permissions Manager for this DocType. Reload Loads the current customizations again. Reset Layout Deletes the Property Setters for field_order and insert_after. Reset All Customizations Deletes all Property Setters and Custom Fields of the DocType that are not system generated. Property Setters for naming_series and options stay. Trim Table Removes database columns that no field uses anymore. You cannot undo this. Export Customizations Shown only in developer mode. See below.

To customize a child table, use Customize Child Table and select the table.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Do not ask users to repeat customizations on each site. Ship them with your app.

Export from the desk. In developer mode, click Actions > Export Customizations. Select a module. Frappe writes the Custom Fields, Property Setters and links to <module>/custom/<doctype>.json in your app, and does the same for each child table. If Sync on Migrate is set, bench migrate applies the file on each site. If Export Custom Permissions is set, the file also holds the Custom DocPerm rules, and migrate force-syncs them.

Create them in code. Use create_custom_fields in an install hook or a patch. It creates the fields that do not exist and updates the ones that do.

# sample_app/setup.py
from frappe.custom.doctype.custom_field.custom_field import create_custom_fields
from frappe.custom.doctype.property_setter.property_setter import make_property_setter


def after_install():
    create_custom_fields(
        {
            "ToDo": [
                {
                    "fieldname": "sample_ref",
                    "label": "Sample Ref",
                    "fieldtype": "Data",
                    "insert_after": "description",
                }
            ]
        }
    )
    make_property_setter("ToDo", "priority", "reqd", 1, "Check")
  • create_custom_fields(custom_fields, ignore_validate=False, update=True) creates the records as Administrator, clears the cache and updates the table.
  • make_property_setter(doctype, fieldname, property, value, property_type, for_doctype=False, ...) ignores permissions. Set for_doctype=True for a DocType property.
  • You can also export Custom Field and Property Setter records with the fixtures hook. See Fixtures and Patches and Extending Apps.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A field type change that makes a column smaller can fail if saved values are too long.
  • Many fields can hit the database row size limit. Frappe then shows "Database Table Row Size Limit".
  • Reset All Customizations also removes Custom Fields that other users added. Export them first if you need them.
  • Customizations that an app ships with is_system_generated set stay after a reset.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: A Workflow controls how a document moves from one state to the next, and which role can move it. Use it when a document needs review or approval before it is submitted, for example "Pending" to "Approved". When a workflow applies to a document, the form shows an Actions menu instead of the standard Submit and Cancel buttons.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
Term DocType Meaning Workflow Workflow The rule set for one DocType: states, transitions, conditions. State Workflow State A named stage, for example "Pending". It has an optional icon and button style. Action Workflow Action Master A named step a user clicks, for example "Approve". Transition Workflow Transition (child) "From state X, role R can do action A to go to state Y." Workflow Action Workflow Action A to-do record that Frappe creates for users who can act on a document in its current state.

The current state of each document is stored in the field named in Workflow State Field (default workflow_state). If the DocType has no such field, Frappe adds a hidden Custom Field of type Link to Workflow State when you save the workflow.

docs.title: Create a workflow
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/workflow/new.
  2. Enter a Workflow Name and select the Document Type.
  3. In Document States, add one row for each state.
  4. In Transitions, add one row for each allowed move between states.
  5. Select Is Active.
  6. Save.

You can also edit states and transitions on a canvas in the Workflow Builder (/desk/workflow-builder). The builder is marked beta.

docs.title: Document States
docs.text: Field Description State (state) A Workflow State record. Doc Status (doc_status) 0 Draft, 1 Submitted, 2 Cancelled. A non-submittable DocType can only use 0. Only Allow Edit For (allow_edit) The role that can edit the document in this state. Update Field / Update Value Set a field of the document when it enters this state. Evaluate as Expression Treat Update Value as a Python expression, for example doc.total * 2. Is Optional State Do not create Workflow Action records for this state. Send Email On State (send_email) Default on. Send the action email when the document enters this state (needs Send Email Alert on the workflow). Next Action Email Template An Email Template for that email. Message A message to show for this state. Don't Override Status Do not show the workflow state as the list view status.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Field Description State / Next State The state before and after the action. Action A Workflow Action Master record. Allowed (allowed) The role that can do this action. Allow Self Approval Default on. When off, the document owner cannot do this action. Administrator is always allowed. Condition Optional Python expression. The action shows only when it is true. Transition Tasks Optional Workflow Transition Tasks record: Server Scripts, Webhooks or app tasks that run with the transition.

Transition conditions get doc (the document as a dict) and a limited frappe object: frappe.db.get_value, frappe.db.get_list, frappe.session, and frappe.utils.now_datetime, add_to_date, get_datetime, now.

doc.total > 0 and doc.customer_name != "Customer A"

Frappe checks these rules when it saves a workflow:

  • An active workflow needs at least one state and one transition.
  • A transition cannot start from a Cancelled state.
  • A transition cannot go from Submitted (1) back to Draft (0).
  • A transition cannot go from Draft (0) to Cancelled (2).

docs.title: Workflow options
docs.text: Field Default Description Is Active 0 Only active workflows apply. Don't Override Status 0 Keep the document status in list view instead of the workflow state. Send Email Alert 0 Email the users who can do the next action. Enable Action Confirmation 0 Ask the user to confirm before an action runs. Priority 0 Higher priority workflows are matched first. Conditions empty Apply the workflow only to documents that match all rows.

docs.title: More than one workflow on a DocType
docs.text:
A DocType can have more than one active workflow when you use Conditions. Each condition row has a Field, an operator (=, !=, >, <, >=, <=) and a Value. A workflow applies to a document only if all rows match. A document with an empty value in a condition field does not match.

Frappe picks the first matching workflow in Priority order (highest first). Two active workflows with the same priority that can match the same document are rejected on save. All active workflows of one DocType must use the same Workflow State Field.

When you activate a workflow with no conditions, Frappe deactivates the other active workflows of that DocType that also have no conditions.

When you save a workflow, Frappe sets the state field of existing documents that match the workflow and have no state yet. It uses the first state row for each docstatus.

docs.title: Use a workflow on a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click Actions.
  3. Select an action.

The menu shows only the transitions from the current state that your roles allow and whose condition is true. After the action, Frappe saves, submits or cancels the document to match the docstatus of the next state. It also adds a "Workflow" comment to the timeline.

To apply an action to many documents, select them in the list view and use the Actions menu. Fewer than 20 documents run at once. From 20 to 500 documents run in a background job. More than 500 documents are rejected.

docs.title: Workflow Action records
docs.text: After each save, cancel or update after submit, Frappe creates Workflow Action records with status Open for the roles that can do the next transition. The user sees them in the Workflow Action list. When Send Email Alert is on, Frappe also emails these users. The email has links to do the action without logging in to desk. When a user does the action, the records change to Completed.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A user can only change the state with a valid transition. A direct edit of the state field fails with "Workflow State transition not allowed".
  • Data Import cannot insert documents in a state other than the first state.
  • If the state stored on a document is not in the workflow, save fails. Update the workflow or the document.
  • A cancelled state blocks the standard Cancel button. Use a transition to the cancelled state.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Server API in frappe/model/workflow.py: apply_workflow(doc, action), get_transitions(doc), bulk_workflow_approval(docnames, doctype, action), get_workflow_name(doctype, doc=None).
  • Add your own transition tasks with the workflow_methods hook. Each entry is a dict with name and method. The method gets the document.
# sample_app/hooks.py
workflow_methods = [
    {"name": "Notify Warehouse", "method": "sample_app.tasks.notify_warehouse"},
]

# sample_app/tasks.py
def notify_warehouse(doc):
    ...
  • Synchronous tasks run in the same transaction as the transition. Tasks marked Asynchronous run in a background job after commit.
  • process_workflow_actions runs from doc_events for * (on_update, on_cancel, on_trash, on_update_after_submit) in frappe/hooks.py.

docs.title: Data, Reports and Printing
docs.text:
Import and export data, run reports, build dashboards and print documents.

Page What it covers Data Import and Export Insert or update many records from CSV, Excel or Google Sheets with Data Import, fix invalid values, read the import log, and export records with Data Export. Reports Build and save Report Builder reports, run Query and Script Reports, use prepared reports for slow reports, and export results to Excel or CSV. Dashboards Show counts and charts with Number Card and Dashboard Chart, group them in a Dashboard, and add them to workspaces. Printing Print documents, download PDFs, and design Print Formats with the Print Format Editor, Jinja HTML or raw commands, plus Letter Head and Print Settings.

docs.title: Dashboards
docs.text: A Number Card shows one number, such as the count of open orders. A Dashboard Chart shows data over time or by group. A Dashboard puts cards and charts on one page. You can also add cards and charts to a workspace. Use them to give users a quick view of the data they work with.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType Route What it is Number Card /desk/number-card One number from a DocType, a report or a whitelisted method. Dashboard Chart /desk/dashboard-chart A chart from a DocType, a report or a custom source. Dashboard /desk/dashboard A named set of charts and cards. Shown at /desk/dashboard-view/<name>. Dashboard Chart Source /desk/dashboard-chart-source Code in an app that gives data to a Custom chart. Dashboard Settings none Per-user chart setup (chart_config), such as saved chart filters.

docs.title: Make a Number Card
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/number-card/new.
  2. Enter a Label. The label is also the name of the card.
  3. Set Type to Document Type.
  4. Select the Document Type, for example Sample Order.
  5. Select the Function: Count, Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum.
  6. If the function is not Count, select the number field in Aggregate Function Based On.
  7. Click the filters table and set filters, for example status = Open.
  8. Save.
  9. Click Add Card to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Field Default Description type Document Type, Report or Custom. function For Document Type. parent_document_type Needed when the Document Type is a child table. report_name, report_field, report_function For Report: the report, the number column, and Sum, Average, Minimum or Maximum. method For Custom: dotted path of a whitelisted method. filters_json Fixed filters. dynamic_filters_json Filters with JavaScript expressions, for example frappe.datetime.get_today(). show_percentage_stats 1 Shows the change from the previous period. stats_time_interval Daily Period for the change: Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly. is_public 0 Makes the card available to all users. color, background_color Card colors. show_full_number 0 Shows the full number instead of a short form.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard Chart
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/dashboard-chart/new.
  2. Enter Chart Name.
  3. Select the Chart Type.
  4. Select the Document Type and set the fields for that chart type.
  5. Select the display Type: Line, Bar, Percentage, Pie, Donut or Heatmap.
  6. Set filters in the filters table.
  7. Save.
  8. Click Add Chart to Dashboard to put it on a Dashboard.
Chart Type Fields to set Result Count Time Series Based On (a date field), Timespan, Time Interval Number of records per period. Sum / Average Same as Count, plus Value Based On Sum or average of a number field per period. Group By Group By Based On, Group By Type (Count, Sum, Average), Number of Groups One value per group, for example per status. Report Report Name, X Field, Y Axis, or Use Report Chart Chart from the data of a report. Custom Chart Source Data from a Dashboard Chart Source in an app.

Timespan can be Last Year, Last Quarter, Last Month, Last Week or Select Date Range. Time Interval can be Yearly, Quarterly, Monthly, Weekly or Daily. Cancelled documents are never counted.

The chart menu on a dashboard has Refresh, Edit, Reset Chart, Export, and a link to the list or report of the source. Chart data is cached. Refresh gets new data and shows the time in Last synced.

docs.title: Make a Dashboard
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/dashboard/new.
  2. Enter Dashboard Name.
  3. Add charts in the Charts table. Set the Width of each chart to Half or Full.
  4. Add cards in the Cards table.
  5. Save.
  6. Click Show Dashboard.

Is Default makes this the default dashboard. Chart Options takes JSON that applies to all charts on the dashboard.

docs.title: Add cards and charts to a workspace
docs.text:
1. Open the workspace.
  2. Click Edit.
  3. Add a Chart block or a Number Card block.
  4. Select an existing chart or card, or make a new one.
  5. Save the workspace.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• System Managers see all charts and cards.
  • A user sees a Document Type chart or card when they can read its DocType. A Report chart or card needs access to the report.
  • If a chart has rows in its Roles table, a user needs one of those roles.
  • Charts and cards are also limited to the modules the user can see.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• A Custom Number Card calls the whitelisted method in method with filters. Return a number, or a dict with value and the formatting keys such as fieldtype.
  • A Custom chart reads frappe.dashboards.chart_sources["<Source Name>"] from <module>/dashboard_chart_source/<source_name>/<source_name>.js in your app. Set method there to the Python method that returns the chart data.
  • Cards and charts with Is Standard set are exported to the module of the app when you save in developer mode. They cannot be edited on a site without developer mode.
  • Chart data comes from frappe.desk.doctype.dashboard_chart.dashboard_chart.get and card data from frappe.desk.doctype.number_card.number_card.get_result.
  • Ship charts and cards in a workspace of your app. See Workspaces, Sidebar and Dock.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Number Card cannot use a Single DocType.
  • A Sum or Average card needs a number or duration field.
  • Chart data is cached per chart. Use Refresh after a large data change.

docs.title: Data Import and Export
docs.text: Data Import inserts or updates many records from a CSV or Excel file, or from a public Google Sheet. Data Export downloads records as CSV or Excel. Use them to move data in from another system, to change many records at once, or to get a template to fill in.

docs.title: Before you import
docs.text:
• The DocType must allow import (Allow Import in the DocType or Customize Form).
  • You need the import permission on the DocType.
  • Most core DocTypes cannot be imported. User, Role and Print Format can.
  • The scheduler must be active, because the import runs in a background job. In developer mode, the import runs in the request.

docs.title: Import records
docs.text: Go to /desk/data-import/new, or open the list view of the DocType and select Import from the new-record menu. The import has four steps: Config, Preview, Fix issues and Import.

docs.title: 1. Config
docs.text:
1. Select the Document Type.
  2. Select the Import Type.
  3. Optional: click Download Template to get a file with the right columns.
  4. Attach the file in Import File, or enter a URL in Import from Google Sheets.
  5. Click Next.
Import Type Result Insert New Records Each row makes a new document. Update Existing Records Each row updates the document in the ID column. A row with no change fails with "No changes to update". Insert or Update Records Update the document if the ID exists, else insert it. Option Default Description Don't Send Emails (mute_emails) 1 Do not send emails or notifications during the import. Submit After Import 0 Submit each document. Submittable DocTypes only. Custom Delimiters / Delimiter Options 0 / ,;\t| For CSV files with a delimiter other than a comma. Detect CSV type (use_csv_sniffer) 0 Let Frappe find the CSV format.

docs.title: 2. Preview
docs.text:
The preview shows the rows of the file. Each column has a field picker. Change it to match a column to another field, or select Don't Import to skip the column. Click Next. Frappe saves your changes and opens the next step.

For a tree DocType, the preview shows the tree. You can change the parent of a node or mark it as a group before the import.

docs.title: 3. Fix issues
docs.text:
Frappe checks Link and Select values, dates and mandatory fields. Each value that is not valid gets a row in Mapping warnings:

  • Enter a valid value in Map To. Frappe uses it for every row with that value.
  • For a Link field, select Create New to create the missing record during the import.
  • Or click Skip to leave out every row that has the value.

After you change a mapping or a skip, click Save. The Import button shows when there are no unsaved changes. The import does not start while there are warnings that are not fixed or skipped.

docs.title: 4. Import
docs.text:
Click Import at the bottom of the Fix issues step. Frappe shows the progress, and then the result: how many records were inserted, updated, failed or skipped.

  • Frappe commits after each successful row. A failed row does not undo the rows before it.
  • The status of the import becomes Success, Partial Success, Error or Timed Out.
  • If some rows fail, fix the data and start the import again. Rows that were imported before are not imported again.
  • Click Cancel Import to stop a running import. Frappe asks you to confirm, then stops the job and sets the status to Error.

docs.title: Import log
docs.text:
Each imported or failed row makes a Data Import Log record with the document name, the row numbers, a success flag and the error. On the Import step you can filter the log, and download:

  • Download Failed Rows (on the Failed count): a file with only the rows that failed, to fix and import again.
  • Download Skipped Rows (on the Skipped count): the rows you chose to skip.
  • Export Import Log: the full log.

Deleting a Data Import also deletes its logs.

docs.title: Export records
docs.text:
There are two ways to export records.

From a list view (recommended): select records, then use Actions > Export. Or open the Data Import form and click Download Template. The Export Data dialog has these options:

Option Values File Type Excel or CSV Export Type All Records, Filtered Records, 5 Records or Blank Template Fields The fields of the DocType and its child tables. Use Select Mandatory or Select All.

The exported file has the same format that Data Import reads, so you can edit it and import it with Update Existing Records.

Data Export page: go to /desk/data-export. Select the DocType, the File Type (Excel or CSV), filters and fields, then click Export. Select Export without main header to leave out the header notes and column descriptions.

To export the rows shown in a report, use Export in the menu of the report view. See Reports.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• When you update records, include the ID column. Frappe finds the document by it.
  • In Insert mode, Frappe sets the name from the file only when the DocType uses Prompt naming.
  • A workflow DocType can only import documents in the first workflow state.
  • Child table rows go on the lines below their parent row, with the parent columns empty.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Import from the command line:
bench --site frappe.localhost data-import --file sample-items.csv --doctype "Sample Item" --type Insert

--type is Insert, Update or Upsert. Add --submit-after-import to submit. The path is relative to the sites folder.

  • Import or export JSON records from code with import_doc(path) and export_json(doctype, path, filters=None) in frappe/core/doctype/data_import/data_import.py. bench import-doc <path> uses import_doc.
  • Take over validation and record creation for one DocType with the data_import_providers hook. Map the DocType to a subclass of ImportProvider in frappe/core/doctype/data_import/import_provider.py.
# sample_app/hooks.py
data_import_providers = {"Sample Order": "sample_app.imports.SampleOrderImport"}
  • Rows per batch: data_import_batch_size in site config (default 1000). See Site Config.

docs.title: Printing
docs.text: Every document in the desk can be printed or saved as a PDF. A Print Format controls what the printed page shows. Use the print view to print, download or email a document. Make a Print Format when the standard layout does not fit, for example when an invoice needs a custom header or a narrow receipt layout.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: Name DocType What it is Print view page print The preview at /desk/print/<DocType>/<name>. You pick the format, letter head, style and paper there. Print Format Print Format A layout for one DocType (or one report). Made in the Print Format Editor, or written as Jinja HTML. Standard format none The layout Frappe makes from the form when no Print Format is selected. Letter Head Letter Head A header and footer (image or HTML) added to the top and bottom of a print. Print Style Print Style Site-wide CSS for printed pages. Standard styles: Redesign, Modern, Classic, Striped, Monochrome. Print Settings Print Settings (Single) Site defaults: PDF engine, page size, draft and cancelled printing, raw printing. Print Heading Print Heading A named heading text that a print can show.

docs.title: Print a document
docs.text:
1. Open the document.
  2. Click the print icon next to the title in the form sidebar, or press Ctrl+P. The print view opens.
  3. In the sidebar, select a Print Format, Language and Letter Head.
  4. Select a Style, a Font, a Paper Size and an Orientation if you need them.
  5. Click Print to send the page to the browser print dialog.

The toolbar icons do these actions:

Icon Action Shortcut Download Download PDF. Makes the PDF on the server. Ctrl+Shift+P Paperclip Attach PDF. Saves the PDF as a file attachment on the document. Mail Email. Opens the email composer with the print attached. Ctrl+Shift+E Form Goes back to the form. Print button Print. Opens the browser print dialog. Ctrl+P

The ... menu has Full Page, Refresh, Set as Default Format, Print Settings and Customize. Raw Printing Setting shows when raw printing is on. Select Network Printer shows when Enable Print Server is on in Print Settings.

Note

Draft documents print with a "Draft" heading when Always add "Draft" Heading for printing draft documents is on in Print Settings. Cancelled documents print only when Allow Print for Cancelled is on.

docs.title: Make a Print Format with the editor
docs.text:
A new Print Format that is not a custom HTML format uses the Print Format Editor (print_format_builder_beta is set on save).

  1. Go to /desk/print-format/new.
  2. Enter a name and select the DocType, for example Sample Order.
  3. Save. The editor opens at /desk/print-format-builder/<name>.
  4. Select Start from default to begin with all fields of the DocType, or Start blank.
  5. Drag fields from the left panel onto the page.
  6. Click Save & Apply to make the change live.

The left panel has four tabs:

Tab Content Fields The fields of the DocType and of its child tables. Layers The tree of sections and fields on the page. Blocks Section, Page Break, Custom HTML (or Typst for a Typst format), Spacer, Divider, Image, Barcode, Custom Table, Text and Linked Field. Library Saved snippets that you can reuse.

The right panel sets font, font size, label and value colors, paper size, orientation, margins, background, PDF renderer, letter head, page numbers, Access (roles that may print with this format), global variables and custom CSS.

The editor keeps your edits as a working draft (draft_data) until you click Save & Apply. The history icon shows saved versions. The record box at the top picks the document used for the preview.

docs.title: PDF renderer
docs.text: Value Label in the editor Notes chrome Chromium Renders HTML with headless Chromium. PlutoPrint PlutoPrint (light) Default. Marked experimental. Falls back to Chromium for a format it cannot render. Typst Typst (fast) Marked experimental. Only for editor formats. Adds a Typst block and removes Custom HTML.

docs.title: Write a Jinja Print Format
docs.text:
Use a Jinja format when you need full control of the HTML.

  1. Open a new Print Format and select the DocType.
  2. Turn on Custom Format.
  3. Keep Print Format Type as Jinja.
  4. Write the template in HTML.
  5. Save.
<h2>{{ doc.customer_name }}</h2>
<p>{{ _("Order Date") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("order_date") }}</p>
<table class="table table-bordered">
  {% for row in doc.items %}
  <tr>
    <td>{{ row.item }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("qty") }}</td>
    <td class="text-right">{{ row.get_formatted("rate", doc) }}</td>
  </tr>
  {% endfor %}
</table>
<p class="text-right">{{ _("Total") }}: {{ doc.get_formatted("total") }}</p>

The template gets doc, meta, layout, no_letterhead, letter_head, footer and print_settings, plus the Jinja globals such as frappe and _. Frappe validates the template on save.

docs.title: Raw printing
docs.text: For label and receipt printers, turn on Custom Format and Raw Printing, then write printer commands in Raw Commands. Turn on Enable Raw Printing in Print Settings first. The browser sends raw commands to the printer through the QZ Tray client.

docs.title: Print Format for a report
docs.text: Set Print Format For to Report and select the Report. Frappe sets Custom Format for report formats, so you write the HTML yourself.

docs.title: Set the default format
docs.text:
• In the Print Format form, click Set as Default. For a custom DocType this sets default_print_format on the DocType. For other DocTypes it makes a Property Setter.
  • In the print view, use ... > Set as Default Format.

Disabling the default format removes it as the default after you confirm.

docs.title: Letter Head
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/letter-head/new.
  2. Enter Letter Head Name.
  3. Set Letter Head Based On to Image or HTML.
  4. Add the header image or the Header HTML.
  5. Set Footer Based On and add the footer the same way.
  6. Turn on Default Letter Head to use it when no letter head is picked.

Header and footer HTML are Jinja. They get doc when they render.

docs.title: Print Settings
docs.text:
Go to /desk/print-settings.

Field Default Description send_print_as_pdf 1 Attach prints to emails as PDF. repeat_header_footer 1 Repeat the letter head header and footer on each PDF page. pdf_generator PlutoPrint Default PDF engine: chrome or PlutoPrint. A format can override it. pdf_page_size A4 Default PDF page size. Custom shows height and width in mm. with_letterhead 1 Print with the default letter head. allow_print_for_draft 1 Allow printing of draft documents. add_draft_heading 1 Add a "Draft" heading to draft prints. allow_print_for_cancelled 0 Allow printing of cancelled documents. allow_page_break_inside_tables 0 Let a table split across pages. enable_print_server 0 Print to a network printer (Network Printer Settings, CUPS server and port 631 by default). enable_raw_printing 0 Allow raw command formats. print_style Redesign Default Print Style. font, font_size Default Default print font. max_bulk_print_docs 100 Most documents in one bulk print. max_concurrent_bulk_exports 5 Most bulk PDF exports one user can run at the same time.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Get the HTML or PDF of a document in Python with frappe.get_print. It uses the PDF engine from the format or Print Settings.
html = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", print_format="Sample Order Print")
pdf = frappe.get_print("Sample Order", "SO-00001", as_pdf=True)  # bytes, starts with b"%PDF-"
  • Use frappe.attach_print(doctype, name, ...) to get a PDF attachment dict for frappe.sendmail.
  • The download URL is /api/method/frappe.utils.print_format.download_pdf?doctype=...&name=...&format=.... It checks print permission and has a rate limit of 30 calls a minute per user.
  • Add Jinja methods and filters for templates with the jinja hook ({"methods": [...], "filters": [...]}).
  • Add a PDF engine with the pdf_generator hook. Frappe registers get_chrome_pdf, get_plutoprint_pdf and get_typst_pdf.
  • Other hooks: get_print_format_template, on_print_pdf, pdf_header_html, pdf_body_html, pdf_footer_html.
  • A Print Format with Standard = Yes is saved in the app and can be changed only in developer mode. See Print Formats.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A standard Print Format cannot be changed on a site. Duplicate it and edit the copy.
  • Edits in the Print Format Editor do not print until you click Save & Apply.
  • Paper Size Custom needs Paper Width and Paper Height above 0 for a classic or custom format.
  • The Access roles hide the format from users without one of the roles.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text: A report shows records as a table, with filters, totals, charts and export. Frappe has four report types. Use Report Builder to save a column and filter setup of one DocType without code. Use a Query Report or a Script Report when you need joins, calculations or data from many DocTypes. Every report is a Report document.

docs.title: Report types
docs.text:
report_type Who makes it Where it runs Notes Report Builder A user with create permission on Report (by default Report Manager, System Manager) Report view of one DocType Columns, filters, sort, group by and totals are saved as JSON in the json field. Query Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /desk/query-report/<name> One SQL SELECT in the query field. Script Report Script Manager (non-standard) or a developer /desk/query-report/<name> Python. In an app: an execute(filters) function. On a site: the Script field. Custom Report Report Manager /desk/query-report/<name> A saved copy of a Query or Script Report with its own columns and filters. reference_report points to the original.

A report is Standard (is_standard = Yes) when it is part of an app. A standard report cannot be changed on a site. Duplicate it, or use Save in the report to make a Custom Report.

docs.title: Make a Report Builder report
docs.text:
1. Open the list of the DocType, for example /desk/sample-order.
  2. Switch the view to Report. The URL becomes /desk/sample-order/view/report.
  3. Add filters with Filter, and a group with Add Group.
  4. Click a column header to sort or remove the column. Use ... > Pick Columns to add columns, also from child tables.
  5. Click ... > Save As and enter a name.

The new report opens at /desk/<doctype>/view/report/<report name>. The page title shows Not Saved after you change it. Click ... > Save to keep the change.

The ... menu of the report view has these items. Some show only when you have the permission.

Item What it does Show Totals Adds a total row for number columns. Print Prints the table. Toggle Chart Shows a chart. Pick the X axis field, Y axis fields and chart type. Pick Columns Selects the columns to show. Export Downloads the rows (see Export). Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report that sends this report on a schedule. Save / Save As Save updates this report. It shows for the report owner and Report Managers. Save As makes a new report. Delete Deletes the saved report. User Permissions Opens the User Permissions of the DocType.

docs.title: Run a Query or Script Report
docs.text:
1. Search for the report name in the awesomebar, or open /desk/query-report/<Report Name>.
  2. Set the filters at the top. The report runs again on each change.
  3. Use the Actions menu or the ... menu for more actions.
Item What it does Refresh Runs the report again. Edit Opens the Report document. Print Prints the report. Export Downloads the data. Setup Auto Email Makes an Auto Email Report. Add Column Adds a column from a linked DocType. User Permissions Opens User Permissions for the report DocType. Save Saves your columns and filters as a Custom Report. Shows for Report Managers only. Create Card Makes a Number Card from a number column. Set Chart / Add Chart to Dashboard Makes a chart from the report and adds it to a Dashboard.

Related Reports shows other saved versions of the same report.

docs.title: Prepared reports
docs.text:
A prepared report runs in a background job and saves the result. Use it for a report that takes a long time.

  • Turn on Prepared Report (prepared_report) in the Report document.
  • For a Script Report, Frappe turns it on for you when one run takes more than 15 seconds. To stop this, turn on Disable Prepared Report Automation.
  • Timeout (In Seconds) sets the job timeout. The default is 25 minutes.
  • Generate CSV also saves the result as a CSV file.

When a report is prepared:

  1. Set the filters and click Generate New Report.
  2. Frappe makes a Prepared Report with status Queued. The status changes to Started when a worker picks it up.
  3. When the job ends, the status is Completed or Error. You get a notification with a link to the result.
  4. Click Edit to change the filters, or Rebuild to run it again with the same filters.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Export opens a dialog with these options:

Option Default Description File Format Excel Excel or CSV. Export in Background off Makes the file in a background job. CSV Delimiter , CSV only. CSV Quoting Non-numeric Minimal, All, Non-numeric or None. CSV Decimal Separator . CSV only.

In the report view, the dialog also asks if you want to export all matching rows when there are more rows than the page shows. Export shows only when you have export permission on the DocType.

docs.title: Access
docs.text:
• A user can open a report when they can read its Ref DocType and have one of the roles in its Roles table.
  • Non-standard Query and Script Reports can be saved only by a user with the Script Manager role.
  • Disabled hides the report.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Write Query and Script Reports in an app as files in <module>/report/<report_name>/. See Reports (developer).
  • Run a report from code or the API with frappe.desk.query_report.run(report_name, filters).
  • frappe.core.doctype.prepared_report.prepared_report.make_prepared_report(report_name, filters) queues a prepared report.
  • frappe.desk.query_report.save_report(reference_report, report_name, columns, filters) makes a Custom Report.
  • frappe.desk.reportview.save_report(name, doctype, report_settings) saves a Report Builder report. It checks create permission on Report and read permission on the DocType.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Report Builder report works on one DocType and its child tables. Use a Query or Script Report for joins.
  • A prepared report shows the result of the last run, not live data. Check the Finished At time.
  • When Administrator saves a new report in developer mode, Frappe sets is_standard to Yes and writes it to the app.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Every settings page in Frappe: what each field does, its default and where it takes effect.

Page What it covers How Settings Work Settings pages are Single DocTypes stored in tabSingles. Learn where to open them, who can edit them, when a change takes effect, and how to read, write and build them in an app. System Settings Every field of System Settings, grouped by form tab, with its default, its effect and the server and desk code that reads it. Security, Session Default and Log Settings Field reference for Security Settings (security.txt), Session Default Settings and Log Settings, with where Frappe reads each field. Desk Settings Field reference for Navbar, Desktop, Global Search, Domain, Document Naming and per-user Notification Settings, with where Frappe reads each field. Website Settings Field reference for Website Settings, Portal Settings, Contact Us Settings, About Us Settings and Website Script, with the website code that reads each field. Print Settings Field reference for Print Settings, with the effect of each field on the print view, PDF generation, letter heads, bulk print and email attachments. Integration Settings Field reference for OAuth Provider Settings, OAuth Settings, LDAP Settings, Push Notification Settings, Geolocation Settings, Google Settings and SMS Settings, with where Frappe reads each field. Automation and AI Settings Field reference for Automation Settings, Flow Settings, Flow Knowledge Settings and Studio Settings, with defaults and the code that reads each field.

docs.title: Automation and AI Settings
docs.text:
This page is the field reference for the settings of the automation engine, Flow (AI agents) and the Studio AI assistant. For each field it gives the default and the code that reads it. For how Single DocTypes work in general, see How Settings Work.

All DocTypes on this page are Single DocTypes. Only the System Manager role can read or write them.

DocType Module Route Automation Settings Automation /desk/automation-settings Flow Settings Flow /desk/flow-settings, or the settings of the /flow page Flow Knowledge Settings Flow /desk/flow-knowledge-settings, or the settings of the /flow page Studio Settings Studio /desk/studio-settings

docs.title: Automation Settings
docs.text:
Automation Settings controls the automation engine that runs Automation Flow records: if it runs, how deep chains can go, retries, cleanup and size limits. Open it at /desk/automation-settings. The controller has no validation. All code reads the values through frappe.automation_engine.settings.get(fieldname), which uses frappe.get_cached_doc. A save takes effect on the next read.

Note

A value of 0 or empty falls back to the default in DEFAULTS (frappe/automation_engine/settings.py). Only Disable Automations, Drain Seconds and Allow Unregistered Events accept 0 as a value. For example, Maximum Recursion Depth 0 means 3.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Field Default Effect Disable Automations (disable_automations) 0 When on, is_enabled() returns False. Document events do not queue automations (dispatch.py), the drain job does not run queued rows (drainer.py), and the Scheduled and Date Based triggers do not fire (scheduler.py). Rows already in Automation Trigger Queue stay there and run after you turn it off. Maximum Recursion Depth (max_depth) 3 An automation that saves a document can trigger another automation. Each level adds 1 to the depth. Above this value, dispatch.py queues nothing and logs the error Automation Flow depth limit reached.

docs.title: Reliability
docs.text: Field Default Effect Failure Threshold (failure_threshold) 10 Consecutive failed runs of one flow, counted in Redis. At this count, runner.py sets Enabled to 0 on the Automation Flow, fills Disabled Reason, marks its waiting queue rows Skipped and sends the flow owner a Notification Log. A successful run resets the count. Stale Running Minutes (stale_running_minutes) 30 requeue_stale_running() sets queue rows that stay Running longer than this back to Pending. It runs every 5 minutes from drain_due. Maximum Attempts (max_attempts) 3 Tries for a queue row whose run fails outside the flow's own steps, for example when the flow was deleted. After the last try the row is Failed. Drain Seconds (drain_seconds) 0 Time a drain job may keep claiming new batches. 0 uses the timeout of the default queue (300 seconds unless the workers config changes it) times 0.6. Commit Every (commit_every) 50 Queue rows a drain runs between database commits. Each row has its own savepoint.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Field Default Effect Queue Retention Days (queue_retention_days) 7 purge_queue() (scheduler event daily_maintenance) deletes Failed and Skipped queue rows older than this. It also deletes Automation Event Subscription rows with status Matched, Timed Out or Cancelled.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: Field Default Effect Step Output Limit (step_output_limit) 65536 Bytes of JSON output a step may pass to later steps. Larger output is replaced with {"truncated": true}. The step does not fail. Event Payload Limit (event_payload_limit) 65536 Bytes of JSON payload frappe.automation_engine.emit() accepts. Larger payloads throw Automation event payload is too large. Allow Unregistered Events (allow_unregistered_events) 0 When off, emit() and a Wait for Event step accept only event names that an app declares in the automation_events hook. When on, any event name is accepted.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.automation_engine import emit, is_enabled, skip_automations
from frappe.automation_engine import settings

settings.get("max_depth")  # value, or the default when 0 or empty

with skip_automations():
    doc.save()  # no automations are queued inside this block
  • automation_disabled in site config stops the engine without a database read, and wins over Disable Automations. See Site Config.
  • The engine does not dispatch during install, patches or migrate.
  • The scheduler events are in frappe/hooks.py: process_cron and drain_due every 5 minutes, process_date_based hourly, purge_queue in daily_maintenance.

docs.title: Flow Settings
docs.text:
Flow Settings holds site-wide options for Flow agents: the helper model, web search and the guest rate limit. Open it at /desk/flow-settings, or under Flow settings in the settings of the /flow page (flow/frontend/src/settings/specs.js).

Field Default Effect Helper Model (small_model) empty A Flow Model for small side jobs, like chat titles. FlowSession in frappe/flow/doctype/flow_session/flow_session.py sends it to the Flow runtime as small_model, only when that model is enabled.

docs.title: Web Search
docs.text: Field Default Effect Search Provider (search_provider) DuckDuckGo DuckDuckGo, Brave, Tavily or Exa. Sent to the Flow runtime as web_search.provider for each session. Search API Key (search_api_key) empty Password field. Shows and is mandatory when the provider is not DuckDuckGo. validate throws <provider> needs a Search API Key. when it is empty. Sent decrypted as web_search.api_key.

docs.title: Guest Chats
docs.text: Field Default Effect Guest Messages per Hour (guest_messages_per_hour) 0 (uses 30) Rate limit per IP address for the guest methods start and send in frappe/flow/api/guest.py, used by public agents. 0 or empty uses 30.

docs.title: Flow Knowledge Settings
docs.text:
Flow Knowledge Settings sets the embedding model, search type and chunking for Flow knowledge bases, chat attachments and agent memory. Open it at /desk/flow-knowledge-settings, or under Knowledge settings in the settings of the /flow page.

Field Default Effect Embedding Model (embedding_model) empty Flow Model that embeds chunks and queries (frappe/flow/knowledge/embedder.py). Its model ID must be an embedding model. While it is empty: Flow Knowledge Base and Flow Knowledge Source cannot be created, agents do not get the attachment search tool, and knowledge search throws Set an embedding model in Flow Knowledge Settings first. validate blocks a change while Flow Knowledge Chunk rows exist. Delete all knowledge sources first. Renaming the Flow Model updates this field. Embedding Dimension (embedding_dimension) 0 Read only. On save, validate calls the model once with a probe text and stores the vector width. Set to 0 when there is no model. Used to create the vector tables for knowledge, attachments and memory. Search Type (search_type) Hybrid Hybrid combines vector similarity with keyword matching. Vector uses similarity only. Read by frappe/flow/knowledge/retriever.py for knowledge search and attachment search.

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text: Field Default Effect Chunk Size (chunk_size) 1000 Maximum characters per chunk. Must be at least 1. A Flow Knowledge Source with its own Chunk Size uses that value instead. Chat attachments always use this value. Chunk Overlap (chunk_overlap) 200 Characters shared by two chunks next to each other. Must be smaller than Chunk Size, or validate throws. A source can override it.

docs.title: Studio Settings
docs.text: Studio Settings holds the API key for the AI assistant in the Studio editor. Open it at /desk/studio-settings.

docs.title: AI Settings
docs.text:
Field Default Effect AI API Key (ai_api_key) empty Password field. An OpenRouter API key. get_api_key() in frappe/studio/ai/llm.py reads it. When it is empty, the run method in frappe/studio/ai/api.py throws OpenRouter API key is not configured. Please set it in Studio Settings. The editor loads this document (studio/frontend/src/data/studioSettings.ts), and AIChatPanel.vue shows the chat only when the field has a value.

Note

The Open Settings button in the Studio AI panel opens the Studio settings dialog, but that dialog has only the App and Pages tabs. Set the key at /desk/studio-settings.

docs.title: Desk Settings
docs.text: This page is the field reference for the settings that change the desk: Navbar Settings, Desktop Settings, Global Search Settings, Domain Settings, Document Naming Settings and Notification Settings. All of them except Notification Settings are Single DocTypes that only System Manager can edit. For the general rules about settings pages, caching and code access, see How Settings Work.

docs.title: Navbar Settings
docs.text: Navbar Settings sets the application logo, the custom items of the sidebar menu and Help menu, and an announcement bar. Open it at /desk/navbar-settings. Only System Manager can edit it. After a save, the form clears the cache and reloads the desk (navbar_settings.js calls frappe.ui.toolbar.clear_cache).

docs.title: Application Logo
docs.text: Field Default Effect Application Logo (app_logo) empty Logo on the login page (frappe/www/login.py), the update password page (frappe/www/update_password.py) and the OAuth confirm page (frappe/integrations/oauth2.py). These pages use get_app_logo(). It takes the app_logo of Website Settings first, then this field, then the app_logo_url hook. The /desk/desktop page reads this field directly as its brand logo, with the Frappe app_logo_url hook as fallback (frappe/desk/page/desktop/desktop.py).

docs.title: Dropdowns
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Settings Dropdown (settings_dropdown) rows from the standard_navbar_items hook (Frappe ships none) Table of Navbar Item rows. Rows that are not hidden show in the menu of the sidebar header (sidebar_header.js, navbar_items). Help Dropdown (help_dropdown) About, System Health, Frappe Support from the standard_help_items hook Table of Navbar Item rows. Rows that are not hidden show under Help in the sidebar header menu, after the help links of the current page (get_help_siblings). Rows whose action contains frappe.ui.toolbar.show_shortcuts are skipped.

Navbar Item row fields:

Field Default Effect Item Label (item_label) empty Menu label, translated with __(). Mandatory when Item Type is Route or Action. Item Type (item_type) empty Route, Action or Separator. Read only on standard rows. Route (route) empty Shows when Item Type is Route, and is then mandatory. A desk route or an external URL. Read only on standard rows. Action (action) empty Shows when Item Type is Action, and is then mandatory. JavaScript that runs with frappe.utils.eval on click. Read only on standard rows. Hidden (hidden) 0 Hides the row from the menu. Is Standard (is_standard) 0 Read only. Set on rows that come from hooks. bench migrate removes standard rows that no hook defines now. Icon (icon) empty Icon of a Settings Dropdown row. The Help menu does not show it. Condition (condition) empty JavaScript expression, run with frappe.utils.eval each time the menu opens. The row shows only when it is true.

NavbarSettings.validate checks the label and the route or action of each Route and Action row and raises frappe.MandatoryError when one is empty.

docs.title: Announcements
docs.text: Field Default Effect Announcement Widget (announcement_widget) empty HTML shown in a bar below the header (navbar.html). When it has text, toolbar.js renders the header so the bar can show. Widget Color (announcement_widget_color) empty Background color of the bar. Empty means var(--bg-blue). Is Dismissible (dismissible_announcement_widget) 1 Shows a close button. A closed bar stays hidden in that browser (localStorage key dismissed_announcement_widget). When the text changes, the bar shows again.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Boot key: frappe.boot.navbar_settings holds the whole document (frappe/sessions.py uses frappe.client_cache.get_doc).
  • frappe.boot.app_logo_url holds the result of get_app_logo(). No desk JavaScript reads it in this version.
  • Add menu items from an app with hooks. frappe/utils/install.py (add_standard_navbar_items) fills the tables on install. sync_standard_items() runs on every bench migrate and adds rows whose item_label is not in the table yet.
# sample_app/hooks.py
standard_navbar_items = [
    {
        "item_label": "Sample Orders",
        "item_type": "Route",
        "route": "/desk/sample-order",
        "is_standard": 1,
    },
]

standard_help_items = [
    {
        "item_label": "Sample Docs",
        "item_type": "Route",
        "route": "https://example.com/docs",
        "is_standard": 1,
    },
]

Note

Set "is_standard": 1 in hook items. The migrate sync removes only standard rows when you delete them from the hook. A row without the flag stays in the table.

docs.title: Desktop Settings
docs.text: Desktop Settings selects what the desktop page shows and the style of the desktop icons. Open it at /desk/desktop-settings. Only System Manager can edit it. The Visit Desktop button opens /desk/desktop.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Desktop Page (desktop_page) Apps Apps shows the apps screen built from the add_to_apps_screen hook. Desktop Icons shows the grid of Desktop Icon records that users can arrange. Read by get_desktop_page() into frappe.boot.desktop_page, which frappe/desk/page/desktop/desktop.js checks. Icon Style (icon_style) Solid Solid or Subtle. Read by get_icon_style() in frappe/boot.py into frappe.boot.desktop_icon_style. frappe.utils uses it for letter icons (utils.js) and desktop_icons_item.html uses it for the icon image.

Side effects in DesktopSettings.on_update, only when desktop_page changes:

  1. Frappe clears the whole cache, so every user gets a new boot.
  2. When the new value is Desktop Icons, a background job (seed_desktop_icons) creates the desktop icons for all installed apps and public workspaces. It runs after commit.

Note

The desktop_page field is being retired (see frappe/desk/RETIRING.md). A patch moved sites that already had desktop icons to Desktop Icons. Those sites show a prompt that invites users to switch to Apps (frappe/utils/new_navigation_nudge.py).

docs.title: Global Search Settings
docs.text: Global Search Settings lists the DocTypes that global search covers, in priority order. Open it at /desk/global-search-settings. System Manager can edit it. Desk User can read it.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Search Priorities (allowed_in_global_search) DocTypes from the global_search_doctypes hook Table of Global Search DocType rows. Only these DocTypes are searched. Results are sorted by row order first, then by relevance (frappe/utils/global_search.py, search and sort_search_results). The search dialog (frappe/public/js/frappe/ui/toolbar/search.js) pins the first 5 rows as default DocType filters.

Global Search DocType row fields:

Field Default Effect Document Type (document_type) empty Link to DocType. The link filter hides Core module DocTypes. Configure (configure) button Opens a dialog to select the fields of the DocType that are indexed. The selection is saved as Property Setters for in_global_search and show_name_in_global_search, the same way as Customize Form. Then a background job rebuilds the index for the DocType.

Validation in GlobalSearchSettings.validate:

  • A DocType of the Core module raises "Core Modules {0} cannot be searched in Global Search."
  • A DocType in two rows raises "Document Type {0} has been repeated."
  • After validation, the cached priority list (global_search / search_priorities in the cache) is deleted.

The Reset button replaces the table with the DocTypes from the global_search_doctypes hook of every active app. It uses the Default key and the keys of the active domains. A progress bar shows over realtime.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Read the list: frappe.desk.doctype.global_search_settings.global_search_settings.get_doctypes_for_global_search(). It is cached.
  • The Global Search tab of the DocType settings panel in a form (frappe/public/js/frappe/form/doctype_settings/tabs/global_search.js) adds or removes the DocType row in this table.
  • Add your DocTypes for the Reset button. An optional index sets the position:
# sample_app/hooks.py
global_search_doctypes = {
    "Default": [
        {"doctype": "Sample Order", "index": 0},
        {"doctype": "Sample Item"},
    ]
}

docs.title: Domain Settings
docs.text: Domain Settings turns on domains. A domain is a set of modules, roles and custom fields that an app makes available only when the domain is active. Open it at /desk/domain-settings. Only System Manager can edit it. Frappe itself defines no domains, so on a site with only Frappe the list is empty.

docs.title: Active Domains
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Domains HTML (domains_html) not stored A checkbox for each Domain record (frappe.boot.all_domains). Checked boxes fill active_domains on save (domain_settings.js). Active Domains (active_domains) empty Hidden, read only table of Has Domain rows (field domain, Link to Domain). frappe.get_active_domains() reads it. The result is cached and is also in frappe.boot.active_domains.

Side effects in DomainSettings.on_update:

  1. For each active domain, Domain.setup_domain() runs. It enables the restricted roles, gives them to the current user, applies property setters and values, creates custom fields and calls on_setup.
  2. restrict_roles_and_modules() sets restrict_to_domain on the domain's Module Def and Role records. For each inactive domain, it disables its roles, removes them from all users and deletes its custom fields.
  3. Frappe clears the whole cache.

Where the active domains take effect:

  • DocTypes, modules and roles with restrict_to_domain set to an inactive domain are hidden from the user (frappe/utils/user.py, frappe/desk/desktop.py).
  • The Reset button of Global Search Settings uses the global_search_doctypes entries of the active domains.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Declare a domain in your app. The module must have a data dict. Keys that frappe/core/doctype/domain/domain.py and domain_settings.py read: modules, restricted_roles, custom_fields, properties, set_value, on_setup, default_portal_role, allow_sidebar_items, remove_sidebar_items.

# sample_app/hooks.py
domains = {
    "Sample Domain": "sample_app.domains.sample_domain",
}

# sample_app/domains/sample_domain.py
data = {
    "modules": ["Sample App"],
    "restricted_roles": ["Sample Role"],
}

Activate domains from code with frappe.get_single("Domain Settings").set_active_domains(["Sample Domain"]). It saves only when it adds a domain.

docs.title: Document Naming Settings
docs.text: Document Naming Settings is a tool to edit naming series options, change series counters and set how amended documents are named. Open it at /desk/document-naming-settings. Only System Manager can edit it. The form has no Save button (frm.disable_save()). Each section has its own button. Most fields are work fields: they hold input for a button and have no effect on their own. For naming rules in general, see Naming.

docs.title: Setup Series for transactions
docs.text: Field Default Effect Select Transaction (transaction_type) empty DocType to edit. The list has the DocTypes with a naming_series field that you can read. Selecting one loads its current options. Series List for this Transaction (naming_series_options) empty Shows when a DocType is selected. One series per line. Update writes them as the options Property Setter of the naming_series field. The first line becomes the default Property Setter. User must always select (user_must_always_select) 0 Shows when a DocType is selected. On Update, an empty first option is added, so the default is empty and the user must select a series. Update (update) button Runs update_series. Each series is validated. A series that another DocType already uses is rejected. Clears the DocType cache. Try a Naming Series (try_naming_series) empty Shows when a DocType is selected. Enter a series to get a preview. Field values in the series come from the last document of the DocType. Preview of generated names (series_preview) empty Read only. The names that preview_series returns. Help HTML (help_html) static Shows when a DocType is selected. Help text about series syntax.

docs.title: Update Series Counter
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Prefix (prefix) empty Series prefix from tabSeries and from series templates. Selecting one loads its counter into Current Value. Current Value (current_value) 0 The number of the last document made with the prefix. Change it, then click the button. Update Series Number (update_series_start) button Runs update_series_start. Only System Manager can run it. Sets the counter and adds a Version record for the Series change.

Warning

A counter set lower than an existing name makes the next insert fail with a duplicate name.

docs.title: Amended Documents
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Default Amendment Naming (default_amend_naming) Amend Counter Amend Counter names an amended document <original>-1, <original>-2 and so on. Default Naming names it like a new document. Read by _set_amended_name in frappe/model/naming.py when no override exists for the DocType. Amendment Naming Override (amend_naming_override) empty Table of Amended Document Naming Settings rows. Each row sets the rule for one DocType. Update Amendment Naming (update_amendment_naming) button Runs update_amendment_rule. Saves the default and the override rows, and deletes rows that you removed.

Amended Document Naming Settings row fields:

Field Default Effect DocType (document_type) none, required Link to DocType. The filter shows only submittable DocTypes. Action (action) Amend Counter Rule for this DocType. Read with frappe.db.get_value(..., cache=True) in _set_amended_name.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Only default_amend_naming and the override rows affect other code. Read the default with frappe.db.get_single_value("Document Naming Settings", "default_amend_naming").
  • The series options are not stored on this DocType. They are Property Setters on the target DocType's naming_series field. Ship them in your app as a Property Setter fixture.
  • The DocType settings panel of a form (frappe/public/js/frappe/form/doctype_settings/tabs/naming.js) and frappe.ui.NamingSeriesDialog call the same whitelisted methods.

docs.title: Notification Settings
docs.text: Notification Settings is not a Single. Each user has one record, named after the user. Frappe creates it when the user is inserted, or at the first desk boot if it is missing. Open your own record from the notification panel (Notification Settings), or go to /desk/notification-settings/<user>. Each user can read and write only their own record. System Manager can open all records except Administrator's (has_permission and get_permission_query_conditions hooks). After a save, the user's cached notification config is cleared.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Default Effect Enable System Notification (enabled) 1 When off, Frappe makes no Notification Log for the user (_get_user_ids in notification_log.py). Frappe sets it to match the user's enabled flag when a user is enabled or disabled. Open Documents (subscribed_documents) empty Table MultiSelect of Notification Subscribed Document rows (document, Link to DocType). When it has rows, the open-document counts of the notification config contain only these DocTypes (get_notification_config in frappe/desk/notifications.py). Empty means all DocTypes.

docs.title: Email Settings
docs.text: Field Default Effect Enable Email Notifications (enable_email_notifications) 1 Master switch. When off, the user gets no notification emails of any type. Email me for these notification types (email_notification_types) every enabled Notification Type except the ones in the notification_skip_email_types hook Shows when emails are on. Hidden table of Notification Type Preference rows (notification_type). An allow-list: a Notification Log sends an email only when its type is in the list (is_email_notifications_enabled_for_type). An empty list means no emails. In-app notifications are not affected. Email me for these notification types (email_notification_types_html) not stored Shows when emails are on. Checkbox grid that edits email_notification_types. Its options come from get_emailable_notification_types. Email Threads on Assigned Document (enable_email_threads_on_assigned_document) 1 Shows when emails are on. Emails the user when an email arrives on a document assigned to them (frappe/core/doctype/communication/mixins.py). Event Reminders (enable_email_event_reminders) 1 Shows when emails are on. Emails reminders for events (frappe/desk/doctype/event/event.py). Mentions (enable_email_mention) 1 Hidden. Not read by Frappe code. Replaced by email_notification_types. A v16 patch used it once to fill the new table. Assignments (enable_email_assignment) 1 Hidden. Not read by Frappe code. Replaced by email_notification_types. Document Share (enable_email_share) 1 Hidden. Not read by Frappe code. Replaced by email_notification_types. Seen (seen) 0 Hidden. Set to 1 when the user opens the notification panel and to 0 when a new notification arrives (notifications.js, set_seen_value).

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Boot key: frappe.boot.notification_settings holds the current user's record.
  • Check settings in Python with the helpers in frappe/desk/doctype/notification_settings/notification_settings.py: is_notifications_enabled(user), is_email_notifications_enabled(user), is_email_notifications_enabled_for_type(user, notification_type) and is_email_enabled_for_feature(user, fieldname). Each returns True when the user has no record.
  • Use is_email_enabled_for_feature only for the per-feature checkboxes. Use is_email_notifications_enabled_for_type for a Notification Type name such as Mention.
