docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text: Five Single DocTypes configure the public website and the portal: Website Settings, Portal Settings, Contact Us Settings, About Us Settings and Website Script. Use this page to find what each field does, its default, and which code reads it. For the concepts behind settings DocTypes, see How settings work. For how-to steps, see Website.

docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text:
Website Settings controls the home page, branding, navbar, footer, login page, analytics, robots.txt and redirects of the website. Open it at /desk/website-settings. Users with the Website Manager role can read and write it. The All role can read it.

Most fields reach the page through get_website_settings() in frappe/website/doctype/website_settings/website_settings.py. It copies a fixed list of fields into the Jinja context of every website page that extends templates/base.html. Other code reads one value with frappe.get_website_settings(key).

docs.title: Home tab: Landing Page
docs.text: Field Default Effect Home Page (home_page) empty The route that / shows. get_home_page() in frappe/website/utils.py uses it only after the role home page, the default_portal_home of Portal Settings (logged-in users), and the get_website_user_home_page / website_user_home_page hooks. If all are empty, Guests get login and users get me (System Users get desk). The controller checks the path with PathResolver. An invalid path shows a message and the field is cleared. Title Prefix (title_prefix) empty Added before each page title as Prefix - Title by set_title_with_prefix() in frappe/website/page_renderers/base_template_page.py. Also the alt text of the brand image in templates/includes/navbar/navbar.html.

docs.title: Home tab: Login Page
docs.text: Field Default Effect App Name (app_name) Frappe The name on the login page (frappe/www/login.py), the <title> of the desk (frappe/www/desk.py), the subject of the login-link email, and the brand name in email headers (get_brand_name() in frappe/email/email_body.py). Falls back to the app_name of System Settings. Disable signups (disable_signup) 1 Hides the sign-up link and form on /login (frappe/www/login.html). frappe.core.doctype.user.user.sign_up refuses new accounts. Social logins with no own sign_ups value also refuse new users (provider_allows_signup() in frappe/integrations/doctype/social_login_key/social_login_key.py). Max signups per minute (max_signups_per_minute) 500 The rate limit of sign_up, per 60 seconds (get_signup_limit() in frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py). Shows only when disable_signup is off. Show footer on login (show_footer_on_login) 0 Shows the website footer on /login. Read in frappe/www/login.py and frappe/templates/includes/login/login.js. App Logo (app_logo) empty The logo on the login and update-password pages, in the OAuth authorize page and in frappe.boot.app_logo_url (get_app_logo() in frappe/core/doctype/navbar_settings/navbar_settings.py). It wins over the app_logo of Navbar Settings and the app_logo_url hook. Also the logo in email headers when the Email Account has no brand logo.

docs.title: Home tab: Theme
docs.text: Field Default Effect Website Theme (website_theme) Standard The active Website Theme (get_active_theme() in frappe/website/doctype/website_theme/website_theme.py). If it is not Standard, templates/includes/head.html loads the theme CSS file instead of website.bundle.css. The theme JS is added to /website_script.js. The Set as Default button on a Website Theme sets this field. Website Theme Image (website_theme_image) empty Hidden. Not read by Frappe code. Website Theme image link (website_theme_image_link) empty Hidden. Not read by Frappe code.

docs.title: Navbar tab: Brand
docs.text: Field Default Effect Brand Image (banner_image) empty The image at the top left of the website navbar when brand_html is empty (templates/includes/navbar/navbar.html, templates/doc.html). Splash Image (splash_image) empty The image on the splash screen (templates/includes/splash_screen.html). Default /assets/frappe/images/frappe-framework-logo.svg. Brand HTML (brand_html) empty HTML at the top left of the navbar. Wins over banner_image. If both are empty, the first brand_html hook value or "Home" shows. Set Banner from Image (set_banner_from_image) button Sets brand_html to an <img> tag for banner_image. Client side only (website_settings.js). FavIcon (favicon) empty The favicon of website pages (templates/base.html). Default /assets/frappe/images/frappe-favicon.svg.

docs.title: Navbar tab: Navbar
docs.text: Field Default Effect Top Bar Items (top_bar_items) empty Table of Top Bar Item rows. The links of the website navbar (templates/includes/navbar/navbar_items.html). See Top Bar Item. Hide Login (hide_login) 0 Hides the Login link in the navbar (templates/includes/navbar/navbar_login.html). Show Language Picker (show_language_picker) 0 Shows a language selector for Guests. Sets window.show_language_picker in templates/base.html. Read by frappe/website/js/website.js and frappe/www/login.html.

docs.title: Navbar tab: Navbar Template
docs.text: Field Default Effect Navbar Template (navbar_template) empty A Web Template of type Navbar to render the navbar. templates/base.html uses Standard Navbar when it is empty. Navbar Template Values (navbar_template_values) empty Hidden JSON. Set by the Edit Values button. Not read by Frappe render code. The template gets the page context instead. Edit Values (edit_navbar_template_values) button Opens an editor for the fields of the Web Template. Shows only for a template other than Standard Navbar that has fields. Call To Action (call_to_action) empty The label of a primary button in the navbar (templates/includes/navbar/navbar_items.html). Call To Action URL (call_to_action_url) empty The link of that button.

docs.title: Navbar tab: Banner
docs.text: Field Default Effect Banner HTML (banner_html) empty HTML shown above the navbar on every website page (templates/base.html).

docs.title: Footer tab
docs.text: Section Field Default Effect Footer Items Footer Items (footer_items) empty Table of Top Bar Item rows. Links in the footer (templates/includes/footer/footer_links.html, footer_grouped_links.html). New rows get right = 0. Footer Details Copyright (copyright) empty Shown as © <value> in templates/includes/footer/footer_info.html. Footer Details Footer Logo (footer_logo) empty Image in the footer (templates/includes/footer/footer_logo_extension.html). Footer Details Hide footer signup (hide_footer_signup) 0 Copied into the page context. Not read by any Frappe template. Footer Details Address (address) empty Shown in the footer as footer_address. Footer Details Footer "Powered By" (footer_powered) empty Replaces the "Built on Frappe" line in the footer. Custom Footer Footer Template (footer_template) empty A Web Template of type Footer. templates/base.html uses Standard Footer when it is empty. Custom Footer Footer Template Values (footer_template_values) empty Hidden JSON. Set by Edit Values. Not read by Frappe render code. Custom Footer Edit Values (edit_footer_template_values) button Same as the navbar button, for footer_template.

docs.title: Integrations tab: Analytics
docs.text: Field Default Effect Enable in-app website tracking (enable_view_tracking) 0 /website_script.js sends a Web Page View log for each page view, unless the browser sends Do Not Track. make_view_log does nothing when it is off (frappe/website/doctype/web_page_view/web_page_view.py). Enable Google indexing (enable_google_indexing) 0 On update or delete of a published website-generator document that Guests can view, Frappe enqueues a Google Indexing API request (send_indexing_request() in frappe/website/website_generator.py). Validation: Google Settings must be enabled. Authorize API Indexing Access (authorize_api_indexing_access) button Starts the Google OAuth flow (google_indexing.authorize_access). Shows only when enable_google_indexing is on. Indexing refresh token (indexing_refresh_token) empty Hidden, read only, deprecated. Not read by Frappe code. Indexing refresh token (indexing_refresh_token_secret) empty Hidden Password field. Set by the OAuth flow. Used to get an access token for the Indexing API. Indexing authorization code (indexing_authorization_code) empty Hidden. Set by the OAuth flow. Google Analytics ID (google_analytics_id) empty Adds Google Analytics to /website_script.js (website pages). Falls back to google_analytics_id in site config. Not added when developer_mode is on. The desk reads only the site config key (frappe/www/desk.py). Google Analytics anonymise IP (google_analytics_anonymize_ip) 1 Adds anonymizeIp to the Google Analytics code in /website_script.js.

docs.title: Integrations tab: Account Deletion Settings
docs.text: Field Default Effect Automatically delete account within (hours) (auto_account_deletion) 72 The hourly job process_data_deletion_request starts the data deletion of each Personal Data Deletion Request in Pending Approval older than this. A value below 1 turns it off. Show account deletion link in My Account page (show_account_deletion_link) 0 Shows the account deletion link on /me (frappe/www/me.html).

docs.title: Header, Robots tab
docs.text: Field Default Effect Subdomain (subdomain) empty Read only. get_url() in frappe/utils/data.py uses it as host name when there is no request host and no frappe.local.site. <head> HTML (head_html) empty HTML added inside <head> of every website page (templates/includes/head.html). Use it for site verification tags. Robots.txt (robots_txt) empty The body of /robots.txt (frappe/www/robots.py). Falls back to the file in the robots_txt site config key. /sitemap.xml leaves out DocType web pages that it disallows.

docs.title: Redirects tab
docs.text: Field Default Effect Route Redirects (route_redirects) empty Table of Website Route Redirect rows. resolve_redirect() in frappe/website/path_resolver.py checks them after the website_redirects hook rules. The controller compiles each source as a regex and throws on an invalid one (not during migrate).

docs.title: Top Bar Item (child table)
docs.text:
Used by top_bar_items and footer_items.

Field Default Effect Label (label) required The link text. URL (url) empty The link. Leave it empty to make a group parent. Open URL in a New Tab (open_in_new_tab) 0 Adds target="_blank". Shows only when url is set. Align Right (right) 1 Puts the item on the right side of the navbar or footer. Parent Label (parent_label) empty Puts the item in the dropdown of that parent. Validation: the parent must exist in the same table and must have no URL.

docs.title: Website Route Redirect (child table)
docs.text: Field Default Effect Source (source) required A regex for the path. Frappe strips / and adds $. Target (target) required The new path. Can use regex groups such as \1. Forward Query Parameters (forward_query_parameters) 0 Adds the query string of the request to the target. Redirect HTTP Status (redirect_http_status) 301 One of 301, 302, 307, 308.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Read one value with frappe.get_website_settings("fieldname"). It caches the document on frappe.local for the request and reads it from frappe.client_cache.
  • On update, the controller clears the Guest cache, the website cache (frappe.website.utils.clear_cache) and then all caches.
  • Add context to every website page with the website_context hook. It overwrites keys from Website Settings.
  • Related hooks: website_redirects, get_website_user_home_page, website_user_home_page, brand_html, app_logo_url, base_template, web_include_js, web_include_css, website_clear_cache. See Hooks reference.
  • get_auto_account_deletion is a guest whitelisted method that returns auto_account_deletion.
import frappe

theme = frappe.get_website_settings("website_theme")  # "Standard"
app_name = frappe.db.get_single_value("Website Settings", "app_name")

Warning

frappe.boot.website_tracking_enabled is read by form_sidebar.js and form_timeline.js to show page view counts, but frappe/boot.py does not set it. Only a change of enable_view_tracking in the open form sets it, for that browser session.

docs.title: Portal Settings
docs.text:
Portal Settings sets the default role of new website users, the portal home page, and the sidebar menu of portal pages. Open it at /desk/portal-settings. Only Website Manager can read and write it.

Field Default Effect Default Role at Time of Signup (default_role) empty Role added to users made by sign_up (frappe/core/doctype/user/user.py) and by social login (frappe/utils/oauth.py). Validation: the role must be enabled and have no desk access. The form lists only such roles. Default Portal Home (default_portal_home) empty Home page for logged-in users with no role home page. Read by get_home_page() in frappe/website/utils.py. Validated as a path.

docs.title: Standard Sidebar Menu
docs.text: Field Default Effect Hide Standard Menu (hide_standard_menu) 0 Leaves the menu rows out of the portal sidebar (get_portal_sidebar_items() in frappe/website/utils.py). Portal Menu (menu) empty Rows that sync_menu() adds from the standard_portal_menu_items hook on install and migrate. The form allows only sorting and editing. The roles in these rows also decide is_portal_user() in frappe/utils/user.py.

docs.title: Custom Sidebar Menu
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Custom Menu Items (custom_menu) empty Your own sidebar rows. Shown after the standard rows.

The Portal Menu Item child table has title, enabled (default 0), route, reference_doctype, role and a read-only target. A row shows only when it is enabled and the user has its role (or it has no role). Rows for disabled DocTypes do not show.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• The Reset button calls reset(). It clears menu and syncs it again from the hooks.
  • Items from the portal_menu_items hook are added after both tables, always enabled.
  • The sidebar is cached per user in the portal_menu_items cache key. on_update clears the website cache and all caches.

docs.title: Contact Us Settings
docs.text: Contact Us Settings controls the /contact page. Open it at /desk/contact-us-settings. Only Website Manager can read and write it. The page code is frappe/www/contact.py and frappe/www/contact.html.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Field Default Effect Disabled (is_disabled) 1 /contact redirects to /404, send_message does nothing, and /sitemap.xml leaves out /contact. Clear it to publish the page. Send Acknowledgement Email (send_acknowledgement_email) 1 send_message emails a thank-you note to the sender. Forward To Email Address (forward_to_email) empty send_message emails the enquiry to this address, with the sender as reply-to. Every enquiry also makes a Communication with status Open. Heading (heading) empty The page heading and title. Default "Contact Us". Introduction (introduction) empty Text above the form. Query Options (query_options) empty Options of the subject select, one per line or comma separated. Default Sales, Support, General.

docs.title: Address
docs.text:
Field Default Effect Address Title (address_title) empty The heading of the address block. The address block shows only when this is set. Address Line 1 (address_line1) empty Shown in the address block. Address Line 2 (address_line2) empty Shown in the address block. City (city) empty Shown in the address block. State/Province (state) empty Shown in the address block. Pincode (pincode) empty Shown in the address block. Country (country) empty Shown in the address block. Phone (phone) empty Shown with a phone icon. Email Id (email_id) empty Shown as a mailto: link. Skype (skype) empty Shown with a message icon.

on_update clears the website cache for contact. send_message is a guest method with a rate limit of 100 calls per hour.

docs.title: About Us Settings
docs.text:
About Us Settings controls the /about page. Open it at /desk/about-us-settings. Only Website Manager can read and write it. The page code is frappe/www/about.py and frappe/www/about.html.

Section Field Default Effect (top) Disabled (is_disabled) 1 /about redirects to /404 and /sitemap.xml leaves it out. (top) Page Title (page_title) empty The page title and hero heading. Default "About Us". (top) Company Introduction (company_introduction) empty The hero subtitle. A placeholder text shows when it is empty. Org History Org History Heading (company_history_heading) empty Heading of the history list. Default "Company History". Org History Org History (company_history) empty Company History rows with year and highlight. Team Members Team Members Heading (team_members_heading) empty Default "Team Members". Team Members Team Members Subtitle (team_members_subtitle) empty Text under the heading. Team Members Team Members (team_members) empty About Us Team Member rows with full_name, image_link and bio. Team Members Footer (footer) empty HTML at the bottom of the page.

about.py reads the document with frappe.get_cached_doc. on_update clears the website cache for about.

docs.title: Website Script
docs.text:
Website Script holds JavaScript that runs on every website page. Open it at /desk/website-script. Only Website Manager can read and write it.

Field Default Effect Javascript (javascript) empty Rendered at the top of /website_script.js by frappe/www/website_script.py. Frappe loads that file on each website page through web_include_js = ["website_script.js"] in frappe/hooks.py. The desk does not load it.

/website_script.js also has the JS of the active Website Theme, Google Analytics and the view tracking code. It is sent with a public cache of 5 minutes when Website Settings, Website Script and the theme were not changed in the last 10 minutes. on_update clears the Guest cache and the website cache.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A change to home_page does not show for a user who has a role home page, a default_portal_home, or a home page hook.
  • navbar_template_values and footer_template_values are saved but not passed to the template.
  • hide_footer_signup has no effect in Frappe templates.
  • Contact and About pages are disabled by default. Clear Disabled to publish them.

docs.title: System Administration
docs.text:
Take backups and monitor logs and jobs.

Page What it covers Backups Take, download, schedule, encrypt and restore site backups with bench and the Download Backups page. Logs and Monitoring Find errors and check site health with Error Log, Activity Log, Access Log, Scheduled Job Log, RQ Job, RQ Worker, Recorder, System Health Report, System Console and Log Settings.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: A site backup has up to four files: the database dump, the public files, the private files, and a copy of site_config.json. You take backups with bench backup and restore them with bench restore. System Managers can download recent database backups from the desk. Take a backup before each update, and schedule regular backups on production servers.

docs.title: Backup files
docs.text:
Frappe saves backups in sites/<site>/private/backups/. You can change the folder with the backup_path key in site_config.json. File names start with the date and time and the site name, with dots changed to underscores:

File Example name Database 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz Site config 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-site_config_backup.json Public files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar Private files 20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • Partial backups (with includes or excludes) have -partial before -database.
  • Encrypted backups have -enc before the extension.
  • With --compress, file archives are .tgz.

Log DocTypes

In develop, Error Log, Access Log, Activity Log, Route History and Web Page View keep their rows in a separate SQLite file, sites/<site>/private/files/sqlite.db. The database backup does not contain these rows. A backup with --with-files contains the file, because it is in the private files folder.

docs.title: Take a backup
docs.text:
# database and site config only
bench --site frappe.localhost backup

# also public and private files
bench --site frappe.localhost backup --with-files

# all sites of the bench
bench --site all backup

Options of bench backup:

Option Description --with-files Also back up public and private files. --compress Compress the file archives (.tgz). -i, --include, --only DocTypes to back up, separated by commas. -e, --exclude DocTypes to leave out, separated by commas. --backup-path Folder for all backup files. --backup-path-db, --backup-path-files, --backup-path-private-files, --backup-path-conf Path for each file. --ignore-backup-conf Ignore the includes and excludes in site config. --verbose Print more output.

bench backup prints a summary with the path and size of each file.

docs.title: Includes and excludes in site config
docs.text:
To always back up only some DocTypes, or to always leave some out, add a backup key to site_config.json:

{
 "backup": {
  "excludes": ["Version", "Deleted Document"]
 }
}

Use includes for the other case. Unknown DocTypes in site config print a warning and are skipped. Unknown DocTypes in --include or --exclude stop the backup with an error.

docs.title: Schedule backups
docs.text:
Frappe does not take backups on its own. On a server, use the bench CLI to add a cron job:

bench setup backups

This adds a cron job that runs bench --verbose --site all backup every 6 hours and writes to logs/backup.log.

docs.title: Old backups
docs.text:
Frappe deletes old backups in two ways:

  • Each new backup first deletes all files in the backup folder that are older than 23 hours. Set keep_backups_for_hours in site config to change this.
  • An hourly job (frappe.desk.page.backups.backups.delete_downloadable_backups) keeps the newest Number of Backups (backup_limit, default 3) sets and deletes the rest.

Copy backups to another server or storage if you need to keep them longer.

docs.title: Download backups from the desk
docs.text:
1. Go to Download Backups (/desk/backups). You need the System Manager role.
  2. Click a backup to download the database file.

The page shows the newest database backups, up to Number of Backups. Each download makes an Access Log entry. The buttons are:

Button What it does Set Number of Backups Opens System Settings at Number of Backups. Download Files Backup Queues a backup with files on the long queue. Frappe emails you the download links when it is done. Get Backup Encryption Key Shows the encryption key after you confirm your password.

docs.title: Encrypt backups
docs.text:
1. Go to System Settings > Backups.
  2. Set Encrypt Backups (encrypt_backup).
  3. Save.

Frappe then encrypts the database and file archives with gpg. The gpg program must be installed on the server. The key is backup_encryption_key in site_config.json. Frappe creates it the first time it needs it. Store the key outside the server. Without it, you cannot restore an encrypted backup.

docs.title: Restore a backup
docs.text:
Warning

bench restore replaces the whole database of the site. Take a backup of the site first.

bench --site frappe.localhost restore \
  sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-database.sql.gz \
  --with-public-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-files.tar \
  --with-private-files sites/frappe.localhost/private/backups/20261122_052729-frappe_localhost-private-files.tar
  • If the path does not exist, bench restore also looks in sites/<site>/private/backups and in the bench folder.
  • For an encrypted file, Frappe uses --encryption-key, then the environment variable FRAPPE_BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, then backup_encryption_key in site config. It asks for the key if none is found, unless you pass --non-interactive.
  • --admin-password sets the Administrator password after the restore.
  • Frappe asks you to confirm when the backup comes from a newer version of Frappe. --force skips this check and the SQL file validation.
  • Run bench --site <site> migrate after a restore from an older version.

A partial backup cannot be restored with bench restore. Use bench --site <site> partial-restore <file>. It restores only the tables in the file, into the existing site.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.utils.backups import new_backup

odb = new_backup(ignore_files=True, force=True)
print(odb.backup_path_db)
  • frappe.utils.backups.new_backup(...) takes a backup and returns the BackupGenerator. Without force=True, it reuses a complete backup set (database, files, private files and config) from the last 6 hours if one exists.
  • frappe.utils.backups.fetch_latest_backups() returns the paths of the latest backups. It needs System Manager.
  • Site config keys: backup, backup_path, keep_backups_for_hours and backup_encryption_key. See Site Config reference.

docs.title: Logs and Monitoring
docs.text: Frappe records errors, logins, data access, scheduled job runs and background jobs in log DocTypes. Use them to find out why something failed, who did what, and whether workers and the scheduler run. Use the Recorder and the System Health Report to look at performance and the state of the site. Most of these DocTypes need the System Manager role.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
DocType Route What it records Error Log /desk/error-log Unhandled exceptions and errors logged by code. Activity Log /desk/activity-log Login, logout and impersonation. Access Log /desk/access-log Exports, printed documents, report views, private file and backup downloads. Scheduled Job Log /desk/scheduled-job-log One row per run of a scheduled job. API Request Log /desk/api-request-log API calls, if Log API Requests is set in System Settings. RQ Job /desk/rq-job Background jobs in Redis queues. RQ Worker /desk/rq-worker Background workers that run now. Recorder /desk/recorder Requests and jobs with their SQL queries, while recording is on. System Health Report /desk/system-health-report A live summary of workers, scheduler, database, cache, email and errors.

Log database

In develop, Error Log, Access Log, Activity Log, Route History and Web Page View store their rows in a separate SQLite database, sites/<site>/private/files/sqlite.db, not in the site database. A log entry stays even when the transaction that caused it rolls back.

docs.title: Error Log
docs.text:
Frappe adds an Error Log for each unhandled exception in a request or a background job. Code can also add one with frappe.log_error.

Label Fieldname Description Title method Short description, often the last line of the traceback. Error error Full traceback. Reference DocType / Reference Name reference_doctype, reference_name The document the error is about, if known. Seen seen Set when a user opens the log. The list shows "Seen" or "Not Seen". Trace ID trace_id ID of the request or job. Fingerprint fingerprint Hash of the stack. The same error has the same fingerprint.

The form shows how often the error occurred, first seen, last seen and a 30-day chart. Use Show Similar Errors to list logs with the same fingerprint, and Open reference document to open the document.

Some errors are queued in Redis first, for example during read-only requests. The list menu then shows Flush Error Logs to save them now. Clear Error Logs in the list menu deletes all Error Logs.

docs.title: Activity Log and Access Log
docs.text:
Activity Log has Operation (operation: Login, Logout or Impersonate), Status (status), User, IP Address and Subject. Failed logins also show here. Use it to audit who logged in and from where.

Access Log has User, Export From, Reference Document, Report Name, Filters, File Type, Method and Timestamp. Use it to see who exported or printed data.

docs.title: Scheduled Job Log
docs.text: Each run of a scheduled job adds a row with Scheduled Job (scheduled_job_type), Status (Scheduled, Complete or Failed) and Details (the traceback if it failed). Open the Scheduled Job Type to see the frequency and the last run. See Scheduler.

docs.title: RQ Job and RQ Worker
docs.text:
RQ Job and RQ Worker are virtual DocTypes. They read the jobs and workers from Redis. Nothing is saved in the database.

RQ Job fields: Job ID, Job Name, Queue (default, short or long), Status (queued, started, finished, failed, deferred, scheduled or canceled), Timeout, Time Taken, Arguments and Exception.

  • The list shows "Scheduler: Active" or "Scheduler: Inactive". If inactive, use Actions > Enable Scheduler.
  • Actions > Remove Failed Jobs deletes all failed jobs of the site.
  • On a job with status started or queued, Force Stop job stops it.

RQ Worker shows Queue(s), Status, Current Job ID, Successful Job Count, Failed Job Count, Last Heartbeat and Utilization %. If the list is empty, no worker runs. See Background Jobs.

docs.title: Recorder
docs.text:
The Recorder captures web requests and background jobs with their SQL queries, timings, call stacks and EXPLAIN output. Only Administrator can use it.

  1. Go to Recorder (/desk/recorder).
  2. Click Start.
  3. Set the options and click Start Recording.
  4. Do the slow action in another tab.
  5. Click Stop.
  6. Open a row to see its queries.

Option Default Description Record Web Requests / Request path filter on, / Records requests whose path starts with the filter. Record Background Jobs / Background Jobs filter on, empty Records jobs whose name matches the filter. Empty records all. Record SQL queries on Generate EXPLAIN for SQL queries on Capture callstack of SQL queries on Capture document lifecycle timeline on Times each controller method and doc_events handler. Run cProfile off Adds Python profile output. It is slow.

Recording stops on its own after 10 minutes. On a recorded request, Suggest Optimizations proposes database indexes, and Add Indexes adds the ones you select. Use Clear to delete all recordings. Export and Import in the menu move recordings between sites.

From the command line, use bench --site <site> start-recording and bench --site <site> stop-recording.

docs.title: System Health Report
docs.text:
Open System Health Report (/desk/system-health-report). Frappe builds the report each time you open it. It does not save it.

Section What it shows Background Jobs Number of workers, pending jobs per queue, worker use. Background Jobs Check runs a test job and shows its status. Scheduler Scheduler Status, the oldest job that did not run, and failing scheduled jobs of the last 7 days. Database Database type and version, storage use, largest tables. MariaDB Variables Buffer pool size and binary logging. Cache Number of Redis keys and memory use. Realtime (SocketIO) SocketIO Ping Check (Pass or Fail) and the transport mode. File Storage and Backups Size of public and private files, number and size of backups on the server. Users Total users, new users and failed logins in the last 30 days, active sessions. Emails Outgoing, pending, failed, handled and unhandled emails. Errors Error count of the last day and the top errors.

docs.title: System Console
docs.text:
System Console (/desk/system-console) runs Python or SQL on the site from the desk. Only Administrator has access.

  • Type Python runs the code in the same restricted environment as Server Scripts. It needs server_script_enabled in common_site_config.json. See Server and Client Scripts.
  • Type SQL runs the query in a read-only transaction.
  • Frappe rolls back all changes unless Commit is set.
  • Each run adds a Console Log with the script and whether it committed.
  • Show Processlist lists the running database queries.

docs.title: Log Settings and cleanup
docs.text:
Log Settings (/desk/log-settings) sets how long Frappe keeps each log. Each row in Logs to Clear has Log DocType and Clear Logs After (days). A daily job deletes older rows. Defaults come from the default_log_clearing_doctypes hook, for example:

Log DocType Days Error Log 14 Scheduled Job Log 7 Email Queue 30 Activity Log 90 API Request Log 90

To shrink a large log table at once, use the CLI. It copies recent rows to a new table and swaps the tables:

bench --site frappe.localhost clear-log-table --doctype "Scheduled Job Log" --days 30

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
try:
    process_sample_order(order)
except Exception:
    frappe.log_error(title="Sample Order sync failed", reference_doctype="Sample Order", reference_name=order.name)
  • frappe.log_error(title=None, message=None, reference_doctype=None, reference_name=None, *, defer_insert=False) saves the current traceback if you do not pass message. It never raises.
  • To make your own log DocType clearable, add a static method clear_old_logs(days) to its controller, and add it to the hook:
# sample_app/hooks.py
default_log_clearing_doctypes = {
    "Sample Sync Log": 30,
}
  • The Recorder API is in frappe/recorder.py (frappe.recorder.start, stop, get, delete). See Performance.

docs.title: Users and Permissions
docs.text:
Manage users and roles, role permissions and user permissions.

Page What it covers Users and Roles Create users, give them roles, group roles with Role Profiles, limit modules with Module Profiles, and set password, login and two-factor rules. Role Permissions Set what each role can do on each DocType with the Role Permissions Manager, permission levels, rights, "Only If Creator" and custom Permission Types. User Permissions Limit a user to specific records with User Permission, including applicable DocTypes, default values, descendants, strict mode and the permitted documents report.

docs.title: Role Permissions
docs.text: Role permissions decide what a user can do with a DocType. Each rule gives one role a set of rights, such as Read or Write, on one DocType at one permission level. A user gets the rights of all their roles together. Use the Role Permissions Manager to change these rules on a site. To limit a user to some records only, add User Permissions on top.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text:
• Rule: one row with a DocType, a role, a level and rights. The DocType JSON of an app holds the standard rules in DocPerm.
  • Custom rules: when you change any rule in the manager, Frappe copies all standard rules of that DocType to Custom DocPerm and edits the copies. From then on, Frappe uses only the Custom DocPerm rules for that DocType.
  • Permission level (permlevel): level 0 controls access to the document. Levels 1 and higher control groups of fields. Each field has a Permission Level property. A role needs access at level 0 first, or the higher levels have no effect.
  • Only If Creator (if_owner): the rule applies only to documents that the user created (owner).
  • Administrator has all rights on all DocTypes.

docs.title: Rights
docs.text:
Right Fieldname What it allows Select select Search and select records in Link fields, without opening them. Read also gives Select. Read read Open and view documents. Write write Change existing documents. Create create Make new documents. Delete delete Delete documents. Submit submit Submit documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Cancel cancel Cancel submitted documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Amend amend Amend cancelled documents. Only for submittable DocTypes. Print print Print and download PDF. Email email Send email from the document. Report report Open the Report view and reports of the DocType. Import import Use Data Import. The DocType must allow import. Export export Export data from the Report view. Share share Share documents with other users. Mask mask See the real value of fields that have the Mask property at this level. Other users see a masked value.

At levels higher than 0, only Read, Write and Mask apply.

docs.title: Open the Role Permissions Manager
docs.text:
1. Go to Role Permissions Manager (/desk/permission-manager). You need the System Manager role.
  2. Select a Document Type, a role in Roles, or both.

You can also open it from the list view menu (Role Permissions Manager) or from Customize Form (Actions > Set Permissions). The route /desk/permission-manager/Sample Item opens it for one DocType.

docs.title: Add a rule
docs.text:
1. Click Add A New Rule.
  2. Select the Document Type, for example Sample Item.
  3. Select the Role, for example Sample Role.
  4. Enter the Permission Level. Use 0 for document access.
  5. Click Add. The new rule has Read set.
  6. Select the other rights in the table. Each click saves at once.

To remove a rule, click the red button at the end of the row. A DocType must keep at least one rule.

docs.title: Restore the standard rules
docs.text:
Click Restore Original Permissions. Frappe deletes all Custom DocPerm rules of the DocType and uses the rules from the DocType JSON again. A Permission Log records the change.

Click View Activity Log to see recent changes to rules, with the user and time.

docs.title: Field-level permissions
docs.text:
1. Open Customize Form for the DocType.
  2. Set Permission Level of the fields to protect, for example 1.
  3. Click Update.
  4. In the Role Permissions Manager, add a rule for the role at level 1.
  5. Set Read, and set Write if the role may change these fields.

Roles without a level 1 rule do not see these fields.

docs.title: Only If Creator
docs.text: Set Only If Creator on a level 0 rule to give the rights only for documents that the user created. The user can still see the list, but only their own documents. You cannot set Report on a rule with Only If Creator. Frappe clears it.

docs.title: Permission Types
docs.text:
A Permission Type adds a custom right to one DocType. Frappe ships one: impersonate on User, which controls the Impersonate button. A custom right shows as an extra checkbox in the manager for that DocType only.

  • Fields: Permission Type (perm_type) and Applies To (DocType) (doc_type). The name is <doctype>_<perm_type>, for example user_impersonate.
  • You can create or delete a Permission Type only in developer mode.
  • The name cannot be a standard right, such as read.
  • On save, Frappe adds a Check Custom Field with that name to DocPerm, Custom DocPerm and DocShare.

docs.title: Pages and reports
docs.text: Use Role Permission for Page and Report (/desk/role-permission-for-page-and-report) to set which roles can open a desk page or a report. Select Set Role For (Page or Report), select the item, and edit the roles.

docs.title: Check a permission
docs.text: Use Permission Inspector (/desk/permission-inspector). Select a DocType, a Document, a User and a Permission Type. The Output explains each step of the check.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
Standard rules live in the permissions list of the DocType JSON in your app. Change them in the DocType form in developer mode. Code that checks permissions:

frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "write")                       # current user, DocType level
frappe.has_permission("Sample Item", "read", doc="Support Plan", user="user1@example.com")
frappe.has_permission("User", "impersonate", user="user1@example.com")  # custom Permission Type

To ship a custom Permission Type, create it in developer mode. Frappe exports it to <module>/permission_type/<name>/<name>.json, for example frappe/core/permission_type/user_impersonate/user_impersonate.json. bench migrate imports these files before DocTypes.

{
 "doctype": "Permission Type",
 "name": "sample_order_approve",
 "doc_type": "Sample Order",
 "perm_type": "approve"
}

For the has_permission and permission_query_conditions hooks, see Permissions for developers.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• After the first change in the manager, app updates to the DocType JSON rules do not apply on that site. Click Restore Original Permissions to get them.
  • Do not give the same rules to many roles. Give one user many roles instead.
  • Rules apply to the Report view and reports. Removing Report hides them.
  • Users who are not Administrator do not see rules for roles marked Is Custom in the manager.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• User Permissions
  • Users and Roles
  • Customize Form
  • Permissions for developers

docs.title: User Permissions
docs.text:
A User Permission limits one user to some records of a DocType. Role permissions say what a user can do with a DocType. User permissions say which records they can do it on. For example, give user1@example.com access to the Sample Item "Support Plan" only. The user then sees only that Sample Item, and only documents whose Link fields to Sample Item point to it.

User permissions do not give access. The user still needs a role rule from the Role Permissions Manager.

docs.title: How Frappe applies a User Permission
docs.text:
Assume a User Permission for user1@example.com with Allow = Sample Item and For Value = Support Plan.

  1. The DocType itself. The user can open only the Sample Items listed in their User Permissions.
  2. Linked DocTypes. In every DocType with a Link field to Sample Item, the user can open only documents where the link value is an allowed Sample Item. When a user opens a document, Frappe also checks the Link fields of its child table rows.
  3. Empty links. Documents with an empty link field stay visible, unless Apply Strict User Permissions is set in System Settings.
  4. Ignored fields. Link fields with Ignore User Permissions (ignore_user_permissions) set are not checked.

Frappe applies the same rules to the list view, reports, Link field search and frappe.get_list. Administrator and Guest are never limited.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Label Fieldname Default Description User user The user to limit. Allow allow The DocType of the allowed record. For Value for_value The allowed record. Is Default is_default 0 Uses this value as the default in Link fields of new documents. A user can have one default per DocType. Apply To All Document Types apply_to_all_doctypes 1 Applies the rule in all DocTypes that link to Allow. Applicable For applicable_for Applies the rule in this DocType only. Shown when Apply To All Document Types is cleared. Hide Descendants hide_descendants 0 For tree DocTypes. Gives access to For Value only, not to the records below it.

Frappe sets apply_to_all_doctypes to 0 when applicable_for has a value. It rejects a duplicate rule with "User permission already exists".

docs.title: Add User Permissions
docs.text:
1. Go to User Permission (/desk/user-permission).
  2. Click Add / Update.
  3. Select For User, for example user1@example.com.
  4. Select Document Type, for example Sample Item.
  5. Select Document Name, for example Support Plan.
  6. Set Is Default if this value should fill new documents.
  7. Select Apply to all Documents Types. It is cleared when the dialog opens.
  8. To limit the rule to some DocTypes, clear Apply to all Documents Types again. Then select the Applicable Document Types.
  9. Click Submit.

If Apply to all Documents Types is cleared and you select no DocType, Submit shows "Please select applicable Doctypes". The dialog makes one User Permission per applicable DocType. If rules exist for the same user and record, the dialog title changes to "Update User Permissions".

You can also open the list from:

  • The User form: Permissions > Set User Permissions.
  • The list view menu of a DocType: User Permissions.
  • The Role Permissions Manager: Set User Permissions.

To delete all rules of one user for one DocType, click Bulk Delete in the User Permission list.

docs.title: Strict user permissions
docs.text:
Apply Strict User Permissions (apply_strict_user_permissions) is in System Settings > Details > Permissions. Default: off.

When it is on, a user with User Permissions for a DocType does not see documents where the link to that DocType is empty. Single DocTypes are never checked in strict mode.

docs.title: Check what a user can see
docs.text:
Report Route Filters Permitted Documents For User /desk/query-report/Permitted Documents For User User, DocType, Show Permissions User Doctype Permissions /desk/query-report/User Doctype Permissions User, Doctype

Both reports need the System Manager role. Permitted Documents For User lists the documents the user can read. With Show Permissions set, it adds one column per right.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
from frappe.permissions import add_user_permission

add_user_permission(
    "Sample Item", "Support Plan", "user1@example.com",
    applicable_for="Sample Order",  # omit to apply to all DocTypes
    is_default=0,
)
  • add_user_permission(doctype, name, user, ignore_permissions=False, applicable_for=None, is_default=0, hide_descendants=0) does nothing if the same rule exists.
  • frappe.core.doctype.user_permission.user_permission.get_user_permissions(user) returns the rules as a dict keyed by DocType. Frappe caches it in Redis under user_permissions and clears it when a rule changes.
  • Set ignore_user_permissions on a Link field in the DocType JSON when the field must not limit access.
  • For the has_permission and permission_query_conditions hooks, see Permissions for developers.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A User Permission on a DocType that many DocTypes link to, such as a company or a department, limits all of them. Use Applicable For to narrow it.
  • Strict mode hides documents with empty links. Users can lose access to records they created before the link was set.
  • In a tree DocType, a rule on a parent also allows all descendants, unless Hide Descendants is set.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Role Permissions
  • Users and Roles
  • System Settings
  • Permissions for developers

docs.title: Users and Roles
docs.text: Every person who logs in is a User. A user gets access through roles. A Role is a name, such as Sample Role, that permission rules refer to. You give roles to users, and you give permissions to roles. Use this page to create users, assign roles, and set login and password rules. To set what a role can do, see Permissions.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType Purpose User One login account. The name is the email address. Role A named set of permissions. Role Profile A saved group of roles. Assign it to many users. Module Profile A saved list of blocked modules. Assign it to many users. User Type System User, Website User, or a custom type with a fixed role and DocTypes.

docs.title: Desk users and website users
docs.text:
The User Type (user_type) field decides if a user can open the desk.

  • System User can open the desk (/desk).
  • Website User can only use the website and portal pages.

You do not set this field by hand for standard types. When you save a user, Frappe sets System User if at least one of the user's roles has Desk Access (desk_access) set. Otherwise it sets Website User.

docs.title: Automatic roles
docs.text:
Frappe adds some roles without a row in the user's role table:

Role Who gets it Guest Every user, and visitors who are not logged in. All Every logged-in user, including website users. Desk User Every System User. Administrator Only the Administrator user. That user has all roles.

Use All or Desk User in a permission rule to give access to a large group.

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
1. Go to User (/desk/user) and click Add User.
  2. Enter Email and First Name.
  3. Keep Send Welcome Email set to send a link to set the password.
  4. Save.
  5. Open the Roles & Permissions tab and select the roles.
  6. Save.

The Roles & Permissions tab has:

  • Role Profiles (role_profiles). When you select one or more profiles, Frappe replaces the user's roles with the roles of these profiles on save. You cannot then add other roles by hand.
  • Roles Assigned (roles). The role checkboxes.
  • Module Profile (module_profile) and the module checkboxes. A cleared module is blocked. Blocked modules do not show in the user's sidebar.

To add or remove roles for many users at once, select them in the User list and use Actions > Add Roles or Actions > Remove Roles. Lists of more than 20 users run in a background job. The limit is 500 users per action.

docs.title: User form buttons
docs.text:
Button What it does Permissions > Set User Permissions Opens the User Permission list for this user. See User Permissions. Permissions > View Permitted Documents Opens the report Permitted Documents For User. Permissions > View Doctype Permissions Opens the report User Doctype Permissions. Password > Change Password / Reset Password Sets a new password or sends a reset link. Password > Reset OTP Secret Makes the user set up two-factor authentication again. Impersonate Logs you in as this user. You must give a reason. Frappe adds an Activity Log and notifies the user.

Impersonate shows for Administrator and for roles that have the impersonate permission on User.

docs.title: Security settings of a user
docs.text:
These fields are in the Settings tab, section Security Settings:

Label Fieldname Default Description Simultaneous Sessions simultaneous_sessions 2 Maximum number of sessions at the same time. Restrict IP restrict_ip Allowed IP addresses, separated by commas. Partial addresses such as 111.111.111 are allowed. Login After login_after The user can log in only after this hour (0-24). Login Before login_before The user can log in only before this hour (0-24). Bypass Restricted IP Address Check If Two Factor Auth Enabled bypass_restrict_ip_check_if_2fa_enabled 0 Lets the user log in from any IP address with two-factor authentication.

The API Access section has Generate Keys. It makes an API key and secret for token authentication. See Authentication.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Go to Role (/desk/role) to create a role.

Label Fieldname Default Description Role Name role_name The name. It is also the document name. Home Page home_page Route to open after login, for example /desk. Disabled disabled 0 If set, Frappe removes this role from all users. Desk Access desk_access 1 Users with this role become System User. Two Factor Authentication two_factor_auth 0 Users with this role must use two-factor authentication, if it is enabled in System Settings.

The Role form also shows the users, DocType permissions, reports, pages and workspaces of the role in separate tabs.

docs.title: Role Profiles and Module Profiles
docs.text:
1. Go to Role Profile (/desk/role-profile) and click Add Role Profile.
  2. Enter Role Name and select the roles.
  3. Save.
  4. Open a user and select the profile in Role Profiles.

A Module Profile works the same way. Enter Module Profile Name, clear the modules to block, and select the profile in the user's Module Profile field. On save, Frappe copies the profile's blocked modules to the user.

docs.title: User Types
docs.text:
System User and Website User are standard. A custom User Type (Is Standard cleared) gives a user a fixed role and access to a list of DocTypes only. Fields:

  • Role (role), required.
  • Apply User Permission On (apply_user_permission_on) and User Id Field (user_id_field). Frappe gives the role only to users who are linked from a document of this DocType through this field.
  • Document Types (user_doctypes) with the rights Read, Write, Create, Submit, Cancel, Amend, Delete, Email, Share and Print.
  • Document Types (Select Permissions Only) and Custom Document Types (Select Permission).
  • User Type Module (user_type_modules), the allowed modules.

On save, Frappe writes Custom DocPerm rules for the role. It also gives the role read, create and write on File.

docs.title: Password policy
docs.text:
Go to System Settings > Password.

Label Fieldname Default Description Enable Password Policy enable_password_policy 1 Checks password strength. Minimum Password Score minimum_password_score 2 From 1 (very weak) to 4 (very strong). Logout All Sessions on Password Reset logout_on_password_reset 1 Ends other sessions after a reset. Force User to Reset Password force_user_to_reset_password Number of days after which users must set a new password. Reset Password Link Expiry Duration reset_password_link_expiry_duration 1200 (seconds) How long a reset link works. Password Reset Link Generation Limit password_reset_limit 3 Reset links per hour.

docs.title: Login settings
docs.text:
Go to System Settings > Login.

Label Fieldname Default Description Session Expiry (idle timeout) session_expiry 170:00 Idle time in hh:mm after which a user is logged out. Allow only one session per user deny_multiple_sessions 0 On login, ends the older sessions beyond the user's Simultaneous Sessions (simultaneous_sessions on User, default 2). With the default, one other session stays open. Disable Username/Password Login disable_user_pass_login 0 Needs an enabled Social Login Key, LDAP, or login with email link first. Allow Login using Mobile Number allow_login_using_mobile_number 0 Allow Login using User Name allow_login_using_user_name 0 Login with email link login_with_email_link 1 Login without a password, with a link sent by email. Allow Consecutive Login Attempts allow_consecutive_login_attempts 10 Failed attempts before Frappe locks the account. Allow Login After Fail allow_login_after_fail 60 Lock time in seconds.

docs.title: Two-factor authentication
docs.text:
1. Go to System Settings > Login.
  2. Set Enable Two Factor Auth (enable_two_factor_auth).
  3. Select Two Factor Authentication method: OTP App (default), SMS or Email.
  4. Save.

When you enable it, Frappe sets Two Factor Authentication on the role All, so all users must use it. To use it only for some users, clear the check on All and set it on the roles that need it. Frappe asks for the second factor when a user has at least one role with two_factor_auth set. The SMS method needs a gateway URL in SMS Settings.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
user = frappe.get_doc("User", "user1@example.com")
user.add_roles("Sample Role")      # saves the user
user.remove_roles("Sample Role")   # saves the user

frappe.get_roles("user1@example.com")
# ['Sample Role', 'All', 'Guest', 'Desk User']
  • frappe.only_for("System Manager") raises frappe.PermissionError if the session user does not have the role.
  • Ship roles with your app as fixtures, or create them in after_install. See Fixtures and Patches.
  • The hooks on_login, on_session_creation and on_logout run with the login_manager argument (frappe/auth.py).
  • Bulk role endpoints: frappe.core.doctype.user.user.bulk_add_roles(users, roles) and bulk_remove_roles(users, roles). Both need write permission on User.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Disabling a role deletes it from all users. Enabling it again does not give it back. Standard roles cannot be disabled.
  • A user with a Role Profile loses roles that are not in the profile on the next save.
  • A user without any desk role becomes a Website User and cannot open /desk.
  • Administrator and Guest cannot be disabled, deleted or renamed.

docs.title: Website and Integrations
docs.text:
Publish web pages and web forms, and connect Frappe to other services.

Page What it covers Website Publish Web Pages and Web Forms, set up the site header, footer and home page in Website Settings, run the portal for website users, and track visits. Integrations Connect a Frappe site to other systems with Webhooks, OAuth clients and provider settings, Connected Apps, Social Login Keys, LDAP, Google settings and push notifications.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text: Frappe can send data to other systems, let other apps log in with Frappe, and let users log in with other providers. All settings are in the Integrations workspace in the desk. Use a Webhook to push document changes to another service. Use OAuth Client when another app needs access to this site. Use Social Login Key or LDAP Settings to let users log in with an outside account.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: DocType Use it to Webhook Send an HTTP request when a document changes. Webhook Request Log See each webhook request, its response and retries. OAuth Client Register an app that logs in to this site with OAuth 2.0. OAuth Provider Settings, OAuth Settings (Single) Set how this site acts as an OAuth server. Connected App Connect this site to an outside OAuth 2.0 provider, to call its API. Social Login Key Let users log in with Google, GitHub, Office 365 and other providers. LDAP Settings (Single) Let users log in with an LDAP or Active Directory account. Google Settings (Single) Google OAuth client and API key for Google Calendar, Google Contacts and the Drive picker. Push Notification Settings (Single) Send mobile push notifications through a relay server. Geolocation Settings (Single) Address autocomplete with the provider Geoapify, Nomatim or HERE.

docs.title: Webhooks
docs.text:
A webhook sends a request to a URL when a document event happens.

  1. Go to /desk/webhook/new.
  2. Enter a Name.
  3. Select the DocType and the Doc Event.
  4. Optional: enter a Condition, for example doc.status == "Open".
  5. Enter the Request URL and select the Request Method.
  6. Set Request Structure to Form URL-Encoded or JSON.
  7. Add the data: rows in Data for form data, or a Jinja template in JSON Request Body.
  8. Save.
  9. Click Preview to check the condition and the request body against a document.

A JSON body is a Jinja template. It gets doc and utils:

{
  "order": "{{ doc.name }}",
  "customer": "{{ doc.customer_name }}",
  "status": "{{ doc.status }}"
}
Field Default Description webhook_docevent after_insert, on_update, on_submit, on_cancel, on_trash, on_update_after_submit, on_change or workflow_transition. condition Python expression with doc and utils. The webhook runs only when it is true. request_url Target URL. is_dynamic_url 0 Renders the URL as a Jinja template with doc. request_method POST POST, PUT or DELETE. webhook_headers Extra headers, as key and value rows. enable_security, webhook_secret 0 Signs each request. See below. timeout 5 Request timeout in seconds. max_retries 3 Retries after a failed request. background_jobs_queue Queue for the request job. enabled 1 Turn off to stop the webhook.

How Frappe sends a webhook:

  • Requests are queued and sent in a background job after the database commit. If a document changes more than once in one request, the last version is sent.
  • Webhooks do not run during data import, patches, install or migrate.
  • Each request makes a Webhook Request Log with status Delivered, Failed or Exhausted.
  • A failed request is retried after 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 5 hours, then every 10 hours, up to Max Retries.
  • A workflow_transition webhook runs as a task of a Workflow transition. It runs at once, and an error stops the transition.
  • Requests go through a guarded session that blocks internal addresses. Set allow_internal_webhook_urls in common_site_config.json to allow them.

docs.title: Verify the signature
docs.text:
With Enable Security on, Frappe adds the header X-Frappe-Webhook-Signature. The value is the Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the request body, with the Webhook Secret as key.

import base64, hashlib, hmac

def is_valid(body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    expected = base64.b64encode(hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)

docs.title: Frappe as an OAuth 2.0 provider
docs.text:
Other apps can log in users with their Frappe account and call the API with a bearer token.

  1. Go to /desk/oauth-client/new.
  2. Enter App Name (Client Name).
  3. Enter the Redirect URIs and the Default Redirect URI of the app.
  4. Set Scopes (default all openid).
  5. Select the Grant Type (Authorization Code or Implicit) and Response Type (Code or Token).
  6. Optional: add Allowed Roles to limit which users can log in through this client.
  7. Save. Give the Client ID and Client Secret to the app.

Endpoints:

Endpoint Path Authorize /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.authorize Token /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.get_token Revoke /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.revoke_token User info /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.openid_profile Introspect /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2.introspect_token OpenID configuration /.well-known/openid-configuration Authorization server metadata /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server Protected resource metadata /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource

OAuth Provider Settings > Skip Authorization sets if users must approve access (Force) or not (Auto). OAuth Settings sets the server metadata, Enable Dynamic Client Registration (on by default), and Allowed Public Client Origins.

docs.title: Connected App
docs.text:
A Connected App lets this site call the API of an outside OAuth 2.0 provider for a user.

  1. Go to /desk/connected-app/new.
  2. Enter Provider Name.
  3. Enter the OpenID Configuration URL and click Get OpenID Configuration to fill the endpoints. Or enter Authorization URI, Token URI and the other URIs.
  4. Enter Client Id and Client Secret from the provider.
  5. Add Scopes.
  6. Save. Frappe sets Redirect URI. Register this URI at the provider.
  7. Click Connect to and the provider name. Log in at the provider to get a token for your user.

The redirect URI is <site>/api/method/frappe.integrations.doctype.connected_app.connected_app.callback/<name>. Tokens are saved per user as Token Cache records.

docs.title: Social login
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/social-login-key/new.
  2. Select the Social Login Provider: Custom, Facebook, Frappe, GitHub, Google, Office 365, Salesforce, fairlogin or Keycloak. Frappe fills the URLs for known providers.
  3. Enter Client ID and Client Secret from the provider.
  4. Turn on Enable Social Login.
  5. Set Sign ups to Allow or Deny new users.
  6. Save. The login page now shows a button for the provider.

Register the Redirect URL at the provider. For Google it is /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2_logins.login_via_google. For Office 365, set Tenant ID.

docs.title: LDAP
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/ldap-settings.
  2. Select the Directory Server: Active Directory, OpenLDAP or Custom.
  3. Enter LDAP Server Url, Base Distinguished Name (DN) and Password for Base DN.
  4. Enter the search paths for users and groups and the LDAP Search String.
  5. Map the LDAP fields for email, username and first name.
  6. Select the Default User Type and, for system users, the Default User Role.
  7. Optional: set SSL/TLS Mode to StartTLS, and map LDAP groups to roles in LDAP Group Mappings.
  8. Turn on Enabled and save.

Users then log in with their LDAP username and password. Frappe makes a user on first login unless Do Not Create New User is on.

docs.title: Google
docs.text:
Fill Google Settings with the OAuth Client ID, Client Secret and API Key from Google Cloud, and turn on Enable. Then:

  • A Google Calendar record syncs Frappe Events with a Google calendar for one user. Click Authorize Google Calendar Access after save.
  • A Google Contacts record syncs contacts.
  • Google Drive Picker Enabled with an App ID adds Google Drive to the file uploader.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.text: Turn on Enable Push Notification Relay in Push Notification Settings. On the first call to the relay server, Frappe registers the site and saves the API Key and API Secret. The relay server URL comes from push_relay_server_url in the site config.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Run code on document events in an app with the doc_events hook instead of a webhook. See Extending Apps.
  • frappe.integrations.doctype.connected_app.connected_app.ConnectedApp.get_active_token(user) returns a valid token and refreshes it when it expired.
  • Hook on_social_login runs after a social login.
  • API authentication with OAuth bearer tokens and API keys is in Authentication.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Use on_update with care. It runs on every save, so the target gets many requests.
  • A webhook body template must make valid JSON, or the request is logged as Exhausted.

docs.title: Website
docs.text: Every Frappe site also serves a website. You can publish pages, collect data with forms, and give website users a portal. Use a Web Page for content, a Web Form to let people add or edit records from the website, and Website Settings for the header, footer and home page. The desk is at /desk. Website routes are at the root of the site.

docs.title: Core concepts
docs.text: DocType What it is Web Page A page at /<route>. Content in Rich Text, Markdown, HTML, Page Builder blocks or a slideshow. Web Form A form at /<route> that makes or edits records of one DocType. Web Form Request A key that lets a person open one record in a Web Form without a login. Website Settings (Single) Home page, brand, navbar, footer, login and signup, redirects, analytics. Portal Settings (Single) The sidebar menu of the portal and the default role of new signups. Website Theme Colors, fonts and SCSS of the website. Website Script (Single) JavaScript added to every website page. Help Category, Help Article A knowledge base at /kb/<category>. UTM Source, UTM Medium, UTM Campaign Names for campaign parameters in tracked visits.

docs.title: Publish a Web Page
docs.text:
1. Go to /desk/web-page/new.
  2. Enter a Title.
  3. Enter a Route, for example sample-page. If you leave it empty, Frappe makes one from the title.
  4. Select the Content Type and write the content.
  5. Keep Published on.
  6. Save. The page is now at /sample-page.
Field Default Description content_type Page Builder Rich Text, Markdown, HTML, Page Builder or Slideshow. published 1 The page is public only when this is on. start_date, end_date A daily job publishes and unpublishes the page on these dates. show_title 0 Shows the title above the content. full_width 1 Uses the full width of the window. show_sidebar, website_sidebar Shows a Website Sidebar. enable_comments 0 Lets visitors comment. meta_title, meta_description, meta_image Tags for search engines and link previews. javascript, css Script and style for this page only. dynamic_template 0 Renders the content as a Jinja template. context_script Python that adds values to the template context. It runs in the safe script sandbox.

docs.title: Make a Web Form
docs.text:
A Web Form lets people make a record from the website, for example a Sample Order.

  1. Go to /desk/web-form/new.
  2. Enter a Title and select the DocType in Select DocType.
  3. Open the Form tab and add fields. You can also click Get Fields to add all fields of the DocType.
  4. Set access in the Settings tab.
  5. Save.
  6. Click Publish. Frappe sets Published and saves the form.
  7. Open the form with the See on Website link in the sidebar.

Visitors see the form at /<route>/new. When Show list is on, they see their records at /<route>/list and edit one at /<route>/<name>/edit.

Field Default Description login_required 0 Only logged-in users can use the form. anonymous 0 Saves responses without the user. Not used with Login required. key_required 0 The form opens only with a key from a Web Form Request. allow_edit 0 Users can edit their record after they send it. Needs Login required or Key required. allow_multiple 0 Users can send more than one response. Turns on Show list. allow_delete 0 Users can delete their responses. Needs Allow multiple. show_list, list_columns 0 Shows a list of the user's records. apply_document_permissions 0 Checks the permissions of the DocType for a record. When off, a user can open only records they own. allow_print, print_format 0 Lets users print their record. allow_comments, show_attachments 0 Shows comments and attachments to logged-in users. allow_incomplete 0 Lets users save without mandatory fields. button_label Save Text of the submit button. success_title, success_message, success_url What happens after the user sends the form. condition_json Filters for the records the form shows in its list. allowed_embedding_domains Origins that may embed the form, one per line. Empty means the same origin only. Use Copy embed code to get the snippet. client_script, custom_css Script and style for this form.

If a form is neither Login required nor Key required, Frappe turns off Allow editing after submit, Allow multiple responses, Allow delete and Show list on save.

docs.title: Send a link to edit one record
docs.text:
Use Key required to let a person without a login edit one record.

  1. Make a Web Form with Key required and Allow editing after submit on, and publish it.
  2. Open the record in the desk, for example a Sample Order.
  3. Click ... > Request via Web Form.
  4. Select the Web Form and an optional Expires On date.
  5. Click Copy Link, or click Email Link.

The link opens /<route>/<name>/edit?web_form_request_key=<key>. The dialog lists earlier requests with the status Not Used, Used or Expired. You need create permission on Web Form Request and write permission on the record.

docs.title: Website Settings
docs.text:
Go to /desk/website-settings.

Field Default Description home_page Route of the home page for visitors. title_prefix Text added before every page title. website_theme Standard The active Website Theme. app_name, app_logo Frappe App name and logo of the site. banner_image, brand_html Brand at the left of the navbar. top_bar_items Navbar links. footer_items, copyright, address Footer content. navbar_template, footer_template Web Templates for a custom navbar and footer. disable_signup 1 Turns off "Sign up" on the login page. max_signups_per_minute 500 Rate limit for signups when signup is on. hide_login 0 Hides the login link in the navbar. route_redirects Redirects from one route to another. head_html HTML added to <head> of every page. robots_txt Content of /robots.txt. google_analytics_id, google_analytics_anonymize_ip Google Analytics. enable_view_tracking 0 Logs visits as Web Page View records. show_language_picker 0 Shows a language picker on the website. show_account_deletion_link, auto_account_deletion 0, 72 Lets users ask to delete their account from /me. The account is deleted after the hours set.

docs.title: Portal
docs.text:
Website users (users without desk access) log in to the portal. /me shows their account page. The sidebar shows the portal menu.

Go to /desk/portal-settings to set:

  • Default Role at Time of Signup (default_role): role given to new users who sign up.
  • Portal Menu (menu): the standard menu items. Turn each one on or off.
  • Custom Menu Items (custom_menu): your own links.
  • Hide Standard Menu: shows only custom items.
  • Default Portal Home: route to open after login.

docs.title: Help articles
docs.text:
1. Make a Help Category. Frappe sets its route to kb/<category>.
  2. Make a Help Article in that category.
  3. Turn on Published.

The article route is the category route plus the article title. When you unpublish a category, Frappe also unpublishes its articles.

docs.title: Track campaigns
docs.text: Turn on Enable in-app website tracking in Website Settings. Each page visit then makes a Web Page View record with the referrer, browser and campaign values. The values come from utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign and utm_content (or source, medium, campaign, content) in the URL. Use UTM Source, UTM Medium and UTM Campaign records to give these values fixed names.

docs.title: For developers
docs.text:
• Add pages in an app with files in www/, and add routes with website_route_rules. See Website (developer).
  • A Web Form with Is standard set is exported to the module folder of the app, with a .py and a .js file. See Web Forms.
  • Hooks: website_route_rules, website_redirects, update_website_context, portal_menu_items, standard_portal_menu_items, has_website_permission, webform_list_context, website_generators.
  • frappe.website.doctype.web_form_request.web_form_request.create_for_document(web_form, docname, expires_on) makes a Web Form Request and returns the edit link.
  • frappe.utils.parse_and_map_trackers_from_url(url, create=False) reads the UTM values from a URL.

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• A Web Page with a past End Date cannot stay published. Frappe clears the date on save.
  • A standard Web Form can only be published or unpublished on a site. Other changes need developer mode.
  • A Link field in a Key required form must point to a DocType that Guest can read.
